answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is the {\it Common Drain} or {\it Source
Follower} stage, the MOS analog of the
emitter/collector follower. $100\%$ voltage
series feedback.

$$\eqalign{
D &\to V_{DD}, {\rm AC\; ground} \cr
G &\to V_{in} \cr
S &\to V_{out}\to R_{S}\to GND}$$

$R_{S}$ is the bias load, in practice often a
current source $I_{SS}$. In the symbol drawn
the $n$-bulk is strapped to the source, $V_{BS}=0$,
no back gate effect. In normal bulk CMOS $V_{B}=0$
and $g_{mb}\ne 0$.

### 1. Large signal - DC

$$V_{OUT}=I_{D}R_{S}$$
$$V_{GS}=V_{IN}-V_{OUT}$$

For $M_{1}$ off, $V_{IN}<V_{TH}$: $I_{D}=0$, $V_{OUT}=0$.

For $M_{1}$ saturated in strong inversion, ignoring
$\lambda $:

$$I_{D}= {k_{n}\over 2}\left(V_{GS}-V_{TH}\right)^{2}
      ={k_{n}\over 2}\left(V_{IN}-V_{OUT}-V_{TH}\right)^{2}
       ={V_{OUT}\over R_{S}} \tag{1}$$

$$k_{n}= \mu_{n}C_{ox}W/L$$

Quiescent point $Q$ for a DC bias $V_{IN}=V_{BIAS}$ is
solution of (1). In saturation:

$$V_{DS}=V_{DD}-V_{OUT}\ge V_{GS}-V_{TH}=V_{IN}-V_{OUT}-V_{TH}$$

$$V_{IN}\le V_{DD}+V_{TH}$$

always satisfied for $V_{IN}\le V_{DD}$, so saturation
can be maintained over the whole useful swing until
cut-off at low $V_{IN}$. In triode for very large $V_{IN}$:

$$I_{D}=k_{n}\left[(V_{GS}-V_{TH})V_{DS}-V_{DS}^{2}/2\right]$$

Hence $DC$ level shift:

$$V_{OUT}=V_{IN}-V_{GS}(I_{D})\approx V_{IN}-V_{TH}
        -\sqrt{2I_{D}/k_{n}}$$

Non linear follower with $\approx 0.3-0.8{\rm V}$ shift.

Limits:

* $V_{OUT,max}\approx V_{DD}-V_{DS,sat}\approx V_{DD}-0.2{\rm V}$
clipped when $M_{1}$ goes deep triode, $R_{S}$ cannot pull up.
* $V_{OUT,min}\approx 0$ clipped when $M_{1}$ cuts off, 
$R_{S}$ pulls to ground with $R_{S}C_{L}$ time constant.
No negative swing without negative supply.

### 2. Small signal

Hybrid $\pi$ at $Q$: $v_{gs}=v_{g}-v_{s}=v_{in}-v_{out}$

$$g_{m}= {\partial I_{D}\over \partial V_{GS}}=
\sqrt{2k_{n}I_{D}}={2I_{D}\over V_{GS}-V_{TH}}$$

$$g_{mb}= \eta g_{m}, \qquad \eta \approx 0.1-0.3$$
$$r_{o}=1/g_{ds}=1/\lambda I_{D}$$

$$ 
\begin{array}{c}
g \;\; o\;  -v_{gs}-+s\\
 \;\;\;|\; \\ 
  g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}
\end{array}
$$

With bulk to source $v_{bs}=0,\;g_{mb}=0$.
With bulk to GND $v_{bs}= -v_{out}$.

KCL at output node:

$$(g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}+g_{ds}v_{ds})+{v_{out}\over R_{S}}=0$$

$$v_{ds}= -v_{out}\;\;{\rm drain\; AC\; ground}$$

#### Voltage gain

Ideal $r_{o}\to\infty $, bulk to source:

$$v_{out}=g_{m}v_{gs}R_{S}=g_{m}(v_{in}-v_{out})R_{S}$$

$$A_{v}\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{in}}={g_{m}R_{S}\over 1+g_{m}R_{S}}
      ={1\over 1+1/g_{m}R_{S}}<1\tag{2}$$

In general:

$$A_{v}= {g_{m}R_{S}^{\prime}\over 1+(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds})R_{S}^{\prime}}$$

$$R_{S}^{\prime}=R_{S}\parallel r_{o}\approx R_{S}\parallel 1/g_{ds}$$

i.e.

$$A_{v}\approx {g_{m}\over g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}+R_{S}^{-1}}$$

If $g_{m}R_{S}^{\prime}\gg 1$,

$$A_{v}\approx {1\over 1+(g_{mb}/g_{m})}\approx 0.8-1.0$$

Typical $0.85$ with body effect, $0.95-0.99$ without.
With active load $R_{S}\to r_{o2}$, $A_{v}=g_{m1}/(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}
+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2})\to \approx 1$.

* No phase inversion, follower action.
* $100\%$ feedback makes it very linear for small signals.
* Distortion for large $v_{in}$ is $g_{m}$ modulation.

#### Input impedance

Gate draws no DC current:

$$Z_{in}= {v_{in}\over i_{g}} =\infty \;\; {\rm ideal}$$

$$Z_{in}(s)= {1\over sC_{gs}+sC_{gd}}\;\;{\rm at\; high\; f}$$

Normally $>{\rm M\Omega}$, capacitive $\sim$ fF-pF.
With bias resistor $R_{G}$ to set $V_{BIAS}$, $R_{in}=R_{G}$.

#### Output impedance

Put $v_{in}=0$, apply $v_{x}$ at source, measure $i_{x}$.

$$v_{gs}= -v_{x},\;v_{bs}= -v_{x}\;{\rm if\; bulk\; to\; GND}$$

$$i_{x}= {v_{x}\over R_{S}}+{v_{x}\over r_{o}}+(g_{m}+g_{mb})v_{x}$$

$$R_{out}= {v_{x}\over i_{x}}={1\over g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}}\parallel R_{S}
        \approx {1\over g_{m}+g_{mb}}\parallel R_{S}\tag{3}$$

$${\rm For\;}g_{mb}=0:\;R_{out}\approx {1\over g_{m}}\parallel r_{o}\parallel R_{S}\approx {1\over g_{m}}$$

Typically $20-200\,\Omega$, very low. That is the whole point.
Output impedance is low, capable of driving capacitive/resistive
loads with current gain

$$A_{i}\approx g_{m}R_{S}\gg 1$$

Voltage gain $\approx 1$ but power gain $\gg 1$.

With source resistance $R_{sig}$ driving the gate:

$$R_{out}=R_{S}\parallel r_{o}\parallel \left[{1\over g_{m}+g_{mb}}+{R_{sig}\over 1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})r_{o}}\right]\approx R_{S}\parallel {1\over g_{m}}$$

for $R_{sig}=0$.

### 3. Properties and use

* Voltage buffer / impedance transformer: high $Z_{in}$, low $Z_{out}$
* Level shifter $V_{OUT}=V_{IN}-V_{GS}$
* No voltage amplification, but current and power amplification.
* Very wide bandwidth: dominant pole at output

$$\omega_{p,out}\approx {1\over R_{out}C_{L}}={g_{m}\over C_{L}}$$

Miller multiplication of $C_{gd}$ is $1-A_{v}\approx 0$, so input
pole $\approx 1/R_{sig}C_{gd}$ is high.

* Feedback makes $THD$ low and $PSRR$ good if $V_{DD}$ is clean, drain is AC ground.

> Replacing $R_{S}$ by a bias current source $I_{SS}$ with
> impedance $r_{o2}\gg R_{S}$ gives $A_{v}\to 1$ more closely,
> $R_{out}=1/(g_{m}+g_{mb})\parallel r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}$ and allows
> DC coupling. The PMOS follower with $n$-well process can have
> bulk tied to source free of body effect and is often preferred.

In short, to first order:

$$A_{v}\approx \dfrac{g_{m}R_{S}}{1+g_{m}R_{S}}\to 1,\quad
  R_{in}\to\infty,\quad R_{out}\to 1/g_{m}\parallel R_{S}$$

with zero phase shift, used as a unity gain buffer that can source
large current into a low impedance load.

answer.text:
This is a {\it Common Drain} or {\it Source Follower} or {\it Grounded Drain Stage} with passive load $R_{S}$. In CMOS with isolated $n$-well it is often drawn with bulk to source:

> $$Bulk(M1) \equiv Source(M1) \rightarrow g_{mb}=0$$

If it is a discrete or $p-Sub$ technology $Bulk = GND$ and body effect $g_{mb} \ne 0$ must be kept.

It is $100\%$ voltage series feedback, no voltage gain $>1$, work as voltage buffer-impedance transformer, level shifter.

### 1. Qualitative - Large signal

$$V_{GS}=V_{G}-V_{S}=V_{in}-V_{out}$$
$$V_{out}=I_{D}\cdot R_{S}$$
$$I_{D}= \begin{cases}
0 & V_{GS}< V_{TH}\;\; {\rm cutoff}\\
k_{n}(V_{GS}-V_{TH})^{2} & V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{TH}\;\; {\rm SAT}\\
k_{n}[2(V_{GS}-V_{TH})V_{DS}-V_{DS}^{2}] & {\rm Triode}
\end{cases}$$

$$k_{n}= \frac{1}{2}\mu_{n}C_{ox}\frac{W}{L}$$

neglecting Channel Length Modulation $\lambda \approx 0$.

With $V_{DS}=V_{DD}-V_{out}$

$$V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{TH} \iff V_{DD}-V_{out}\ge V_{in}-V_{out}-V_{TH}$$
$$V_{in}\le V_{DD}+V_{TH}$$

so for all $0<V_{in}<V_{DD}$ it is in saturation once on.

* $V_{in}<V_{TH}$ : $M_{1}$ OFF, $I_{D}=0$, $V_{out}=0$ pulled to $GND$ by $R_{S}$.

* $V_{in}>V_{TH}$ : $M_{1}$ ON in SAT

$$I_{D}=k_{n}(V_{in}-I_{D}R_{S}-V_{TH})^{2} \tag{1}$$

$$V_{out}=V_{in}-V_{GS}=V_{in}-V_{TH}-\sqrt{\frac{I_{D}}{k_{n}}}$$

i.e. $V_{out}$ {\it follows} $V_{in}$ with a DC level shift $\approx V_{GS0}=V_{TH}+V_{OV}$ where $V_{OV}= \sqrt{I_{DQ}/k_{n}}$ is the overdrive.

Transfer characteristic is quasi linear with square law non linearity. The $R_{S}$ provides DC bias and local series feedback that linearizes.

Solution of (1) for the $Q$ point for a $DC$ bias $V_{IN,Q}$:

$$I_{DQ}= \frac{1}{R_{S}^{2}k_{n}}\left[1+k_{n}R_{S}(V_{INQ}-V_{TH})-\sqrt{1+2k_{n}R_{S}(V_{INQ}-V_{TH})}\right]$$

$$V_{OUT,Q}=I_{DQ}R_{S}$$

$$g_{m}= \left.\frac{\partial I_{D}}{\partial V_{GS}}\right|_{Q}=2k_{n}V_{OV}= \sqrt{2\mu_{n}C_{ox}W/L\cdot I_{DQ}}= \frac{2I_{DQ}}{V_{OV}}$$

$$r_{o}=1/g_{ds}\approx 1/\lambda I_{DQ} \;\to \infty \;{\rm for\; long\; channel}$$

Voltage swing:

$$0\le V_{out}\le V_{DD}-V_{OV1}$$

at low swing cut-off, at high swing $M_{1}$ remains in saturation up to $V_{DD}$ but $R_{S}$ cannot pull up beyond $V_{DD}-V_{GS}$.

It can {\it source} large current $I_{D}$ but can only {\it sink} $V_{out}/R_{S}$. Class A.

### 2. Small signal model

```
Vin o---||---+
             | vgs
            +-+
             |  gm.vgs      ro
D=VDD ac gnd ----+---||----+----o Vout
                  |       |
                  +--gmb.vbs
                  |
                 Rs to GND + CL
```

$v_{gs}=v_{in}-v_{out}$, $v_{bs}= -v_{out}$ if bulk = GND, $=0$ if bulk = source.

KCL at output node:

$$g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}+g_{ds}(v_{out}-0)+ \frac{v_{out}}{R_{S}}=0$$

with $v_{gs}=v_{in}-v_{out}$

$$(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}+G_{S})v_{out}=g_{m}v_{in}$$

$$G_{S}=1/R_{S}$$

> $$A_{v}\equiv \frac{v_{out}}{v_{in}} = \frac{g_{m}}{g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}+G_{S}} \tag{2}$$

If bulk tied to source $g_{mb}=0$:

$$A_{v}= \frac{g_{m}}{g_{m}+g_{ds}+G_{S}} = \frac{g_{m}(r_{o}||R_{S})}{1+g_{m}(r_{o}||R_{S})}$$

For $r_{o}>>R_{S}$ :

> $$A_{v}\approx \frac{g_{m}R_{S}}{1+g_{m}R_{S}} = \frac{1}{1+1/g_{m}R_{S}} <1$$

Typically $0.8-0.95$. $A_{v}\to 1$ for $g_{m}R_{S}>>1$.

With body effect to $GND$, $g_{mb}= \eta g_{m}$, $\eta \approx 0.1-0.3$ :

$$A_{v}= \frac{g_{m}R_{S}'}{1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{S}'} \approx \frac{1}{1+\eta+1/g_{m}R_{S}} < 0.8$$

No phase inversion. With active load $R_{S}\to r_{o2}$ :

$$A_{v}= \frac{g_{m}}{g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}} \approx \frac{1}{1+\eta}$$

Input impedance:

> $$Z_{in}= \frac{v_{in}}{i_{g}} \approx \frac{1}{sC_{gg}} \to \infty \; {\rm at\; low\; freq.}$$

Only capacitive $C_{gs}+C_{gd}$. No Miller multiplication because $A_{v}\approx 1$:

$$C_{in}\approx C_{gd}+(1-A_{v})C_{gs}\approx C_{gd}$$

Output impedance - turn $V_{in}=0$, apply $v_{x}$ at source:

$$i_{x}= (g_{m}+g_{mb})v_{gs}+g_{ds}v_{x}+ G_{S}v_{x}$$
$$v_{gs}= -v_{x}$$

> $$R_{out}= \frac{v_{x}}{i_{x}} = R_{S}||\frac{1}{g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}} \approx R_{S}||\frac{1}{g_{m}} \approx \frac{1}{g_{m}} \tag{3}$$

for $g_{m}R_{S}>>1$. Typically $50-500\,\Omega$. Low.

Hence voltage buffer: high $R_{in}$, low $R_{out}$, current and power gain $\approx g_{m}R_{S}$.

No Miller effect, wide bandwidth. Dominant pole at output:

$$p_{out}\approx \frac{1}{R_{out}C_{L}} = \frac{g_{m}+g_{mb}+G_{S}}{C_{L}}$$
$$p_{in}\approx \frac{1}{R_{sig}C_{gd}}$$

### 3. Properties and Use

* Buffer stage between high impedance node and low impedance load. As output stage of op-amp.
* Level shifter by $V_{GS}\approx 0.5-1V$.
* Feedback : voltage-shunt? The $R_{S}$ is series current feedback sampling $V_{out}$.
* Linearity improved by feedback, distortion $\propto 1/(1+g_{m}R_{S})$.
* Disadvantages: $A_{v}<1$, not for voltage amplification, limited negative swing and sinking capability, DC shift, body effect degrades gain if $n$-MOS in $p$-sub.
* To get $A_{v}\approx 0.99$ and larger swing replace $R_{S}$ by $NMOS/PMOS$ current source $I_{SS}$ with $r_{o2}>>1/g_{m}$.

Want a numeric design give $V_{DD}$, $W/L$, $R_{S}$ or $I_{DQ}$ and $C_{L}$ and $A_{v}$, $R_{out}$, swing and $BW$ can be calculated from (1)-(3).

answer.text:
It is the grounded gate - common gate - stage:

$$\eqalign{
M_{1}&: n{\hbox -}{\rm MOS}\cr
S&= B =V_{in}\cr
G&=V_{DD} = {\rm gnd}_{ac}\cr
D&=V_{out}=V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{D}\cr}$$

If the $n$ substrate does not allow
$B=S$ you get the conventional CG with $B=0$,
$g_{mb}\ne 0$ in {\it ac}. The $B=S$ connexion
suppresses the $g_{mb}$ term.

> {\it Gate is $ac$ ground, signal in at the
> low $Z$ source, signal out at the high $Z$
> drain through $R_{D}$. A voltage controlled
> current source. A current buffer - voltage
> amplifier with $A_{v}>0$ and $A_{i}\approx 1$.}
> The building block of the cascode and of
> the $50\,{\rm \Omega }$ wide band LNA.}

In small signal $V_{DD}=0$.

* {\it dc - Large signal} ${\rm .}$

Let for ${\rm NMOS}$ $V_{GS}=V_{G}-V_{S}=V_{DD}-V_{in}$,
$V_{DS}=V_{D}-V_{S}=V_{out}-V_{in}=V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{D}
-V_{in}$, $V_{BS}=0$. With long channel

$$I_{D}={k_{n}\over 2}\left(V_{GS}-V_{Tn}\right)^{2}
\left(1+\lambda V_{DS}\right)\;\;{\rm SAT.}$$

$$I_{D}=k_{n}\left[\left(V_{GS}-V_{Tn}\right)V_{DS}-
{V_{DS}^{2}\over 2}\right]\;\;{\rm TRIODE}$$

$$\beta =k_{n}= \mu_{n}C_{ox}W/L$$

Cut off for

$$V_{GS}<V_{Tn}\;\;:\;\;V_{in}>V_{DD}-V_{Tn}\;\;I_{D}=0,
\;V_{out}=V_{DD}$$

Saturation $V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{Tn}$ i. e.

$$V_{DD}-V_{in}-I_{D}R_{D}\ge V_{DD}-V_{in}-V_{Tn}$$

$$I_{D}R_{D}\le V_{Tn}\tag{1}$$

at the edge

$${k_{n}\over 2}\left(V_{DD}-V_{in}-V_{Tn}\right)^{2}
R_{D}=V_{Tn}$$

$$V_{DD}-V_{in}-V_{Tn}= \sqrt{{2V_{Tn}\over {k_{n}R_{D}}}}$$

i. e. a very narrow $\sim 50-200\,{\rm mV}$ window
below cut off is saturated. For larger $V_{GS}$,
{\it i. e.} $V_{in}$ low, (1) fails and the device is
in triode. With $V_{GS}=A=V_{DD}-V_{in}$ and
$X=V_{DS}=V_{out}-V_{in}$

$${V_{DD}-V_{out}\over {R_{D}}}=I_{D}
= k_{n}\left[(A-V_{Tn})X-X^{2}/2\right] \tag{2}$$

and $V_{out}=V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{D}$.
Putting $A=V_{DD}-V_{in}$, $X=V_{out}-V_{in}$

$${A-X\over {R_{D}}}=k_{n}\left[(A-V_{Tn})X-X^{2}/2\right]$$

$${k_{n}R_{D}\over 2}X^{2}-[k_{n}R_{D}(A-V_{Tn})+1]X+A=0$$

two roots, the physical $X<V_{Tn}$ branch is the VTC.
In SAT.

$$V_{out}=V_{DD}-{k_{n}R_{D}\over 2}\left(V_{DD}-V_{in}
-V_{Tn}\right)^{2}\tag{3}$$

parabolic, rising with $V_{in}$, $dV_{out}/dV_{in}>0$.
For $V_{in}\to -\infty $ (2) $\to V_{out}\approx
V_{in}+V_{DS(sat)}$, $I_{D}$ limited by $R_{D}$.

In a normally biased amplifier you bias in the
narrow SAT. window, e. g. $V_{inQ}\approx V_{DD}-V_{Tn}
-\Delta V$, $\Delta V =\sqrt{2V_{Tn}/k_{n}R_{D}}$,
so that the signal sits on a $\pm {\rm few}\times 10\,{\rm mV}$
swing. This is the reason the gate is normally {\it not}
tied to $V_{DD}$ but to a lower bias $V_{B}\approx
0.5-1.0\,{\rm V}$ to allow a source DC level near
ground and $V_{DS}\sim V_{DD}/2$ with current source
load. Tying $G$ to $V_{DD}$ sacrifices headroom and puts
the device in triode for any normal $R_{D}$ and/or
$g_{m}R_{D}>1$.

* {\it ac - Small signal} ${\rm .}$

In SAT. with $\lambda \ne 0$, $r_{o}=1/g_{ds}
=1/\lambda I_{DQ}$,

$$g_{m}=k_{n}\left(V_{GSQ}-V_{Tn}\right)=\sqrt{2k_{n}I_{DQ}}$$
$$g_{mb}= \chi g_{m},\;\;\chi \approx 0.1-0.3$$

$g_{mb}=0$ for the $B=S$ connexion of the figure.
Otherwise $g_{mb}\ne 0$ and $g_{m}\to g_{m}+g_{mb}$
below.

Low frequency model $g=0$, $s=v_{in}$, $d=v_{out}$,
$v_{gs}=-v_{in}$, $v_{bs}=0\;( -v_{in}$ if $B=0)$,
$v_{ds}=v_{out}-v_{in}$,

$$i_{d}=g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}$$

KCL at $D$ : $v_{out}/R_{D}+i_{d}=0$ {\it i. e.}
$i_{d}=-v_{out}/R_{D}$, so with $g_{mb}=0$,

$$-{v_{out}\over {R_{D}}}=-g_{m}v_{in}+g_{ds}(v_{out}-
v_{in})$$

$$v_{out}\left({1\over {R_{D}}}+g_{ds}\right)
=v_{in}\left(g_{m}+g_{ds}\right)$$

$$A_{v}\equiv {v_{out}\over {v_{in}}}
={g_{m}+g_{ds}\over {g_{ds}+1/R_{D}}}
=\left(g_{m}+g_{ds}\right)\left(R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\right)$$

$$\approx g_{m}\left(R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\right)
\approx g_{m}R_{D}\;\;{\rm for}\;R_{D}\ll r_{o}\tag{4}$$

and $A_{v}>0$, non inverting, with

$$g_{m}\to g_{m}+g_{mb}\;\;{\rm if}\;B={\rm GND.}$$

i. e. $A_{v}\approx (g_{m}+g_{mb})(R_{D}\parallel r_{o})$
for bulk to GND, numerically the same to $10-20\%$.

In triode $g_{m}=k_{n}V_{DSQ}$, $g_{ds}=
k_{n}(V_{GSQ}-V_{Tn}-V_{DSQ})$ and (4) is still
formally valid but $g_{ds}\gg g_{m}$ and

$$A_{v,{\rm tri}}\approx {g_{m}\over {g_{ds}}}\,
{ R_{D}g_{ds}\over {1+R_{D}g_{ds}}}<1$$

explaining the low gain if (1) is violated.

Current gain, $i_{in}$ at the source. KCL at
$S$ for a test source $v_{x}=v_{in}$, $i_{x}$ into
$S$, $v_{d}=v_{x}(g_{m}+g_{ds})/(g_{ds}+1/R_{D})$:

$$i_{x}=-i_{d}= -\left[-g_{m}v_{x}+g_{ds}(v_{d}-v_{x})\right]$$

$$i_{x}=v_{x}(g_{m}+g_{ds}){1/R_{D}\over {g_{ds}+1/R_{D}}}$$

$$R_{in}\equiv {v_{x}\over {i_{x}}}={1+g_{ds}R_{D}\over
{g_{m}+g_{ds}}} = {1+R_{D}/r_{o}\over {g_{m}+g_{ds}}}$$

$$={R_{D}+r_{o}\over {1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})r_{o}}}\tag{5}$$

$$R_{in}\approx {1\over {g_{m}+g_{mb}}}\parallel r_{o}
\approx {1\over {g_{m}}}\;\;R_{D}\ll r_{o}$$

$20-200\,{\rm \Omega}$ typical. It is the low
impedance input that makes the CG attractive as a
$50\,{\rm \Omega }$ terminated LNA and as a current
buffer. With a source resistance $R_{S}$ in series
with $v_{in}$ the over all voltage gain becomes

$$A_{vT}={R_{in}\over {R_{in}+R_{S}}}\,A_{v}
\approx {g_{m}R_{D}\over {1+g_{m}R_{S}}}$$

Output resistance, de-activate $v_{in}$,
$R_{S}=0$, $g=0$, $s=0$:

$$R_{o}|_{D}= r_{o}\tag{6}$$

so at the $V_{out}$ node

$$R_{out}=R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\approx R_{D}$$

If the source is driven through a finite $R_{S}$

$$R_{o}=r_{o}\left[1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{S}\right]+R_{S}
\approx (g_{m}r_{o})R_{S}$$

which is exploited in the cascode to get
$R_{o}\approx g_{m}r_{o}^{2}$ on top of a CS device.

Input capacitance $\approx C_{gs}+C_{sb}$, output
capacitance $\approx C_{gd}+C_{db}$, no Miller
multiplication of $C_{gd}$ because $g$ is $ac$
ground, so bandwidth

$$\omega_{p,in}\approx {1\over {R_{S}\parallel R_{in}\,
C_{in}}},\;\;\omega_{p,out}\approx {1\over
{R_{out}C_{out}}}$$

both high, $f_{T}$ limited, wide band.

In short

> $A_{v}\approx +g_{m}R_{D}$, $A_{i}\approx -1$,
> $R_{in}\approx 1/g_{m}$ low, $R_{out}\approx R_{D}$
> high, non inverting, no Miller, good high frequency
> current buffer. For practical bias the gate must be
> returned to $V_{B}<V_{DD}$ or $R_{D}$ replaced by a
> $p{\rm MOS}$ current source; the cascade of a CS
> stage driving this CG stage is the telescopic cascode.

Replacing $R_{D}$ by an active $p{\rm MOS}$ load
$r_{op}$ gives $A_{v}\approx g_{m}(r_{o}\parallel r_{op})
\approx g_{m}r_{o}/2$, $20-40\,{\rm dB}$.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is the grounded gate - common base
of MOS. $V_{D}=V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{D}$ is
taken as o/p . $V_{G}=V_{DD}$ is
a. c. ground.

$$V_{g}=0\;\;{\rm for\;signals}\;\;V_{d}=V_{out}\;\;V_{s}=V_{in}$$

$$v_{gs}=v_{g}-v_{s}=-v_{s}\quad v_{ds}=v_{d}-v_{s}$$

In ordinary use $M_{1}$ is in saturation
in inversion, ${\rm NMOS}$, ${\rm body}=
{\rm source}$ in the 3T symbol shown.
If the $4{\rm T}$ device is taken with
$p$ sub to $GND$, $V_{SB}=V_{S}>0$ and
$V_{T}=V_{T0}+\gamma \left[\sqrt{2\phi _{F}+V_{SB}}
-\sqrt{2\phi _{F}}\right]$,
$g_{m}^{^{\prime}}=g_{m}+g_{mb}$ is to
be substituted for $g_{m}$.

With $\left|V_{DS}\right|\ge \left|V_{GS}
-V_{T}\right|$, $\left|V_{GS}\right|> \left|
V_{T}\right|$

$$I_{D}\approx {1\over 2}k_{n}\left(V_{GS}-
V_{T}\right)^{2}\left[1+\lambda V_{DS}\right]
\tag{DC}$$

$$V_{GS}=V_{G}-V_{S}=V_{DD}-V_{I\,DC}$$
$$V_{DS}=V_{D}-V_{S}=V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{D}-V_{I\,DC}$$

$$V_{out}=V_{DD}-R_{D}{1\over 2}k_{n}
\left(V_{DD}-V_{in}-V_{T}\right)^{2},\,{\rm sat.}$$

Cut off for $V_{in}>V_{DD}-V_{T}\;:\;V_{GS}<V_{T},
\;I_{D}=0,\;V_{out}=V_{DD}$.

Triode for $V_{out}<V_{DD}-V_{T}\;:\;V_{DS}<
V_{GS}-V_{T}$.

Normal amplifying bias $V_{out}\approx V_{DD}
-I_{D}R_{D} \ge V_{G}-V_{T}=V_{DD}-V_{T}$.

In small signal, gate is a.c. ground:

```
          RD
   0 -----/\/\/\------o Vout = vd
                      |
        vg=0 o----|   |
                  |G  |
                  M1  |
              D --|   |-- S---o vs=vin
                  |   vs
                 _|_
```

Hybrid $\pi $: $g_{m}v_{gs}$ from $D\to S$,
$r_{o}=1/g_{ds}\approx 1/\lambda I_{D}$
between $D$ and $S$, $v_{gs}=-v_{s}$.

At the $D$ node, $V_{DD}=0$ for a.c.,

$${{v_{d}}\over {R_{D}}}+{{v_{d}-v_{s}}\over{r_{o}}}
+g_{m}v_{gs}=0\tag{1}$$

$$v_{gs}=-v_{s}$$

$${{v_{d}}\over {R_{D}}}+{{v_{d}-v_{s}}\over{r_{o}}}
-g_{m}v_{s}=0$$

$$\;v_{d}\left({1\over{R_{D}}}+{1\over{r_{o}}}\right)
=v_{s}\left(g_{m}+{1\over{r_{o}}}\right)\; \tag{2}$$

> $${A_{v}\equiv {{v_{out}}\over{v_{in}}}={{v_{d}}\over{v_{s}}}=
> {{g_{m}+g_{ds}}\over{g_{ds}+G_{D}}}={{g_{m}r_{o}+1}\over{1+r_{o}/R_{D}}}
> ={{R_{D}}\over{r_{o}+R_{D}}}\left(1+g_{m}r_{o}\right) } \tag{3}$$

$G_{D}=1/R_{D}$, $g_{ds}=1/r_{o}$.
For $g_{mb}\ne 0$ put $g_{m}\to g_{m}+g_{mb}$.

In particular

$$A_{v}\approx g_{m}R_{D}{\,1\over{1+R_{D}/r_{o}}}
\approx g_{m}(R_{D}\parallel r_{o})>0$$

for $g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1$.  With $r_{o}\gg R_{D}$

$$A_{v}\approx +\,g_{m}R_{D}\;\;{\rm including\; }R_{L}\;:\;
A_{v}\approx +g_{m}(R_{D}\parallel R_{L})$$

to be compared with the $CS$ stage $A_{v}\approx
-g_{m}(R_{D}\parallel r_{o})$. The common gate is
{\it non inverting} current buffer - voltage
amplifier. Large signal: $V_{in}\uparrow \to
V_{GS}\downarrow \to I_{D}\downarrow \to
I_{D}R_{D}\downarrow \to V_{out}\uparrow $.

Neglecting feedback through $r_{o}$,
$v_{gs}=-v_{in}$, $i_{d}=g_{m}v_{gs}=-g_{m}v_{in}$,
$v_{out}=-i_{d}R_{D}=g_{m}R_{D}v_{in}$.

Input resistance at the source. Put $v_{x}$ at
$S$, $v_{g}=0$, $D$ terminated in $R_{D}$ to
a.c. ground, measure $i_{x}$ entering $S$.

From (1) $v_{d}=-R_{D}I_{DS}$, $I_{DS}=g_{m}v_{gs}
+(v_{d}-v_{s})/r_{o}$ is the $D\to S$ current.
At $S$: $i_{x}=-I_{DS}$ so that

$$i_{x}={{v_{d}}\over{R_{D}}}\tag{4}$$

and with (2)

$${R_{in}\equiv {{v_{x}}\over{i_{x}}}={{v_{s}}\over{v_{d}}}R_{D}
={{R_{D}}\over{A_{v}}}={{1+R_{D}/r_{o}}\over{g_{m}+g_{ds}}} }$$

> $${R_{in}={{r_{o}+R_{D}}\over{1+g_{m}r_{o}}}\approx {1\over{g_{m}}}{1\over{1+1/g_{m}r_{o}}}\parallel r_{o}\approx {1\over{g_{m}}}\;\;r_{o}\gg R_{D} } \tag{5}$$

In general, with $g_{mb}$,

$$R_{in}\approx {1\over{g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}}}\approx
{1\over{g_{m}+g_{mb}}}$$

A low impedance, $\sim 10-10^{2}\Omega$ for
typical $g_{m}$. It is often sized to give
$R_{in}=R_{s}=50\Omega$ for RF matching:
$g_{m}\approx 20\,{\rm mS}$.

With a source generator resistance $R_{S}$ the
effective voltage gain to the source node is
divided:

$$A_{v,tot}={{v_{d}}\over{v_{sig}}}=A_{v}{{R_{in}}\over{R_{in}+R_{S}}}
\approx {{g_{m}R_{D}}\over{1+g_{m}R_{S}}}\xrightarrow{R_{S}=1/g_{m}} {1\over 2}g_{m}R_{D}$$

The short circuit current gain $i_{d}/i_{s}\approx -1$.

Output resistance at the drain. Deactivate
$v_{sig}$, $R_{S}$ from $S$ to ground, apply
$v_{x}$ at $D$, measure $i_{x}$.

$$-{{v_{s}}\over{R_{S}}}+I_{DS}=0,\;\;
I_{DS}=g_{m}(-v_{s})+{{v_{x}-v_{s}}\over{r_{o}}}$$

$${{v_{x}}\over{r_{o}}}=v_{s}\left(g_{m}+g_{ds}+G_{S}\right)
\;\;G_{S}=1/R_{S}$$

$$I_{DS}=v_{s}/R_{S}$$

For the impedance looking {\it into} the drain
alone, $i_{x}=I_{DS}$:

$$R_{o,d}= {{v_{x}}\over{I_{DS}}}=r_{o}+\left(1+g_{m}r_{o}\right)R_{S}
\;\xrightarrow{g_{mb}}\;r_{o}+\left[1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})r_{o}\right]R_{S}\tag{6}$$

Including the $R_{D}$ to $V_{DD}$,

$${R_{out}=R_{D}\parallel R_{o,d}=R_{D}\parallel \left[r_{o}+(1+g_{m}r_{o})R_{S}\right] }$$

For an ideal voltage drive $R_{S}\to 0$, $R_{out}\to
R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\approx R_{D}$; for a high
impedance drive the drain impedance is boosted by
$g_{m}r_{o}$, as in a cascode,
$R_{out}\approx g_{m}r_{o}R_{S}$.

Remarks:

* No Miller multiplication of $C_{gd}$ because
$G$ is a.c. ground. $C_{gd}$ is from o/p to
ground, $C_{gs}$ is from i/p to ground. Poles are

$$\omega _{p,in}\approx {1\over{(R_{S}\parallel R_{in})C_{in}}},\;\;
C_{in}\approx C_{gs}+C_{sb}$$
$$\omega _{p,out}\approx {1\over{(R_{D}\parallel R_{L})C_{out}}},\;\;
C_{out}\approx C_{gd}+C_{db}+C_{L}$$

Wide band, dominant pole usually at the
o/p. This is why the $CG$ and the cascode
$CS-CG$ are the workhorses of wide band and
RF LNAs, current buffers, impedance translators.

* Power gain $\approx A_{v}^{2}R_{in}/R_{out}\approx
g_{m}R_{D}^{2}/R_{out}$ is modest because of
low $R_{in}$.

* With $V_{G}=V_{DD}$ the available swing at
the source is limited to $V_{DD}-V_{GS}$.
Usually $V_{G}=V_{B}<V_{DD}$ is provided by a
bias network and $V_{in}$ is a.c. coupled to
the source through a capacitor, $S$ biased by a
current source $I_{B}$.

In the active load version $R_{D}$ is replaced
by a $p{\rm MOS}$ current source $r_{op}\parallel
r_{on}$, $A_{v}\approx g_{m}(r_{on}\parallel r_{op})$.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies the source-input, AC-grounded-gate common-gate stage and gives the non-inverting gain and approximately 1/gm input resistance, including reasonable ro refinements.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is the grounded gate - {\it Common Gate}
stage with ${\rm R_{D}}$ load. For small signals
${\rm V_{DD}}$ is $ac$ ground so $v_{g}=0$.

> $${\rm M_{1}}: n-{\rm MOS}, \;V_{GS}=V_{G}-V_{S}=V_{DD}-V_{in}$$
> $${\rm M_{1}}\; {\rm ON}\iff V_{GS}>V_{Tn} \iff
> V_{in}<V_{DD}-V_{Tn}$$
> Body is drawn shorted to source. If it is to $GND$
> $V_{SB}=V_{in}$ and $V_{T}=V_{T0}+\gamma \left[
> \sqrt{2\phi_{F}+V_{SB}}-\sqrt{2\phi_{F}} \right]$.

```
 AC ground
   |
   RD
   |  Vout
   +---o
   |
   D
  M1 G---AC ground = VDD
   S
   |
  Vin
```

Small signal, saturation, $i_{d}=g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}$
$g_{ds}=1/r_{o}=\lambda I_{D}$ , $g_{m}= \mu_{n}C_{ox}{W\over L}
\left(V_{GS}-V_{T}\right)=\sqrt{2\mu_{n}C_{ox}{W\over L}I_{D}}
=2I_{D}/V_{ov}$ .

With source-bulk short $g_{mb}=0$. With bulk to $GND$
replace $g_{m}\rightarrow g_{m}+g_{mb}$,
$g_{mb}= \eta g_{m}$, $\eta =\gamma /2\sqrt{2\phi_{F}+V_{SB}}$.

$$\eqalign{
v_{gs}&=v_{g}-v_{s}=-v_{in}\cr
v_{ds}&=v_{d}-v_{s}=v_{out}-v_{in}}$$

KCL at $D$, currents leaving $D$:

$${v_{out}\over R_{D}}+{v_{out}-v_{in}\over r_{o}}+g_{m}v_{gs}=0$$

$${v_{out}\over R_{D}}+{v_{out}-v_{in}\over r_{o}}-g_{m}v_{in}=0\tag{1}$$

$${v_{out}\over v_{in}}={g_{m}+g_{ds}\over G_{D}+g_{ds}}=
{(g_{m}r_{o}+1)R_{D}\over R_{D}+r_{o}}=(g_{m}r_{o}+1){R_{D}\Vert r_{o}\over r_{o}}$$

> $$A_{v}\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{in}}\approx g_{m}(R_{D}\Vert r_{o})
> \xrightarrow[r_{o}\gg R_{D}]{} g_{m}R_{D}>0 \tag{2}$$

Non inverting. ${v_{in}}\uparrow \rightarrow V_{GS}\downarrow
\rightarrow I_{D}\downarrow \rightarrow I_{R_{D}}\downarrow
\rightarrow v_{out}\uparrow $. With $g_{mb}\ne 0$,
$A_{v}\approx (g_{m}+g_{mb})(R_{D}\Vert r_{o})$.

Current gain $\approx 1$. The stage is a {\it current buffer}
{\it voltage amplifier}. It is the dual of the common
drain, low $R_{in}$ , high $R_{out}$.

KCL at $S$: $i_{in}$ entering $S$

$${v_{in}-v_{out}\over r_{o}}-g_{m}v_{gs}-i_{in}=0$$

$$i_{in}={v_{in}-v_{out}\over r_{o}}+g_{m}v_{in}\tag{3}$$

With (1),

$$i_{in}=v_{in}{1+g_{m}r_{o}\over r_{o}+R_{D}}$$

> $$R_{in}\equiv {v_{in}\over i_{in}}={r_{o}+R_{D}\over 1+g_{m}r_{o}}
> \approx {1\over g_{m}}{1+R_{D}/r_{o}\over 1+1/g_{m}r_{o}}
> \xrightarrow[r_{o}\gg R_{D}]{} {1\over g_{m}} \tag{4}$$

With $g_{mb}$: $R_{in}\approx 1/(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds})$.
$R_{in}\approx 50-500\, \Omega$ typ. so it can terminate
e.g. $50\Omega$ line. Driven from a source with
$R_{Sig}$ the effective gain is

$$A_{v,tot}={R_{in}\over R_{in}+R_{Sig}}A_{v}
\approx {g_{m}R_{D}\over 1+g_{m}R_{Sig}}$$

so a high $R_{Sig}$ kills the gain. It is a good
{\it voltage} amplifier only for low $R_{Sig}$.

Output resistance: de-activate $v_{in}$, $R_{Sig}$ from source
to ground. Impedance looking into $D$:

$$R_{d}=r_{o}+(1+g_{m}r_{o})R_{Sig}\;\; \left[+(1+g_{mb}r_{o})R_{Sig}\right]$$

At the output node

> $$R_{out}=R_{D}\Vert R_{d}\approx R_{D}\Vert r_{o}\xrightarrow[R_{Sig}=0]{}
> R_{D}\Vert r_{o}\approx R_{D} \tag{5}$$

for ideal $V_{in}$ source $R_{Sig}=0$, $R_{out}\approx r_{o}\Vert R_{D}$,
high.

### Large signal - DC bias window

Let ${k_{n}\over 2}= {\mu_{n}C_{ox}\over 2}{W\over L}$.

Cut-off: $V_{in}>V_{DD}-V_{T}$ : $I_{D}=0$, $V_{out}=V_{DD}$.

Saturation: $V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{T}$

$$V_{DS}=V_{D}-V_{S}=V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{D}-V_{in}\ge V_{DD}-V_{in}-V_{T}$$

$$I_{D}R_{D}\le V_{T}\tag{6}$$

$$I_{D}=k_{n}(V_{DD}-V_{in}-V_{T})^{2}(1+\lambda V_{DS})$$
$$V_{out}=V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{D}=V_{DD}-k_{n}R_{D}(V_{DD}-V_{in}-V_{T})^{2}$$

in saturation, a rising parabola to $V_{DD}$.
The saturation condition is

$$k_{n}R_{D}(V_{DD}-V_{in}-V_{T})^{2}\le V_{T}$$

$$V_{in}\ge V_{DD}-V_{T}-\sqrt{V_{T}/k_{n}R_{D}}$$

and $V_{in}<V_{DD}-V_{T}$ for ON. The bias window is
narrow and set by the DC value of $V_{in}$ itself.
In practice the source is biased with a DC current
source through a capacitor or with a $R_{S}$ to ground
so that $V_{GS}$ is set independent of the signal source.

For

$$V_{in}<V_{DD}-V_{T}-\sqrt{V_{T}/k_{n}R_{D}}$$

$I_{D}R_{D}>V_{T}$, $V_{out}<V_{DD}-V_{T}$ $\rightarrow$ triode:

$$I_{D}=k_{n}\left[2(V_{GS}-V_{T})V_{DS}-V_{DS}^{2}\right]$$

gain collapses.

In saturation the small signal gain is essentially
$g_{m}R_{D}$, with $g_{m}\propto \sqrt{I_{D}}$ set
by the $Q$-point.

### Remarks

* No Miller multiplication of $C_{gd}$. Input pole
$\omega_{p,in}\approx 1/R_{in}C_{in}$, $R_{in}\approx 1/g_{m}$
small $\rightarrow$ very high frequency pole. Output pole
$\omega_{p,out}\approx 1/R_{out}C_{L}$. CG is inherently
wide band. Used as RF LNA input stage, $50\Omega$ match
by $1/g_{m}=50\Omega$, as current buffer and as the
upper device of a cascode - it shields the input device
from the output giving high $R_{out}\approx g_{m}r_{o}^{2}$
and suppressing Miller effect.

* Dual of common drain; dual of common source in impedance.

* Disadvantage: low $R_{in}$ is bad for voltage source
with high $R_{Sig}$, DC level shifting problem because
$V_{S,DC}=V_{DD}-V_{GS,DC}\approx V_{DD}-V_{T}-V_{ov}$ is
high.

Addition of a source bias current $I_{B}$ or $R_{S}$ to
ground decouples $Q$-point from $V_{in,DC}$ and is the
usual practical form.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
With the usual convention that is the circuit
as drawn is degenerate it is instructive. In
normal form it is the {\it grounded gate}
or {\it common gate} stage

```
                    V_{DD}(ac=0)
                     |
                    R_{D}
                     | D
                +----o----+
                |    || G vb(ac=0)
                |   M_{1}
                |    || S<^ B
               C_{L}  |
                |  +--o--+
                |  |     |  if the wire is taken
               R_{L} C_{1}   literally R_{S}=0
                |  |     |  normally
                gnd + Vin  R_{S} or I_{S}gnd
                       -     |
                       gnd  gnd
```

with $V_{B}$ signal ground.

> {\it Remark on the figure:} As literally drawn
> $ S\equiv ac\; {\rm ground}$. $v_{S}=0$ for all
> $v_{in}$ and the stage has $A_{v}=0$.
> $C_{1}$ is shorted by the wire to ground.
> Normally the wire to ground is a dc bias
> impedance, high for $ac$, $R_{S}$ in the figure
> to the right, most often an $n$MOS current source
> $I_{S}$, $r_{OS}>>1/g_{m}$ . In the following
> $R_{S}$ is put $=0$ for DC but $=\infty $ for
> AC , i. e. the textbook $CG$.
> If you keep the literal short $R_{S}=0$ also for
> $ac$ put $R_{S}=0$ in the formulas below.
> You get $R_{in}=0\parallel 1/g_{m}=0$,
> $A_{v}=0$.

{\bf 1. DC bias} Take $M_{1}$ to be $n$MOS,
bulk $=p$ sub. {\rm ,} $S$ is the arrow terminal.

$$V_{GS0}=V_{B}-V_{S0}$$

and with the idealisation above $V_{S0}=0$

$$V_{GS0}=V_{B}\tag{1}$$

$$I_{D0}= {1\over 2}{\mu _{n}C_{ox}}{W\over L}
\left(V_{B}-V_{T}\right)^{2}\left(1+\lambda V_{DS0}\right)
\tag{2}$$
for $V_{B}>V_{T}$ in saturation and

$$V_{DS0}=V_{D0}-V_{S0}=V_{DD}-I_{D0}R_{D} \tag{3}$$

Saturation, $V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{T}$, requires:

$$V_{DD}-I_{D0}R_{D} \ge V_{B}-V_{T} \tag{4}$$

and determines the maximum symmetric swing

$$V_{o,max}=V_{DD}-I_{D0}R_{D} -V_{DS,sat}$$
$$V_{o,min}=V_{DS,sat}\approx V_{GS}-V_{T}$$

$V_{B}$ is the whole bias control. The
circuit has no source degeneration to desensitize
(2) and is very $V_{T}$ sensitive. In practice
$R_{S}$ or $I_{S}$ is used to set $I_{D0}$ and
$V_{B}=V_{S0}+V_{GS0}$.

For the 3 terminal symbol $B$ is strapped to $S$
$$V_{BS0}=0\qquad g_{mb}=0$$
If the bulk is to the global $gnd$ and $R_{S}\ne
0$, $V_{BS}\ne 0$, the threshold is

$$V_{T}=V_{T0}+\gamma \left(\sqrt{2\phi _{F}-V_{BS}}
-\sqrt{2\phi _{F}}\;\right)$$

and an extra $g_{mb}= \eta g_{m}$ appears in $ac$.

{\bf 2. Low frequency $ac$ model} $V_{B}=ac\,0$,
$V_{DD}=ac\,0$, $C_{1}=ac$ short for
$\omega >> \omega _{H}=1/R_{in}C_{1}$.  $R_{D}$
is the $ac$ load, in general $R_{D}^{\prime}=R_{D}\parallel
R_{L}\parallel C_{L}$.

Standard $ac$ model of the $n$MOS in saturation

$$i_{d}=g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}\tag{5}$$
$$g_{m}= \left.{\partial I_{D}\over \partial V_{GS}}\right|_{Q}
= \sqrt{2\mu C_{ox}{W\over L}I_{D0}}={2I_{D0}\over V_{GS0}-V_{T}}$$
$$g_{ds}=r_{o}^{-1}= \lambda I_{D0}$$
$$g_{mb}= -{\partial I_{D}\over \partial V_{BS}}=
{g_{m}\gamma \over 2\sqrt{2\phi _{F}-V_{BS}}}$$

Put $v_{g}=0$, $v_{b}=0$, $v_{s}=v_{in}$,
$v_{d}=v_{out}$.

$$v_{gs}= -v_{in}\tag{6a}$$
$$v_{bs}= -v_{in}\;\;{\rm if}\;B=gnd\tag{6b}$$
$$v_{ds}=v_{out}-v_{in}\tag{6c}$$

KCL at the $D$ node, current $i_{d}$ entering the
drain, $i_{R_{D}}=-v_{out}/R_{D}$ entering the drain
from $R_{D}$:

$$i_{d}+v_{out}/R_{D}^{\prime}=0 \tag{7}$$

for the unloaded stage $R_{D}^{\prime}=R_{D}$.
With (5)-(6)

$$-g_{m}v_{in}-g_{mb}v_{in}+g_{ds}(v_{out}-v_{in})
+{v_{out}\over R_{D}^{\prime}}=0$$

$$\left(g_{ds}+{1\over R_{D}^{\prime}}\right)v_{out}
=\left(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}\right)v_{in}\tag{8}$$

Hence the mid band voltage gain, non inverting,

$${A_{v}\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{in}}=
{g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}\over g_{ds}+1/R_{D}^{\prime}}
=\left(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}\right)\,
\left(r_{o}\parallel R_{D}^{\prime}\right) \tag{9}}$$

> $$A_{v}\approx \left(g_{m}+g_{mb}\right)
> \left(r_{o}\parallel R_{D}^{\prime}\right)
> \approx g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}\qquad {\rm for}\;\;
> r_{o}>>R_{D}^{\prime},\,g_{m}>>g_{ds},g_{mb}=0\tag{9a}$$

positive. No Miller multiplication of $C_{gd}$.

If $R_{S}$ is finite between $S$ and $ac$ ground
the usual voltage divider $R_{S}/(R_{S}+R_{in})$
appears:

$$A_{v, overall}= {R_{S}\over R_{S}+R_{in}}A_{v}\tag{9b}$$

with $R_{in}$ below. For $R_{S}\to 0$,
$A_{v, overall}\to 0$, the degenerate case of the
figure, and for $R_{S}\to\infty $ (ideal current
source bias) $A_{v, overall}\to A_{v}$.

Input resistance looking into the source with the
drain load present. KCL at $S$:

$$i_{in}= -i_{s}= -i_{d}\;\;+i_{g}\approx -i_{d}$$

more precisely with (5) $i_{s}=-i_{d}$.

$$i_{in}= g_{m}v_{in}+g_{mb}v_{in}+g_{ds}(v_{in}-v_{out})$$

Use (8) to eliminate $v_{out}$:

$$R_{in}\equiv {v_{in}\over i_{in}}=
{1\over g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}}\,
{1+g_{ds}R_{D}^{\prime}\over 1+R_{D}^{\prime}/r_{o,eff}}$$

In compact form

$${R_{in}= {R_{D}^{\prime}+r_{o}\over
1+\left(g_{m}+g_{mb}\right)r_{o}}\approx
{1\over g_{m}+g_{mb}}\parallel r_{o}\approx {1\over g_{m}}\tag{10}}$$

for $r_{o}>>R_{D}^{\prime}$.  Without body effect

$$R_{in}\approx {1\over g_{m}}\parallel r_{o} \approx
{1\over g_{m}}\;\; 20-500\,{\rm \Omega\;typical}\tag{10a}$$

So the $CG$ is a low $Z_{in}$ stage, current buffer,
often used for $50\,{\rm \Omega}$ matching, as
cascode device and as wide band stage because
$C_{gd}$ is not Miller multiplied.

With a finite source bias resistor $R_{S}$ to $ac$
ground the resistance seen by the source $v_{in}$

$$R_{in,tot}=R_{S}\parallel R_{in}\approx R_{S}\parallel
{1\over g_{m}}\tag{10b}$$

For the literal figure $R_{S}=0$, $R_{in,tot}=0$.

Output resistance looking into the drain with source
resistance $R_{S}$ ($R_{sig}$) :

$$R_{o,drain}=r_{o}\left[1+\left(g_{m}+g_{mb}\right)
R_{S}^{\prime}\right]+R_{S}^{\prime}\tag{11}$$

where $R_{S}^{\prime}=R_{S}\parallel R_{sig}$.
For $R_{S}^{\prime}=0$:

$${R_{o,drain}=r_{o}\tag{11a}}$$

and the total $ac$ resistance at the output node

$${R_{out}=R_{D}\parallel R_{o,drain}\approx R_{D}\parallel r_{o}
\approx R_{D}\tag{12}}$$

For $R_{S}^{\prime}\ne 0$ the $CG$ boosts $r_{o}$ by
$g_{m}r_{o}$, the cascode effect.

{\bf 3. Frequency response}

* Low frequency: $C_{1}$ gives the input high pass

$$f_{L}= {1\over 2\pi R_{in,tot}C_{1}}\tag{13}$$

with $R_{in,tot}$ from (10b). For the ideal
$R_{S}=\infty $ case $f_{L}= g_{m}/2\pi C_{1}$.
$C_{1}$ must be chosen $\gg 1/\omega R_{in}$.

* High frequency: dominant pole at the output

$$\omega_{p,o}\approx {1\over R_{out}C_{out}},\qquad
C_{out}=C_{db}+C_{gd}+C_{L}\tag{14}$$

and pole at the low $Z$ input

$$\omega_{p,in}\approx {g_{m}+g_{mb}\over C_{gs}+C_{sb}+C_{in}}
\approx {g_{m}\over C_{gs}} =\omega_{T}\tag{15}$$

very high, which is why the $CG$ and cascode are
wide band. Zero $\approx g_{m}/C_{gd}$.

Intrinsic voltage gain $\times$ bandwidth $\approx
g_{m}/C_{out}$.

Corrected practical $CG$ stage therefore consists of
Fig. 1 with the direct ground wire replaced by
$R_{S}$ to ground or better $I_{S}$ to $-V_{SS}$,
$R_{S}=r_{OS}$, $C_{1}$ coupling to $S$, $R_{D}$
to $V_{DD}$. With $I_{S}$ bias $V_{S0}$ self
adjusts to $V_{B}-V_{GS0}(I_{S})$.

In words: common gate $=$ common base bipolar,
current follower, voltage gain $+g_{m}R_{D}$, current
gain $\approx 1$, low input, moderate high output
impedance, non-inverting, excellent high frequency
performance, used as $50\,{\rm \Omega}$ input,
current buffer, and as the upper device of a
cascode. As drawn it is shorted and the $ac$
gain is zero; the short must be replaced by a
high $ac$ impedance bias.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: It explicitly notices that the source is hard-shorted to ground and concludes that the as-drawn circuit has ideally zero gain. The additional common-gate analysis is clearly identified as applying to a corrected, nonliteral circuit.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
The device is an $N$ ch. and the conventional
symbol is used with ${\rm arrow}=S=B$.
In conventional form:

$$\eqalign{
D &\to R_{D}\to V_{DD} \cr
G &\to V_{B}={\rm const.} \cr
S=B &\to C_{1}\to V_{in} \cr
{\rm and} &S\to {\rm ground} }$$

is a grounded gate stage.
$V_{B}$ makes $G$ an a. c. ground {\it if
properly decoupled} and $C_{1}$ is the
d.c. block, $Z_{C1}=1/sC_{1}\to 0$ for
$s\to j\omega $ in band.

Put $v_{b}=0$ for signals.

> {\it As drawn in the literal sense the
> amplifier is degener at because the $S$
> node is hard wired to a.c. ground in
> parallel with $V_{in}$.
> For $Z_{C1}\to 0$ $v_{s}=v_{in}\parallel 0\equiv 0$
> so that $v_{gs}=0$ and $v_{o}=0$.
> In practice the wire marked ground on the
> $S$ node is a high impedance d.c. bias
> element, a resistance $R_{S}$ or, ideally,
> a d.c. current sink $I_{SS}$ with
> $r_{SS}\to \infty $ for signals.
> With an ideal voltage source driving $C_{1}$
> you must interpose a finite generator
> resistance $R_{sig}$. In the following $R_{S}$
> denotes the total resistance from $S$ to
> a.c. ground external to the transistor.
> In the figure $R_{S}=0$ and the formulae
> can be put $R_{S}=0$. With $R_{S}=0$ the
> input {\it looking into} the source is
> shorted out.}

With that understanding it is the conventional
common gate, gate common, source in, drain out,
current buffer, wide band stage.

\subsubsection*{1. D.C.}

$$V_{GS0}=V_{B}-V_{S0}$$

With the figure $V_{S0}=0$,

$$V_{GS0}=V_{B}\tag{1}$$

$$I_{D0}={1\over 2}k_{n}\left(V_{GS0}-V_{T}\right)^{2}
\left[1+\lambda V_{DS0}\right]\tag{2}$$

$$k_{n}= \mu_{n}C_{ox}{W\over L}\;\;,\;\;V_{T}=V_{T0}
+\gamma \left(\sqrt{2\phi _{F}+V_{SB}}-\sqrt{2\phi _{F}}\right)$$

If $B=S$ as drawn $V_{SB}=0$, $V_{T}=V_{T0}$,
$g_{mb}=0$.  If $B$ is the substrate ground
$V_{SB}=V_{S0}$ and $g_{mb}=\chi g_{m}\ne 0$.

$$V_{DS0}=V_{DD}-I_{D0}R_{D}-V_{S0}\tag{3}$$

Saturation, long channel,

$$V_{DS0}\ge V_{GS0}-V_{T} \tag{4}$$

i. e.

$$V_{DD}-I_{D0}R_{D}\ge V_{B}-V_{T}$$

in the figure, which fixes the permissible
$V_{B},R_{D}$.

$$g_{m}={\partial I_{D}\over \partial V_{GS}}
=k_{n}\left(V_{GS0}-V_{T}\right)\left(1+\lambda V_{DS0}\right)
\approx \sqrt{2k_{n}I_{D0}} \tag{5}$$

$$g_{mb}=\chi g_{m}\;\;,\;\;r_{o}=1/g_{ds}=1/\lambda I_{D0}\tag{6}$$

Power $P_{DC}\approx V_{DD}I_{D0}$.

\subsubsection*{2. Low frequency small signal}

For $\omega $ in band $C_{1}$ is a short,
$C_{1}\gg 1/\omega R_{in}$.

Model, $v_{g}=0$,

$$\eqalign{
v_{gs}&=v_{g}-v_{s}=-v_{s}\cr
v_{bs}&=v_{b}-v_{s}\cr
v_{ds}&=v_{d}-v_{s}\cr
i_{d}&=g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}}$$

with $g_{mb}=0$ if $B=S$.
At the $D$ node, $V_{DD}$ a.c. ground,

$$\eqalign{
{i_{R_{D}}}&={-v_{d}\over R_{D}}\cr
{i_{R_{D}}}&=i_{d}}$$

so that, for $g_{mb}=0$,

$$-{v_{d}\over R_{D}}= -g_{m}v_{s}+{v_{d}-v_{s}\over r_{o}} \tag{7}$$

$${v_{d}\over v_{s}} ={{g_{m}r_{o}+1\over r_{o}}R_{D}\over
1+R_{D}/r_{o}} = {(g_{m}r_{o}+1)R_{D}\over r_{o}+R_{D}} \tag{8}$$

$$A_{v0}\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{s}}=
g_{m}\left(R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\right)+{R_{D}\over r_{o}+R_{D}}
\approx g_{m}\left(R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\right)\approx g_{m}R_{D}
\;\;{\rm for}\;\;r_{o}\gg R_{D}\tag{9}$$

In phase.  With $B\ne S$ replace $g_{m}\to g_{m}+g_{mb}$.
In general with a source resistance $R_{S}$,

$$A_{v}= {v_{d}\over v_{in}}={v_{d}\over v_{s}}{v_{s}\over v_{in}}$$

and $v_{s}=v_{in}R_{in}/(R_{sig}+R_{in})$,
see below.

Nominally $A_{v}>0$.  $v_{s}\uparrow\to v_{gs}\downarrow
\to i_{d}\downarrow\to V_{R_{D}}\downarrow\to v_{d}\uparrow$.

Current gain

$$A_{i}={i_{R_{D}}\over i_{s}}\approx -{g_{m}R_{D}\over 1+g_{m}R_{S}}
\cdot {1\over R_{D}}\,R_{in}\approx 1 \tag{10}$$

for $r_{o}\to\infty $, $R_{S}\to 0$. It is a current
follower, power gain $\approx A_{v}$.

With normal $R_{D}$ the voltage gain is $10$ to $30\,{\rm
dB}$.

\subsubsection*{3. Terminal impedances}

Looking {\it into} the source with $R_{D}$ loading the
drain, $v_{test}$ at $S$, $R_{D}$ to ground:

$$R_{in0}\equiv {v_{s}\over i_{s}}\Bigl|_{v_{g}=0}
={{R_{D}+r_{o}}\over {1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})r_{o}+r_{o}/R_{D}}\,}}
\approx {1\over g_{m}+g_{mb}}\parallel r_{o} \approx {1\over g_{m}}
\tag{11}$$

for $r_{o}\gg R_{D}$.  Low, $20-200\,{\rm \Omega}$ typical.
If the hard wire to ground in the figure is counted
$R_{in}=R_{in0}\parallel 0 =0$.

Total resistance seen by $V_{in}$ through $C_{1}$ is
$R_{in,tot}=R_{S}\parallel R_{in0}$. In the figure
$R_{S}=0$.

Looking {\it into} the drain with generator resistance
$R_{sig}$ in series with $S$,

$$R_{out0}\equiv {v_{d}\over i_{d}}\Bigl|_{v_{in}=0}
= r_{o}\left[1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{S}^{\prime}\right]+R_{S}^{\prime}
\tag{12}$$

$$R_{S}^{\prime}=R_{sig}\parallel R_{S}$$

Seen at the output terminal through $R_{D}$:

$$R_{out}=R_{D}\parallel R_{out0}\tag{13}$$

For $R_{S}^{\prime}=0$, $R_{out}=R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\approx R_{D}$.
For $R_{S}^{\prime}\ne 0$ the output is boosted by
$\approx g_{m}r_{o}$; this is the cascode effect.
That is why $CG$ is used as the upper device of a
cascode.

If $R_{S}=0$ as drawn $R_{out0}=r_{o}$.

\subsubsection*{4. Frequency response}

Add $C_{1}$:

$$H(s)={sC_{1}R_{in,tot}\over 1+sC_{1}R_{in,tot}}\,
A_{v0}\,{1\over 1+sR_{out}C_{L}} \tag{14}$$

with $C_{L}$ the load at $D$ including $C_{gd},C_{db}$.
Low cut off

$$f_{L}\approx {1\over 2\pi R_{in,tot}C_{1}} \tag{15}$$

very high because $R_{in,tot}$ is small.
High cut off dominated by $R_{out}C_{L}$,

$$f_{H}\approx {1\over 2\pi R_{out}C_{L}} \tag{16}$$

No Miller multiplication of $C_{gd}$ because $G$ is
grounded. Hence the $CG$ is intrinsically wide band,
used as RF LNA input stage with $1/g_{m}=50\,{\rm \Omega}$
match, as current buffer and as cascode device.

For the literal figure $R_{in,tot}=0$, $f_{L}\to\infty $,
no signal is transmitted at any finite $C_{1}$.

In practice replace the hard ground by e.g.

$$\;S\to R_{S}\to {\rm ground\;or}\;S\to I_{SS}\to {\rm ground}\;$$

with $R_{S}=V_{S0}/I_{D0}$ or $I_{SS}=I_{D0}$, choose $V_{B}$
so that (4) is satisfied, decouple $V_{B}$ to ground with a
large $C_{B}$ so that $v_{g}=0$, and choose $C_{1}\gg
1/2\pi f_{min}R_{in0}$.  Then (9),(11),(13) are the
useful design equations.  With body effect $g_{m}\to
g_{m}+g_{mb}$ throughout.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly notices that the source is hard-shorted to ground and concludes that the input signal is nulled, giving ideally zero output gain. The additional common-gate discussion does not change that conclusion for the circuit as drawn.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is a nominally $Grounded$ $Gate$, 
$Source$ $Driven$, $Drain$ $Loaded$ stage.
i.e. a $Common$ $Gate$ $CG$ voltage / current
buffer. As drawn it is degenerate.

```
               VDD AC gnd
                |
               RD
                | Vout = VDD-ID.RD -id.RD
                D
        Vb --- G M1   vgs = vg-vs
                S <-- body if 3T
                |
 Vin --C1--+----o---- GND DC = Vs = 0
           |         AC = vs (?)
           GND ?
```

> The circuit as drawn ties the signal source `Vin`
> through `C1` to a hard `GND`. `GND` is `AC` $0$.
> So for `AC` $vs =0$ identically, $v_{gs}=0$,
> $i_{d}=0$, $v_{out}=0$. Voltage gain $ =0$.
> Input is shorted. It is a drafting error.

The {\it intended} circuit is

```
Vin --C1-- S M1 D --RD-- VDD
            G --Vb AC gnd
            |
           ZB -- GND
```

where $Z_{B}$ is the DC bias impedance for the
source, $R_{S}$ resistor or $I_{S}$ current source,
$Z_{B} \rightarrow \infty$ for $AC$ if it is a
current source and $\approx R_{S}$ if it is a
resistor. In the limit of the drawing $Z_{B}=0$,
so the comments below are for $Z_{B}\ne 0$ and
for $C_{1}$ $AC$ short. Put $R_{sig}$ = Thevenin
resistance of $V_{in}$. For $C_{1}$ short,
$r_{sig}=R_{sig}$ seen by the source.

### 1. DC bias

$$V_{S,DC}=0\;{\rm if}\;Z_{B}=0$$

$$V_{GS,DC}=V_{G,DC}-V_{S,DC}=V_{b}$$

$$I_{D}= \frac12 \mu_{n}C_{ox}\frac{W}{L}
\left(V_{b}-V_{th}\right)^{2}
\left[1+\lambda V_{DS}\right] $$

in saturation

$$V_{DS,DC}=V_{D,DC}-V_{S,DC}=V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{D}$$

Saturation condition:

$$V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{th}=V_{ov}$$

$$V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{D} \ge V_{b}-V_{th}$$

$V_{b}$ is chosen to set $I_{D}$ and hence
$g_{m}$.

$$g_{m}= \mu_{n}C_{ox}\frac{W}{L}V_{ov}
      =\sqrt{2\mu_{n}C_{ox}\frac{W}{L}I_{D}}
      =\frac{2I_{D}}{V_{ov}}$$

$$g_{mb}= \chi g_{m}\;\;,\;\;\chi =\frac{\gamma}
{2\sqrt{2\phi_{F}+V_{SB}}}\approx 0.1-0.3$$

$$r_{o}=1/g_{ds}=1/\lambda I_{D}$$

If as symbolised the body is tied to the source
$V_{SB}=0$, $g_{mb}=0$. If in a $n$-well process
the body is the global $GND$, $V_{SB}= -v_{s}$
for $AC$ and $g_{mb}\ne 0$.

$C_{1}$ is a DC block. Its $DC$ value is $0$
so it does not enter the bias. If the source
$V_{in}$ has DC component it is blocked.

### 2. Small signal $AC$ - $C_{1}$ short, $V_{DD},V_{b}$ $AC$ $0$

Gate grounded, source $=v_{in,ac}=v_{s}$,
drain $=v_{out}$.

Model:

$$v_{gs}=v_{g}-v_{s}=-v_{s}$$
$$v_{bs}=v_{b}-v_{s}=-v_{s}\; {\rm if\; body=GND}$$
$$=0\; {\rm if\; body=source}$$
$$v_{ds}=v_{d}-v_{s}=v_{out}-v_{s}$$

$$i_{d}=g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}$$

KCL at drain: $AC$ current in $R_{D}$ + $i_{d}=0$

$$ -\frac{v_{out}}{R_{D}} = i_{d}$$

with sign $I_{R_{D}}=(V_{DD}-V_{out})/R_{D}$ downwards.

#### Voltage gain

$$-\frac{v_{out}}{R_{D}} = -g_{m}v_{s}-g_{mb}v_{s}
+g_{ds}(v_{out}-v_{s})$$

$$-\frac{v_{out}}{R_{D}}-g_{ds}v_{out}=
-(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds})v_{s}$$

$$A_{v}\equiv \frac{v_{out}}{v_{s}}=
\frac{g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}}{g_{ds}+G_{D}}$$

where $G_{D}=1/R_{D}$

$$A_{v}= (g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds})\, R_{D}\parallel r_{o}
      \approx (g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{D}\parallel r_{o}$$

If body tied to source $g_{mb}=0$:

$$\;A_{v}\approx g_{m}R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\approx g_{m}R_{D}\;,
\;r_{o}\gg R_{D}\; {\rm non-inverting}$$

Positive, no phase inversion, same as source
follower but with voltage amplification.
Current gain $A_{i}=i_{d}/i_{in}\approx 1$ - it is
a current buffer.

With finite source resistance $R_{sig}$ in series
with $C_{1}$ the divider with $R_{in}$ gives

$$A_{v,eff}= \frac{v_{out}}{v_{in}} = A_{v}
\frac{R_{in}}{R_{in}+R_{sig}}=
\frac{g_{m}R_{D}}{1+g_{m}R_{sig}}\; {\rm approx.}$$

For $R_{sig}=0$, $A_{v}=g_{m}R_{D}$.

In the degenerate $Z_{B}=0$, $R_{sig}=0$ drawing,
$$R_{in}=0$$ as seen from $C_{1}$, $v_{s}=0$ so
$$A_{v,eff}=0$$ .

#### Input resistance at the source

By definition $R_{in}=v_{s}/-i_{s}$, $i_{s}=-i_{d}$
neglecting body.

General:

$$R_{in}= \frac{R_{D}+r_{o}}{1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})r_{o}+g_{ds}R_{D}}
 \approx \frac{1}{g_{m}+g_{mb}} \parallel r_{o}$$

More exactly including $R_{D}$:

$$R_{in} \approx \frac{1}{g_{m}+g_{mb}}\left(1+\frac{R_{D}}{r_{o}}\right)
\approx \frac{1}{g_{m}+g_{mb}}$$

typically $20-500\Omega$. Body tied to source:

$$\;R_{in}\approx 1/g_{m}\;$$

$$R_{in}\approx 1/g_{m}\parallel R_{S}\; {\rm if}\;Z_{B}=R_{S}$$

This low $Z_{in}$ is used for $50\Omega$ input
matching in LNAs: set $g_{m}=20mS$.

#### Output resistance at the drain

Looking into drain with $R_{sig}$ at source:

$$R_{o,drain}= r_{o}\left[1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{sig}\right]+R_{sig}$$

Total:

$$R_{out}=R_{D}\parallel R_{o,drain}$$

For $R_{sig}=0$:

$$R_{o,drain}=r_{o}\;\;,\;\;R_{out}=R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\approx R_{D}$$

For $R_{sig}\ne 0$, $R_{out}$ is boosted to
$\approx g_{m}r_{o}R_{sig}$ - high impedance
current source, good for cascode.

### 3. Frequency response

* $C_{1}$ with $R_{sig}+R_{in}$ forms input high pass:

$$f_{L}= \frac{1}{2\pi C_{1}(R_{sig}+R_{in})}\approx
\frac{g_{m}}{2\pi C_{1}}$$

must be $\ll f_{sig}$. Usually $C_{1}$ large.

* Output pole:

$$f_{H,out}\approx \frac{1}{2\pi (R_{D}\parallel r_{o})C_{L}}$$

where $C_{L}=C_{db}+C_{gd}+C_{load}$.

* No Miller multiplication of $C_{gd}$ because gate
grounded. Hence $CG$ has much wider band than $CS$.

Intrinsic input pole $1/2\pi R_{sig}C_{gs}$ etc.
is at very high frequency.

### 4. Summary for the intended $CG$

| Parameter | Expression $r_{o}\to\infty$ | With $r_{o}$ |
|-----------|------------------------------|--------------|
| $A_{v}$ | $+g_{m}R_{D}$ | $+(g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{D}\parallel r_{o}$ |
| $A_{i}$ | $\approx 1$ | $g_{m}/(g_{m}+G_{D})$ |
| $R_{in}$ | $1/g_{m}$ | $1/(g_{m}+g_{mb})\parallel r_{o}$ |
| $R_{out}$| $R_{D}$ | $R_{D}\parallel r_{o}[1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{sig}]$ |
| Phase | non-inverting $0^{\circ}$ | |
| Bandwidth | very wide | |

Advantages: low $R_{in}$, high $R_{out}$, no Miller,
wideband, current buffer, good for cascode and
for RF $50\Omega$ matched LNA.

Disadvantages: $R_{in}$ too low for voltage amplifier,
voltage gain limited by $R_{D}$.

### 5. Fix

Remove hard $GND$ short at source. Replace by

$$S -- R_{S} -- GND$$ or $$S -- I_{S} -- GND$$

with $R_{S}=V_{S}/I_{D}$ or $I_{S}=I_{D}$. Then
$C_{1}$ couples $v_{in}$ to $S$ across $R_{in}
\approx 1/g_{m}$ without short. Gate $V_{b}$ should
be bypassed to $GND$ with large capacitor if it
comes from a resistive divider.

Example: $I_{D}=1mA$, $g_{m}=5mS$, $R_{D}=2k\Omega$
$\Rightarrow A_{v}\approx 10$, $R_{in}\approx 200\Omega$.

That is the classical common-gate / grounded-gate
amplifier.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies that the source node is hard-shorted to ground, so the input is shorted and the ideal voltage gain from Vin is zero. The additional discussion concerns a hypothetical corrected circuit and does not undermine the essential conclusion.

answers.question: How many poles does the circuit shown in the figure have?

answer.text:
If you want to count the ${\rm s}=\infty $ pole the
circuit is a 4 energy store, 4 pole, circuit.  One of the
stores,

$${\cal N}_{C}=4\qquad C_{GS}\;,\;C_{GD}\;,\;C_{DB}\;,\;C_{SB}
\tag*{Fig.}$$

is shorted out by the {\it a. c.} earth on the source so that
in conventional language it is a 3 store circuit, Fig. 1.  At
finite frequencies it is a 2 store circuit, {\it i. e.} a low
pass of nominal second order, one zero, Fig. 2.

> {\it Remark:} In the conventional ``one pole per capacitor''
> jargon the circuit is normally quoted as a {\it three}, {\it
> four} with $C_{SB}$, {\it pole} circuit.  The conventional
> count includes the pole at ${s}=\infty $ associated with the
> shorted $C_{SB}$, and, for $C_{DB}\ne C_{GD}$, counts $C_{GD}$
> and $C_{DB}$ as two different poles, although in an exact
> analysis they coalesce into one second order denominator,
> Fig. 2.

Put ${R_{0}}^{-1}=0$ for brevity.  With

$$V_{g}\equiv V_{G}\qquad V_{d}\equiv V_{o}$$

$$\eqalign{
{\left({{1}\over {R_{S}}}+{\rm s}C_{GS}+{\rm s}C_{GD}\right)V_{g}
-{\rm s}C_{GD}V_{d}}&={{V_{i}}\over {R_{S}}}\cr
{\left(g_{m}-{\rm s}C_{GD}\right)V_{g}
+\left({{1}\over {R_{D}}}+{\rm s}C_{DB}+{\rm s}C_{GD}\right)V_{d}}&=0\cr}\tag 1$$

so that, e. {\it g.}, with

$${\cal D}({\rm s})=\left|{\matrix{
{{1}\over {R_{S}}}+{\rm s}\left(C_{GS}+C_{GD}\right) &-{\rm s}C_{GD}\cr
g_{m}-{\rm s}C_{GD} &{{1}\over {R_{D}}}+{\rm s}\left(C_{DB}+
C_{GD}\right)\cr}}\right| \tag 2$$

$${\cal D}({\rm s})={{1}\over {R_{S}R_{D}}}
+{\rm s}\left[{{C_{DB}+C_{GD}}\over {R_{S}}}+{{C_{GS}+C_{GD}}\over
{R_{D}}}+g_{m}C_{GD}\right]
+{\rm s}^{2}\left[C_{GS}C_{DB}+C_{GS}C_{GD}+C_{GD}C_{DB}\right] \tag 3$$

and

$$V_{o}/V_{i}=-{{g_{{m}}-{\rm s}C_{GD}}\over {R_{S}{\cal D}({\rm
s})}}\tag 4$$

is nominally second order with the familiar RHP zero

$${\rm s}_{z}=+{{g_{m}}\over {C_{GD}}}\tag 5$$

The ${\rm s}^{2}$ coefficient in (3) is

$$\Delta_{2}=C_{GS}C_{GD}+C_{GS}C_{DB}+C_{GD}C_{DB}\tag 6$$

so that, if you want to keep the ${\rm s}=\infty $ pole
associated with the shorted

$$C_{SB}\tag 7$$

in the count, (3) is normally written in the conventional
``${{1}\over {R_{S}}}+{\rm s}C_{GS}$ is the input pole and
${{1}\over {R_{D}}}+{\rm s}C_{DB}$ is the output pole and
${\rm s}C_{GD}$ Miller multiplies to $C_{GD}(1+g_{m}R_{D})$''
form as a {\it three} pole denominator,

$${\cal D}({\rm s})\propto 
\left(1+{{\rm s}\over {{\rm s}_{GS}}}\right)
\left(1+{{\rm s}\over {{\rm s}_{GD}}}\right)
\left(1+{{\rm s}\over {{\rm s}_{DB}}}\right) \tag 8$$

with, to first order in the Miller approximation,

$${\rm s}_{GS}^{-1}\approx R_{S}\left[C_{GS}+C_{GD}(1+g_{m}R_{D})\right]
\qquad 
{\rm s}_{DB}^{-1}\approx R_{D}\left[C_{DB}+C_{GD}\right]\tag 9$$

the third, $C_{GD}$, pole coalescing with (9) to give the
second order (3).  Including the conventional $s=\infty $ pole
of the shorted $C_{SB}$ the circuit is quoted as a four pole
circuit with

$${\rm s}_{SB}^{-1}=R_{SB}C_{SB}\;\;,\;\;R_{SB}\rightarrow 0\tag{10}$$

at infinity.  With $R_{SB}\ne 0$, {\it e. g.} with ordinary
source degeneration $R_{S}\rightarrow R_{S}^{\,\prime}$,
$R_{SB}\ne 0$ (3) becomes third order in the conventional
count, fourth order with (10), and (4) exhibits two finite
zeros.  In the $R_{SB}\rightarrow 0$ limit the $C_{SB}$ pole
goes to ${\rm s}_{SB}\rightarrow \infty $ and the finite
determinant collapses to the second order, one zero, function
(3)--(4) above, normally referred to for brevity as the
``two pole'', Miller split input and output pole, plus one RHP
zero response of the conventional common source stage.  Any
finite $R_{o}=r_{o}\ne \infty $ just puts $R_{D}\rightarrow
R_{D}\parallel r_{o}$ in (1)--(9).

> {\it N. B.:} If you count $C_{GD}$ and $C_{DB}$ as distinct
> poles and keep the $s=\infty $ pole the textbook answer is
> ``three finite poles, four poles in toto, one RHP zero'';
> ``two finite poles plus the pole at infinity'' in exact
> analysis.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: The derivation correctly identifies a second-order finite-frequency transfer function and notes that C_SB is shorted, but it then counts spurious poles at infinity and gives three- or four-pole totals. The circuit has two poles.

answers.question: How many poles does the circuit shown in the figure have?

answer.text:
With the conventional small signal model the energy
storage element which is put in evidence in the
figure is

$$\eqalign{
C_{GS}&{\rm gate/node}\cr 
C_{GD}&{\rm feed back}\cr 
C_{DB}&{\rm drain/node}\cr 
C_{SB}&{\rm source/node\;\;shorted}}$$

put $g_{o}=0$ for brevity.  With $V_{G}=V_{g}$,
$V_{D}=V_{o}$

$$\eqalign{
{{V_{g}-V_{i}}\over {R_{S}}}+sC_{GS}V_{g}+sC_{GD}\left(V_{g}-V_{o}\right)&=0 \cr 
{{V_{o}}\over {R_{D}}}+sC_{DB}V_{o}+sC_{GD}\left(V_{o}-V_{g}\right)+g_{m}V_{g}&=0}$$

i. {\it e.}

$$\left[ \matrix{
{1\over {R_{S}}}+s\left(C_{GS}+C_{GD}\right) &-sC_{GD}\cr 
g_{m}-sC_{GD}&{1\over {R_{D}}}+s\left(C_{DB}+C_{GD}\right)\cr}\right]
\left[ \matrix{V_{g}\cr V_{o}\cr}\right] =\left[ \matrix{V_{i}/R_{S}\cr 0\cr}\right]\tag{*}$$

so that, with $D(s)={\rm det}(*)$,

$$D(s)={1\over {R_{S}R_{D}}}+s\left[{{C_{GD}+C_{DB}}\over {R_{S}}}+
{{C_{GS}+C_{GD}}\over {R_{D}}}+g_{m}C_{GD}\right]+s^{2}
\left[C_{GS}C_{DB}+C_{GD}\left(C_{GS}+C_{DB}\right)\right] \tag{**}$$

and

$${{V_{o}}\over {V_{i}}}={{-g_{m}+sC_{GD}}\over {R_{s}D(s)}}\tag{***}$$

is {\it a priory} second order in $s$ with one finite
{\it feed forward} zero at $s=+g_{m}/C_{GD}$.  In $(**)$
the $s^{2}$ coefficient is

$$\Delta =\left(C_{GS}+C_{GD}\right)\left(C_{DB}+C_{GD}\right)-C_{GD}^{2}
>0\tag{+}$$

so that the three capacitors put in evidence in the
figure, $C_{GS},C_{GD},C_{DB}$, form the conventional
capacitive loop

$$C_{GS}-C_{GD}-C_{DB}-{\rm earth}-C_{GS}\tag{++}$$

and $(+)$ is the $\Delta $ of the loop.  Normally
$(**)$ is written in the familiar zero value time
constant, Miller, form as the product of three,
formally first order, associated poles.  Putting
formally $D(s)\approx \left(1+s\tau_{GS}\right)
\left(1+s\tau _{GD}\right)\left(1+s\tau_{DB}\right)$

$$\eqalign{
\tau_{GS}&=R_{S}C_{GS}\cr
\tau_{GD}&=\left(R_{S}+R_{D}\right)C_{GD}\approx 
R_{S}C_{GD}^{{\rm Miller,in}}+R_{D}C_{GD}^{{\rm Miller,out}}\cr
\tau_{DB}&=R_{D}C_{DB}\cr} \tag{+++}$$

so that in the conventional {\it one time constant per
capacitor} language the circuit is normally quoted as
{\it three pole, one zero}, {\it i. e.} in the Miller
approximation

$$\eqalign{
\omega_{p,in}^{-1}&\approx R_{S}\left[C_{GS}+C_{GD}\left(1+g_{m}R_{D}\right)\right]\cr
\omega _{p,out}^{-1}&\approx R_{D}\left[C_{DB}+C_{GD}\right]\cr
\omega _{p,GD}^{-1}&\approx \left(R_{S}\parallel R_{D}\right)C_{GD}\cr}$$

and $(***)$ is normally quoted, with $(+++)$, as

$${{V_{o}}\over {V_{i}}}\approx -{{g_{m}R_{D}}\over {
\left(1+s/\omega_{p,in}\right)\left(1+s/\omega_{p,out}\right)
\left(1+s/\omega_{p,GD}\right)}}\left(1-s/\omega_{z}\right)\tag{++++}$$

with $\omega_{z}=g_{m}/C_{GD}$, {\it i. e.} two
dominant Miller poles $\omega_{p,in}$, $\omega_{p,out}$
and the normally non dominant feed back pole
$\omega_{p,GD}$.  Formally $(**)$ is second order,
so that one of the three poles in $(++++)$ is
dependent on the other two through the loop relation
$(+)$--$(++)$.

If you keep the normal fourth small signal capacitor,
the source bulk capacitor $C_{SB}$ in the figure, the
conventional count is four capacitors, four associated
time constants,

$$\tau_{SB}=R_{S,S}C_{SB}\tag{+++++}$$

Normally, as in the figure, the source is a
conventional earth, $R_{S,S}=0$, so that

$$\omega_{p,SB}={1\over {R_{S,S}C_{SB}}}\rightarrow \infty \tag{++++++}$$

and $C_{SB}$ is normally said to be {\it shorted out}
or {\it at infinity} and does not appear in $(*)$--
$(++++)$.  With $R_{S,S}\ne 0$, {\it e. g.} with a
source degeneration resistor $R_{S,S}$, $(**)$ becomes
third order, $D(s)=D_{0}+sD_{1}+s^{2}D_{2}+s^{3}D_{3}$
with $D_{3}=R_{S}R_{D}R_{S,S}\Delta C_{SB}\ne 0$.

> {\it Remark:} In compact form: two finite poles and
> one finite RHP zero, three associated first order time
> constants, $C_{GS},C_{GD},C_{DB}$, four with the
> normally shorted $C_{SB}$.  In the conventional
> open circuit time constant - Miller jargon the circuit
> is quoted as a three pole - four pole with $C_{SB}$ -
> one zero circuit.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: The exact nodal determinant is second order, and the answer correctly notes that CSB is shorted while CGS, CGD, and CDB form a capacitor loop. Thus the circuit has two poles; the approximate three-time-constant discussion does not change the exact count.

answers.question: How many poles does the circuit shown in the figure have?

answer.text:
In the Miller approxiamtion the small signal
circuit is second order. Put ${\rm g}_{o}\rightarrow 0$

$$\eqalign{
{\rm KCL}G:&\;{{V_{g}-V_{i}}\over {R_{S}}}+V_{g}sC_{GS}+
\left(V_{g}-V_{d}\right)sC_{GD}=0\cr
{\rm KCL}D:&\;{{V_{d}}\over {R_{D}}}+V_{d}sC_{DB}+
\left(V_{d}-V_{g}\right)sC_{GD}+{\rm g}_{m}V_{g}=0\tag{*}}$$

so that with

$${\cal D}(s)={\rm det}\left|\matrix{
{1\over {R_{S}}}+s\left(C_{GS}+C_{GD}\right) &-sC_{GD}\cr
{\rm g}_{m}-sC_{GD} &{1\over {R_{D}}}+s\left(C_{DB}+C_{GD}\right)}\right|$$

$$\eqalign{
{\cal D}(s)&=s^{2}R_{S}R_{D}\left[C_{GS}C_{DB}+C_{GD}
\left(C_{GS}+C_{DB}\right)\right] \cr
&+s\left[R_{S}\left(C_{GS}+C_{GD}\right)+R_{D}\left(C_{DB}+
C_{GD}\right)+{\rm g}_{m}R_{S}R_{D}C_{GD}\right]+1\cr
&\propto \left(1+{s\over {\omega _{{p}_{1}}}}\right)
\left(1+{s\over {\omega _{{p}_{2}}}}\right)}$$

is second order in $s$.  E. {\rm g}. in the conventional
Miller approximation

$$\eqalign{
\omega _{{p}_{1}}^{-1}&\approx R_{S}\left[C_{GS}+
C_{GD}\left(1+{\rm g}_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}\right)\right]\cr
\omega _{{p}_{2}}^{-1}&\approx R_{D}^{\prime}\left[C_{DB}+
C_{GD}{{1+C_{GS}/C_{GD}}\over {1+{\rm g}_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}}}\right]
\approx R_{D}^{\prime}C_{DB}\qquad {\rm g}_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}\gg 1\cr
R_{D}^{\prime}&=R_{D}\Vert r_{o}\approx R_{D}}$$

and, from the ${\rm g}_{m}-sC_{GD}$ term in $(*)$ a
{\it bona fide} right half plane zero,

$${\cal N}(s)\propto {\rm g}_{m}-sC_{GD}\tag{**}$$

i. {\rm e}.

$${{V_{o}}\over {V_{i}}}(s)\propto -{{{\rm g}_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}
\left(1-sC_{GD}/{\rm g}_{m}\right)}\over 
{\left(1+s/\omega _{{p}_{1}}\right)\left(1+s/\omega _{{p}_{2}}
\right)}}\tag{***}$$

normalised to $-{\rm g}_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}$ at $s=0$, viz.
a two pole and one zero small signal circuit.  In
particular the {\lq\lq} Miller'' zero is at

$$\omega _{z}=+{{{\rm g}_{m}}\over {C_{GD}}}\tag{****}$$

in the RHP.  Topologically there are three
[four] small signal storage elements in the drawer,
$C_{GS}$, $C_{GD}$ and $C_{DB}$ [and $C_{SB}$] so that
the network is normally quoted as third [fourth] order.
$C_{SB}$ is connected between two incremental grounds,
Fig. 1, so that its pole is normally said to have been
pushed to

$$\omega _{{p}_{SB}}={1\over {R_{SB}}C_{SB}}\rightarrow \infty
\qquad R_{SB}=0\tag{\dag }$$

and is normally neglected, neglected altogether in $(*)$.
If you want to keep the count it is a $3$ pole [$4$
pole] network with $\left|\omega _{{p}_{SB}}\right|=
\infty $.  In the conventional language the circuit is
normally referred to as a {\lq\lq} $3$ pole'' circuit,
two finite poles plus the pole at infinity associated
with the short circuited $C_{SB}$.  With the zero $(**)$
counted as a pole at infinity it is a fourth order
network.

> {\it Remark:}  With $r_{o}<\infty $ put $R_{D}\rightarrow
> R_{D}\Vert r_{o}=R_{D}^{\prime}$ {\it passim.}

In most text books the $\left|\omega _{{p}_{SB}}\right|
\rightarrow \infty $ pole is simply neglected and the
circuit is quoted as the conventional two pole Miller
amplifier $(***)$--$(****)$.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: The determinant correctly gives a second-order denominator and two finite poles, but the answer then explicitly counts a third pole from the shorted C_SB (and even a fourth order by counting the zero). C_SB contributes no pole, so this conflicting pole count is a major error.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is the 1 transistor series - shunt
{\it voltage - series } feedback amplifier.
Usually drawn as

$$V_{in}\to {\rm Source}~~,~~{\rm Gate}=V_{F}=
{\cal F}(V_{out})~~,~~{\rm Drain}=V_{out}=V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{D}$$

$$\eqalign{
I_{D}&=I_{D}(V_{GS},V_{DS})\cr
V_{F}&=V_{out}{\cal F}\cr
V_{GS}&=V_{F}-V_{in}\cr
V_{DS}&=V_{out}-V_{in}}$$

For $R_{1},R_{2}>>R_{D}$ the feedback network is
almost unilateral and
$${\cal F}_{0}\approx \beta ={R_{2}\over R_{1}+R_{2}}\tag{1}$$
and
$$V_{F}= \beta V_{out} \qquad i_{G}=0$$

In the more exact low frequency unilateral model the
output node is loaded by $R_{1}+R_{2}$ so that with
AC ground on $V_{DD}$

$$R_{p}=R_{D}\parallel (R_{1}+R_{2})\parallel r_{o}\approx R_{D}$$
$${\cal F}= \beta =R_{2}/(R_{1}+R_{2})$$

M1 is supposed in saturation, bulk to source so no
$g_{mb}$:

$$I_{D}={k_{n}\over 2}(V_{GS}-V_{T})^{2}(1+\lambda V_{DS})$$
for hand calculation $\lambda =0$

$$I_{D0}(V_{F0}-V_{in0},V_{out0})={V_{DD}-V_{out0}\over R_{D}}
- {V_{out0}\over R_{1}+R_{2}}\approx {V_{DD}-V_{out0}\over R_{D}}$$

$$V_{GS0}=V_{F0}-V_{in0}>V_{T}\tag{2}$$
$$V_{DS0}=V_{out0}-V_{in0}>V_{GS0}-V_{T}\tag{3}$$

(2)(3) + $V_{F0}=\beta V_{out0}$ determine the Q sec bias.
Put $V_{GS0}=V_{F0}-V_{in0}$ in $I_{D}$, $V_{out}=V_{DD}-R_{D}I_{D}$
the usual quadratic for $V_{GS0}$.
E.{\it g.} for $\lambda =0$

$$V_{out}=V_{DD}-R_{D}{k_{n}\over 2}(\beta V_{out}-V_{in}-V_{T})^{2}$$

$$V_{out}(V_{in})\;\;{\rm decreasing\;with\;}V_{in}.$$

For $V_{in}$ large $V_{GS}<V_{T}$, $M_{1}$ off

$$V_{out,off}=V_{DD}{R_{1}+R_{2}\over R_{D}+R_{1}+R_{2}}\approx V_{DD}$$

for $V_{in}$ very negative $M_{1}$ in triode.

In normal bias with $R_{1}+R_{2}>>R_{D}$ it is approx.
common gate.

> Negative feedback: $V_{out}\uparrow \to V_{F}\uparrow
\to V_{GS}\uparrow \to I_{D}\uparrow \to R_{D}I_{D}\uparrow
\to V_{out}\downarrow $

de-sensitised.

### Small signal - loop

$$g_{m}=\left.{\partial I_{D}\over \partial V_{GS}}\right|_{Q}
\qquad g_{ds}=1/r_{o}=\left.{\partial I_{D}\over \partial V_{DS}}\right|_{Q}
\qquad g_{mb}=0$$

$$i_{d}=g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}
      =g_{m}(v_{f}-v_{in})+g_{ds}(v_{out}-v_{in})\tag{4}$$

and, AC,

$$v_{f}=\beta v_{out}\tag{5}$$

KCL at the output, no test source:

$$i_{D\;{\rm into\;D}}+i_{R_{D}}+i_{R_{1}}=0$$

$${\rm AC:}\;\;i_{d}+{v_{out}\over R_{D}}+{v_{out}-v_{f}\over R_{1}}=0$$

$$ -i_{d}=v_{out}\left({1\over R_{D}}+{1\over R_{1}+R_{2}}\right)
       =v_{out}/R_{p0}\tag{6}$$
$$R_{p0}=R_{D}\parallel (R_{1}+R_{2})$$

Neglecting $1/(R_{1}+R_{2})$ vs $1/R_{D}$, $R_{p0}\approx R_{D}$.

From (4)(5)(6)

$$-g_{m}(\beta v_{out}-v_{in})-g_{ds}(v_{out}-v_{in})=v_{out}/R_{p0}$$

$$v_{in}(g_{m}+g_{ds})=v_{out}\left({1\over R_{p0}}+g_{ds}+g_{m}\beta\right)$$

> $$\;A_{vf}\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{in}}=
{g_{m}+g_{ds}\over g_{ds}+1/R_{p0}+g_{m}\beta }\; \tag{7}$$

For $r_{o}\to \infty ,\;R_{1}+R_{2}\to \infty ,\;R_{p0}\to R_{D}$

> $$A_{vf}\approx {g_{m}R_{D}\over 1+g_{m}R_{D}\beta }
={1\over \beta}{L\over 1+L}\tag{8}$$

$$L=g_{m}R_{p0}\beta \approx g_{m}R_{D}\beta \tag{9}$$

is the loop gain. The open loop, $\beta =0$, gate AC
ground, is the ordinary common gate stage

$$A_{v0}= (g_{m}+g_{ds})R_{p0}\parallel r_{o}\approx g_{m}R_{D}$$
positive, non inverting at the source.

$$A_{vf}= {A_{v0}\over 1+A_{v0}\beta}$$

de-sensitised to $g_{m},R_{D}$.

For large $L>>1$

$$A_{vf}\to A_{vf,ideal}=1/\beta ={R_{1}+R_{2}\over R_{2}}
=1+{R_{1}\over R_{2}}\tag{10}$$

as for the non inverting op-amp.
Normally $L\sim 2-10$ for a single MOS so (10) is
only approx. E.g. $g_{m}=5{\rm mA/V},R_{D}=2{\rm k},
\beta =0.2$, $L=2$, $A_{vf}=g_{m}R_{D}/(1+L)=3.3$
vs $A_{ideal}=5$.

With finite $r_{o}$

$$L = g_{m}\beta \,R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\parallel (R_{1}+R_{2})$$
$$A_{vf}= {(g_{m}r_{o}+1)\over 1+r_{o}/R_{p0}+g_{m}r_{o}\beta}$$

If bulk to GND, $g_{m}\to g_{m}+g_{mb}$.

Feedback is {\it voltage sampled, series mixed} ,
series-shunt in 2 port terminology. Ideal
feedback theory:

* voltage sampling $\to Z_{out}$ lowered by $1+L$
* series mixing $\to Z_{in}$ raised by $1+L$

Indeed, with input shorted $v_{in}=0$, inject $v_{x}$ at
output, $v_{f}=\beta v_{x}$

$$i_{x}= {v_{x}\over R_{p0}}+i_{d}=v_{x}/R_{p0}+g_{m}\beta v_{x}+g_{ds}v_{x}$$

> $$Z_{out,f}= {v_{x}\over i_{x}}={1\over 1/R_{p0}+g_{ds}+g_{m}\beta }
={R_{p0}\parallel r_{o}\over 1+L}\approx {R_{D}\over 1+g_{m}R_{D}\beta}\tag{11}$$

Without feedback, $Z_{out,0}=R_{p0}\parallel r_{o}\approx R_{D}$
as expected. Feedback makes the output a good voltage
source, $Z_{out,f}\to 1/g_{m}\beta$ for large $L$.

Looking into the source with $v_{in}=v_{x}$, $v_{out}=A_{vf}v_{x}$,
the current injected into the source is $i_{x}=-i_{d}$
and from (6) $-i_{d}=v_{out}/R_{p0}$ so that

$$i_{x}=v_{out}/R_{p0}=A_{vf}v_{x}/R_{p0}$$

More directly $i_{x}=-g_{m}(\beta v_{out}-v_{x})-g_{ds}(v_{out}-v_{x})$.
Using (7)

> $$Z_{in,f}={v_{x}\over i_{x}}={1/R_{p0}+g_{ds}+g_{m}\beta\over (g_{m}+g_{ds})1/R_{p0}}
={1+g_{m}\beta R_{p0}+g_{ds}R_{p0}\over g_{m}+g_{ds}}\tag{12}$$

$$Z_{in,0}= {1+g_{ds}R_{p0}\over g_{m}+g_{ds}}\approx 1/g_{m}$$

is the ordinary low CG input resistance.

> $$Z_{in,f}\approx {1\over g_{m}}+ \beta R_{p0}\approx {1\over g_{m}}+{R_{D}R_{2}\over R_{1}+R_{2}}\tag{13}$$
for $r_{o}\to\infty$.

i.e. increased by $\approx (1+L)/g_{m}R_{p0}\times R_{p0}$.
This is used to get $50\,{\rm \Omega}$ match with modest
$g_{m}$ for wide band LNA, etc.

In Blackman form $Z_{in}=Z_{in,0}(1+L_{sc})/(1+L_{oc})$.

Consequences: gain stabilized to resistor ratio, linearity
and PSRR improved by $1+L$, bandwidth extended by $1+L$,
dominant pole at output $\omega_{p,out}=1/R_{p0}C_{out}$
pushed to $\omega_{p,f}=(1+L)/R_{p0}C_{out}$.

Single pole loop, unconditionally stable, phase margin
$\sim 90^{o}$ if $R_{1}+R_{2}$ parasitic small.

In large signal the circuit is the basic shunt regulator
/LDO error amplifier, wide band voltage amplifier,
regulated cascode input stage. With $R_{1},R_{2}\to\infty$
it reverts to open loop common gate $A_{v}=g_{m}R_{D}$,
$Z_{in}=1/g_{m}$, $Z_{out}=R_{D}\parallel r_{o}$.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies the source-driven transistor, output-divider feedback to the gate, and negative feedback. Its closed-loop gain is consistent with the golden result, approaching 1/β = 1 + R1/R2 at high loop gain; extra secondary discussion does not undermine the essential analysis.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
In its essential form it is a shunt at the output
series at the input, voltage series feedback
$=$ series shunt in Gray-Meyer
${\rm sampling}- {\rm shunt} \; :{\rm voltage}$
${\rm mixing}-{\rm series}\;:{\rm voltage}$ amplifier.
In discrete form it is a common gate with its
gate slaved to the output by $R_{1},R_{2}$ so
that it looks like a non inverting ${\rm OP AMP}$
with gain $1+R_{1}/R_{2}$. In the ideal
feedback sense it is a transconductance

$$\eqalign{
M_{1}-CG & {\rm forward\; path}\cr
R_{1}-R_{2} & {\rm feedback\; path} \cr}$$

$$V_{F}= \beta V_{o}\qquad 
\beta ={{V_{F}}\over {V_{o}}}\bigg|_{{g_{m}=0}}$$

If the gate draws no current

$${{(V_{o}-V_{F})}\over {R_{1}}}={{V_{F}}\over {R_{2}}}$$

$$V_{F}={{R_{2}}\over {R_{1}+R_{2}}}V_{o}\tag{1}$$

$$\beta _{0}={{R_{2}}\over {R_{1}+R_{2}}}= {1\over {1+R_{1}/R_{2}}}\tag{2}$$

in the conventional two port sense the $R_{1}+R_{2}$
loads the output so that with $V_{DD}$ a.c. ground

$$R_{D}^{\prime}=R_{D}\parallel (R_{1}+R_{2})\parallel
R_{L} \tag{3}$$

is the load seen by the drain for $R_{L}=\infty $,
$R_{D}^{\prime}=R_{D}\parallel (R_{1}+R_{2})$.
For $R_{1}+R_{2}\gg R_{D}$, $R_{D}^{\prime}\approx
R_{D}$.

Let for $M_{1}$

$$I_{D}=F(V_{GS},V_{DS})\qquad V_{GS}=V_{F}-V_{in}\qquad
V_{DS}=V_{o}-V_{in}$$

$$i_{d}=g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}
\tag{4}$$

where in the usual 4 terminal $n$MOS
$v_{bs}=-v_{in}$ if the bulk is to
ac ground and $v_{bs}=0$ if the bulk is
strapped to the source as drawn.
Put $g_{m}^{\prime}=g_{m}+g_{mb}$ for the
former and $g_{m}^{\prime}=g_{m}$ for the
latter and $g_{o}=g_{ds}=r_{o}^{-1}$.

In small signal for ac ground on $V_{DD}$

$$\eqalign{
v_{gs}&=v_{F}-v_{in}= \beta v_{o}-v_{in}\cr
v_{ds}&=v_{o}-v_{in}\cr
i_{d}&=g_{m}(\beta v_{o}-v_{in})+g_{mb}(-v_{in})
+g_{o}(v_{o}-v_{in})\cr
&= (g_{m}\beta +g_{o})v_{o}-(g_{m}^{\prime}+g_{o})v_{in}
\tag{5}}$$

KCL at the $V_{o}$ node, $i_{d}$ taken as
from $D$ to $S$ {\it i. e.} out of the
$V_{o}$ node into the drain

$$i_{d}+{{v_{o}-v_{F}}\over {R_{1}}}+{{v_{o}}\over {R_{D}}}=0
\tag{6}$$

with the gate open

$${{v_{o}-v_{F}}\over {R_{1}}}={{v_{F}}\over {R_{2}}}
={{v_{o}}\over {R_{1}+R_{2}}} \tag{7}$$

so that

$$i_{d}=-v_{o}\left[{1\over {R_{D}}}+{1\over {R_{1}+R_{2}}}\right]
=-{v_{o}\over {R_{D}^{\prime}}} \tag{8}$$

$$v_{o}=-R_{D}^{\prime}i_{d} \tag{9}$$

The conventional common gate voltage
fall is recovered for $\beta =0$, $R_{1}+R_{2}\to \infty $,
$v_{o}=-g_{m}R_{D}v_{gs}$ with sign taken
with $v_{gs}=-v_{in}$.

Insert (5) in (8):

$$(g_{m}\beta +g_{o})v_{o}-(g_{m}^{\prime}+g_{o})v_{in}
=-{v_{o}\over {R_{D}^{\prime}}}$$

$$v_{o}\left[g_{m}\beta +g_{o}+{1\over {R_{D}^{\prime}}}\right]
=(g_{m}^{\prime}+g_{o})v_{in} \tag{10}$$

$$\;A_{v}\equiv {{v_{o}}\over {v_{in}}}=
{{g_{m}^{\prime}+g_{o}}\over {g_{m}\beta +g_{o}+1/R_{D}^{\prime}}}\;
>0 \tag{11}$$

For $r_{o}\to \infty $, $g_{o}\to 0$ and

$$A_{v}\approx {{g_{m}^{\prime}}\over {g_{m}\beta +1/R_{D}^{\prime}}}
={1\over \beta }{{g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}\beta }
\over {1+g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}\beta }}{g_{m}^{\prime}\over g_{m}} \tag{12}$$

E.g. with the bulk to source, $g_{m}^{\prime}=g_{m}$,

$$A_{v}= {1\over \beta }{T\over {1+T}}\qquad 
T=g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}\beta \tag{13}$$

$T$ is the return ratio, loop gain, of the
circuit. In two port loop language the
common source forward gain is

$$A_{0}= -g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}\tag{14}$$

with inversion, so that the loop gain is

$$LG = -A_{0}\beta = g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}\beta =T \tag{15}$$

and (13) is the Blackman asymptotic gain formula
$A_{v}=A_{0}/(1-LG\cdot {\rm sign})=1/\beta \times
T/(1+T)$.

For

$$T=g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}{{R_{2}}\over {R_{1}+R_{2}}}\gg 1$$

$$A_{vf}\approx {1\over \beta }={{R_{1}+R_{2}}\over {R_{2}}}
=1+{{R_{1}}\over {R_{2}}} \tag{16}$$

independent of $g_{m},R_{D}$ to first order.
The feedback is negative: $\uparrow V_{in}\to
\downarrow V_{GS}\to \downarrow I_{D}\to \uparrow
V_{o}\to \uparrow V_{F}\to \uparrow V_{GS}$ which
opposes the initial decrease. The closed loop
gain is desensitized $dA_{vf}/A_{vf}=
(1/1+T)dA_{0}/A_{0}$, non linear distortion
reduced by $1+T$, bandwidth increased by
$1+T$. With the usual sign taken with respect
to the gate, $v_{o}/v_{g}=-g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}$
inverting, so that with $v_{in}$ applied to the
gate $A_{vf}\approx -R_{1}/R_{2}$ the familiar
inverting ${\rm OP}$.

With the bulk to ground $g_{m}^{\prime}=g_{m}+g_{mb}$

$$A_{vf}\approx {1\over \beta }\left(1+{{g_{mb}}\over {g_{m}}}\right)
 \approx {1+{R_{1}/R_{2}}\over {1+g_{mb}/g_{m}}^{-1}} \tag{16a}$$

normally $<20\%$ correction.

> {\it Remarks:} The $+1+R_{1}/R_{2}$ is the ideal
> non inverting gain. If the input is taken at the
> gate and the source grounded, the same circuit
> becomes the inverting shunt-shunt amplifier with
> $A_{v}\approx -R_{1}/R_{2}$.

Input resistance at the source: $R_{i0}\approx
1/(g_{m}^{\prime}+g_{o})$ for the open loop CG
stage. Series mixing raises it:

Put $v_{in}=v_{x}$ test at the source, $v_{o}=-i_{d}
R_{D}^{\prime}$. From (5) $i_{d}=-i_{in}$ the
current entering the source

$$i_{in}=-i_{d}= -g_{m}\beta v_{o}+g_{m}^{\prime}v_{x}
-g_{o}v_{o}+g_{o}v_{x}$$

$$i_{in}=v_{x}(g_{m}^{\prime}+g_{o})+v_{o}(g_{m}\beta +g_{o})$$

with $v_{o}=-i_{d}R_{D}^{\prime}=i_{in}R_{D}^{\prime}$

$$i_{in}\left[1-R_{D}^{\prime}(g_{m}\beta +g_{o})\right]
=v_{x}(g_{m}^{\prime}+g_{o})$$

With sign consistent with (8) $i_{in}= -i_{d}$,

$$\,R_{if}\equiv {{v_{x}}\over {i_{in}}}=
{{1+(g_{m}\beta +g_{o})R_{D}^{\prime}}\over {g_{m}^{\prime}+g_{o}}}\, \tag{17}$$

$$\approx {1\over {g_{m}^{\prime}}}+ \beta {g_{m}\over
g_{m}^{\prime}}R_{D}^{\prime}\approx {1\over {g_{m}}}
+{{R_{2}}\over {R_{1}+R_{2}}}R_{D}^{\prime}\qquad g_{o}\to 0 \tag{18}$$

$$R_{if}=R_{i0}(1+T)\tag{19}$$

voltage series feedback raises $R_{in}$.
E.g. $R_{D}^{\prime}=2\,{\rm k}\Omega $,
$R_{1}=9\,{\rm k}$, $R_{2}=1\,{\rm k}$, $\beta =0.1$,
$g_{m}=5\,{\rm mS}$: $R_{i0}=200\,\Omega$, $T=1$,
$R_{if}\approx 400\,\Omega$; for large $T$,
$R_{if}\approx \beta R_{D}\sim 0.2-1\,{\rm k}\Omega $,
usable for wide band $50\,\Omega $ matching
by proper choice of $R_{D}$ and $\beta $.

Output resistance: With $v_{in}=0$ put $v_{x}$ at
the output, bulk to source for simplicity,

$$\eqalign{
v_{gs}&=\beta v_{x}\cr
v_{ds}&=v_{x}\cr
i_{d}&=g_{m}\beta v_{x}+g_{o}v_{x}\cr
i_{x}&={{v_{x}}\over {R_{D}}}+i_{d}+{{v_{x}}\over {R_{1}+R_{2}}}\cr
&={{v_{x}}\over {R_{D}^{\prime}}}+v_{x}(g_{m}\beta+g_{o})
\tag{20}}$$

$${R_{of}\equiv {{v_{x}}\over {i_{x}}}=
{1\over {1/R_{D}^{\prime}+g_{m}\beta+g_{o}}}\tag{21}}$$

the impedance seen looking into the whole
stage including $R_{D}$. The impedance looking
into the drain itself, $R_{o}^{\ast}=v_{x}/(i_{x}-
v_{x}/R_{D})$,

$$R_{o}^{\ast}={1\over {1/(R_{1}+R_{2})+g_{m}\beta+g_{o}}}
\approx {1\over {g_{m}\beta}}\qquad T\gg 1 \tag{22}$$

$$\;R_{of}=R_{o0}/(1+T)\parallel R_{D}\;$$

with $R_{o0}\approx r_{o}$ for $R_{S}=0$;
shunt, voltage, sampling lowers $R_{out}$ by
$1+T$, as expected for a voltage amplifier.
With a finite source resistance $R_{S}$ at the
input the familiar CG formula
$R_{o0}\approx r_{o}[1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{S}]+R_{S}$
is divided by $1+T$.

DC bias: $V_{o}=V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{D}$,
$V_{F}=V_{o}R_{2}/(R_{1}+R_{2})$,
$V_{GS}=V_{F}-V_{in,DC}$,
$I_{D}=(k_{n}/2)(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda V_{DS})$
in saturation, $V_{DS}=V_{o}-V_{in,DC}>V_{GS}-V_{Tn}$.
Solved self consistently it sets the gate bias
without extra supply.

Frequency and stability: Loop $T(s)=g_{m}Z_{D}(s)\beta(s)$,
$Z_{D}=R_{D}^{\prime}\parallel 1/sC_{L}$,
$\beta(s)=R_{2}\parallel 1/sC_{F}$/$[(R_{1}\parallel 1/sC_{F})+\cdots]$
Usually $p_{1}\approx 1/R_{D}^{\prime}C_{L}$ dominant at
the output, $p_{2}\approx 1/(R_{1}\parallel R_{2})C_{gg}$
at the gate. With $p_{2}\gg GBW=T_{0}p_{1}$ the
amplifier is single pole stable with $\approx 90^{o}$
phase margin and closed loop bandwidth
$BW_{f}\approx (1+T_{0})BW_{0}$. $C_{gd}$ gives a
feed forward zero. Elaborated with $r_{o}$ it is
the low voltage regulated cascode building block
used for wide band LNA input matching, as level
shifter, and as error amplifier in LDO's.

In short the circuit is a stable negative
feedback voltage amplifier whose closed loop gain
is set by the resistor ratio and whose $Z_{in}$
is raised and $Z_{out}$ lowered by the return
ratio $T=g_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}R_{2}/(R_{1}+R_{2})$.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies the source input, output-divider feedback to the gate, and negative feedback; its high-loop-gain result is the correct non-inverting gain, 1 + R1/R2.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is the 1 transistor realization of the

$${V_{o}/V_{i}}\approx 1/{\beta }$$

voltage sampling, series mixing, $=$
series shunt $=$ voltage series feedback
$={\cal R}_{vi}$ N. I. amplfier.

With the usual notation : $k\equiv \beta $

>$$\beta ={V_{F}\over V_{out}}\Bigl |_{I_{F}=0}$$
$${\cal A}_{0}= {V_{out}\over V_{id}}$$
$$V_{id}=V_{F}-V_{in}=V_{gs}$$

In ordinary terminology, Fig. 1 is a
common gate stage whose gate is not $ac$ ground
but is driven with a sample of its own drain
voltage through the divider $R_{1},R_{2}$.

```
             VDD ac gnd
              |
              RD
              | Vout = Vd
              +---------+------o Vout
              |         |      |
              D        R1      R1+R2
             M1         |      |
              S----+    V_F =kVout
              |    |     |
             Vin  Vgs   R2
                   |     |
                  gnd   gnd
```

$V_{gs}=V_{F}-V_{in}$ is the error voltage.

$${\rm if}\;V_{in}\uparrow \to V_{gs}\downarrow 
\to I_{D}\downarrow \to I_{RD}\downarrow \to V_{out}\uparrow 
\to V_{F}\uparrow \to V_{gs}\uparrow $$

negative feedback for $0<k<1$.  $M_{1}$ is in effect
a differential transconductor with $+$ input $V_{F}$,
$-$ input $V_{in}$ and single ended
$v_{o}=-g_{m}v_{gs}r_{o}\parallel R_{D}$, i. e.
the one transistor op. amp. in the non inverting
configuration.  For $g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1$ you get the
op. amp. result ${\cal A}_{CL}\to 1/\beta $.

### DC bias

Gate current $\approx 0$,

$$V_{F}=V_{G}=V_{out}{R_{2}\over R_{1}+R_{2}}=kV_{out}\tag{1}$$

$$V_{out}=V_{DD}-R_{D}I_{D}\tag{2}$$

$$I_{D}={1\over 2}\mu C_{ox}{W\over L}\left(V_{GS}-V_{T}\right)^{2}
\left(1+\lambda V_{DS}\right)\;{\rm sat.}\tag{3}$$

$$V_{GS}=V_{G}-V_{S}=kV_{out}-V_{S}\tag{4}$$

$$V_{DS}=V_{out}-V_{S}\tag{5}$$

With $V_{S}=V_{in,DC}$, (1)-(4) defines the $Q$ point

$$V_{DD}-V_{out}=R_{D}{\beta _{0}\over 2}\left(kV_{out}-V_{S}-V_{T}\right)^{2}$$

in saturation $V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{T}$.
It is a self bias through $R_{1}R_{2}$ and is
DC $100\%$ negative feedback so the $Q$ point is
stabilized.  In small signal we normally consider
$V_{in}=V_{s}+v_{in}$ superposed on the $Q$ point.

Up to the biasing details it is the usual CG
stage if you put $k=0$, $V_{G}=0$.

### Small signal with loading

Put $V_{DD}\;ac\;0$, $r_{o}=1/g_{ds}$, ignore
$C_{gs},C_{gd}$ at low frequency, $r_{g}=\infty $,
in Fig.1 body to source so $g_{mb}=0$, if not
replace $g_{m}$ by $g_{m}+g_{mb}$.

$$v_{gs}=v_{f}-v_{in}\tag{6}$$
$$v_{ds}=v_{out}-v_{in}\tag{7}$$
$$i_{d}=g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}\;\;{\rm into\; D,
\; out\; of\; S}\tag{8}$$

KCL at $V_{F}$: $i_{g}=0$,

$${v_{f}-v_{out}\over R_{1}}+{v_{f}\over R_{2}}=0$$

$${\rm so }\;v_{f}=v_{out}{R_{2}\over R_{1}+R_{2}}=kv_{out}\tag{9}$$

$$k={R_{2}\over R_{1}+R_{2}}\qquad 1-k={R_{1}\over R_{1}+R_{2}}\tag{10}$$

KCL at the output node, currents leaving the node:

$${v_{out}\over R_{D}}+{v_{out}-v_{f}\over R_{1}}+i_{d}=0\tag{11}$$

i.e. with (8)(9)

$${v_{out}\over R_{D}}+v_{out}{1-k\over R_{1}}+g_{m}\left(kv_{out}-v_{in}\right)
+g_{ds}\left(v_{out}-v_{in}\right)=0\tag{12}$$

$${1-k\over R_{1}}={1\over R_{1}+R_{2}}\tag{13}$$

Hence
