$$v_{out}\left[{1\over R_{D}}+{1\over R_{1}+R_{2}}+g_{m}k+g_{ds}\right]
=v_{in}\left(g_{m}+g_{ds}\right)\tag{14}$$

>$$A_{v}\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{in}}=
{{g_{m}+g_{ds}}\over {g_{ds}+{1\over R_{D}}+{1\over R_{1}+R_{2}}+g_{m}k}}\tag{15}$$

For $r_{o}\to \infty $,

>$$A_{v}\approx {g_{m}\over {1/R_{D}+1/(R_{1}+R_{2})+g_{m}k}}\tag{15a}$$

$${1\over R_{D}}+{1\over R_{1}+R_{2}}={1\over R_{D}\parallel \left(R_{1}+R_{2}\right)}
\equiv {1\over R_{D}'}\tag{16}$$

If the loop is built $g_{m}kR_{D}'\gg 1$,

$$A_{v}\to {1\over k}={R_{1}+R_{2}\over R_{2}}=1+{R_{1}\over R_{2}}>0\tag{17}$$

the non inverting op. amp. result.
The sign is $+$ .  A rise in $v_{in}$ at the
source cuts $v_{gs}$, cuts $i_{d}$ and pulls
$v_{out}$ up.  Normally $R_{1}+R_{2}\gg R_{D}$
and $1/(R_{1}+R_{2})$ can be neglected

$$A_{v}\approx {g_{m}R_{D}\over 1+g_{m}R_{D}k}=
{1\over k}{T\over 1+T}\tag{18}$$

with

$$T=g_{m}k\,R_{D}\parallel \left(R_{1}+R_{2}\right)\parallel r_{o}\tag{19}$$

is the usual ${\cal A}_{0}\beta /1+{\cal A}_{0}\beta $ form.

Including $R_{1}+R_{2}$ as part of the load,

$${\cal A}_{0}= -g_{m}R_{D}'\;\;{\rm for\; gate\; drive }$$
$${\cal A}_{0}= +g_{m}R_{D}'\;\;{\rm for\; source\; drive }$$
$$\beta =k$$

The exact feedback expression with loading is (15).
In ideal feedback language, to first order,
open circuit gain loaded by the feedback network is

$$A_{vo}=g_{m}R_{D}'\approx g_{m}R_{D}$$

closed loop gain (15a) is $A_{vo}/(1+A_{vo}\beta )$ seen
from the source, i. e. $1/\beta $ for $A_{vo}\beta \gg 1$.
The resistors set the gain, its sensitivity to
$g_{m},r_{o}$ to $dA_{v}/A_{v}=dA_{vo}/A_{vo}/(1+T)$
is made small. Linearity is improved by $1+T$.

Numerically e. g. $R_{D}=5\,{\rm k}$,
$R_{1}=9\,{\rm k}$, $R_{2}=1\,{\rm k}$, $k=0.1$,
$g_{m}=2\,{\rm mA/V}$, $r_{o}\to\infty $,
$R_{D}'=3.3\,{\rm k}$, $T\approx 0.66$,
$A_{v}\approx 4$ , $T=6.6$ for $g_{m}=20\,{\rm mA/V}$
$\to A_{v}\approx 8.7\to 10$ ideal.

Return ratio: break the loop at the gate,
ground the source for $ac$, drive $v_{t}$ at the
gate, $v_{out}=-g_{m}v_{t}R_{D}'$,
$v_{r}=kv_{out}=-g_{m}kR_{D}'v_{t}$,
$T=-v_{r}/v_{t}=g_{m}kR_{D}'$ as above.
Single pole at the output, unconditionally
stable, phase margin $ \approx 90^{o}$.

### Input and output impedance - Blackman

Voltage sampling wants $Z_{out}\downarrow $,
series mixing wants $Z_{in}\uparrow $.

Let $v_{x}$ be injected at the output, $v_{in}=0$.
From (11) with $v_{out}=v_{x}$,

$$i_{x}={v_{x}\over R_{D}}+{v_{x}-v_{f}\over R_{1}}+g_{m}v_{f}+g_{ds}v_{x}$$

with (9) $v_{f}=kv_{x}$,

$$i_{x}=v_{x}\left[{1\over R_{D}}+{1\over R_{1}+R_{2}}+g_{m}k+g_{ds}\right]$$

>$$Z_{out}\equiv {v_{x}\over i_{x}}=
{1\over g_{ds}+1/R_{D}+1/(R_{1}+R_{2})+g_{m}k}
={R_{D}'\parallel r_{o}\over 1+T}\tag{20}$$

$Z_{out}$ without feedback but with the $R_{1}+R_{2}$
load is $R_{D}'\parallel r_{o}$ and is divided by
$1+T$.  For $T\gg 1$ $Z_{out}\approx 1/g_{m}k\ll R_{D}$.

For the impedance looked into the source define
$i_{x}$ entering the source.  Device source
current entering the device is $-i_{d}$.  So
$i_{x}= -i_{d}$.

From above $i_{d}=(g_{m}k+g_{ds})v_{out}-(g_{m}+g_{ds})v_{in}$
and with (15) $v_{out}=A_{v}v_{in}$,

$$i_{d}=-(g_{m}+g_{ds})\left[{1/R_{D}+1/(R_{1}+R_{2})\over g_{ds}+1/R_{D}+1/(R_{1}+R_{2})+g_{m}k}\right]v_{in}$$

so for current entering the source

$$Z_{in}\equiv {v_{in}\over i_{x}}={v_{in}\over -i_{d}}
={g_{ds}+1/R_{D}+1/(R_{1}+R_{2})+g_{m}k\over (g_{m}+g_{ds})\left(1/R_{D}+1/(R_{1}+R_{2})\right)}\tag{21}$$

$$Z_{in}\approx {1\over g_{m}}+k\,R_{D}' = {1+T\over g_{m}}\tag{22}$$

for $g_{ds}\to 0$, $T=g_{m}kR_{D}'$.
The CG low impedance $\approx 1/g_{m}$ without feedback
$(k\to 0)$ is raised by $\approx kR_{D}'$ or by $1+T$.
This can be used for $50\,{\rm \Omega }$ matching with
much smaller $g_{m}$.  With body effect $g_{m}\to g_{m}+g_{mb}$.

In summary to order $r_{o}\to\infty $,
$R_{1}+R_{2}\gg R_{D}$

$$\eqalign{
\beta &=R_{2}/(R_{1}+R_{2})\cr
T &=g_{m}\beta R_{D}\parallel (R_{1}+R_{2}) \cr
A_{CL}&\approx (1/\beta )\,T/(1+T)\cr
R_{in,CL}&\approx (1+T)/g_{m}\cr
R_{out,CL}&\approx R_{D}/(1+T)\cr}$$

i. e. all the usual series-shunt virtues:
accurate resistor defined voltage gain, desensitivity,
low $R_{out}$, high $R_{in}$, improved linearity and
bandwidth by $1+T$ at the expense of gain.  The
price is the DC coupling of $Q$ point to $R_{1},R_{2}$
and output swing limited by $R_{D}I_{D}$ headroom.
With $R_{1}+R_{2}$ not $\gg R_{D}$ replace $R_{D}$
by $R_{D}'=R_{D}\parallel (R_{1}+R_{2})$ and include
$r_{o}$ in parallel.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies the source as the input, the output divider as gate feedback, and the loop as negative feedback. Its closed-loop gain also approaches 1/β = 1 + R1/R2.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is the {\it active loaded
common drain} or {\it source follower} Class $A$
voltage buffer. In discrete form:

$$\eqalign{
M_{1}&{\rm driver} \cr
M_{2}&:I_{SS}{\rm  current source}}$$

$$I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{SS}$$

> {\it Remark on symbol:} As drawn the arrow is the
source. The bulk is strapped to the source so
in principle $V_{BS1}=V_{BS2}=0$ and there is
no bulk modulation. If realized in a normal
$p-{\rm sub}$ $n-{\rm well}$ CMOS process the
$p-{\rm sub}$ is $GND$ and $M_{1}$ suffers
bulk modulation $V_{BS1}=-V_{o}$ with
$V_{T1}=V_{T0}+\gamma \left[\sqrt{2\Phi_{F}+V_{o}}-
\sqrt{2\Phi_{F}}\right]$ .

In normal operation both devices are in saturation.

$$\eqalign{
I_{SS}&={1\over 2}\mu_{n}C_{ox}\left({W\over L}\right)_{2}
\left(V_{b}-V_{T2}\right)^{2}\left(1+\lambda_{2}V_{o}\right) \cr
I_{D1}&={1\over 2}\mu_{n}C_{ox}\left({W\over L}\right)_{1}
\left(V_{GS1}-V_{T1}\right)^{2}\left(1+\lambda_{1}V_{DS1}\right)}$$

$$V_{GS1}=V_{in}-V_{o} \qquad V_{DS1}=V_{DD}-V_{o}
 \qquad V_{DS2}=V_{o}$$

so large signal

$$V_{o}=V_{in}-V_{GS1}=V_{in}-V_{T1}-\sqrt{{2I_{SS}\over
\mu_{n}C_{ox}(W/L)_{1}}}$$

with

$$V_{T1}=V_{T10}+{\rm bulk\;if\;not\;strapped}$$

Saturation conditions

$$\eqalign{
M_{2}:&V_{DS2}\ge V_{GS2}-V_{T2}\;\;{\rm i.e.}\;\;
V_{o}\ge V_{b}-V_{T2}=V_{ov2}\cr
M_{1}:&V_{DS1}\ge V_{GS1}-V_{T1}\;\;{\rm i.e.}\;\;
V_{DD}-V_{o}\ge V_{in}-V_{o}-V_{T1}\cr
&V_{in}\le V_{DD}+V_{T1}}$$

Hence the $DC$ transfer is a level shift by $\approx V_{GS1}$
with unity slope until

* $V_{in}$ low : $M_{1}$ cuts off, $V_{o}=I_{SS}r_{o2}$
pulled to $0$ through $M_{2}$
* $V_{in}$ high : $M_{1}$ goes triode $V_{o,max}\approx
V_{DD}-V_{ov1}$ and for $V_{o}>V_{b}-V_{T2}$ $M_{2}$ stays
saturated.

Usable swing to first order

$$V_{ov2}< V_{o} < V_{DD}-V_{ov1}$$

Small signal with $V_{b}$ $AC$ ground:

```
          D1=VDD AC gnd
           |
          gds1
    G1 o---||---+---o Vout
           |gm1+gmb1
           |  gds2
          D2----+
           |gm2 gds2
          S2=GND AC gnd
```

$G_{2}$ $AC$ gnd, so $M_{2}$ is simply $r_{o2}=1/g_{ds2}$
to ground in parallel with $r_{o1}=1/g_{ds1}$.

KCL at output:

$$g_{m1}v_{gs1}+g_{mb1}v_{bs1}+g_{ds1}(v_{o}-0)+g_{ds2}v_{o}=0$$
$$v_{gs1}=v_{in}-v_{o}\qquad v_{bs1}=-v_{o}\;{\rm if\;bulk=GND},
\;0\;{\rm if\;bulk=source}$$

$$g_{m1}(v_{in}-v_{o})-g_{mb1}v_{o}-(g_{ds1}+g_{ds2})v_{o}=0$$

> $$A_{v}\equiv {v_{o}\over v_{in}}=
> {g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}=
> {g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}\,{1\over 1+{g_{o}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}}$$

where $g_{o}=g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}=r_{o1}^{-1}+r_{o2}^{-1}$.

If bulk strapped to source $g_{mb1}=0$:

$$A_{v}\approx {g_{m1}r_{o}\over 1+g_{m1}r_{o}}\qquad 
r_{o}=r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}={1\over g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}$$

For $g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1$

$$A_{v}\approx 0.8-0.95 {\rm \;without\;bulk\;,\; 0.6-0.8 \;with\;bulk}
<1, {\rm \;non\;inverting}$$

and to first order $A_{v}\to 1$ if $r_{o}\to \infty$.

Small signal impedances by driving $v_{x}$ at output
with $v_{in}=0$:

$$i_{x}=(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})v_{x}+g_{ds1}v_{x}+g_{ds2}v_{x}$$

> $$R_{out}={v_{x}\over i_{x}}={1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}
> \approx {1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}\parallel r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}
> \approx {1\over g_{m1}} $$

typically $50$ to $500\;\Omega$.

> $$R_{in}= \infty \;\;{\rm capacitive\;\; }C_{in}\approx C_{gs1}
> +(1-A_{v})C_{gd1} \approx C_{gs1}$$

$$C_{out}\approx C_{gs1}+C_{sb1}+C_{db1}+C_{db2}+C_{L}$$

Dominant pole

$$p_{1}\approx {1\over R_{out}C_{L}}={g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{o}\over C_{L}}$$

Non dominant pole at the gate $p_{2}\approx 1/R_{sig}C_{in}$.

Properties:

* Voltage buffer, impedance transformer $R_{in}\gg R_{out}$
* Current gain, power gain $\approx g_{m}R_{L}$
* No voltage gain
* Class $A$: can source
$I_{max}\approx {1\over 2}\mu C_{ox}(W/L)_{1}(V_{DD}-V_{o}-V_{T})^{2}$
but can only sink $I_{SS}$. Slew rate $SR_{-}=I_{SS}/C_{L}$.
* Distortion determined by $g_{m}$ variation with $I_{D1}$.

Used universally as output stage, source follower buffer,
level shifter, second stage of op-amp after high gain
stage, etc. Replacing $M_{2}$ by a resistor gives
same analysis with $r_{o2}\to R_{S}$, but $M_{2}$ gives
much higher $r_{o}$ and better $A_{v}\to 1$, better
$PSRR$ and smaller area.

With $M_{1}$ as $PMOS$ the circuit becomes the familiar
common source high gain inverter with active load
$A_{v}=-g_{m1}r_{o}$ .

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies M1 as a source follower and M2 as its current-source load, and gives a positive gain below but approaching unity with body effect and finite output resistance included.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
The diagram is often drawn as

$$\eqalign{
M_{2}&= {\rm actire}\;{\rm load}\cr 
M_{1}&= {\rm driver}}$$

with the conventional $4$ terminal MOS symbol.
The supply connections ${\rm B}_{1}\to V_{DD}$,
${\rm B}_{2}\to {\rm GND}$ identify

* $M_{2}$ : $n-$ channel, ${\rm S}_{2}={\rm GND}$,
${\rm D}_{2}=V_{out}$, ${\rm G}_{2}=V_{b}=$ d.c.
bias $=$ d.c. current source

* $M_{1}$ : $p-$ channel, ${\rm S}_{1}=V_{DD}$,
${\rm D}_{1}=V_{out}$, ${\rm G}_{1}=V_{in}$ in the
usual CMOS notation.

With the symbol as drawn the arrow is on the source,
i. e. it is a $n-$MOS source follower,
${\rm D}_{1}=V_{DD}$, ${\rm S}_{1}=V_{out}$,
${\rm D}_{2}=V_{out}$, ${\rm S}_{2}={\rm GND}$.
The two are duals to each other and differ only by
the ${\rm B}_{1}$ connection and the sign of the
gain.  In what follows ${\rm CS}$ means $pM_{1}$,
common source with active load, ${\rm CD}$ means
$nM_{1}$ common drain, source follower with active
load.  Put ${\rm B}_{1}={\rm S}_{1}$ for the ${\rm CS}$.
For the ${\rm CD}$ with ${\rm B}_{1}=V_{DD}\ne
{\rm S}_{1}$ the back gate transconductance $g_{mb1}$
must be kept.

> In many text books the circuit is quoted as
> {\it the} single transistor high gain stage, or
> as the $n{\rm MOS}$ source follower with current
> source bias.  $M_{2}$ is {\it not} diode
> connected and presents a small signal resistance
> $r_{o2}=1/g_{ds2}\gg 1/g_{m}$.

$$\eqalign{
I_{D}&={1\over 2}\mu C_{ox}{W\over L}
\left(V_{GS}-V_{T}\right)^{2}\left(1+\lambda V_{DS}\right)  \cr
g_{m}&=\left.{\partial I_{D}\over \partial V_{GS}}\right|_{Q}
 =\mu C_{ox}{W\over L}\left(V_{GS}-V_{T}\right)
 =\sqrt{2\mu C_{ox}{W\over L}I_{D}}={2I_{D}\over V_{ov}}\cr
g_{mb}&=\eta g_{m}\;\;,\;\;\eta ={g_{mb}\over g_{m}}
\approx {\gamma \over 2\sqrt{2\phi _{F}+V_{SB}}}\cr
r_{o}&={1\over g_{ds}}={1\over \lambda I_{D}}\propto {L\over I_{D}}}$$

with $V_{ov}=V_{GS}-V_{T}$ for $n$MOS,
$V_{ov}=V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|$ for $p$MOS.

### 1. Large signal - d.c. bias

Put both devices in saturation, strong inversion.

* $n$-load:

$$I_{D2}={1\over 2}k_{n}^{\prime}{\left({W\over L}\right)}_{2}
\left(V_{b}-V_{Tn}-V_{ov2}\right)^{2}\left(1+\lambda _{n}V_{out}\right)
\approx {1\over 2}k_{n}{\left({W\over L}\right)}_{2}
\left(V_{b}-V_{Tn}\right)^{2} \tag{1}$$

fixes the bias current $I_{D0}$. $V_{b}$ is normally
generated by a $n$MOS current mirror and $V_{b}>V_{Tn}$,
$V_{b}-V_{Tn}=V_{ov2}$ a few $100\,{\rm mV}$.

* $p$-driver, ${\rm CS}$:

$$I_{D1}={1\over 2}k_{p}^{\prime}{\left({W\over L}\right)}_{1}
\left(V_{DD}-V_{in}-|V_{Tp}|\right)^{2}
\left(1+\lambda _{p}(V_{DD}-V_{out})\right) \tag{2a}$$

* $n$-driver, ${\rm CD}$ source follower:

$$I_{D1}={1\over 2}k_{n}^{\prime}{\left({W\over L}\right)}_{1}
\left(V_{in}-V_{out}-V_{Tn}(V_{SB})\right)^{2}
\left(1+\lambda _{n}(V_{DD}-V_{out})\right) \tag{2b}$$

$$V_{Tn}(V_{SB})=V_{T0}+\gamma\left(\sqrt{2\phi_{F}+V_{SB}}
-\sqrt{2\phi_{F}}\right)\;\;,\;\;V_{SB}=V_{S}-V_{B}$$

For the ${\rm CS}$ with ${\rm B}_{1}={\rm S}_{1}$,
$V_{SB1}=0$, $g_{mb1}=0$. For the follower with
${\rm B}_{1}=V_{DD}$ or ${\rm GND}$, 
$V_{SB1}=V_{out}-0\ne 0$ for $n$MOS with ${\rm B}={\rm GND}$,
$V_{SB1}=V_{B}-V_{S}=V_{DD}-V_{out}$ for the drawing,
threshold is modulated and

$$V_{out}=V_{in}-V_{GS1}=V_{in}-V_{Tn}(V_{SB1})-V_{ov1} \tag{3}$$

i.e. a level shift $\approx V_{T}+V_{ov}$.

In the steady state $I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{D0}$.

Saturation conditions, $\lambda =0$ for illustration:

* $M_{2}$ saturated: $V_{DS2}\ge V_{GS2}-V_{Tn}$

$${\rm CS/CD:}\;\;V_{out}\ge V_{b}-V_{Tn}=V_{ov2}\tag{4}$$

otherwise $M_{2}$ triode.

* $M_{1}$ saturated

$${\rm CS}\;p{\rm MOS:}\;V_{SD1}\ge V_{SG1}-|V_{Tp}|$$
$$V_{DD}-V_{out}\ge V_{DD}-V_{in}-|V_{Tp}|\;\;,\;\;
V_{out}\le V_{in}+|V_{Tp}| \tag{5a}$$

$${\rm CD}\;n{\rm MOS:}\;V_{DS1}\ge V_{GS1}-V_{Tn}$$
$$V_{DD}-V_{out}\ge V_{in}-V_{out}-V_{Tn}\;\;
V_{in}\le V_{DD}+V_{Tn} \tag{5b}$$

normally satisfied. For the ${\rm CS}$

$$V_{ov2}\le V_{out}\le V_{in}+|V_{Tp}|$$

is the high gain window. Outside it one device
enters triode and the small signal resistance collapses.
Because $r_{o1}||r_{o2}$ is very large the d.c.
value of $V_{out}$ in the ${\rm CS}$ version is very
sensitive to $W/L$ mismatch and to $\lambda $ and is
normally stabilised by feedback.  In the follower
version $V_{out}$ is well defined by (3).

Large signal voltage transfer, ${\rm CS}$:

* $V_{in}\approx V_{DD}$ : $pM_{1}$ off, $M_{2}$
pulls $V_{out}\to V_{ov2}\approx 0$
* $V_{in}$ lowered by $|V_{Tp}|+V_{ov1}$ : $M_{1}$
turns on, $V_{out}$ rises sharply with slope
$-g_{m1}(r_{o1}||r_{o2})$
* $V_{in}\ll V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$ : $M_{1}$ triode,
$V_{out}\to V_{DD}-V_{SD,sat1}$

For the follower $V_{out}$ follows $V_{in}$ with a
d.c. shift, slope $\approx +1$.

It is a class A stage, static power
$P_{D}=V_{DD}I_{D0}$.

### 2. Small signal low frequency

Gate draws no current.

$$R_{in}= \infty \;\;{\rm at\; d.c.}\;\;,\;\;Z_{in}=1/sC_{gs1}
+{\rm Miller\; }C_{gd}$$

Small signal model: $V_{dd}=gnd$ for a.c.

```
         Vin o---||---+----+
                 Cgs  |   gmb1*Vbs1
                      g_m1*Vgs1  gds1
                      |    |      |
                      +--+-+------+---o Vout
                                 |   |
                                gds2 C_L
                                 |   |
                                GND GND
```

* ${\rm CS}\;pM_{1}$ with ${\rm B}_{1}={\rm S}_{1}$:

$V_{sg1}= -V_{gs1}=V_{in}$ with sign.  KCL at
$V_{out}$:

$$g_{m1}v_{sg1}+g_{ds1}v_{out}+g_{ds2}v_{out}=0$$

$$A_{v}\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{in}}=-{g_{m1}\over g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}
=-g_{m1}\left(r_{o1}||r_{o2}\right)
=-{g_{m1}\over (\lambda_{n}+\lambda_{p})I_{D}} \tag{6}$$

Typical $20-60\,{\rm dB}$ for a single stage.
If $\lambda\to 0$, $|A_{v}|\to\infty$ - the
load is an ideal current source. In practice

$$|A_{v}|\approx {2\over (\lambda_{n}+\lambda_{p})V_{ov1}}
\approx {1\over V_{ov}}\sqrt{{2\mu C_{ox}W/L\over \lambda^{2}I_{D}}}$$

and can be increased by increasing $L$, decreasing
$I_{D}$.  Sign is inverting, $180^{o}$ phase shift.
No $g_{mb}$ because $V_{bs1}=0$.

Output resistance seen from $V_{out}$ with $v_{in}=0$:

$$R_{out}=r_{o1}||r_{o2}={1\over g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\approx {1\over \lambda I_{D}}
\tag{7}$$

$10\,{\rm k\Omega}$ to $>1\,{\rm M\Omega}$.  $R_{out}$ is
high - the stage must drive a capacitive load $C_{L}$.

Dominant pole

$$\omega_{p}= {1\over R_{out}C_{L}}={g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}\over C_{L}}
\;\;,\;\;GBW\approx {g_{m1}\over C_{L}} \tag{8}$$

Miller capacitance $C_{gd1}$ gives input pole
$\omega_{in}\approx 1/R_{sig}C_{gd1}(1+|A_{v}|)$.

* ${\rm CD}\;nM_{1}$ source follower:

$$v_{gs1}=v_{in}-v_{out}\;\;,\;\;v_{bs1}=v_{b1}-v_{s1}
=-v_{out}\;\;{\rm if}\;B_{1}=GND\;(AC\;gnd)$$

KCL:

$$g_{m1}(v_{in}-v_{out})-g_{mb1}v_{out}
- g_{ds1}v_{out}-g_{ds2}v_{out}=0$$

$${A_{v}= {v_{out}\over v_{in}}=
{g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}
={g_{m1}r_{o1}||r_{o2}\over 1+(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})r_{o1}||r_{o2}}
\approx {g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}<1 \tag{9}}$$

For $r_{o}\to\infty$

$$A_{v0}={1\over 1+\eta}\approx 0.7-0.9$$

Body effect is the main loss.  If the $n$-well allows
${\rm B}_{1}={\rm S}_{1}$, $g_{mb1}=0$,

$$A_{v}= {g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\approx 0.95-0.99$$

and is non-inverting, no Miller multiplication.

Output resistance, $v_{in}=0$, test source $v_{x}$ at
$V_{out}$:

$$R_{out}={1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}||r_{o2}
\approx {1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}} \tag{10}$$

$ \sim 1/g_{m}= 100\,{\rm\Omega}-1\,{\rm k\Omega}$.
Hence the follower is a voltage buffer: high
$R_{in}$, low $R_{out}$, current gain.

Input resistance remains $\infty$ at low frequency,
capacitive $C_{gs1}+C_{gb1}$ at high frequency.

In either case $M_{2}$ provides an active load whose
small signal resistance $r_{o2}$ is $\sim 1/\lambda I_{D}$
much larger than a resistive or diode connected load
$1/g_{m}$, giving the maximum possible voltage gain
for a single device or the lowest $R_{out}$ for a
follower without extra power.  Cascoding $M_{1}$ or
$M_{2}$ raises $R_{out}$ to $g_{m}r_{o}^{2}$ and
$|A_{v}|$ to $g_{m}r_{o}^{2}$ for the ${\rm CS}$.

> In short: with the conventional CMOS assignment
> $M_{1}=p$MOS, $M_{2}=n$MOS the circuit is the
> CMOS inverter used as a high gain common source
> voltage amplifier $A_{v}=-g_{m1}(r_{o1}||r_{o2})$,
> $R_{out}=r_{o1}||r_{o2}$, $R_{in}=\infty$, inverting.
> With the symbol literally as drawn $M_{1}=n$MOS it is
> the common drain/source follower voltage buffer
> $A_{v}\approx g_{m1}/(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}) \approx 1$,
> $R_{out}\approx 1/(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})$, non-inverting,
> wide band, no Miller effect.
> Both are the core of operational amplifiers, source
> follower as output buffer, CS stage as gain stage.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Identifies the circuit as drawn as an NMOS source follower with an NMOS current-source load and gives the correct positive, slightly sub-unity gain. The extra discussion of an alternative common-source topology is unnecessary, but the answer’s final identification of the actual circuit is correct.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is nominally a {\it $n-$ channel}
{\it common drain with $n$ channel active load},
i.e. a {\bf source follower - voltage buffer}
and, by interchanging the reading of the symbol,
a {\bf $p-${\rm common} source with active load},
the elementary CMOS voltage gain stage.
With the conventional $4T$ symbol as drawn it is the
former. $V_{DD}$ is $ac$ ground.

$$\eqalign{
M_{1}&:g_{1}-d_{1}-s_{1}= V_{in}-V_{DD}-V_{out}\cr
M_{2}&:g_{2}-d_{2}-s_{2}= V_{b}-V_{out}-0}$$

> {\it Remark on the symbol:} $M_{2}$ is unambiguously
an $nMOS$, $d=V_{out}$, $s=GND$, $b=GND$ ${\rm arrow}\;b\to {\rm channel}$.
$M_{1}$ is drawn with $d=V_{DD}$, $s=V_{out}$ and
$b\to s$, i. e. $nMOS$ with bulk tied to source in order
to cancel the $g_{mb}$ body effect.  In a normal
$p-sub$ process $b=GND$ and $g_{mb1}\ne 0$.
If you read $M_{1}$ as a $pMOS$, $s=V_{DD}$, $b=V_{DD}$,
$d=V_{out}$, ${\rm arrow}\;s\to b$, the circuit is the
complementary common source voltage amplifier, Fig.2.
The analysis is dual with $g_{m1}\rightarrow g_{mp}$.

In the following $1\equiv n_{1}$ follower, $2\equiv n_{2}$
load. For $pMOS$ common source replace $Av\approx +1$
by $Av\approx -g_{m1}r_{01}\!\parallel\! r_{02}$.

```
VDD ac gnd
  |
  d
  M1  gm1,gmb1,gds1=1/ro1  Cgs1,Cgd1
  s ___ Vout
  |   |
  d   |
  M2  gm2,gds2=1/ro2     Vb ac gnd for
  s                     signal
  |
 GND ac gnd
```

### 1. D.C. large signal

Put in saturation, long channel, $\lambda =0$ for first
order:

$$I_{D}= {k_{n}\over 2}\left(V_{GS}-V_{T}\right)^{2}\qquad 
k_{n}= \mu_{n}C_{ox}W/L$$

$M_{2}$ is diode connected as a current source:

$$I_{D2}= {k_{2}\over 2}\left(V_{b}-V_{T2}\right)^{2}
\left[1+\lambda_{2}V_{out}\right] =I_{B}= {\rm const}$$

$$V_{GS2}=V_{b}\tag{1}$$

$$I_{D1}= {k_{1}\over 2}\left(V_{GS1}-V_{T1}\right)^{2}
\left[1+\lambda_{1}(V_{DD}-V_{out})\right] \tag{2}$$

and $I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{B}$ in series.

Hence

$$V_{GS1}=V_{in}-V_{out}=V_{T1}
+\sqrt{{2I_{B}\over k_{1}}}$$

$$\;V_{out}=V_{in}-V_{T1}-\sqrt{{2I_{B}\over k_{1}}}\;
\approx V_{in}-V_{T1}-\sqrt{k_{2}/k_{1}}\,(V_{b}-V_{T2})\tag{3}$$

i. e. $V_{out}$ {\it follows} $V_{in}$ with a
level shift $V_{GS1}$. Ideal follower $dV_{out}/dV_{in}=1$.

With bulk to $GND$,

$$V_{T1}=V_{T0}+\gamma \left(\sqrt{2\phi_{F}+V_{SB1}}-
\sqrt{2\phi_{F}}\right),\qquad V_{SB1}=V_{out}-0$$

for $b=s$, $V_{SB1}=0$, $V_{T1}=V_{T0}$ constant and
$g_{mb1}=0$, $g_{mb}=g_{m}\gamma /2\sqrt{2\phi+V_{SB}}$ otherwise.

Saturation conditions:

$$\eqalign{
M_{1}:& V_{DS1}\ge V_{GS1}-V_{T1}\cr
& V_{DD}-V_{out}\ge V_{in}-V_{out}-V_{T1}\cr
& V_{in}\le V_{DD}+V_{T1}\tag{4a}\cr
M_{2}:& V_{DS2}\ge V_{GS2}-V_{T2}\cr
& V_{out}\ge V_{b}-V_{T2}=V_{ov2}\tag{4b}}$$

and $V_{GS1}>V_{T1}\Rightarrow V_{in}>V_{out}+V_{T1}$ for
$M_{1}$ on. Normally (4a) is always satisfied.
The useful swing is therefore

$$V_{ov2}\le V_{out}\le V_{DD}-V_{ov1}\tag{5}$$

$$V_{ov}=V_{GS}-V_{T}= \sqrt{2I_{D}/k}$$

Below $V_{ov2}$ $M_{2}$ triodes and $r_{o2}$ collapses,
above $V_{DD}-V_{ov1}$ $M_{1}$ triodes. Cut-off for low
$V_{in}$.

$V_{b}$ is normally generated by a $nMOS$ current mirror
reference, so $I_{B}$ is well defined.

That is why $M_{2}$ is often drawn with $W/L$ ratioed to
the reference device.

### 2. Small signal low frequency

$V_{b}$ ac ground, $V_{DD}$ ac ground, $M_{1}$ common drain,
$M_{2}$ common gate load $=r_{o2}$ to ground.

Small signal model, gate $v_{in}$, source $v_{out}$:

$$v_{gs1}=v_{in}-v_{out}$$
$$g_{m1}v_{gs1}+g_{mb1}v_{bs1}+g_{ds1}v_{ds1}+g_{ds2}v_{out}=0$$

with $v_{bs1}=-v_{out}$ if $b_{1}=GND$ and $0$ if $b_{1}=s_{1}$,
$v_{ds1}=-v_{out}$, $v_{ds2}=v_{out}$.

$$\left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}\right)v_{out}=
g_{m1}v_{in} $$

$$\;A_{v}\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{in}}
={g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\;
\tag{6}$$

$$={g_{m1}r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\over 
1+\left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\right)r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}}$$

If bulk tied to source $g_{mb1}=0$,

$$A_{v}={g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}
={g_{m1}r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\over 1+g_{m1}r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}}
\approx 1-{1\over g_{m1}r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}}<1\tag{7}$$

Normally $g_{m}r_{o}\sim 20-100$, so

$$A_{v}\approx 0.8-0.98$$

without body effect, $0.6-0.8$ with body effect because
$g_{mb}\approx (0.1-0.3)g_{m}$.

With $\lambda\to 0$, $r_{o}\to\infty$, $A_{v}\to g_{m1}/(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})
\to 1$.

Phase non-inverting.

If read as $pMOS$ common source, $M_{1}$ $s=V_{DD}$ $ac$ gnd,
$d=V_{out}$, $g=v_{in}$:

$$A_{v}=-g_{m1}\,r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\approx -20{\rm\;to\;}
-100 \tag{6p}$$

inverting high gain stage, the core of the CMOS op-amp.

Input impedance:

$$\;Z_{in}=1/sC_{g1}\to\infty\;{\rm low\;freq}\tag{8}$$

essentially the gate capacitance.

Output impedance: zero $v_{in}$, apply $v_{x}$ at output,
measure $i_{x}$.

$$i_{x}= \left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}\right)v_{x}$$

$$\;R_{out}= {1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}
\parallel r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\approx {1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}
\parallel r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\approx {1\over g_{m1}}\;
\tag{9}$$

Typically $1/g_{m}\sim 0.1-1\,{\rm k\Omega}$, $r_{o}\sim 10-100\,{\rm k\Omega}$.
So low impedance, can drive capacitive / small resistive loads.
No current gain is $ \approx g_{m1}R_{L}$.

For the $pMOS$ common source reading
$R_{out}=r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}$ high impedance.

### 3. High frequency

Dominant poles:

* input pole $1/R_{sig}C_{g1}$ - very high because $R_{sig}$ sees $C_{gs1}+C_{gd1}(1-A_{v})\approx C_{gs1}$ small Miller.
* output pole $1/R_{out}C_{L}$ with $C_{L}=C_{s1}+C_{d2}+C_{load}+C_{sb1}$

Because $R_{out}\approx 1/g_{m}$ is small, the follower is
intrinsically wide band, can be used as source follower buffer
to drive large $C_{L}$. Approx unity gain bandwidth
$\approx g_{m1}/C_{L}$.

### 4. Properties and use

* voltage gain $\approx 1$, no voltage amplification
* current / power amplification $ \gg 1$
* high $Z_{in}$, low $Z_{out}$ - ideal voltage buffer, impedance transformer
* level shift by $V_{GS}\approx V_{T}+V_{ov}$
* very linear if $I_{B}$ constant, distortion $\propto v_{out}/V_{ov}$
* poor swing compared to rail-to-rail if $b=GND$ due to body effect $V_{T}(V_{out})$.

Applications: output stage of op-amps, source follower buffer
between common source gain stage and load, level shifter,
$DC$ shifter in cascades, input stage of voltage regulator.

To increase swing and $A_{v}\to 1$, use $pMOS$ follower in
$n$-well with bulk to source, or triple well $nMOS$ with
deep $n$-well bulk to source, or use super source follower,
flipped voltage follower.

In its complementary reading as $pMOS$ input / $nMOS$ load
it is the elementary unbuffered CMOS OTA gain stage, $A_{v}\approx -g_{m}r_{o}$, used in every CMOS op-amp with active load.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies the drawn circuit as an NMOS source follower, places the output at M1’s source, and derives a positive gain slightly below unity with body effect and finite output resistance. The speculative pMOS common-source discussion and the “diode connected” label for M2 are extraneous or mistaken, but do not change the correct analysis of the shown circuit.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
The circuit is the **Complementary MOS In - NOT - {\it Inverter}**. 
It is the basic ${\it ratioless}$ static CMOS logic
gate. $M_{1}= n-MOS$ , $M_{2}= p-MOS$, enhancement mode.

$$S_{1}= {\rm GND}, B_{1}= {\rm GND} \;\;,\;\; S_{2}= V_{DD}, B_{2}=V_{DD}$$

so source-body junctions always reverse biased. 
Gates common $=V_{in}$ , Drains common $=V_{out}$ - push - pull
common source with active load.

In digital terms:

$$V_{out}= \bar V_{in}$$

| $V_{in}$ | $M_{1}$ nMOS | $M_{2}$ pMOS | $V_{out}$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| $0 = GND =``0"$ | $V_{GS1}=0<V_{Tn}$ {\it OFF} | $V_{SG2}=V_{DD}>|V_{Tp}|$ {\it ON} lin. | $V_{DD}=``1"$ |
| $V_{DD}=``1"$ | $V_{GS1}=V_{DD}>V_{Tn}$ {\it ON} lin. | $V_{SG2}=0<|V_{Tp}|$ {\it OFF} | $0=``0"$ |

No DC path $V_{DD}\to GND$ in either stable logic state. Static current $I_{DD}=0$ except leakage and during transition. High input impedance $\approx \infty$, rail to rail output swing, large noise margin.

### 1. DC Transfer Characteristic $V_{out}=f(V_{in})$ $0\le V_{in}\le V_{DD}$

With $I_{Dn}= -I_{Dp}$ current:

* nMOS: $I_{Dn}=0$ if $V_{GS}<V_{Tn}$, $k_{n}(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})^{2}/2$ in saturation, $k_{n}[2(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})V_{DS}-V_{DS}^{2}]/2$ in triode.

* pMOS: $I_{Dp}=0$ if $V_{SG}<|V_{Tp}|$, analogous with $V_{SG}, V_{SD}$

where $k_{n,p}= \mu_{n,p}C_{ox}(W/L)_{n,p}= \beta_{n,p}$

$$V_{Tn}>0 \;\;,\;\; V_{Tp}<0$$

In the sweep $V_{in}:0\to V_{DD}$ 5 regions:

1.  $0\le V_{in}<V_{Tn}$ : $M_{1}$ cut-off, $M_{2}$ triode
    $$I_{D}=0,\; V_{out}=V_{DD}=V_{OH}$$

2.  $V_{Tn}<V_{in}< V_{IL}$ : $M_{1}$ saturation, $M_{2}$ triode

3.  $V_{IL}<V_{in}<V_{IH}$ : **both saturation** - high gain transition. $I_{D}$ maximum. 
    The logic threshold $V_{M}$ defined by $V_{in}=V_{out}$ and $I_{Dn}=-I_{Dp}$ in saturation:
    $$\frac{k_{n}}{2}(V_{M}-V_{Tn})^{2}= \frac{k_{p}}{2}(V_{DD}-V_{M}+V_{Tp})^{2}$$
    $$V_{M}= \frac{V_{Tn}+ \sqrt{k_{p}/k_{n}}\,(V_{DD}+V_{Tp})}{1+\sqrt{k_{p}/k_{n}}}$$
    For symmetric inverter $V_{Tn}=|V_{Tp}|=V_{T}$ and matched $\beta$ ,
    $$V_{M}\approx V_{DD}/2$$
    Condition for $V_{M}=V_{DD}/2$:
    $$\frac{(W/L)_{p}}{(W/L)_{n}} = \frac{\mu_{n}}{\mu_{p}}\approx 2-3$$

4.  $V_{IH}<V_{in}<V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$ : $M_{1}$ triode, $M_{2}$ saturation

5.  $V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|<V_{in}\le V_{DD}$ : $M_{2}$ cut-off, $M_{1}$ triode
    $$I_{D}=0,\; V_{out}=0=V_{OL}$$

This gives the familiar sharp, inverting VTC with three points $V_{IL},V_{M},V_{IH}$ defined by $dV_{out}/dV_{in}=-1$.

$$V_{OH}=V_{DD},\;V_{OL}=0$$
$$NM_{L}=V_{IL}-V_{OL}\approx V_{M},\; NM_{H}=V_{OH}-V_{IH}\approx V_{DD}-V_{M}$$
Ideal $\approx V_{DD}/2$ - maximum noise immunity.

> In current domain $I_{DD}(V_{in})$ is $\approx 0$ in regions 1,5 and is a narrow peaked pulse $\approx k(V_{M}-V_{T})^{2}/2$ in region 3 - the short circuit current during switching.

### 2. Small signal - Analog amplifier

Biased at $V_{in}=V_{M}$, both in saturation:

$$A_{v}= \frac{v_{out}}{v_{in}} = -\frac{g_{m1}+g_{m2}}{g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}} = -(g_{m1}+g_{m2})(r_{o1}||r_{o2})$$

Typical $|A_{v}| \approx 10-100$, inverting common source. $g_{m}=k(V_{GS}-V_{T})$, $r_{o}=1/\lambda I_{D}$. Used as high gain inverting stage, crystal oscillator, etc.

Input capacitance $C_{in}=C_{gs1}+C_{gs2}+C_{gd1}+C_{gd2}$ Miller, output resistance $r_{o1}||r_{o2}$.

### 3. Dynamic - Transient

Capacitive load $C_{L}$ at $V_{out}$.

* Pull-up through $M_{2}$ : $t_{pLH}\approx 0.69\,R_{p}C_{L}$
* Pull-down through $M_{1}$ : $t_{pHL}\approx 0.69\,R_{n}C_{L}$

with $R_{n,p}\approx 1/k_{n,p}(V_{DD}-V_{T})$ in triode.

Dynamic power :

$$P_{D}= P_{stat}+P_{sc}+P_{dyn}\approx C_{L}V_{DD}^{2}f + V_{DD}I_{sc,av}$$

$P_{stat}\approx V_{DD}I_{leak}\to 0$ is the great advantage of CMOS.

Inverter is ratioless, can be scaled, fundamental cell for NAND, NOR, SRAM, ring oscillators and every CMOS digital IC. Equal sized $W_{p}\approx 2-3\,W_{n}$ gives symmetric rise/fall times.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies the standard CMOS inverter with an NMOS pull-down and PMOS pull-up, and describes its inverting operation. Minor imprecision in secondary details does not contradict the inverter’s operation.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is the fundamental CMOS logic building
block - the {\it Complementary MOS Inverter} or {\it NOT Gate}
and at the same time a {\it class A push-pull inverting amplifier}.

$$M_{1}: NMOS\;\; ,S=GND \;\; V_{BS1}=0$$
$$M_{2}: PMOS\;\; ,S=V_{DD} \;\; V_{BS2}=0$$

no body effect if $n-$ well/$p-$ substrate is tied to the
source. Common gate input $V_{in}$, common drain output $V_{out}$.

It is {\it ratio-less}, {\it rail to rail} logic with ideally
{\it zero static power}.

### 1. Principle of operation

$$I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{D}\;\;{\rm in\;d.c.\;steady\;state}$$

For a long channel, neglect $\lambda$ for first order:

$$I_{Dn}=k_{n}(V_{GSn}-V_{Tn})^{2}/2\;\; {\rm sat.}$$
$$k_{n}= \mu_{n}C_{ox}(W/L)_{1}\;\;,k_{p}= \mu_{p}C_{ox}(W/L)_{2}$$
$$I_{Dp}=k_{p}(V_{SGp}+V_{Tp})^{2}/2\;\; {\rm sat.}\;\;V_{Tp}<0$$

* $V_{in}=0 = V_{OL}<V_{Tn}$:

$V_{GS1}=0<V_{Tn}\to M_{1}$ {\bf OFF}, $V_{SG2}=V_{DD}>|V_{Tp}|\to M_{2}$ {\bf ON}
No DC path to GND. $M_{2}$ charges the output capacitance to $V_{DD}$ through its low $R_{on}$, in steady state $V_{OH}=V_{DD}$, $I_{DD}=0$ ( leakage only). $M_{2}$ is in triode/linear because $V_{SD2}=0< V_{SG2}+V_{Tp}$.

* $V_{in}=V_{DD}=V_{OH}>V_{Tn}$:

$V_{GS1}=V_{DD}>V_{Tn}\to M_{1}$ {\bf ON}, $V_{SG2}=0<|V_{Tp}|\to M_{2}$ {\bf OFF}
No DC path to $V_{DD}$. $M_{1}$ discharges the load to $GND$, $V_{OL}=0$, $I_{DD}=0$. $M_{1}$ is in triode.

In words: Pull-up network ($M_{2}$) and pull-down network ($M_{1}$) are never ON simultaneously in steady state. Logic function:

$$V_{out} = \bar V_{in}$$

| $V_{in}$ | $M_{1}$ NMOS | $M_{2}$ PMOS | $V_{out}$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| $0$ | OFF | Linear | $V_{DD}$ |
| $L$ | OFF/Sat | Linear | $\approx V_{DD}$ |
| $V_{M}$ | Sat | Sat | $V_{M}\approx V_{DD}/2$ |
| $H$ | Linear | Sat/OFF | $\approx 0$ |
| $V_{DD}$ | Linear | OFF | $0$ |

### 2. Voltage Transfer Characteristic - VTC

Five regions for increasing $V_{in}$ $0\to V_{DD}$:

1.  $M1$ off, $M2$ linear : $V_{out}=V_{DD}$
2.  $M1$ saturation, $M2$ linear
3.  $M1$ {\bf saturation}, $M2$ {\bf saturation} : High gain transition. Both saturated only for a narrow $V_{in}$ around the logic threshold.
4.  $M1$ linear, $M2$ saturation
5.  $M1$ linear, $M2$ off : $V_{out}=0$

Ideal VTC is very steep in region 3, approximating an ideal inverter.

The logic threshold or switching point $V_{M}$ defined by $V_{in}=V_{out}=V_{M}$ where $I_{Dn}=|I_{Dp}|$ both in saturation:

$$\frac{k_{n}}{2}(V_{M}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda_{n}V_{M}) = \frac{k_{p}}{2}(V_{DD}-V_{M}+V_{Tp})^{2}(1+\lambda_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{M}))$$

For $\lambda\approx 0$:

$$V_{M}= \frac{V_{Tn}+ \sqrt{k_{p}/k_{n}}\,(V_{DD}+V_{Tp})}{1+\sqrt{k_{p}/k_{n}}}$$

If inverter is symmetric $k_{n}=k_{p}$, $V_{Tn}=|V_{Tp}|=V_{T}$:

$$V_{M}=V_{DD}/2$$

Noise margins are obtained from $dV_{out}/dV_{in}=-1$ points $V_{IL},V_{IH}$:

$$NM_{L}=V_{IL}-V_{OL}\approx V_{IL}$$
$$NM_{H}=V_{OH}-V_{IH}\approx V_{DD}-V_{IH}$$

For symmetric design $NM_{L}=NM_{H}\approx 0.4\,V_{DD}$, excellent noise immunity and full $0$ to $V_{DD}$ swing.

Current characteristic is a narrow peak at $V_{M}$ with
$I_{D,max}\approx k(V_{DD}/2-V_{T})^{2}/2$, zero elsewhere. Hence static power $P_{s}=V_{DD}I_{leak}\approx 0$.

### 3. Small signal - analog amplifier view

Biased at $V_{M}$ in region 3, both devices saturated, the circuit is a high gain push-pull common source amplifier.

Small signal model: Gates common, drains common.

$$g_{m}=g_{m1}+g_{m2}$$
$$g_{o}=g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}= \lambda_{n}I_{D}+ \lambda_{p}I_{D}$$
$$r_{o}=1/g_{o}=r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}$$

$$A_{v}= \frac{v_{out}}{v_{in}} = -\frac{g_{m1}+g_{m2}}{g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}} = -(g_{m1}+g_{m2})(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})$$

Typically $20$ to $>40\,dB$ with $r_{o}\sim 10k - 100k\Omega$, $g_{m}\sim 0.1-1\,mA/V$. Input resistance $\to \infty$, output resistance $r_{o}$.

Transition gain in large signal:

$$A_{v}\approx -\frac{1}{(V_{M}-V_{Tn})\lambda_{n}+ (V_{DD}-V_{M}+V_{Tp})\lambda_{p}}$$

Bandwidth limited by load capacitance $C_{L}$ at output node:

$$f_{-3dB}\approx 1/2\pi r_{o}C_{L}$$

Slew rate $SR = I_{D}/C_{L}$.

Dynamic power when switching at frequency $f$:

$$P_{D}= C_{L}V_{DD}^{2}f + V_{DD}I_{sc}$$

where $I_{sc}$ is short circuit current during transition when both conduct, and propagation delay for a step input:

$$t_{pLH}\approx 0.69 R_{p}C_{L}\;\;,\;\;t_{pHL}\approx 0.69 R_{n}C_{L}$$
$$t_{p}= (t_{pLH}+t_{pHL})/2$$

with $R_{n,p}\approx 1/k_{n,p}(V_{DD}-V_{T})$.

> In digital application it is used as a NOT gate, buffer, and the basic element for NAND/NOR, SRAM, latch, ring oscillator. In analog it is the simplest CMOS operational transconductance inverter stage, often used as output stage or as a high gain stage with active load - essentially $M_{1}$ is the driver and $M_{2}$ is its active load and vice versa.

Ideal characteristics: full logic swing, regenerative VTC, high $NM$, zero static current, ratioless design - area and operation independent of transistor sizing ratio except for $V_{M}$ and speed.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is the Complementary MOS, CMOS, NOT gate - {\bf Inverter} the basic building block of all static CMOS logic.

$$M_{1}= NMOS\; driver \;\; ; \;M_{2}= PMOS\; active\; load$$
$$M_{1}: V_{GS1}= V_{in} \;, \;V_{DS1}=V_{out}$$
$$M_{2}: V_{SG2}= V_{DD}-V_{in}\;, \; V_{SD2}=V_{DD}-V_{out}$$

Bulk of $M_{1}$ to $GND$ and bulk of $M_{2}$ to $V_{DD}$ so for this connection $V_{SB}=0$ no body effect. Both are enhancement mode, $V_{Tn}>0 ,\;V_{Tp}<0$.

$$I_{Dn}= \begin{cases}
0 & V_{GS}<V_{Tn}\;\;cut-off\\
k_{n}\left[(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})V_{DS}-V_{DS}^{2}/2\right] & V_{DS}<V_{GS}-V_{Tn}\;\;triode\\
\frac{k_{n}}{2}(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda_{n}V_{DS}) & V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{Tn}\;\;saturation
\end{cases}$$

$$k_{n}= \mu_{n}C_{ox}(W/L)_{1} \quad , \quad k_{p}= \mu_{p}C_{ox}(W/L)_{2}$$

and dual for $M_{2}$ with $V_{SG},V_{SD},|V_{Tp}|$.

In DC steady state $I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{D}$.

### 1. Logic Operation

| $V_{in}$ | $M_{1}$ NMOS | $M_{2}$ PMOS | $V_{out}$ | Logic |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $0 = GND$ | $V_{GS}<V_{Tn} \rightarrow OFF$ | $V_{SG}=V_{DD} >|V_{Tp}|\rightarrow ON$ | $V_{out}=V_{DD}$ through $M_{2}$ | $0 \rightarrow 1$ |
| $V_{DD}$ | $V_{GS}=V_{DD} \rightarrow ON$ | $V_{SG}=0 \rightarrow OFF$ | $V_{out}=0$ through $M_{1}$ | $1 \rightarrow 0$ |

Hence $V_{out}= \bar V_{in}$ . In static state one transistor is always OFF so ideal {\it static current $=0$} and static power $P_{stat}\approx 0$.

$$V_{OH}=V_{DD} \quad , \quad V_{OL}=0$$

Full rail to rail swing - ratioless logic.

### 2. Voltage Transfer Characteristic - 5 Regions

With $V_{in}$ swept $0 \to V_{DD}$:

* {\bf A: $0 \le V_{in} < V_{Tn}$} 
  $M_{1}$ OFF, $M_{2}$ triode. $I_{D}=0$, $V_{out}=V_{DD}$.

* {\bf B: $V_{Tn} < V_{in} < V_{in,1}$}
  $M_{1}$ saturation, $M_{2}$ triode.

* {\bf C: $V_{in} \approx V_{M}$} 
  Both saturation. Very high gain region. This is the switching threshold where $I_{D1}=I_{D2}$.

  Ignoring $\lambda$:
  $$\frac{k_{n}}{2}(V_{M}-V_{Tn})^{2}= \frac{k_{p}}{2}(V_{DD}-V_{M}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}$$

  $$V_{M}= \frac{V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|+ \sqrt{k_{n}/k_{p}}\;V_{Tn}}{1+\sqrt{k_{n}/k_{p}}}= \frac{V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|+ \sqrt{\beta_{R}}V_{Tn}}{1+\sqrt{\beta_{R}}}$$

  with $\beta_{R}=k_{n}/k_{p}$. For matched device $k_{n}=k_{p}$ and $V_{Tn}=|V_{Tp}|=V_{T}$:

  $$V_{M}=V_{DD}/2$$

  Commonly $(W/L)_{p} \approx 2-3 (W/L)_{n}$ to compensate $\mu_{n}\approx 2-3\mu_{p}$ and get symmetric $V_{M}$.

* {\bf D: $V_{in,2} < V_{in} < V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$}
  $M_{1}$ triode, $M_{2}$ saturation.

* {\bf E: $V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}| < V_{in} \le V_{DD}$}
  $M_{1}$ triode, $M_{2}$ OFF. $I_{D}=0$, $V_{out}=0$.

> VTC is a sharp inverted S. Slope $dV_{out}/dV_{in} \approx 0$ in regions A and E, slope $<<-1$ in C.

```
Vout
VDD |******
    |      *
    |       *
    |        *
    |         *
    |          *******
    +------------------ Vin
    0   VIL VM VIH  VDD
```

Noise margins defined by $|dV_{out}/dV_{in}|=1$:

$$N_{M_{L}} = V_{IL}-V_{OL} \quad , \quad N_{M_{H}} = V_{OH}-V_{IH}$$

For ideal symmetric inverter $N_{M_{L}} \approx N_{M_{H}} \approx 0.4\,V_{DD}$ - maximum.

### 3. Analog Small Signal Behaviour

If biased at $V_{in}=V_{M}$ region C both devices in saturation it is a high gain push-pull common source amplifier. Loaded by $C_{L}$:

$$A_{v} = \left.\frac{dV_{out}}{dV_{in}}\right|_{V_{M}} = -\frac{g_{m1}+g_{m2}}{g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}} = -\frac{g_{m1}+g_{m2}}{r_{o1}^{-1}+r_{o2}^{-1}}$$

$$g_{m}=k(V_{GS}-V_{T})\;\;,\;\; r_{o}=1/\lambda I_{D}$$

Typically $|A_{v}| = 20$ to $100$ for long channel, $>10$ for short channel. This is why the transition is so sharp.

### 4. Dynamic Behaviour

No DC path, current only flows during switching when both transistors briefly conduct, short circuit current spike + charging/discharging $C_{L}$.

$$P_{dyn}= C_{L}V_{DD}^{2}f + V_{DD}I_{sc} + P_{leak}$$

Propagation delay for $C_{L}$ load approx:

$$t_{pLH} \approx \frac{C_{L}V_{DD}}{2I_{Dp,sat}} \quad , \quad t_{pHL} \approx \frac{C_{L}V_{DD}}{2I_{Dn,sat}}$$

$$t_{p}= \frac{t_{pLH}+t_{pHL}}{2}$$

Designed for $t_{pLH}=t_{pHL}$ via $k_{n}=k_{p}$ sizing.

In short: As {\bf digital gate} it is an ideal inverter with near zero static power, full logic swing and regenerative VTC. As {\bf analog circuit} at $V_{M}$ it is a high gain inverting amplifier.

If you give $V_{DD}, V_{Tn}, |V_{Tp}|, (W/L)_{1,2}, k_{n}',k_{p}'$ the $V_{M}, V_{IL},V_{IH}$, gain and $t_{p}$ can be calculated numerically.

Want the numeric VTC/current for a specific technology? Provide $V_{DD}$ and transistor parameters.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
With the symbology as drawn the circuit is
{\it not} a complementary stage but the {\sl pseudo}
ratioed stage of Fig.1. In the literature the upper
device is normally drawn as a ${\cal P}$ device and the
circuit is then the conventional ${\cal C}{\cal MOS}$
``NOT''.

\begin{center}
{\tt M1 = load, M2 = driver } 
\end{center}

{\rm I} will put the analysis in the form most text
books want it, i.e. with

$${\rm M1}={\cal P}-{\rm MOS}\;\; {\rm on\;top},\qquad 
  {\rm M2}={\cal N}-{\rm MOS}\;\; {\rm on\;bottom}$$

If you take the figure literally, ${\rm M1}\equiv {\cal
N}$ put ${\rm |V_{Tp}|=V_{Tn}=V_{T}>0}$ and
${\rm g_{m1}\rightarrow -g_{m1}}$ in what follows.

\begin{figure}[h]
Vin=0 -> M1 ON, M2 OFF -> Vo=VDD
Vin=VDD -> M1 OFF, M2 ON -> Vo=0
\end{figure}

> {\it Normally the arrow on ${\rm M1}$ is reversed
> with respect to ${\rm M2}$. With the arrow as drawn
> ${\rm M1}$ and ${\rm M2}$ are the same polarity and
> the stage is ratioed, has a $Hi-Z$ state for
> $V_{in}<V_{T}$ and can never pull to $V_{DD}$. It is
> normally rejected as a logic gate.}

\subsection*{1. Large signal - ideal ${\cal C}{\cal MOS}$}

Let

$${\rm M1}:S=V_{DD},\; D=V_{o},\;G=V_{i}\;\;{\cal P},
\;\;|V_{T1}|=|V_{Tp}|$$
$${\rm M2}:D=V_{o},\;S=0,\;G=V_{i}\;\;{\cal N},
\;\;V_{T2}=V_{Tn}$$

$$I_{Dn}=k_{n}\left[(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})V_{DS}-{\frac12}V_{DS}^{2}
\right]\;{\rm triode}$$
$$I_{Dn}= {\frac12}k_{n}(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda _{n}V_{DS})
\;{\rm sat.},\;V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{Tn}$$
$$I_{Dp}= {\frac12}k_{p}(V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}(1+\lambda _{p}V_{SD})
\;{\rm sat.}$$
with $k=\mu C_{ox}W/L$, $\beta =k$.

Put $I_{Dn}=I_{Dp}=I_{D}$ for the series connection.

In static operation one device is always {\it off}}:

* {\bf A: $0\le V_{i}<V_{Tn}$ :} ${\rm M2}$ cut off,
${\rm M1}$ linear - in fact $V_{SG1}=V_{DD}-V_{i}>
|V_{Tp}|$, $V_{SD1}=V_{DD}-V_{o}$ small. No DC path
to ground. $I_{D}=0$ and

$$V_{o}=V_{OH}=V_{DD}\tag{1}$$

within the leakage current.

* {\bf B: $V_{Tn}<V_{i}<V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$ :} both on.
For low $V_{o}$ ${\rm M2}$ sat., ${\rm M1}$ linear,
for high $V_{o}$ vice versa. In the middle

$$V_{Tn}<V_{i}<V_{DD}/2\;\;{\rm approx.}$$

both are saturated. This is the high gain transition
region.

* {\bf C: $V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|<V_{i}\le V_{DD}$ :} ${\rm M1}$
cut off, ${\rm M2}$ linear,

$$V_{o}=V_{OL}=0\tag{2}$$

Hence

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
V_{i} & {\rm M1(P)} & {\rm M2(N)} & V_{o}\\ \hline
0 & {\rm ON} & {\rm OFF} & 1\equiv V_{DD}\\
V_{DD} & {\rm OFF} & {\rm ON} & 0\equiv 0
\end{array}\tag{3}$$

i.e. the Boolean

$$V_{o}= \bar V_{i}\tag{4}$$

and the voltage transfer characteristic, VTC, of
Fig.2 is obtained, with 5 regions:

1. M1 linear, M2 off
2. M1 linear, M2 sat.
3. M1 sat., M2 sat. - high gain
4. M1 sat., M2 linear
5. M1 off, M2 linear

In region 3, $I_{Dn}(sat)=I_{Dp}(sat)$,

$$\frac12 k_{n}(V_{i}-V_{Tn})^{2}=
\frac12 k_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}\tag{5}$$

at the logic threshold where by definition
$V_{i}=V_{o}=V_{M}$,

$$V_{M}= \frac{V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|+V_{Tn}\sqrt{k_{n}/k_{p}}}
{1+\sqrt{k_{n}/k_{p}}}\tag{6}$$

For the symmetric $k_{n}=k_{p}$, $|V_{Tp}|=V_{Tn}=V_{T}$

$$V_{M}=V_{DD}/2\tag{7}$$

$$V_{IL},V_{IH}:\; \left.\frac{dV_{o}}{dV_{i}}\right|_{V_{IL},V_{IH}}=-1$$

$$NM_{L}=V_{IL}-V_{OL}\qquad NM_{H}=V_{OH}-V_{IH}\tag{8}$$

$NM_{L},NM_{H}\approx 0.4\,V_{DD}$ for the symmetric
case. No static current in state {\bf A} or {\bf C},

$$P_{stat}=0\;\;{\rm ideally}\tag{9}$$
$$P_{dyn}=C_{L}V_{DD}^{2}f_{clk}+V_{DD}I_{sc}\tag{10}$$

$C_{L}$ is the load capacitance, $I_{sc}$ the short
circuit current in region 3.

Small signal at $V_{M}$ with both sat., $V_{DD}$ AC
ground,

$$v_{gs1}=v_{sg1}= -v_{i},\;v_{gs2}=v_{i}$$

$$g_{m1}v_{sg1}+g_{ds1}v_{o}+g_{m2}v_{gs2}+g_{ds2}v_{o}=0$$

$$A_{v}\equiv \frac{v_{o}}{v_{i}}= -\,\frac{g_{m1}+g_{m2}}
{g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}= -\,\frac{g_{m1}+g_{m2}}{g_{o1}+g_{o2}}\tag{11}$$

$$|A_{v}|\approx \frac{2}{(\lambda _{n}+\lambda _{p})(V_{GS}-V_{T})}
\approx 20-50\,{\rm dB}$$

$$r_{o}=r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\tag{12}$$

The bodies are strapped to the supplies, $S\equiv B$,
so there is no back gate effect, $g_{mb}=0$.

\subsection*{2. What the figure actually draws: ${\rm M1}={\rm M2}={\cal N}$}

Put now ${\rm M1}$ also ${\cal N}$: $D_{1}=V_{DD}$,
$S_{1}=V_{o}$, $G_{1}=V_{i}$ so $V_{GS1}=V_{i}-V_{o}$,
$V_{DS1}=V_{DD}-V_{o}$; $V_{GS2}=V_{i}$, $V_{DS2}=V_{o}$.

* $V_{i}<V_{T}$: both cut off. $V_{o}$ is {\it
floating, $Hi-Z$}. It is held by the previous charge on
$C_{L}$. It is not a logic level - the circuit is not
restoring.

* $V_{i}>V_{T}$: both on. KCL $I_{D1}=I_{D2}$.

E.G. both saturated,

$$\frac12k_{1}(V_{i}-V_{o}-V_{T1})^{2}= 
\frac12k_{2}(V_{i}-V_{T2})^{2}\tag{13}$$

$$V_{o}=V_{i}-V_{T1}-\sqrt{\frac{k_{2}}{k_{1}}}\,(V_{i}-V_{T2})
\tag{14}$$

In any case $V_{o}$ is a voltage divider,

$$V_{o}\approx V_{DD}\frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}+R_{2}}<V_{DD}\tag{15}$$

and there is static current

$$I_{stat}\approx \frac12k_{2}(V_{i}-V_{T})^{2}\tag{16}$$

for $V_{i}=V_{DD}$.

Small signal, $V_{o1}=0$ AC,

$$I_{d1}=g_{m1}(v_{i}-v_{o})+g_{o1}(-v_{o})$$
$$I_{d2}=g_{m2}v_{i}+g_{o2}v_{o}$$

$$I_{d1}=I_{d2}\Rightarrow A_{v}= \frac{v_{o}}{v_{i}}=
\frac{g_{m1}-g_{m2}}{g_{m1}+g_{o1}+g_{o2}}\tag{17}$$

If $k_{1}=k_{2}$, $g_{m1}\approx g_{m2}$ and
$|A_{v}|\ll 1$, typically $<1$. The stage degenerates
to a source follower loaded by a common source device.
It can never pull to $V_{DD}$, $V_{OH}=V_{i}-V_{T}$ at
best, has $\approx V_{T}$ loss, finite $V_{OL}>0$
given by the $k_{1}/k_{2}$ ratio, dissipates DC power
when $V_{i}=1$ and is $Hi-Z$ when $V_{i}=0$. 

For that reason the circuit is not used as a logic
inverter. The useful ${\cal N}{\cal MOS}$ inverter is
obtained by connecting $G_{1}$ to $V_{DD}$ [depletion
load, $V_{T1}<0$] or to $V_{o}$ [saturated enhancement
load] to give a ratioed inverter with $V_{OH}=V_{DD}$,
$V_{OH}=V_{DD}-V_{T1}$ respectively.

> In short: {\it intended} as drawn as a ${\cal P}$ on
> top, ${\cal N}$ on bottom it is the textbook
> ${\cal C}{\cal MOS}$ inverter, the basis of all
> ${\cal C}{\cal MOS}$ logic, with rail to rail swing,
> essentially zero static power and high noise margin.
> {\it Literally} as drawn with two ${\cal N}$ devices
> it is a non-restoring, ratioed, $Hi-Z$ for $V_{i}=0$,
> source follower / common source divider with $\approx 0$
> small signal gain and threshold loss, and is not a
> usable inverter without rewiring ${\rm M1}$ as a load
> device.

If you give $W/L$, $V_{T}$, $k_{n},k_{p}$ and $V_{DD}$
the 5 region VTC, $V_{M}$, $V_{IL},V_{IH}$, $V_{OL},V_{OH}$
and $t_{pLH},t_{pHL}\approx 0.69R_{on}C_{L}$ can be
evaluated quantitatively.

The extra conventional-inverter discussion and imperfect detailed analysis do not override the full-credit rule.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
In normal {\it CMOS} technology this is
with the standard assign convention

$$M_{1}= {\rm PUN}\sim PMOS\qquad M_{2}= {\rm PDN}\sim NMOS$$

the complementary {\it push pull inverter},
i. e. the {\bf NOT gate}. With the literal
bulk connexion as drawn it is miss drawn.

> {\it R. m.:} In the conventional symbol the
> arrow is on the {\it source} , resp. on the {\it $n$-bulk--$p$-channel}
> junction. I. e. for a $PMOS$ the arrow is
> {\it out} of the channel and for a $NMOS$ {\it in} to the
> channel. With that convention the upper transistor has
> its arrow on the wrong side in Fig. and the $n$-well
> must go to $V_{DD}$, not $V_{out}$. Otherwise the
> source to bulk $p-n$ junction goes forward for
> $V_{out}<V_{DD}-0.6{\rm V}$, body effect
> $$V_{T}=V_{T0}+\gamma\left[\sqrt{2\phi_{F}+V_{SB}}-
> \sqrt{2\phi_{F}}\right] $$
> makes $M_{1}$ signal dependent and the circuit
> latches. Taken litteraly as two $NMOS$ with
> $B_{1}=V_{out}$ $B_{2}=0$ and $D_{1}=V_{DD}\;S_{1}=V_{out}
> \;D_{2}=V_{out}\;S_{2}=0$ the circuit has
> no complementary action. For $V_{in}<V_{T}$ it is
> high $Z$ and for $V_{in}>V_{T}$ a ratioed divider. Normally it
> is used as in Fig. 1 {\it corr}.

$$\eqalign{
S_{1}&=V_{DD}\cr D_{1}&=V_{out}\cr S_{2}&=0\cr D_{2}&=V_{out}\cr
G_{1}&=G_{2}=V_{in}\cr B_{2}&=0\;,\;B_{1}=V_{DD}\;{\rm corr.}}$$

{\it Put $M_{1}PMOS$, $M_{2}NMOS$ enhancement, $|V_{T}|\ll V_{DD}$}

* {\it Digital operation:}

$$\eqalign{
V_{in}=0&\to V_{GS2}=0<V_{Tn}\;M_{2}{\rm OFF}\cr
&V_{SG1}=V_{DD}>|V_{Tp}|\;M_{1}{\rm ON\;triode}\cr
&I_{D1}=I_{D2}=0\;\;V_{out}=V_{OH}\approx V_{DD}\cr
V_{in}=V_{DD}&\to V_{SG1}=0<|V_{Tp}|\;M_{1}{\rm OFF}\cr
&V_{GS2}=V_{DD}>V_{Tn}\;M_{2}{\rm ON\;triode}\cr
&V_{out}=V_{OL}\approx 0\cr}$$

Truth table

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}
V_{in} & M_{1} & M_{2} & V_{out}\\ \hline
L\simeq 0 & ON & OFF & H\simeq V_{DD}\\
H\simeq V_{DD} & OFF & ON & L\simeq 0\\
\hline
\end{array}\qquad V_{out}= \bar V_{in}$$

Staticaly no DC path $V_{DD}\to 0$ except leakage,
$$P_{stat}\approx I_{leak}V_{DD}\approx 0$$
rail to rail logic swing, $R_{in}\approx \infty $ at
DC.

With long channel square law, $k= k^{\prime}W/L$,
neglecting body effect,

* {\it VTC:} 5 regions, Fig.

{\bf A:} $0\le V_{in}<V_{Tn}$ \;\; $M_{2}$ off, $M_{1}$
triode $V_{out}=V_{DD}$

{\bf B:} $M_{2}$ sat., $M_{1}$ triode

{\bf C:} $M_{2}$ sat., $M_{1}$ sat., high gain

{\bf D:} $M_{2}$ triode, $M_{1}$ sat.

{\bf E:} $V_{in}>V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$ \;\; $M_{1}$ off,
$M_{2}$ triode $V_{out}=0$

Switching threshold defined by $V_{in}=V_{out}=V_{M}$
and $I_{Dn}=|I_{Dp}|$ saturated:

$$k_{n}(V_{M}-V_{Tn})^{2}=k_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{M}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}$$

$$(1+\lambda {\rm corr:})$$

$$V_{M}={\displaystyle V_{Tn}+ \sqrt{k_{p}/k_{n}}\;(V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|)
\over 1+\sqrt{k_{p}/k_{n}} }$$

For matched $k_{n}=k_{p}$, $V_{Tn}=|V_{Tp}|=V_{T}$

$$V_{M}\approx V_{DD}/2$$
$$V_{IL}\approx {1\over 8}\left(3V_{DD}+2V_{T}\right)\;\;
  V_{IH}\approx {1\over 8}\left(5V_{DD}-2V_{T}\right)$$

in first order. So

$$NM_{L}=V_{IL}-V_{OL}\qquad NM_{H}=V_{OH}-V_{IH}\approx
V_{DD}/2-V_{T}$$

large.

Unit gain points $dV_{out}/dV_{in}=-1$ delimit the
transition region {\bf B-C-D}.

* {\it Analog - small signal:}

Bias at $V_{M}$ both saturated, common source with
active load.

$$g_{m}=k(V_{GS}-V_{T})\qquad r_{o}=1/\lambda I_{D}$$

$$\eqalign{
A_{v}&={v_{out}\over v_{in}}=-{g_{m1}+g_{m2}\over g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}
\approx -{g_{m}\over g_{ds}}\approx -30{\rm \;to\;} -80{\rm dB}\cr
R_{in}&\approx \infty\cr
R_{out}&=r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\cr}$$

inverting high gain amplifier, can be used as linear
$CMOS$ inverter amplifier.

Dynamically $C_{L}$ at the output, Fig.,

$$P_{dyn}=C_{L}V_{DD}^{2}f_{clk}+V_{DD}I_{sc}+P_{leak}$$

with short circuit current $I_{sc}$ during {\bf C} when
both conduct,

$$I_{sc,max}\approx {k\over 2}(V_{DD}/2-V_{T})^{2}$$

Rise/fall time first order

$$t_{pLH}\approx 0.69 R_{p}C_{L}\qquad t_{pHL}\approx 0.69 R_{n}C_{L}$$

$$t_{p}={t_{pLH}+t_{pHL}\over 2}\qquad 
R_{p,n}\approx {1\over k_{p,n}(V_{DD}-V_{T})}$$

Equal $t_{pLH}=t_{pHL}$ requires
$(W/L)_{p}\approx \mu_{n}/\mu_{p}\;(W/L)_{n}\approx 2-3\;(W/L)_{n}$.

That is the workhorse of $CMOS$ logic: $NOT$, and
with the same PUN/PDN duality $NAND$, $NOR$, etc., and
the simplest $CMOS$ class $B$ push pull output stage/analog
inverter. Proper layout: $M_{2}$ in $p$-substrate $B= GND$,
$M_{1}$ in $n$-well $B=V_{DD}$, separated to avoid
latch up.

> With the {\it litteral} $B_{1}=V_{out}$ the threshold
> of $M_{1}$ is modulated $V_{Tp}(V_{out})=V_{Tp0}+
> \gamma[\sqrt{2\phi_{F}+V_{DD}-V_{out}}-\sqrt{2\phi_{F}}]$
> and $D_{B1}$ forward biases for low $V_{out}$.
> The circuit will not pull correctly low. Do not connect
> the $PMOS$ bulk to the output.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is with conventional notation the
{\it Complementary MOS PUSH-PULL } {\it static Inverter}
{\tt NOT} gate. In normal drawing

* $M_{2}$ is the $N$ driver, $S_{2}\to {\rm GND}$, $D_{2}\to V_{out}$
* $M_{1}$ is the $P$ load, $S_{1}\to V_{DD}$, $D_{1}\to V_{out}$

$$G_{1}=G_{2}=V_{in}\;\;\;\;D_{1}=D_{2}=V_{out}$$

> {\it Note on the symbol:} As drawn on your figure
> both transistors have the $N$ arrow. With two
> enhancement $N$ MOS the circuit as drawn is
> {\it not} ratioless logic. $V_{in}=0$ leaves
> both devices {\it OFF} and $V_{out}$ floating
> and for $V_{in}=V_{DD}$, $V_{out}=V_{DD}-V_{Tn}$
> on account of the $V_{T}$ drop in the common
> drain $M_{1}$. In $n$ MOS technology $M_{1}$ must
> be a {\it depletion} load, $V_{T1}<0$, with
> $G_{1}$ to $S_{1}$ or to $D_{1}$. The normal
> use today is $M_{1}=p$ MOS, $M_{2}=n$ MOS and the
> arrow of $M_{1}$ is reversed. It is assumed in
> the following.

In $CMOS$ the bulks are to the supplies:
$B_{1}\to V_{DD}$, $B_{2}\to {\rm GND}$ so that the
source - bulk junctions are reverse biased.

Put in saturation for long channel, neglect
modulation:

$$\eqalign{
I_{Dn}&=k_{n}\left(V_{GSn}-V_{Tn}\right)^{2}\;\;V_{GSn}>V_{Tn}\cr
I_{Dp}&=k_{p}\left(V_{SGp}-|V_{Tp}|\right)^{2}\;\;V_{SGp}>|V_{Tp}|\cr}
\qquad k=\tfrac12 \mu C_{ox}W/L$$

$$V_{GSn}=V_{in}\qquad V_{SGp}=V_{DD}-V_{in}$$

$$I_{Dn}=I_{Dp}=I_{D}$$ in D.C. steady state.

#### 1. Logical operation - large signal

| $V_{in}$ | $M_{1}P$ | $M_{2}N$ | $V_{out}$ | $I_{D}$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $0 = GND = {\rm L}$ | $V_{SG}=V_{DD}>\vert V_{Tp}\vert$ ON | $V_{GS}=0<V_{Tn}$ OFF | $\approx V_{DD}= {\rm H}$ through $R_{on,p}$ | $0$ |
| $V_{DD}={\rm H}$ | $V_{SG}=0$ OFF | $V_{GS}=V_{DD}>V_{Tn}$ ON | $\approx 0 ={\rm L}$ through $R_{on,n}$ | $0$ |

$$V_{out}= \bar V_{in}$$

Ideal levels: $V_{OH}=V_{DD}$, $V_{OL}=0$ {\it ratioless}
full swing. Static power $P_{s}=V_{DD}I_{D}\approx 0$
except during transition, only leakage.

In between there is a high gain transition.

#### 2. Voltage transfer characteristic

5 regions for increasing $V_{in}$ $0\to V_{DD}$:

{\bf I:} $0\le V_{in}< V_{Tn}$ : $M_{2}$ cut off,
$M_{1}$ deep triode: $V_{out}=V_{DD}$.

{\bf II:} $V_{in}>V_{Tn}$ : $M_{2}$ saturation,
$M_{1}$ triode. $I_{D}$ rises $\propto (V_{in}-V_{Tn})^{2}$.

{\bf III:} Both saturation: $V_{in}\approx V_{M}$

$$k_{n}(V_{M}-V_{Tn})^{2}=k_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{M}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}$$

$$V_{M}= {V_{Tn}+ \sqrt{k_{p}/k_{n}}\left(V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|\right)
\over 1+\sqrt{k_{p}/k_{n}} }$$

For matched device

$$k_{n}=k_{p}\;\;V_{Tn}=|V_{Tp}|=V_{T}\; \Rightarrow\; V_{M}=V_{DD}/2$$

and

$$-A_{v}= {dV_{out}\over dV_{in}}\approx {g_{m1}+g_{m2}\over g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\gg 1$$

typically 20-50, used as linear amplifier about $V_{M}$.

{\bf IV:} $M_{2}$ triode, $M_{1}$ saturation.

{\bf V:} $V_{in}> V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$ : $M_{1}$ cut off,
$M_{2}$ triode: $V_{out}=0$.

Sketch:

```
Vout
VDD |******
    |      *
    |       *
    |        *
    |         *
    |          *
    |           ******
    +------------------ Vin
    0   VIl  VM  VIh  VDD
```

Noise margins

$$NM_{L}=V_{IL}-V_{OL}\qquad NM_{H}=V_{OH}-V_{IH}$$

$\approx 0.4\,V_{DD}$ for $V_{M}=V_{DD}/2$, maximum.

#### 3. Dynamical

$$P_{dyn}=C_{L}V_{DD}^{2}f + V_{DD}I_{sc}$$

where $C_{L}$ is load capacitance at $V_{out}$ and
$I_{sc}$ is short circuit current in region III.

Propagation delay for $C_{L}$ load, to first order

$$t_{pLH}\approx 0.69R_{p}C_{L}\qquad t_{pHL}\approx 0.69R_{n}C_{L}$$

$$t_{p}= \tfrac12\left(t_{pLH}+t_{pHL}\right)$$

with $R_{n,p}\approx 1/k_{n,p}(V_{DD}-V_{T})$ in triode.

> In short: with $M_{1}=p$, $M_{2}=n$ it is the
> fundamental $CMOS$ inverter, inverting, full swing,
> zero static power, high input impedance, low output
> impedance in both states, high gain in the transition.
> It is the basis of all static $CMOS$ logic and of
> the $CMOS$ analog push-pull OTA inverter amplifier.

If you keep literally the $n-n$ symbol as drawn,
replace $M_{1}$ by a depletion $n$ MOS with
$V_{T1}<0$ to get the classic $n$ MOS inverter
with enhancement driver $M_{2}$ and depletion
load $M_{1}$. Its $VTC$ is ratioed, $V_{OH}<V_{DD}$,
$V_{OL}>0$ and $P_{s}>0$.
