The golden solution explicitly assigns 0 for this topology error.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is the {\it common source stage with
diode connected load} also described as a
{\it pseudo MOS inverter with $P$-active load}.
Sometimes described loosely as a $CMOS$ inverter
with diode connection.

$$\eqalign{
M_{1}&: driver, nMOS, CS, S\equiv GND, {\rm bulk}\equiv GND\cr
M_{2}&: active load, pMOS, G\equiv D , S\equiv V_{DD},
{\rm bulk}\equiv V_{DD}\cr}$$

so that $M_{2}$ is always $S=D$ when it conducts

$${V_{S2}=V_{DD}\atop V_{G2}=V_{D2}=V_{out}} 
\;\;V_{SG2}=V_{DD}-V_{out}\;\;,\;\;V_{SD2}=V_{DD}-V_{out}=V_{SG2}$$

> For a $p$MOS in saturation $V_{SD}\ge V_{SG}+V_{Tp}\;\;V_{Tp}<0$
> $V_{SD}\ge V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|$.
> Hence $V_{SD}=V_{SG}\Rightarrow $ if
> $M_{2}$ is $ON$ it is $SAT$. It is $OFF$ for
> $V_{SG2}<|V_{Tp}|$ i. e. $V_{out}>V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$.

Small signal to $ac$ ground $V_{DD}$ is ground, $M_{2}$
is a one terminal impedance to ground.

{\it Logic function:---} Inverted. $V_{in}=0\Rightarrow V_{out}=
H$, $V_{in}=1\Rightarrow V_{out}=L$.

### 1. Large signal - Voltage Transfer Characteristic

Put $K_{n}=\mu_{n}C_{ox}(W/L)_{1}$ , $K_{p}=\mu_{p}C_{ox}(W/L)_{2}$
$I_{Dn}=K_{n}/2\,(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda_{n}V_{DS})$ in $SAT$,
$I_{Dn}=K_{n}\left[(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})V_{DS}-V_{DS}^{2}/2\right]$ in triode
and similarly for $p$MOS with $V_{SG},V_{SD},|V_{Tp}|$.

$I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{D}$ by KCL.

* {\bf I : $V_{in}<V_{Tn}$ :} $M_{1}$ $OFF$. $I_{D}=0$. 
$V_{SG2}=0\Rightarrow M_{2}$ $OFF$. The output node is
floating in first order. Any leakage to ground pulls
$V_{out}$ down till $M_{2}$ supplies it. In steady state

$$V_{OH}\approx V_{DD}\;\; {\rm ideal}\;\;,V_{OH}=V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|
\;{\rm with\;leakage\;to\;maintain\;}I_{D}>0$$

In most digital hand calculations $V_{OH}=V_{DD}$.

* {\bf II : $V_{Tn}<V_{in}<V_{out}+V_{Tn}$ :} $M_{1}$ $SAT$, $M_{2}$
$SAT$, high gain region

$$ {1\over 2}K_{n}(V_{in}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda_{n}V_{out})
      ={1\over 2}K_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{out}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}(1+\lambda_{p}
        (V_{DD}-V_{out})) \tag{1}$$

Neglecting $\lambda$:

$$V_{out}=V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|-\sqrt{K_{n}/K_{p}}\,(V_{in}-V_{Tn})$$

so $V_{out}$ falls linearly with $V_{in}$ with slope
$\sqrt{K_{n}/K_{p}}$.

The inverter threshold $V_{M}$ defined by
$V_{in}=V_{out}=V_{M}$ in saturation:

$$\sqrt{K_{n}}(V_{M}-V_{Tn})=\sqrt{K_{p}}(V_{DD}-V_{M}-|V_{Tp}|)$$

$$V_{M}={\sqrt{K_{n}/K_{p}}\,V_{Tn}+V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|
        \over 1+\sqrt{K_{n}/K_{p}}} \approx
        {V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|+V_{Tn}\sqrt{(W/L)_{1}\mu_{n}/(W/L)_{2}\mu_{p}}
        \over 1+\sqrt{(W/L)_{1}\mu_{n}/(W/L)_{2}\mu_{p}}}$$

Normally sized for $V_{M}\approx V_{DD}/2$ requires
$K_{n}>K_{p}$ because $|V_{Tp}|\approx V_{Tn}$.

* {\bf III : $V_{in}>V_{out}+V_{Tn}$ :} $M_{1}$ triode, $M_{2}$ $SAT$

$$K_{n}\left[(V_{in}-V_{Tn})V_{out}-{V_{out}^{2}\over 2}\right]
   ={1\over 2}K_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{out}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2} \tag{2}$$

For $V_{in}=V_{DD}$

$$V_{OL}{\rm \;solves\;(2)\;with\;}V_{in}=V_{DD}$$

E. g. neglecting $V_{OL}$ on RHS to first order

$$V_{OL}\approx {K_{p}\over 2K_{n}(V_{DD}-V_{Tn})}
            (V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}\;\;{\rm for}\;V_{OL}\ll V_{DD}$$

Exact quadratic solution of (2) must be used for accurate value.
$V_{OL}>0$, typically $0.1-0.3\,{\rm V}$. 
To make $V_{OL}$ small need $K_{n}\gg K_{p}$,
i.e. $(W/L)_{1}\gg (W/L)_{2}\cdot \mu_{p}/\mu_{n}$.

This gives the familiar inverter VTC with sharp high gain
transition between $V_{OH}\approx V_{DD}$ and $V_{OL}>0$,
asymmetric, with reduced low noise margin.

> Static current $I_{D}>0$ flows whenever $M_{1}$ is $ON$.
> $P_{DC}=V_{DD}I_{D}$ in the $L$ state. This is why the
> complementary $CMOS$ inverter with $G_{2}\equiv V_{in}$
> replaced it for logic.

Conceptually:

```
Vout
 VDD |------------------\
      |                   \
      |                    \
      |                     \  II - high gain
      |                      \
VOL  |_ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _\_________
      0  VTn                VM       VDD Vin
```

### 2. Small signal

$V_{DD}$ is $ac$ ground. Hybrid pi for $M_{1}$: $g_{m1}v_{in}$
from $D$ to $S$, $r_{o1}=1/g_{ds1}=1/\lambda_{n}I_{D}$.
For $M_{2}$ $G\equiv D$, $V_{g2}=v_{out}$:

$$i_{d2}=g_{m2}v_{sg2}+g_{mb2}v_{sb2}+g_{ds2}v_{sd2}$$
$$v_{sg2}=-v_{out}\;\;,v_{sd2}=-v_{out}$$

If bulk $\equiv$ source $v_{sb2}=0$, otherwise
$v_{sb2}=-v_{out}$. Hence $M_{2}$ looks like a conductance to
ground

$$G_{2}=g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2} \approx g_{m2}+g_{ds2}$$

$$Z_{2}= {1\over G_{2}}={1\over g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2}}\approx {1\over g_{m2}}$$

Output resistance at $V_{out}$ node

$$R_{out}=r_{o1}\parallel Z_{2}= {1\over g_{ds1}}\parallel
          {1\over g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2}}
          \approx {1\over g_{m2}} \parallel r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}$$

For $\lambda\approx 0$, $R_{out}\approx 1/g_{m2}$.

Voltage gain:

$$A_{v}={v_{out}\over v_{in}}=-g_{m1}R_{out}
      =-{g_{m1}\over g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}$$

$$\left|A_{v}\right|\approx {g_{m1}\over g_{m2}} 
        = \sqrt{{K_{n}\over K_{p}}}=
          \sqrt{{\mu_{n}(W/L)_{1}\over \mu_{p}(W/L)_{2}}}$$

neglecting $\lambda$ and body effect, independent of bias
current to first order. Including $\lambda$,

$$|A_{v}|={g_{m1}\over g_{m2}+(\lambda_{n}+\lambda_{p})I_{D}}$$

Typically $5$ to $20$ depending on sizing and $L$. Much less
than a current source load $g_{m1}r_{o}$. Including body
effect $|A_{v}|=g_{m1}/(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})$ is even smaller.

Input impedance $Z_{in}\approx \infty$ , capacitive
$C_{gs1}$. Output pole $\omega_{p}=1/R_{out}C_{L}$ where
$C_{L}=C_{db1}+C_{db2}+C_{gd1}+C_{gd2}+C_{wire}$.

This is a Class A inverting amplifier. It inverts phase
$180^{o}$ at low frequency, has moderate gain set by geometry
ratio, limited output swing $V_{OL}$ to $V_{DD}$, finite
static dissipation, and $R_{out}\sim 1/g_{m}$.

It is useful as an analog gain stage, as a load in a
differential pair with diode connected load, for biasing,
and as a textbook active load. As a logic inverter it is the
pre-$CMOS$ ``enhancement load'' or ``diode load'' inverter,
now superseded by the complementary $CMOS$ inverter
$M_{2}$ gate $=V_{in}$ which gives rail to rail swing,
$r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}$ gain and zero static power.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies the common-source NMOS stage with a diode-connected PMOS load and gives the inverting gain as approximately −gm1/gm2. Its channel-length-modulation expression includes both devices’ output conductances; the body-effect nuance does not alter the essential answer.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
It is the prototype of a MOS analog stage,
a $n$ - channel common source - common gate
with {\it active load} - a $p$ channel
load in {\it diode conection} .

$${\cal M}_{1}:n{\rm -MOS}  ~~ g=g(V_{in}),s=0,d=V_{out}$$
$${\cal M}_{2}:p{\rm -MOS} ~~ s=V_{DD},g=d=V_{out}$$

i.e. the normal CMOS inverter with the gate of the
$p$ tied to the output. In analog language the
CS driver loaded by $1/g_{m}$.

$$V_{GS1}=V_{in} \;\; ,V_{DS1}=V_{out}$$
$$V_{SG2}=V_{SD2}=V_{DD}-V_{out}\;\; ,V_{G2}=V_{D2}$$
$$V_{SB1}=0\;\;,V_{SB2}=0$$

No body effect to first order, $p$ well to $GND$
and $n$ well to $V_{DD}$ if twin well process.

For the $p$, $${\rm sat} : V_{SD} \ge V_{SG}+V_{Tp}
= V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|$$ with $V_{Tp}<0$.

But $V_{SD2}=V_{SG2}$, so if it conducts

$$V_{SG2}\ge V_{SG2}-|V_{Tp}|$$

is always satisfied. The $p$ is

* OFF for $V_{SG2}<|V_{Tp}|$, $V_{out}>V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$
* SAT for $V_{SG2}>|V_{Tp}|$, $V_{out}<V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$

For the $n$ $${\rm sat} : V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{Tn}$$

$$V_{out} \ge V_{in}-V_{Tn}\;\;{\rm sat} \qquad 
  V_{out} \le V_{in}-V_{Tn}\;\;{\rm triode}$$

$$V_{in}<V_{Tn}\;\;{\rm cut off}$$

In ordinary first order square law, $\lambda =0$:

$$I_{D1}= \begin{cases}
0 & V_{in}<V_{Tn}\\
k_{n}(V_{in}-V_{Tn})^{2} & V_{in}>V_{Tn}\;{\rm sat}\\
k_{n}\left[ 2(V_{in}-V_{Tn})V_{out}-V_{out}^{2}\right] 
& {\rm triode}
\end{cases}$$

$$k_{n}=\tfrac12\mu_{n}C_{ox}(W/L)_{1}\;\;,
  k_{p}=\tfrac12\mu_{p}C_{ox}(W/L)_{2}$$

$$I_{D2}= \begin{cases}
0 & V_{out}>V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|\\
k_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{out}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2} & V_{out}<V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|
\end{cases}$$

and $I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{D}$ in DC steady state.

* 1. $V_{in}<V_{Tn}$ : ${\cal M}_{1}$ OFF, $I_{D}=0$,
${\cal M}_{2}$ OFF.

Any $V_{out}<V_{DD}$ turns ${\cal M}_{2}$ ON and
charges the output node to $V_{DD}$. Strictly
$I_{D}=0$, $V_{SG2}=0$.

> $$V_{out}=V_{OH}=V_{DD}\tag{a}$$

Neglecting leakage/subthreshold.

* 2. $V_{in}>V_{Tn}$ small so that both SAT:

$$k_{n}(V_{in}-V_{Tn})^{2}=k_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{out}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}$$

> $$V_{out}=V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|-\sqrt{\frac{k_{n}}{k_{p}}}\,
\left(V_{in}-V_{Tn}\right) \tag{b}$$

linear $V_{in}-V_{out}$ characteristic. This is the
useful {\it amplifier} region.

It is valid while $V_{out}\ge V_{in}-V_{Tn}$, i. e.

$$V_{in}\le V_{Tn}+\frac{V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|}
{1+\sqrt{k_{n}/k_{p}}}=V_{I\,sat}$$

At $V_{in}=V_{I\,sat}$ , $V_{out}=V_{I\,sat}-V_{Tn}$.

* 3. $V_{in}>V_{I\,sat}$ : ${\cal M}_{1}$ triode,
${\cal M}_{2}$ sat:

$$k_{n}\left[2(V_{in}-V_{Tn})V_{out}-V_{out}^{2}\right]
      =k_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{out}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}\tag{c}$$

which gives low

$$V_{OL}$$

for $V_{in}=V_{DD}$ as the root of (c). For
$V_{OL}\ll V_{in}-V_{Tn}$,

$$V_{OL}\approx \left(V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|\right)
 \sqrt{\frac{k_{p}}{k_{n}}}\Big/ \sqrt{2(V_{DD}-V_{Tn})}$$

more generally solution of the quadratic in $V_{OL}$.
$V_{OL}>0$, static current $\ne 0$, so poor logic
inverter. The DC voltage transfer curve is

```
Vout
VDD |********
    |        *
    |         \
    |          \  both sat, slope -sqrt(kn/kp)
    |           \
    |            * triode
    |             ******** VOL
    +------------------------ Vin
    0   VTn   VIsat   VDD
```

With $\lambda >0$, $I_{D}=k(V_{GS}-V_{T})^{2}(1+\lambda V_{DS})$,
the slope is rounded and a finite output conductance appears.

Small signal at a bias $Q$ in (b):

$${\cal M}_{1}: g_{m1},g_{ds1}=r_{o1}^{-1}=\lambda_{n}I_{D},
\qquad {\cal M}_{2}: g_{m2},g_{ds2}=r_{o2}^{-1}=\lambda_{p}I_{D}$$

Diode connected : $g_{2}$ tied to $d_{2}$.

$$Z_{2}= \frac{v_{x}}{i_{x}}\Big|_{s_{2}=ac\,gnd} 
      =\frac{1}{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2}}\approx \frac{1}{g_{m2}}$$

If well to source, $g_{mb2}=0$.
At the output node

> $$R_{out}=r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\parallel \frac{1}{g_{m2}+g_{ds2}+g_{mb2}}
      \approx \frac{1}{g_{m2}}\parallel r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\tag{d}$$

Since $g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1$, $R_{out}\approx 1/g_{m2}$,
very low for a CS stage, wide band.

Voltage gain:

> $$A_{v}= \frac{v_{out}}{v_{in}}=-g_{m1}R_{out}
      = -\frac{g_{m1}}{g_{m2}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}+g_{mb2}} \tag{e}$$

$$\approx -\frac{g_{m1}}{g_{m2}} 
      =-\sqrt{\frac{k_{n}}{k_{p}}}\,
        \sqrt{\frac{1+\lambda_{n}V_{out}}{1+\lambda_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{out})}}$$

$$\;A_{v0}\approx -\sqrt{\frac{\mu_{n}(W/L)_{1}}{\mu_{p}(W/L)_{2}}}\;
      =-\sqrt{\frac{(W/L)_{1}}{(W/L)_{2}}}\sqrt{\frac{\mu_{n}}{\mu_{p}}}\;$$

for $\lambda =0$ and $(V_{GS}-V_{T})$ elimination using
$g_{m}=2k(V_{GS}-V_{T})= \sqrt{2\mu C_{ox}(W/L)I_{D}}$.

Typically $|A_{v}|\sim 2-20$ depending on sizing.
To get gain magnitude $>1$ you need
$(W/L)_{1} > (\mu_{p}/\mu_{n})(W/L)_{2}$.
Intrinsic gain $g_{m}r_{o}\sim 20-100$ is killed by the
$1/g_{m}$ load.

Input resistance $\approx \infty$ at low frequency,
$C_{in}=C_{gs1}+(1-A_{v})C_{gd1}$ with Miller.

Frequency response: dominant pole at output

$$\omega_{p}\approx \frac{1}{R_{out}C_{L}} \approx \frac{g_{m2}}{C_{L}}$$

with $C_{L}=C_{db1}+C_{db2}+C_{gd1}+C_{gd2}+C_{ext}$,
so GBW $\approx g_{m1}/C_{L}$.

Remarks:

* Non inverting from $V_{DD}$ - good PSRR is poor.
* Burns static power $I_{D}V_{DD}$ when ${\cal M}_{1}$ is ON.
  Not ratio-less logic like complementary CMOS inverter.
* Used where low gain, low $R_{out}$, large swing to
 $V_{DD}$ on top is wanted and simplicity prevails over
 gain: level shifter, $V_{GS}$ multiplier, wide band
 CS stage, $I$ to $V$ converter, load for differential
 pair when diode connected load differential pair is needed.
 For high gain the load is replaced by a current source
 $r_{o2}$, $A_{v}=-g_{m1}(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})$ or
 cascode.

With body effect if bulk not tied, $g_{mb2}\ne 0$,
$A_{v}=-g_{m1}/(g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2})$ still lower.
The $p$ load is preferred to $n$ diode load precisely
because its $n$-well can be strapped to $V_{DD}$ eliminating
$g_{mb}$.

This is sometimes called NMOS inverter with PMOS
enhancement active load or pseudo-NMOS with saturated load.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies the common-source NMOS with a diode-connected PMOS load and gives the inverting gain, including a consistent form with both devices’ output conductances. This satisfies the golden solution’s full-credit rule; the extra large-signal analysis is not essential.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is the saturation loaded or diode loaded
common source stage

$$M_{1} : N ~{\rm driver}~~~M_{2}: P~ {\rm load,
~~}G_{2}\equiv D_{2}$$

> For small signal often drawn ``upside down''
> $M_{1}$ with $S_{1}=0$, $G_{1}=V_{in}$,$D_{1}=V_{out}$,
> $M_{2}$ with $S_{2}=V_{DD}$, $G_{2}=D_{2}=V_{out}$.
> $n-$well of $M_{2}$ to $V_{DD}$, $p-$sub of $M_{1}$
> to $GND$, so $V_{BS1}=V_{BS2}=0$ if ideal.

It is the CMOS version of the $nMOS$ saturated
enhancement load inverter. It is ratioed, it draws
static current and it is to-day used only as a
wide band small signal amplifier or as the active
resistor load of a differential pair. With normal
notation $K_{n}=k_{n}W_{1}/L_{1}$, $k_{n}=\mu _{n}C_{ox}$,
$K_{p}=k_{p}W_{2}/L_{2}$, $V_{TN}>0$, $V_{TP}=-|V_{TP}|<0$.

In long channel square law, $ \lambda =0$ first order

$$I_{D} = \frac{1}{2}K(V_{GS}-V_{T})^{2} ~~{\rm sat.}$$
$$I_{D} = K\left[(V_{GS}-V_{T})V_{DS}-V_{DS}^{2}/2\right]~~{\rm triode}$$
$$g_{m}=K(V_{GS}-V_{T}) =\sqrt{2KI_{D}}\;\;,\;\;r_{o}=1/g_{ds}=1/\lambda I_{D}$$

For $M_{2}$

$$V_{SG2}=V_{DD}-V_{out}\;\;,\;\;V_{SD2}=V_{DD}-V_{out}=V_{SG2}$$

so that

$$V_{SD2}\ge V_{SG2}+V_{TP}=V_{SG2}-|V_{TP}|\tag{*}$$

is identically satisfied for $|V_{TP}|>0$. {\it The
diode transistor is always saturated when on.}

For $M_{1}$

$$V_{DS1}=V_{out}\;\;,\;\;V_{GS1}=V_{in}$$

saturation:

$$V_{out}\ge V_{in}-V_{TN}\tag{**}$$

### 1. Large signal $V_{TC}$

$I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{D}$.

{\rm I:}$V_{in}<V_{TN}$ : $M_{1}$ off. $I_{D}=0$.
$M_{2}$ can be off with $V_{SG2}<|V_{TP}|$ and the
output node is pulled to the rail

$$V_{out}=V_{DD}\qquad V_{OH}=V_{DD}$$

In this region $M_{2}$ is off or in subthreshold.

{\rm II:}$V_{in}>V_{TN}$ and (**) satisfied: Both saturated.
Neglecting $r_{o}$:

$$\frac12 K_{n}(V_{in}-V_{TN})^{2}= \frac12 K_{p}
\left(V_{DD}-V_{out}-|V_{TP}|\right)^{2}$$

$$\;V_{out}=V_{DD}-|V_{TP}|-\sqrt{\frac{K_{n}}{K_{p}}}\,
\left(V_{in}-V_{TN}\right)\; \tag{1}$$

in saturation. Linear decreasing characteristic with
incremental slope

$$\frac{dV_{out}}{dV_{in}}=-\sqrt{\frac{K_{n}}{K_{p}}}
 =-\sqrt{\frac{\mu_{n}}{\mu_{p}}\frac{(W/L)_{1}}{(W/L)_{2}}}$$

This is already the low frequency large signal
voltage gain. If $K_{n}=K_{p}$ the slope is $-1$.
Normally $\mu_{n}\approx 2-3\mu_{p}$ so with equal
geometry $|A_{v}|\approx 1.5-2$.

With $\lambda \ne 0$

$$K_{n}(V_{in}-V_{TN})^{2}(1+\lambda_{n}V_{out})
 =K_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{out}-|V_{TP}|)^{2}(1+\lambda_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{out}))$$

to first order the same Eq.1.

Region II exists while (**) holds, i.e.

$$V_{DD}-|V_{TP}|-\sqrt{\frac{K_{n}}{K_{p}}}(V_{in}-V_{TN})
 \ge V_{in}-V_{TN}$$

$$V_{in}\le V_{TN}+ \frac{V_{DD}-|V_{TP}|}{1+\sqrt{K_{n}/K_{p}}}=V_{IL}$$

and $V_{in}\ge V_{TN}$.

{\rm III:}$V_{in}$ large, $V_{out}<V_{in}-V_{TN}$ : $M_{1}$
triode, $M_{2}$ saturation.

$$K_{n}\left[(V_{in}-V_{TN})V_{out}-V_{out}^{2}/2\right]
 =\frac12 K_{p}\left(V_{DD}-V_{out}-|V_{TP}|\right)^{2} \tag{2}$$

quadratic in $V_{out}$, $V_{out}$ falling slowly to a
finite

$$V_{OL}>0$$

Solution of (2) for $V_{in}=V_{DD}$ gives the logic
low level. E.G. for $K_{n}=K_{p}$, $V_{DD}=1.8\,{\rm V}$,
$V_{TN}=|V_{TP}|=0.4\,{\rm V}$, $V_{OL}\approx 0.3-0.4\,{\rm V}$.
$V_{OL}$ can be lowered only by making
$K_{n}\gg K_{p}$, i.e. a ratioed inverter.

Hence the familiar $VTC$:

$$V_{DD}\xrightarrow{V_{in}<V_{TN}}{\rm flat}\xrightarrow{\rm II}
{\rm linear\;with\;slope\;-\sqrt{K_{n}/K_{p}}}\xrightarrow{\rm III}
{\rm triode\;tail\;to\;}V_{OL}$$

Maximum swing $V_{OH}-V_{OL}<V_{DD}$, limited on
the low side. No rail to rail operation.

In normal amplifier use the $Q-$point is put in region
II by biasing $V_{in}=V_{BIAS}>V_{TN}$ so that
$I_{D}= {\tfrac12}K_{n}(V_{BIAS}-V_{TN})^{2}$ and
$V_{out}=V_{DD}-|V_{TP}|-\sqrt{K_{n}/K_{p}}(V_{BIAS}-V_{TN})$
in the middle of the allowed $V_{out}$ range.

Power dissipation in the on state

$$P_{DC}=V_{DD}I_{D}$$

### 2. Small signal

Gate input, $R_{in}= \infty $ at low frequency.

For small signal $m_{2}$ has $g_{2}\equiv d_{2}$ so

$$v_{gs2}= -v_{out}\;\;,\;\;v_{ds2}= -v_{out}$$

$$i_{d2}=g_{m2}v_{sg2}+g_{ds2}v_{sd2}= (g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2})v_{out}
\approx (g_{m2}+g_{ds2})v_{out}$$

i.e. the impedance looking into the source of a
diode is $1/(g_{m}+g_{ds}+g_{mb})$. To ground from the
output node the load is

$$Z_{2}= \frac{1}{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2}}\approx \frac{1}{g_{m2}}\;\;,\;\;g_{m2}\gg g_{ds2}$$

The driver $M_{1}$ is a normal $g_{m1}$ stage with
$g_{ds1}$ to ground.

Small signal equivalent at $V_{out}$: current source
$g_{m1}v_{in}$ to ground in parallel with $g_{ds1}$
and $Z_{2}^{-1}$ .

$$v_{out}\left[g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}+g_{m2}+g_{mb2}\right] = -g_{m1}v_{in}$$

$$\;A_{v}\equiv \frac{v_{out}}{v_{in}}=
 -\frac{g_{m1}}{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\;$$

With no body effect $g_{mb}=0$ and

$$A_{v}\approx -\frac{g_{m1}}{g_{m2}}\frac{1}{1+(g_{ds1}+g_{ds2})/g_{m2}}$$

If $r_{o}=\infty$,

$$\;A_{v0}= -\frac{g_{m1}}{g_{m2}}=
 -\sqrt{\frac{K_{n}}{K_{p}}}\,
   \sqrt{\frac{1+\lambda_{n}V_{out}}{1+\lambda_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{out})}}
 \approx -\sqrt{\frac{\mu_{n}(W/L)_{1}}{\mu_{p}(W/L)_{2}}}\;$$

typically $5-10$ with reasonable ratio, $20$ at most
before the swing is killed. Including $r_{o}$

$$|A_{v}| = \frac{g_{m1}}{g_{m2}}\frac{1}{1+\frac{\lambda_{n}+\lambda_{p}}{g_{m2}}I_{D}} < g_{m1}/g_{m2}$$

Output resistance at the output node

$$\;R_{out}= r_{o1}\parallel \frac{1}{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2}}
 \approx \frac{1}{g_{m2}}\parallel r_{o1}\approx \frac{1}{g_{m2}}\;$$

Normally $1/g_{m2}\sim {\rm k\Omega }$.

Input capacitance $C_{gs1}+C_{gd1}(1+|A_{v}|)$ Miller,
output pole

$$p_{out}\approx \frac{1}{R_{out}C_{L}} \approx \frac{g_{m2}}{C_{L}+C_{db1}+C_{db2}+C_{gd1}+C_{gd2}}$$

wide band, low gain stage. Gain $\times$ bandwidth
$\approx g_{m1}/C_{L}$.

In short: inverter with low, ratio dependent gain,
low $R_{out}\approx 1/g_{m2}$, infinite $R_{in}$,
inverting, class A, static power, reduced logic
swing. It can be used as a simple transconductance
to resistance converter.

High gain $\gg 10$ requires replacing the diode by
a true current source $r_{o2}$ load, cascode, or
differential active current mirror load.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies the common-source NMOS stage with a diode-connected PMOS load and gives the inverting gain −gm1/gm2, with both output conductances included in its channel-length-modulation form. The extra body-effect detail does not change the essential result.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
With the 3 electrode convention the arrow
is the source.

$$\eqalign{
M_{2}&:{\rm source} \equiv V_{{\rm DD}}\cr
&:{\rm drain}\equiv V_{o}\cr
&:{\rm gate}\equiv V_{i}\cr
M_{1}&:{\rm source}\equiv V_{o}\cr
&:{\rm drain}\equiv 0\cr
&:{\rm gate}\equiv 0}$$

both $p$ channel.
Put $|V_{T}|=-V_{T}>0$

$$I_{D}^{p}={k_{p}\over 2}(V_{SG}-|V_{T}|)^{2}
\left[1+\lambda V_{SD}\right] $$
triode
$$I_{D}^{p}=k_{p}\left[(V_{SG}-|V_{T}|)V_{SD}-{1\over 2}V_{SD}^{2}
\right]$$
$$k_{p}=\mu _{p}C_{ox}W/L\qquad g_{m}=k_{p}(V_{SG}-|V_{T}|)=
\sqrt{2k_{p}I_{D}}\qquad g_{ds}=\lambda I_{D}=r_{o}^{-1}$$

$${\rm sat:}\;V_{SD}\ge V_{SG}-|V_{T}|\tag{*}$$

For $M_{1}$

$$\eqalign{
V_{SG1}&=V_{S1}-V_{G1}=V_{o}-0=V_{o}\cr
V_{SD1}&=V_{S1}-V_{D1}=V_{o}-0=V_{o}}$$

so that if it is on

$$V_{SD1}=V_{SG1}$$

and {\rm (*)} is $V_{o}\ge V_{o}-|V_{T}|$ always in
saturation :

$$I_{D1}={k_{1}\over 2}(V_{o}-|V_{T1}|)^{2}\;\;V_{o}>|V_{T1}|
\tag{1}$$
$$I_{D1}=0\;\;V_{o}\le |V_{T1}|\tag{1a}$$
cut off.

$$I_{S1}=g_{m1}v_{sg1}+g_{ds1}v_{sd1}+g_{mb1}v_{sb1}$$

With the normal 3 T connection the $n$ well is on the
source $v_{sb1}=0$.  If the well is on $V_{DD}$,
$v_{sb1}=V_{DD}-V_{o}$, $g_{mb1}\ne 0$ and

$$|V_{T1}|=|V_{T0}|+\gamma \left[
\sqrt{2\phi _{F}+V_{SB1}}-\sqrt{2\phi _{F}}\right],\qquad
V_{SB1}=V_{o}-V_{B}$$

In the small signal sense $M_{1}$ is a diode

$$i_{s1}=(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1})v_{o} \approx g_{m1}v_{o}$$

i. e. a resistance to ground

$$R_{1}={1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}}\approx {1\over g_{m1}}
\tag{2}$$

with the body to source $g_{mb1}=0$.

For $M_{2}$

$$\eqalign{
V_{SG2}&=V_{DD}-V_{i}\cr
V_{SD2}&=V_{DD}-V_{o}}$$

saturation {\rm (*)} is

$$V_{DD}-V_{o}\ge V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{T2}|$$

$$V_{o}\le V_{i}+|V_{T2}|\tag{3}$$

$$I_{D2}^{sat}={k_{2}\over 2}(V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{T2}|)^{2}
\tag{4}$$
$$I_{D2}^{tri}=k_{2}\left[(V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{T2}|)(V_{DD}-V_{o})
-{1\over 2}(V_{DD}-V_{o})^{2}\right] \tag{5}$$

The circuit is a ratioed $p$ only inverter, the $p$
common source stage $M_{2}$ loaded by the $p$ diode
$M_{1}$.  The old $p{\rm MOS}$ saturated load
inverter, the $p$ analogue of the $n{\rm MOS}$
enhancement load inverter or of the pseudo $n{\rm MOS}$
inverter.  $KCL$ at the output, neglecting $\lambda $,

$$I_{D2}(V_{i},V_{o})=I_{D1}(V_{o})\tag{6}$$

gives the large signal voltage transfer characteristic.

* $V_{i}>V_{DD}-|V_{T2}|$ : $V_{SG2}<|V_{T}|$, $M_{2}$
cut off, $I_{D2}=0$.  From (1a) $I_{D1}=0$ for
$V_{o}\le |V_{T1}|$.  The output node is high
impedance. In the ideal square law model any
$V_{o}<|V_{T1}|$ satisfies (6). Leakage pulls the
node to ground, in strong inversion analysis

$$V_{OL}\approx |V_{T1}| \tag{7}$$

with body to $V_{DD}$ $V_{OL}=|V_{T1}(V_{OL})|> |V_{T0}|$.
This is the source follower limit of the $p$ load:
a $p$ device with gate at $0$ can pull no lower than
$V_{G}+|V_{T}|$.  The analogue of $V_{OH}=V_{DD}-V_{Tn}$
for the $n{\rm MOS}$ enhancement load inverter.

On raising $V_{DD}-V_{i}$ above $|V_{T2}|$, $M_{2}$
turns on in saturation, (3) satisfied because $V_{o}$
is low.

* Both saturated. From (1) (4)

$${k_{2}\over 2}(V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{T2}|)^{2}=
{k_{1}\over 2}(V_{o}-|V_{T1}|)^{2}$$

$$V_{o}=|V_{T1}|+\sqrt{{k_{2}\over k_{1}}}
\left(V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{T2}|\right)\tag{8}$$

linear $V_{o}(V_{i})$ with incremental slope

$${dV_{o}\over dV_{i}}=-\sqrt{{k_{2}\over k_{1}}}
=-{g_{m2}\over g_{m1}} \tag{9}$$

which is the low frequency small signal voltage gain
with $\lambda =0$.

The both saturated regime ends when (3) is violated,
i. e.

$$V_{o}=V_{i}+|V_{T2}|\tag{10}$$

* $M_{2}$ triode, $M_{1}$ saturated. From (1)(5)

$$k_{2}\left[(V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{T2}|)(V_{DD}-V_{o})
-{1\over 2}(V_{DD}-V_{o})^{2}\right]=
{k_{1}\over 2}(V_{o}-|V_{T1}|)^{2}\tag{11}$$

parabolic $VTC$, gain falling.

For $V_{i}\to 0$, $V_{SG2}=V_{DD}$, $M_{2}$ in deep
triode, $V_{o}$ approaches $V_{DD}$ to within the
drop on $R_{on2}$.  E. {\rm g}. $k_{1}=k_{2}$, $|V_{T1}|
=|V_{T2}|=|V_{T}|$, $y=V_{DD}-|V_{T}|$, $x=V_{DD}-V_{o}$,
(11) gives

$$yx-{1\over 2}x^{2}={1\over 2}(y-x)^{2}$$

$$2x^{2}-4yx+y^{2}=0$$

$$x=y\left(1-{1\over\sqrt{2}}\right)\approx 0.29y$$

$$V_{OH}=V_{DD}-0.29\left(V_{DD}-|V_{T}|\right)
\approx 0.70V_{DD}+0.30|V_{T}|<V_{DD}\tag{12}$$

in general $V_{OH}$ is the solution of (11) for
$V_{i}=V_{IL}\approx 0$.  $V_{OH}\to V_{DD}$ only for
$k_{2}/k_{1}\gg 1$, $R_{on2}\ll R_{1}$.

So the $VTC$ is inverter like, Fig.1, but ratioed
and of very limited swing:

$$|V_{T1}|\le V_{o}\le V_{OH}<V_{DD}$$

the high level is $V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{on2}$, the low level
is the $V_{T}$ drop of the $p$ source follower.
For $k_{1}=k_{2}$ the logic threshold $V_{i}=V_{o}=V_{M}$
from (8) is

$$V_{M}= {V_{DD}+|V_{T1}|-|V_{T2}|\sqrt{k_{2}/k_{1}}
\over 1+\sqrt{k_{2}/k_{1}}}$$

for $|V_{T1}|=|V_{T2}|$ and $k_{1}=k_{2}$, $V_{M}=V_{DD}/2$,
as usual.

> {\it Small signal:}  Ac ground $V_{DD}$.

$M_{2}$: common source, $v_{sg2}=-v_{i}$,
$v_{sd2}=-v_{o}$

$M_{1}$: common gate, source input, gate and drain ac
ground.

Nodal at $v_{o}$:

$$\left(g_{m2}v_{sg2}+g_{ds2}v_{sd2}\right)=
\left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}\right)v_{o}$$

$$-g_{m2}v_{i}-g_{ds2}v_{o}=(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1})v_{o}$$

$$A_{v}\equiv {v_{o}\over v_{i}}=
-{g_{m2}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\tag{13}$$

and with $g_{mb1}=0$ for body to source,

$$A_{v}\approx -{g_{m2}\over g_{m1}}
= -\sqrt{{k_{2}\over k_{1}}}\;
{\sqrt{I_{D2}}\over\sqrt{I_{D1}}}=
-\sqrt{{(W/L)_{2}\over (W/L)_{1}}}$$

at the both saturated bias point $I_{D1}=I_{D2}$.
Neglecting $\lambda $ the magnitude is the square
root of the aspect ratio.  To get gain $>1$,
$(W/L)_{2}>(W/L)_{1}$.  With body effect,
$A_{v}=-g_{m2}/(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})$ reduced $10-30\%$.
Including $r_{o}$,

$$R_{out}=r_{o2}\parallel {1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}}
\approx {1\over g_{m1}}\tag{14}$$

$$R_{in}= \infty ,\;\;C_{in}\approx C_{gs2}+C_{gd2}(1+|A_{v}|)$$

Single pole at the output

$$A_{v}(s)={A_{v0}\over 1+sR_{out}C_{L}}$$

$$\omega _{-3{\rm dB}}={1\over R_{out}C_{L}}
\approx {g_{m1}\over C_{L}}\tag{15}$$

$$GBW = |A_{v0}|\omega _{-3{\rm dB}}\approx g_{m2}/C_{L}$$

Static power

$$P_{DC}=V_{DD}I_{D}\approx {V_{DD}k_{1}\over 2}
(V_{o}-|V_{T1}|)^{2}>0$$

always dissipates in the both on state; class A.
The circuit is therefore obsolete for dense digital
CMOS - it is ratioed, draws static current, has
$|A_{v}|\sim 1-5$ and reduced logic swing and noise
margins - but historically the basic $p{\rm MOS}$
logic inverter and still used as a low gain wideband
transimpedance/active load, level shifter, or as the
load device in a differential pair with $p$ active
load where the $1/g_{m}$ load gives
$A_{d}=g_{m,in}/(g_{m,load}+g_{ds})$.

With $V_{i}$ biased at $V_{M}$ so that both devices
are saturated the circuit is a small signal amplifier
with voltage gain (13), output resistance (14) and
bandwidth (15). Any other bias puts one device in
triode/cut off and the gain collapses.  Cascoding
$M_{1}$ or using a current source load is required
for high gain.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies both devices as PMOS, M2 as the common-source input device, M1 as the diode-connected PMOS load, and derives the gm/gm gain (approximately −gm2/gm1). Extra logic-level discussion does not replace or contradict the essential interpretation.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is a {\it ratioed} $p$-only inverter in
enhancement - saturated load
configuration. i. e. $p$ channel common-source with
$p$ channel diode load.

$$M_{2}: {\rm driver} ~S=V_{DD}{\rm ,\;G}=V_{in}{\rm ,\;D}=V_{out}$$

$$M_{1}: {\rm load} ~S=V_{out}{\rm ,\;D}=0{\rm ,\;G}=0,\;
{\rm diode\; connected\;}G\equiv D$$

Both are $p{\rm MOS}$, $|V_{T}|=-V_{Tp}>0$, 
$k_{p}=\mu _{p}C_{ox}W/L$,
$I_{SD}=(k_{p}/2)(V_{SG}-|V_{T}|)^{2}(1+\lambda V_{SD})$
in saturation. For the symbol as drawn $B\equiv S$
so $V_{SB}=0$, $V_{T}=V_{T0}$, $g_{mb}=0$ on the
signal. If the two devices share the $n$ - well
$B_{1}=V_{DD}$, $V_{SB1}=V_{DD}-V_{out}\ne 0$ and

$$V_{T1}=V_{T0}+\gamma \left(\sqrt{2\phi _{f}+V_{SB}}-
\sqrt{2\phi _{f}}\right) \;\;,g_{mb}\ne 0$$

is to be added.

In 3T language the arrow is the source :

> $M_{2}$ CS device $S_{2}=V_{DD}$ ac ground
> $M_{1}$ CG device $S_{1}=V_{out}$,$G_{1}=$ ac ground,
> $D_{1}=$ ac ground.

So $M_{1}$ looks from its source as a small
non linear resistor.

### 1. Large signal

$$V_{SG1}=V_{out}-0=V_{out}$$
$$V_{SG2}=V_{DD}-V_{in}$$
$$V_{SD1}=V_{out}-0=V_{out}$$
$$V_{SD2}=V_{DD}-V_{out}$$

$p{\rm MOS}$ saturation

$$V_{SD}\ge V_{SG}+V_{Tp}=V_{SG}-|V_{T}|$$

*For $M_{1}$:* $V_{SD1}=V_{SG1}$ so if ON,
$V_{SG1}>|V_{T}|$, it is {\it always saturated},

$$I_{1}={\frac{k_{1}}{2}}(V_{out}-|V_{T1}|)^{2}
\left(1+\lambda _{1}V_{out}\right)\;\;V_{out}>|V_{T}|$$
$$I_{1}=0\;\;V_{out}\le |V_{T}|$$

*For $M_{2}$:* ON for $V_{DD}-V_{in}>|V_{T}|$

SAT for $V_{DD}-V_{out}\ge V_{DD}-V_{in}-|V_{T}|$

$$V_{out}\le V_{in}+|V_{T}|$$

With $I_{1}=I_{2}$ :

* a) $V_{in}>V_{DD}-|V_{T}|$ : $M_{2}$ cut-off.
No dc path except leakage. $M_{1}$ discharges $V_{out}$
until it cuts off:

$$V_{OL}\approx |V_{T1}|\ne 0$$

with $\lambda$ and subthreshold it goes $\to 0$ with
small current. Not rail to rail.

* b) Both saturated, $\lambda =0$ for illustration:

$${\frac{k_{1}}{2}}(V_{out}-|V_{T}|)^{2}=
{\frac{k_{2}}{2}}(V_{DD}-V_{in}-|V_{T}|)^{2}$$

$$\;V_{out}=|V_{T}|+\sqrt{{\frac{k_{2}}{k_{1}}}}
\left(V_{DD}-|V_{T}|-V_{in}\right)\;tag{1}$$

straight line slope

$${\frac{dV_{out}}{dV_{in}}}= -\sqrt{k_{2}/k_{1}}
=-\sqrt{{(W/L)_{2}\over (W/L)_{1}}}$$

Valid to

$$V_{out}=V_{in}+|V_{T}|$$

i. e.

$$V_{in,t}= {\sqrt{k_{2}/k_{1}}\over 1+\sqrt{k_{2}/k_{1}}}
\left(V_{DD}-|V_{T}|\right)$$

* c) $V_{in}<V_{in,t}$ : $M_{2}$ triode, $M_{1}$ sat.

$$I_{2}=k_{2}\left[(V_{SG2}-|V_{T}|)V_{SD2}-V_{SD2}^{2}/2\right]
= I_{1}$$

$V_{out}\to V_{DD}$ and saturates.

$$V_{OH}\approx V_{DD}$$

In practice for $(W/L)_{1}=(W/L)_{2}$ the whole
SAT region is $0<V_{in}<V_{DD}-|V_{T}|$ with
$V_{out}(0)=V_{DD}$, $V_{out}(V_{DD}-|V_{T}|)=|V_{T}|$.
If $(W/L)_{2}>(W/L)_{1}$, the high side clips in
triode to $V_{DD}$. Fig. is normal inverter VTC but
with low $\left|dV_{out}/dV_{in}\right|\approx 1-3$
and $V_{OL}=|V_{T}|$.

It is ratioed logic. The trip point $V_{in}=V_{out}$
from (1)

$$V_{M}= { |V_{T}|(1-\,{\rm ratio}) + {\rm ratio}\,V_{DD}\over
1+{\rm ratio}} \qquad {\rm ratio}=\sqrt{k_{2}/k_{1}}$$

### 2. Small signal ac

$V_{DD}$ ac ground. $R_{i}=\infty $ at the gate.

Hybrid $\pi $: $i_{d}=g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}$,
$g_{m}=k(V_{SG}-|V_{T}|)$ in SAT, $g_{ds}=1/r_{o}=\lambda I_{D}$.

* $M_{2}$ : $v_{gs2}=v_{in}$, $v_{ds2}=v_{out}$,
$v_{bs2}=0$,

$$i_{d2}=g_{m2}v_{in}+g_{ds2}v_{out}\;\;{\rm into\;drain}$$

* $M_{1}$ : $v_{gs1}=-v_{out}$, $v_{ds1}=-v_{out}$,
$v_{bs1}=0$ if $B\equiv S$, $=-v_{out}$ if $B=V_{DD}$,

$$i_{d1}= -g_{m1}v_{out}-g_{mb1}v_{bs1}-g_{ds1}v_{out}$$

KCL at $V_{out}$: $i_{d2}=i_{d1}$ with $i_{s1}=-i_{d1}$,
or $i_{d2}+i_{s1}=0$, gives

$$g_{m2}v_{in}+g_{ds2}v_{out}+ (g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1})v_{out}=0$$

$$A_{v}={v_{out}\over v_{in}}=
- {g_{m2}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\tag{2}$$

With separate well $g_{mb1}=0$:

$$A_{v}\approx -{g_{m2}\over g_{m1}} 
{1\over 1+(g_{ds1}+g_{ds2})/g_{m1}}\approx -{g_{m2}\over g_{m1}}$$

In SAT $g_{m}= \sqrt{2k_{p}I_{D}}$ and $I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{D}$

$$|A_{v}|\approx \sqrt{{k_{2}\over k_{1}}}=
\sqrt{{(W/L)_{2}\over (W/L)_{1}}}$$

in agreement with large signal slope. Can be made $>1$
by $(W/L)_{2}>(W/L)_{1}$ at the expense of area and
static current.

Output resistance is the resistance seen looking into
$S_{1}$ in parallel with $r_{o2}$ :

$$R_{out}=r_{o2}\parallel
{1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}}\approx
{1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\approx {1\over g_{m1}}$$

typically $1-10\,{\rm k\Omega }$, low.
Input capacitance $C_{in}\approx C_{gs2}+C_{gbo}$, output
pole $p_{o}=-1/R_{out}C_{L}$, $GBW\approx g_{m2}/C_{L}$
divided by $g_{m1}R_{out}$.

In words: $M_{2}$ is a $g_{m2}$ voltage to current converter,
$M_{1}$ is a diode load $\approx 1/g_{m1}$ to ground.
$A_{v}=-g_{m2}\times R_{out}$.

Ideal $\lambda =0$, no body effect:

$$A_{v}=-g_{m2}r_{o2}\parallel {1\over g_{m1}}
\approx -{g_{m2}\over g_{m1}}$$

With body effect the gain is reduced to
$-g_{m2}/(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})$.

### 3. Properties

* Inverting, single stage, open loop, no Miller multiplication.
Dominant pole at the output.
* Ratioed, static dissipation $P_{DC}=V_{DD}I_{D}>0$ even
when $V_{in}$ high. Standby current $\approx
(k_{1}/2)(V_{OL}-|V_{T}|)^{2}$ small but non zero.
* Limited swing $ |V_{T}|<V_{out}<V_{DD}$, low noise margin,
low voltage gain $1-10$ typical. Poor $PSRR$.
* Can be used as a very simple $p$-only inverting
amplifier, level shifter, pseudo-$p$MOS inverter,
or as active load for $p$MOS logic where CMOS is not
available. For analog use bias $V_{in}$ in the middle
of region b) so both devices saturated.
* For high gain replace the diode load by a current
source $g_{m}=0$ load: $A_{v}=-g_{m2}(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})$
or by a current mirror. Increase $L_{1}$ to reduce
$g_{ds1}$ and $g_{m1}$.

This is the $p$-channel dual of the classic $n$MOS
enhancement-saturated-load inverter. In modern CMOS
it is normally superseded by the complementary CMOS
inverter/CS stage with $n$MOS driver / $p$MOS load
giving $A_{v}=-g_{m}(r_{on}\parallel r_{op})$ and
rail to rail swing with zero static power.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies both devices as PMOS, M2 as the common-source input device, and M1 as a diode-connected PMOS load with gate and drain grounded. It derives the expected gm/gm gain, approximately Av = -gm2/gm1; the extra inverter framing does not replace or contradict the essential interpretation.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is a {\it ratioed} PMOS only
inverter. In CMOS terminology it is a
$$CS+CG \;\;{\rm stage}\approx CS+{\rm sat.}{\rm Enh.}{\rm load}$$

$$M_{2}: PMOS\; driver,\;\; S\equiv V_{DD},\;D\equiv V_{o},\;G\equiv V_{i},\;B\equiv V_{DD}$$
$$M_{1}: PMOS\; load,\;\; S\equiv B\equiv V_{o},\; D\equiv GND,\;G\equiv GND$$

i. e. a $PMOS$ with $G=D$ {\it diode connected}
between $V_{o}$ and ground, with $B$ strapped to
$S$ so that $V_{BS1}=0$.

> Note on symbolism: The arrow is the $B\to $ channel
junction. In a normal $p$-sub process both $PMOS$ are
in $n$-wells. For $M_{2}$ the well is at the highest
potential $V_{DD}$: $S-B$ short, $D-B$ reverse.
For $M_{1}$ the well must follow $V_{o}$ otherwise the
$p^{+}/n$ junctions would forward bias. I. e. $M_{1}$
needs its own $n$-well. With $B=S=V_{o}$,
$$V_{SB1}=0\;\; , \;\; V_{DB1}=V_{o}>0$$
both junctions reverse for $0<V_{o}<V_{DD}$. 
$g_{mb1}=0$. If you tie $B_{1}$ to $GND$ you get a
forward $S-B$ diode for $V_{o}>0.6{\rm V}$ and a very
large $g_{mb}$.

Neglecting for the moment $\lambda \ne 0$ in square law:

$$I_{D}= \frac12\mu_{p}C_{ox}\frac{W}{L}
\left(V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|\right)^{2}
\left(1+\lambda V_{SD}\right) \;\;V_{SG}>|V_{Tp}|$$
$$0\;\;{\rm else}$$

$$V_{SG1}=V_{S1}-V_{G1}=V_{o}-0=V_{o}$$
$$V_{SD1}=V_{o}-0=V_{o}$$
$$V_{SG2}=V_{DD}-V_{i}$$
$$V_{SD2}=V_{DD}-V_{o}$$

Saturation:

$$PMOS:\;V_{SD}\ge V_{SG}+V_{Tp}=V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|$$

$$M_{1}:V_{o}\ge V_{o}-|V_{Tp}|\;\;{\rm always\;sat.\;if\;ON}$$
$$M_{2}:V_{DD}-V_{o}\ge V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{Tp}|\iff V_{o}\le V_{i}+|V_{Tp}|$$

So for low $V_{o}$ $M_{2}$ is saturated, for high
$V_{o}$ $M_{2}$ goes triode.

### D. C. large signal - $VTC$

$I_{D1}=I_{D2}$ in series.

* $V_{i}\approx V_{DD}:\;V_{SG2}\approx 0<M_{2}$
cut off. No d.c. path to $V_{DD}$. $M_{1}$ discharges
$C_{L}$ to

$$V_{OL}\approx 0\;\;{\rm subthreshold\;leakage\;only}$$

In square law $M_{1}$ also off for $V_{o}<|V_{Tp}|$.

* Decrease $V_{i}$ so $V_{SG2}>|V_{Tp}|$. Both saturated:

$$k_{1}(V_{o}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}\approx k_{2}(V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}$$

$$k_{i}=\mu_{p}C_{ox}W_{i}/L_{i}$$

$$V_{o}\approx |V_{Tp}|+\sqrt{\frac{k_{2}}{k_{1}}}
\left(V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{Tp}|\right)\tag{1}$$

linear inverting. Clipped to $0$ and to the boundary
$V_{o}=V_{i}+|V_{Tp}|$.

* For $V_{i}\ll V_{DD}$ $M_{2}$ triode:

$$k_{1}(V_{o}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}\approx 2k_{2}\left[(V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{Tp}|)
(V_{DD}-V_{o})-\tfrac12(V_{DD}-V_{o})^{2}\right]$$

$$V_{OH}<V_{DD}$$

produced by the divider $M_{2}({\rm triode})/M_{1}({\rm sat})$.
Typical

$$V_{OH}\approx V_{DD}-\Delta,\;\;
\Delta\sim |V_{Tp}| {\rm\;for\;}k_{2}\sim k_{1}$$
and only $\to V_{DD}$ for $k_{2}\gg k_{1}$.
This is the classic ratioed inverter: $V_{OH}$, the
switching threshold $V_{M}$ where $V_{o}=V_{i}$ and
$V_{OL}$ depend on $k_{2}/k_{1}$.

E.g. with $\lambda =0$, $V_{M}$ from (1) with $V_{o}=V_{i}=V_{M}$:

$$V_{M}= \frac{|V_{Tp}|+\sqrt{k_{2}/k_{1}}\,(V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|)}
{1+\sqrt{k_{2}/k_{1}}}$$

$V_{M}\to V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$ for $k_{2}\gg k_{1}$,
$V_{M}\to |V_{Tp}|$ for $k_{2}\ll k_{1}$.
Normally $k_{2}>k_{1}$ to get gain $>1$.

The circuit draws static current

$$I_{DD}=I_{D1}=I_{D2}\approx \frac{k_{1}}{2}(V_{o}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}$$

when $M_{2}$ is on. Unlike CMOS it is {\it not} ratioless
and not rail to rail.

In $NMOS$ terms it is the exact complement of the
$NMOS$ inverter with enhancement saturated load,
$V_{OH}=V_{DD}-V_{Tn}$. Here $V_{OL}\approx 0$,
$V_{OH}=V_{DD}- {\rm drop}$.

### Small signal

Bias at $V_{I}=V_{M}$ both saturated. AC $V_{DD},GND=0$.

$M_{2}:$ common source, $v_{sg2}=-v_{i}$, $v_{sd2}=-v_{o}$

$$i_{d2}=g_{m2}v_{sg2}+g_{ds2}v_{sd2}= -g_{m2}v_{i}-g_{ds2}v_{o}$$

$M_{1}:$ gate and drain ac ground, source $=v_{o}$,
$b=s$ so $v_{bs1}=0$, $v_{sg1}=v_{o}$, $v_{sd1}=v_{o}$

$$i_{d1}=g_{m1}v_{sg1}+g_{ds1}v_{sd1}= (g_{m1}+g_{ds1})v_{o}
\;+\;g_{mb1}v_{bs1}$$

$g_{mb1}=0$ with $B=S$. If $B=GND$ add $g_{mb1}$:

$$i_{d1}=(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1})v_{o}$$

KCL at $v_{o}$: $i_{d2}=i_{d1}$,

$$-g_{m2}v_{i} = \left(g_{m1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}(+g_{mb1})\right)v_{o}$$

$$A_{v}\equiv \frac{v_{o}}{v_{i}}=
-\frac{g_{m2}}{g_{m1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}+g_{mb1}}\tag{2}$$

$$\approx -\frac{g_{m2}}{g_{m1}}\;\;{\rm if}\;g_{m}\gg g_{ds},g_{mb}$$

$$A_{v}\approx -\sqrt{\frac{(W/L)_{2}}{(W/L)_{1}}}$$

because $g_{m}=\sqrt{2\mu_{p}C_{ox}(W/L)I_{D}}$ and
$I_{D1}=I_{D2}$,

$$|A_{v}|\approx \sqrt{k_{2}/k_{1}}$$

To get $|A_{v}|>1$ need $k_{2}>k_{1}$. Typical 3-10
gives $5-10\,{\rm dB}$, much less than
CMOS $-g_{m}(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})$.

Output impedance at $V_{o}$ is $M_{2}$ drain
$\parallel$ impedance looking into $S_{1}$.

For $M_{1}$

$$Z_{s1}= \frac{v_{x}}{i_{x}}=
\frac{1}{g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}}\approx \frac{1}{g_{m1}}$$

With $B=S$, $g_{mb1}=0$:

$$R_{out}= \left(g_{m1}+g_{ds1}\right)^{-1}\parallel r_{o2}
\approx \frac{1}{g_{m1}}\parallel r_{o2}\approx \frac{1}{g_{m1}}$$

for $r_{o2}=1/g_{ds2}\gg 1/g_{m1}$.

Input impedance $Z_{in}\approx 1/sC_{gs2}\to\infty$ at d.c.

Pole at output:

$$\omega_{p}\approx \frac{1}{R_{out}C_{L}}\approx
\frac{g_{m1}}{C_{L}}$$

Input pole $\approx 1/R_{sig}C_{gs2}$, Miller multiplication of
$C_{gd2}$ by $|A_{v}|$.

In words: a very low gain, low $R_{out}$ inverting
stage, class A, with static dissipation. It can be used
as an analog inverting gain cell, as a level shifter,
or historically as a PMOS-only logic inverter before
complementary CMOS, and in modern CMOS as a
pseudo-PMOS load when only PMOS is available or as a
simple $1/g_{m}$ active load for a PMOS CS stage.

Improvements: replace $M_{1}$ by current mirror,
cascode, or use $NMOS$ to make true CMOS inverter
$$A_{v}=-g_{m}(r_{on}\parallel r_{op})$$
rail to rail, no static power, gain 20-40 dB.

If the intent was a normal CMOS inverter $M_{1}$ should be
$NMOS$ with $S=GND$, $D=V_{o}$, $G=GND$? - i.e. with arrow
reversed - then $M_{1}$ as enhancement pull down would be
off and the circuit would be the usual CMOS inverter after
swapping $M_{1}$ type. As drawn it is deliberately PMOS-PMOS.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: It identifies both devices as PMOS, M2 as the common-source input device, and M1 as a diode-connected PMOS load, and derives the required gm/gm gain. These satisfy the golden solution’s full-credit rule.

answers.question: Find Rout in the figure.

answer.text:
With a ${\rm ac}$ short on the $Vb_{i}$
the small signal circuit is, for the $p$ device

$$i_{sd}=g_{m}v_{sg}+g_{mb}v_{sb}+g_{o}v_{sd}\qquad 
g_{o}=r_{o}^{-1}$$

Put $V_{DD}={\rm ac}\;0$ and put a current $I_{x}$
in the $M_{1}$ drain , Fig.1, with a voltage $V_{x}$ .

$$\eqalign{
M_{2}:&V_{sg2}=0\;\;V_{sd2}=-V_{{\rm x}}\cr
&I_{2}=g_{o2}V_{sd2}=-g_{o2}V_{X}\cr
M_{1}:&V_{sg1}=V_{X}\;\;V_{sb1}=V_{X}-{\rm ac}\;V_{B}\cr
&V_{sd1}=V_{X}-V_{x}\cr
&I_{1}=g_{m1}V_{X}+g_{mb1}V_{sb1}+g_{o1}(V_{X}-V_{x})}$$

In the Fig. $B_{1}\equiv X$, {\it i. e.} the $n$ well
of $M_{1}$ is strapped to its source so that in the
Fig. $g_{mb1}=0$.  With the conventional $n$ well to
$V_{DD}$ keep $g_{mb1}$.

At the internal node

$$I_{2}=I_{1}\tag{1}$$

so that

$$-g_{o2}V_{X}=(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{o1})V_{X}-g_{o1}V_{x}$$

$$V_{X}={g_{o1}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{o1}+g_{o2}}V_{x}\tag{2}$$

and

$$\eqalign{
I_{1}&=(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{o1})V_{X}-g_{o1}V_{x}\cr
&= -{g_{o1}g_{o2}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{o1}+g_{o2}}V_{x}}$$

with the conventional sign $I_{1}$ is the
source to drain current, {\it i. e.} $I_{x}=-I_{1}$ for
the current normally taken as entering the output node.
In magnitude

$$|I_{x}|=|I_{1}|={g_{o1}g_{o2}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{o1}+g_{o2}}V_{x}$$

$$\eqalign{
R_{o}&={V_{x}\over |I_{x}|}={g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{o1}+g_{o2}\over 
g_{o1}g_{o2}}\cr
&={1\over g_{o1}}+{1\over g_{o2}}+{g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\over 
g_{o1}g_{o2}}\cr
&=r_{o1}+r_{o2}+(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})r_{o1}r_{o2}\cr
&=r_{o1}+\left[1+(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})r_{o1}\right]r_{o2}\tag{3}}$$

the usual cascode multiplication of the impedance that
is seen in the source of the common gate device.
For the connection of the Fig. $B_{1}=S_{1}$, $g_{mb1}=0$,

$$R_{o}=r_{o1}+r_{o2}+g_{m1}r_{o1}r_{o2}
      =r_{o1}+\left(1+g_{m1}r_{o1}\right)r_{o2}\tag{4}$$

and for $g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1$

$$R_{o}\approx (g_{m1}+g_{mb1})r_{o1}r_{o2}\;\;{\rm with}\;
B_{1}\to V_{DD}\tag{5a}$$

$$R_{o}\approx g_{m1}r_{o1}r_{o2}\;\;{\rm with}\;B_{1}=S_{1}
\;{\rm as\;drawn}\tag{5b}$$

For $M_{1}\equiv M_{2}\equiv M$, $g_{o1}=g_{o2}=g_{o}$,
$r_{o1}=r_{o2}=r_{o}$, $g_{m1}=g_{m}$,

$$R_{o}=2r_{o}+g_{m}r_{o}^{2}\approx g_{m}r_{o}^{2}\tag{6}$$

normally ${\cal O}(1\,{\rm M}\Omega )$, the intrinsic
gain $g_{m}r_{o}$ times the $r_{o}$ of a simple
current source.  With $B_{1}\to V_{DD}$ put
$g_{m}\to g_{m}+g_{mb}$.  Interchanging the
labels $1\rightleftharpoons 2$, {\it i. e.} calling the
cascode device $M_{2}$,

$$R_{o}\approx (g_{m2}+g_{mb2})r_{o1}r_{o2}$$

in the conventional notation.  Any resistance from
$V_{b}{\rm ac}$ to ground is in parallel with (3).

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly treats the devices as PMOS, identifies M1 as the common-gate cascode, and derives Rout = ro1 + ro2 + (gm1 + gmb1)ro1ro2, with the correct approximation. The body-effect discussion is optional.

answers.question: Find Rout in the figure.

answer.text:
With ${\rm ac\; ground}$
on $V_{DD}$ put $v_{x}=0$ on $V_{b1,2}$ and drive the
output, Fig. 1, with $v_{o}$ and let $i_{o}$ be the current
pulled out of the drain of ${\rm M}_{1}$.

$$i_{o}=i_{d1}=i_{d2}\tag {*}$$

in the first order.  Put for the ${\rm p}$ ${\rm MOST}$

$$i_{d}=g_{m}v_{sg}+g_{mb}v_{sb}+g_{os}v_{sd}\qquad 
g_{os}=1/r_{o}\tag{1}$$

for the ${\rm n}$ ${\rm MOST}$

$$i_{d}=g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}+g_{os}v_{ds}\tag{1a}$$

the two are dual.  Put $r_{o1}=1/g_{o1}$, $r_{o2}=1/g_{o2}$.

For ${\rm M}_{2}$

$$v_{sg2}=0\qquad v_{sd2}=v_{x}\tag{2}$$

modulo the body effect of ${\rm M}_{2}$ which is $0$ because
${\rm S}_{2}$ is on ${\rm ac}$ ground,

$$i_{d2}=g_{o2}v_{x}=v_{x}/r_{o2}\tag{3}$$

For ${\rm M}_{1}$ with its source on $x$

$$\eqalign{
v_{sg1}&=v_{x}\cr
v_{sd1}&=v_{x}-v_{o}\cr
v_{sb1}&=v_{x}-v_{b1}\cr} \tag{4}$$

up to the sign, $g_{m}$ is taken positive, so that

$$i_{d1}=g_{m1}v_{sg1}+g_{mb1}v_{sb1}+g_{o1}v_{sd1}\tag{5}$$

i. {\it e.} for the conventional $+$ from
drain to source in an ${\rm n}$ ${\rm MOST}$,

$$\eqalign{
i_{d1}&=-g_{m1}v_{x}-g_{mb1}v_{x}+g_{o1}\left(v_{o}-v_{x}\right)
\;\;{\rm with}\;v_{b}=0\cr
i_{d1}&=-g_{m1}v_{x}+g_{o1}\left(v_{o}-v_{x}\right)
\;\;{\rm with}\;v_{b}=v_{x}\tag{6}}$$

The second is the case drawn in the figure, the $n$ well of
${\rm M}_{1}$ is strapped to its source, $v_{sb1}\equiv 0$,
$g_{mb1}\equiv 0$.  In a normal $n$ well process the well is
on $V_{DD}$, {\it i. e.} on ${\rm ac}$ ground and
$g_{mb1}\ne 0$ and $v_{sb1}= -v_{x}$.  With $*$

$$\eqalign{
i_{o}&=i_{d2}=v_{x}/r_{o2}\cr
i_{o}&=i_{d1}=g_{o1}v_{o}-\left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{o1}\right)v_{x}\cr
&{\rm or}\;g_{o1}v_{o}-\left(g_{m1}+g_{o1}\right)v_{x}\;\;{\rm for}\;
g_{mb1}=0\tag{7}}$$

Eliminating $v_{x}=i_{o}r_{o2}$

$$i_{o}=g_{o1}v_{o}-i_{o}r_{o2}\left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{o1}\right) \tag{8}$$

$${{v_{o}}\over {i_{o}}}=R_{o}=r_{o1}+r_{o2}+\left(g_{m1}+
g_{mb1}\right)r_{o1}r_{o2} \tag{9}$$

$$R_{o}=r_{o1}+\left[1+\left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\right)r_{o1}\right]r_{o2}
\tag{9a}$$

normalised to $g_{mb1}=0$ for the connection drawn,

$$R_{o}=r_{o1}+r_{o2}+g_{m1}r_{o1}r_{o2}
      =r_{o1}+\left(1+g_{m1}r_{o1}\right)r_{o2}\tag{10}$$

For $g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1$

$$R_{o}\approx \left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\right)r_{o1}r_{o2}
\tag{11}$$

and for the strapped well

$$R_{o}\approx g_{m1}r_{o1}r_{o2}\gg r_{o1},r_{o2} \tag{12}$$

the conventional cascode multiplication by the intrinsic gain
$g_{m}r_{o}$ of the cascode device.  E. {\it g.} with
$r_{o}=1/\lambda I_{D}$

$$R_{o}\approx {{g_{m}}\over {\lambda ^{2}I_{D}^{2}}} \tag{13}$$

For matched devices $r_{o1}=r_{o2}=r_{o}$,
$g_{m1}=g_{m}$,

$$R_{o}= \left(2+g_{m}r_{o}\right)r_{o}\approx g_{m}r_{o}^{2}\tag{14}$$

with the body on ground $g_{m}\rightarrow g_{m}+g_{mb}
=(1+\chi )g_{m}$, $\chi =g_{mb}/g_{m}\approx 0.1-0.3$.

In the ideal square law with no channel length modulation
$r_{o}\rightarrow \infty $, $R_{o}\rightarrow \infty $ as it
should for a current source.  Any $R_{L}\ll R_{o}$ to ground at
the output sees essentially the short circuit cascode current
$I_{D1}=I_{D2}$.

> {\it Remark:}  In most text books Eq. {\rm 9a} is quoted in
> the form $R_{o}\approx \left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\right)r_{o1}r_{o2}$.
> For the triple well or {\it p} well with the well of  ${\rm M}_{1}$
> on $X$, $g_{mb1}=0$ as drawn.

The source follower resistance seen looking into the source of
${\rm M}_{1}$ with $r_{o2}$ on its source is
$R_{x}=r_{o2}$ and Eq. 9a is $R_{o}=r_{o1}+(1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})r_{o1})
R_{x}$.  Looking into the source {\it per se},
$R_{s1}=1/(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{o1})\approx 1/(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})$.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Identifies the PMOS cascode action of M1 and gives the correct output resistance, including the optional body-effect term and the usual approximation. The body-connection discussion does not change the essential result.

answers.question: Find Rout in the figure.

answer.text:
With ${\rm  AC\;ground}$ on the two gates, in the
small signal sense the {\it upper} transistor is the
${R_{S}}$ that degenerates the ${\rm CG}$
{\it lower} transistor. Put ${V_{b1}}=V_{b2}=0$ and

$$\eqalign{
r_{oi}&={1\over {g_{dsi}}}={1\over {\lambda _{i}I_{D}}}\cr
g_{oi}&=g_{dsi}\cr}$$

for the normal sign convention,

$${\rm Fig.\;1\over R_{o}}={\rm Fig.\;2}\tag*{Fig.2}$$

Put a $V_{x}$ on the drain of $M_{1}$ and call $V_{s1}=V_{X}$
the ${\rm S}$ of $M_{1}\equiv {\rm D}$ of $M_{2}$.
Neglecting for the moment the well effect

$$I_{d2}=g_{o2}V_{X}\tag{1}$$

$$I_{d1}=g_{m1}V_{gs1}+g_{o1}V_{ds1}
      =-g_{m1}V_{X}+g_{o1}\left(V_{x}-V_{X}\right) \tag{2}$$

and for the current injected in the output

$$I_{x}=I_{d1}\tag{3}$$

$${\rm KCL}\;\;{\rm at}\;\;X:\;\;I_{s1}=I_{d2}\;\;{\rm i.\;e.}\;\;
I_{d1}=I_{d2}\tag{4}$$

so that from (1)(2)

$$g_{o1}V_{x}=V_{X}\left(g_{m1}+g_{o1}+g_{o2}\right) \tag{5}$$

$$V_{X}={{g_{o1}}\over {g_{m1}+g_{o1}+g_{o2}}}V_{x}\tag{6}$$

and e. {\rm g.} from (1) and (3)

$$I_{x}=g_{o2}V_{X}={{g_{o1}g_{o2}}\over
{g_{m1}+g_{o1}+g_{o2}}}V_{x} \tag{7}$$

$${{V_{x}}\over {I_{x}}}={{g_{m1}+g_{o1}+g_{o2}}\over {g_{o1}g_{o2}}} \tag{8}$$

i. e., in $r$'s,

$$R_{o}= {1\over {g_{o}}}\;\;{\rm with}\;\;g_{o}={{g_{o1}g_{o2}}
\over {g_{m1}+g_{o1}+g_{o2}}}$$

$$R_{o}={{1}\over {g_{o1}}}+{{1}\over {g_{o2}}}+
{{g_{m1}}\over {g_{o1}g_{o2}}}\tag{9}$$

$$R_{o}=r_{o1}+r_{o2}+g_{m1}r_{o1}r_{o2}
      =r_{o1}+\left(1+g_{m1}r_{o1}\right)r_{o2}\tag{10}$$

the well known impedance of a ${\rm CG}$ stage degenerated
by $R_{S}=r_{o2}$,

$$R_{o}=R_{S}+\left[1+\left(g_{m}+g_{mb}\right)r_{o}\right]R_{S}
       +r_{o}\tag*{in general}$$

In (9)(10) $g_{m1}$ is the $g_{m}$ of the cascode , i. e.
bottom, device.  With $g_{o}r_{o}=1$ and $g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1$

$$R_{o}\approx g_{m1}r_{o1}r_{o2}\tag{11}$$

For the matched case $r_{o1}\approx r_{o2}=r_{o}$,
$g_{m1}=g_{m}$,

$$R_{o}\approx \left(2+g_{m}r_{o}\right)r_{o}\approx g_{m}r_{o}^{2}
      ={{g_{m}}\over {\left(\lambda I_{D}\right)^{2}}}
      ={{2}\over {\lambda^{2}I_{D}\left(V_{GS}-V_{T}\right)}} \tag{12}$$

normally ${{10}^{5}}-{{10}^{7}}{\rm \Omega }$, to first order
infinity if $\lambda \rightarrow 0$, the ideal cascode current
source.  In ordinary $0.5-0.18\mu$ CMOS
$g_{m}r_{o}\sim 20-100$, so that the cascode increases the
$r_{o}$ of the simple mirror by $1-2$ orders of magnitude.

With the $n$ well normally returned to the most positive
supply the source of $M_{1}$ is not at AC ground for the
substrate and $V_{bs1}=-V_{X}$.  In (2)

$$I_{d1}=g_{m1}V_{gs1}+g_{mb1}V_{bs1}+g_{o1}V_{ds1}$$

$$I_{d1}=-\left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\right)V_{X}+g_{o1}\left(V_{x}-V_{X}\right)$$

so that everywhere

$$g_{m1}\rightarrow g_{m1}+g_{mb1}=g_{m1}\left(1+\eta \right)
      =g_{m1}\left(1+{{\gamma }\over {2\sqrt{2\phi _{F}+V_{SB}}}}\right) \tag{13}$$

and, e. {\rm g.},

$$R_{o}=r_{o1}+r_{o2}+\left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\right)r_{o1}r_{o2}
     =r_{o1}+\left[1+\left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\right)r_{o1}\right]r_{o2}
     \approx \left(g_{m}+g_{mb}\right)r_{o}^{2} \tag{14}$$

for $r_{o1}=r_{o2}$.  $\eta =g_{mb}/g_{m}\approx 0.1-0.3$.
If as drawn the $n$ well of $M_{1}$ is strapped to its source,
$V_{bs1}\equiv 0$, $g_{mb1}\equiv 0$ and (9)-(12) apply as
written.  Interchanging the labels $1\leftrightarrow 2$,

$$R_{o}=r_{o2}+\left[1+\left(g_{m2}+g_{mb2}\right)r_{o2}\right]r_{o1}$$

is the form most often quoted.  Any finite impedance
from the bias lines $V_{b1},V_{b2}$ to ground appears in
parallel with $r_{o2}$ and/or as source degeneration of the
${\rm CG}$ device and rapidly degrades (14).  Put
$R_{b2}=0$ in (14) to first order.

> {\it Remark:}  $g_{m}r_{o}=2V_{A}/(V_{GS}-V_{T})$ with
> $r_{o}=V_{A}/I_{D}$, $g_{m}=2I_{D}/(V_{GS}-V_{T})$ in strong
> inversion saturation, $\propto \sqrt{W/LI_{D}}$.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies M1 as the common-gate cascode and derives Rout = ro1 + ro2 + gm1 ro1 ro2, with the appropriate body-effect extension. This matches the golden result.

answers.question: How do we ensure that M2 is in saturation in the figure?

answer.text:
With the (p) threshold voltage negatively counted the
cascode has only a high $R_{o}$ if {\it both \/} devices
remain, for the normal signal swing of $V_{o}$, in
the pentode region, Fig.1. For the $p$ channel with
$V_{T}<0$:

$${\rm sat}\;\;:\;\;|V_{DS}|>|V_{GS}|-|V_{T}| \tag{*}$$

i. e. $V_{SD}\ge V_{SG}+V_{T}$ , $V_{T}<0$, or

$$V_{D}\le V_{G}-V_{T}\tag{1}$$

$$V_{T}=-|V_{T}| \qquad V_{D}\le V_{G}+|V_{T}|$$

up to the $\gamma$ correction.  Let

$$V_{EB}=V_{SG}=V_{S}-V_{G}>0\qquad 
V_{EC}=V_{SD}=V_{S}-V_{D}>0$$
$$V_{EB}=|V_{T}|+V_{ov}\qquad V_{ov}=\sqrt{2I_{D}/k_{p}}=
V_{EB}+V_{T}>0\tag{2}$$
$$I_{D}={{k_{p}}\over {2}}V_{ov}^{2}\qquad 
k_{p}=k_{p}^{\prime}W/L\tag{3}$$
$$V_{ov}=V_{EC,{\rm sat}}\tag{4}$$
is the saturation - triode limit.  For $M_{2}$

$$\eqalign{
V_{EB2}&=V_{DD}-V_{b2}\cr
V_{EC2}&=V_{DD}-V_{X}} \tag{5}$$

so that (*) is

$$V_{EC2}\ge V_{EB2}+V_{T2}\tag{6}$$

$${\rm i.\,e.}\;\;V_{DD}-V_{X}\ge V_{DD}-V_{b2}+V_{T2}$$

$$V_{X}\le V_{b2}-V_{T2}=V_{b2}+|V_{T2}|\tag{7}$$

and, with $|V_{T}|$,

$$V_{EC2}\ge V_{ov2}\;\;,\;\;V_{DD}-V_{X}\ge V_{ov2}\tag{8}$$

$$V_{X}\le V_{DD}-V_{ov2}\tag{9}$$

The drain of $M_{2}$ is the source of $M_{1}$.  Neglecting
for the moment the $n$ well body effect

$$\eqalign{
V_{EB1}&=V_{X}-V_{b1}=|V_{T1}|+V_{ov1}\cr
V_{EC1}&=V_{X}-V_{o}} \tag{10}$$

so that, in saturation,

$$V_{X}=V_{b1}+|V_{T1}|+V_{ov1}=V_{b1}-V_{T1}+V_{ov1}\tag{11}$$

and for $M_{1}$ itself, (1),

$$V_{o}\le V_{b1}-V_{T1}=V_{b1}+|V_{T1}|\tag{12}$$

$$V_{EC1}=V_{X}-V_{o}\ge V_{ov1}\tag{13}$$

In saturation the voltage on the inter cascode node is
fixed, for a fixed $I_{D}$, by the $V_{b1}$ bias via
(11).  Putting (11) in (7)

$$V_{b1}+|V_{T1}|+V_{ov1}\le V_{b2}+|V_{T2}| \tag{14}$$

for equal, body tied to source, $|V_{T}|$

$$V_{b2}\ge V_{b1}+V_{ov1} \tag{15}$$

$$V_{b2}-V_{b1}\ge \sqrt{{{2I_{D}}\over {k_{p1}}}}\tag{16}$$

In terms of the conventional $V_{DD}$ referred bias

$$V_{EB2}=|V_{T}|+V_{ov2}\;\;,\;\;V_{b2}=V_{DD}-|V_{T}|-V_{ov2}\tag{17}$$

(11) becomes

$$V_{b1}=V_{X}-|V_{T}|-V_{ov1}=V_{DD}-|V_{T}|-V_{ov2}-V_{ov1}\tag{18}$$

so that

$$V_{b1}=V_{b2}-V_{ov1}\tag{19}$$

is the bias for the minimum voltage drop across the
cascode, the ``wide swing'' cascode.  Any $V_{b2}$
higher than (15) by $\Delta V$ just adds $\Delta V$
to the minimum voltage that must be dropped across the
cascode to keep $M_{2}$ pentode.  Any $V_{b2}$ lower
than (15) puts $M_{2}$ in the triode for the current
defined by $V_{b1},(W/L)_{1}$.  Normally $V_{b1,2}$
are generated by a replica bias so that (19) tracks with
process, $I_{D}$ and temperature.

With (12)(13)

$$V_{o}\le V_{b1}+|V_{T1}|\le V_{DD}-V_{ov1}-V_{ov2}\tag{20}$$

i. e. the conventional

$$V_{DD}-V_{o}\ge V_{ov1}+V_{ov2}=V_{EB1}+V_{EB2}+V_{T1}+V_{T2}\tag{21}$$

must be dropped across the cascode to keep {\it both\/}
devices pentode.  If $V_{o}$ is allowed to rise, go
more positive, toward $V_{DD}$ so that (12) fails,
$M_{1}$ goes triode, its $V_{X}$ is pulled up toward
$V_{o}$ toward $V_{DD}$ and (7)(9) fails and $M_{2}$
goes triode as well.  The $R_{o}$ looking into the
drain of $M_{1}$,

$$R_{o}\approx g_{m1}r_{o1}r_{o2}\qquad {\rm sat/sat}\tag{22}$$

$$R_{o}\approx r_{o1}\qquad {\rm sat/triode}\tag{23}$$

collapses.

In the usual form $V_{T1}$ is increased by body effect
if the $n$ well is common to $V_{DD}$,

$$|V_{T1}|=|V_{T0}|+\gamma \left[
\sqrt{2\phi _{F}+V_{SB1}}-\sqrt{2\phi _{F}}\right]\tag{24}$$

$$V_{SB1}=V_{SB1}=V_{B}-V_{S1}=V_{DD}-V_{X}>0\tag{25}$$

normally quoted as $V_{S1}-V_{B}<0$, and (14)(20) become

$$V_{X}\le V_{b2}+|V_{T0}|$$
$$V_{X}=V_{b1}+|V_{T1}(V_{X})|+V_{ov1}\tag{26}$$

solved iteratively, normally $\Delta |V_{T}|\sim 0.1-0.3\,{\rm V}$.
With separate $n$ wells, Fig.1 as drawn, $V_{SB}=0$.

> {\it Remark:} For the $n$ channel dual interchange
> $V_{DD}\leftrightarrow Gnd$, $V_{b}\to V_{b}$ positive
> with respect to $Gnd$, $|V_{T}|\to V_{T}$, $V_{X}\ge
> V_{b2}-V_{T}$, $V_{o}\ge V_{b1}-V_{T}$, $V_{o}\ge
> V_{ov1}+V_{ov2}$, $V_{b2}\le V_{b1}-V_{ov1}$, etc.

The conventional wide swing replica bias is e.{\rm g}. a
diode connected $p$ device $(W/L)_{2}$ carrying $I_{D}$
generating (17) and a source follower level shift of
$V_{ov1}+|V_{T1}|$ to generate (18).  Any bias with
(15) satisfied and with $V_{o}$ constrained by (20) will
keep $M_{2}$, and $M_{1}$, pentode and the output
impedance high.  Making $(W/L)_{1,2}$ large, $V_{ov1,2}
\sim 100-200\,{\rm mV}$, minimises the headroom (21)
required to keep the cascode pentode.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly gives M2’s PMOS saturation condition and relates the interstage voltage to Vb1 through M1, yielding Vb2 − Vb1 ≥ M1’s overdrive for equal thresholds.

answers.question: How do we ensure that M2 is in saturation in the figure?

answer.text:
For a ${\rm p}$ channel

$$V_{SG}> \vert V_{T}\vert \tag {on}$$
$$V_{SD}\ge V_{SD{\rm sat}}=V_{SG}-\vert V_{T}\vert \tag {sat.}$$
with $V_{T}<0$.
With the sign as in the figure , the conventional
$n$ channel $V_{DS{\rm sat}}=V_{GS}-V_{TN}$
becomes with $1\to 2$ , $D\to S$

$$V_{{D_{2}}}\le V_{{G_{2}}}-V_{T}\tag *$$

For $M_{2}$

$$\eqalign{
V_{S_{2}}&=V_{DD}\cr
V_{G_{2}}&=V_{b2}\cr
V_{D_{2}}&=V_{X}}$$

$$V_{SD_{2}}=V_{DD}-V_{X}\tag1$$
$$V_{SG_{2}}=V_{DD}-V_{b2}\tag2$$

so that at the edge of saturation

$$V_{SD_{2}{\rm sat}}=V_{SG_{2}}-\vert V_{Tp2}\vert \tag3$$

$$V_{DD}-V_{X}\ge V_{DD}-V_{b2}-\vert V_{Tp2}\vert $$

$${{V_{X}\le V_{b2}+\vert V_{Tp2}\vert =V_{b2}-V_{Tp2}}}\tag4$$

in the conventional $V_{Tp}<0$ notation $V_{X}\le V_{b2}
-V_{Tp2}$.
With $\vert V_{Tp}\vert +V_{ov}=V_{SG}$

$$V_{X}\le V_{DD}-V_{ov2}\tag{4a}$$

i. e. the drain of $M_{2}$ must be at least one
overdrive below $V_{DD}$.
That voltage is the source voltage of $M_{1}$.

If $M_{1}$ itself is on

$$V_{X}=V_{S_{1}}=V_{b1}+V_{SG_{1}}=V_{b1}+\vert V_{Tp1}\vert
+V_{ov1}\tag5$$

$$\vert V_{Tp1}\vert +V_{ov1}= \vert V_{Tp1}\vert +
\sqrt{{2I_{D}\over {\mu _{p}C_{ox}(W/L)_{1}}}} \tag6$$

with the body effect

$$\vert V_{Tp1}\vert =\vert V_{Tp0}\vert
+\gamma \left[\sqrt{2\phi _{F}+V_{SB_{1}}}-\sqrt{2\phi _{F}}\right]
\qquad V_{SB_{1}}=V_{X}-V_{DD}$$

if the $n$ well of $M_{1}$ is common with $M_{2}$.
If you put $M_{1}$ in its own $n$ well and strap the well
to $X$, $V_{SB_{1}}=0$ and $\vert V_{Tp1}\vert =\vert V_{Tp2}
\vert =\vert V_{Tp0}\vert $.

Putting (5) in (4)

$$V_{b1}+\vert V_{Tp1}\vert +V_{ov1}\le V_{b2}+\vert V_{Tp2}\vert $$

$${{V_{b2}\ge V_{b1}+V_{ov1}+\vert V_{Tp1}\vert -\vert V_{Tp2}\vert }}\tag7$$

With no body effect and $\vert V_{Tp1}\vert =\vert V_{Tp2}\vert$,

$${{V_{b2}\ge V_{b1}+V_{ov1}}}\tag{7a}$$

$${{V_{b1}\le V_{b2}-V_{ov1}}}\tag{7b}$$

$${{V_{b1}\le V_{DD}-\vert V_{Tp}\vert -V_{ov2}-V_{ov1}}}\tag{7c}$$

when $V_{b2}$ is normally set to put $M_{2}$ itself about
saturated

$$V_{b2}=V_{DD}-\vert V_{Tp2}\vert -V_{ov2}\tag8$$

i. e. $V_{b2}$ is about one overdrive voltage {\it above}
$V_{b1}$. In normal design $V_{ov}\approx 0.1-0.3{\rm V}$ so

$$V_{b2}\approx V_{b1}+0.15\pm 0.1{\rm V}$$

with $50-100{\rm mV}$ of margin left for $PVT$.

At the optimum high swing bias $M_{2}$ is left at the
edge of saturation so

$$\eqalign{
V_{X}&=V_{DD}-V_{ov2}=V_{b2}+\vert V_{T}\vert \cr
V_{b1}&=V_{X}-\vert V_{T}\vert -V_{ov1}=V_{b2}-V_{ov1}}$$

Any $V_{X}>V_{b2}+\vert V_{T}\vert $ puts $M_{2}$ in the triode
and the impedance looking into the drain of $M_{1}$

$$R_{out}\approx g_{m1}r_{o1}r_{o2}\;\;{\rm sat/sat}$$

collapses to $\approx r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}$.

In practice $V_{b1},V_{b2}$ are made to track (7) by
generating them from a replica bias branch that carries
the same $I_{D}$ : a diode connected $M_{2R}\equiv M_{2}$
gives (8) and a level shift of $V_{ov1}+ \Delta V_{T}$
{\it down} from $V_{b2}$, normally a $M_{1R}\equiv M_{1}$
diode or a source follower, gives (7) over corners.

> {\it Remark:} For $M_{1}$ itself to stay saturated
> $$V_{SD_{1}}\ge V_{SG_{1}}-\vert V_{Tp1}\vert $$
> $$V_{X}-V_{out}\ge V_{X}-V_{b1}-\vert V_{Tp1}\vert $$
> $$V_{out}\le V_{b1}+\vert V_{Tp1}\vert  \tag9$$
> so the allowable swing at the output is (9).  Keeping
> (9) satisfied keeps $V_{X}$ given by (5) essentially
> constant and (4) satisfied.  Going beyond (9) pushes
> $M_{1}$ into triode, $V_{X}$ is pulled up to $V_{out}$
> and $M_{2}$ goes triode as well.

With body effect (7) becomes

$$V_{b2}\ge V_{b1}+ \Delta \vert V_{T}\vert _{body}+V_{ov1}$$

which can be $0.3-0.4{\rm V}$.  It is customary to remove
it by putting $M_{1}$ in a separate $n$ well tied to $X$,
or to allow for it by increasing $V_{b2}-V_{b1}$ or by
making $(W/L)_{2}> (W/L)_{1}$ i. e. $V_{ov2}<V_{ov1}$.

With normal $0.18\mu $ numbers $V_{DD}=1.8$,
$\vert V_{Tp}\vert \approx 0.4$, $V_{ov}\approx 0.2$,

$$\eqalign{
V_{b2}&\approx 1.2{\rm V}\cr
V_{X\,{\rm max}}&\approx 1.6{\rm V}\cr
V_{b1\,{\rm max}}&\approx 1.0{\rm V}\cr
V_{out\,{\rm max}}&\approx 1.4{\rm V}}$$

Any $V_{b1}$ lower than that lowers $V_{X}$ and helps
(4) at the expense of $W_{1}$ for the same $V_{ov1}$.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies both devices as PMOS, gives M2’s saturation condition, and relates VX to Vb1 to derive the required bias inequality. Extra body-effect discussion does not alter the essential result.

answers.question: How do we ensure that M2 is in saturation in the figure?

answer.text:
For a $P$ the pinch off is at the $D$ end

$$\left |V_{SD}\right| > \left |V_{SG}\right|-
\left |V_{Tp}\right| \tag{*}$$

$V_{Tp}<0$.  With $\left |V_{T}\right|=-V_{Tp}$
and overdrive $V_{ov}=V_{SG}-\left |V_{T}\right|>0$

$$\eqalign{
V_{SG} &=V_{S}-V_{G} \cr
V_{SD} &=V_{S}-V_{D}\cr
V_{ov} &=V_{SD{sat}}}$$

$(*)$ is $V_{SD}\ge V_{ov}$ .

Put $D\equiv X$ for $M_{2}$.

$$\eqalign{
S_{2}&=V_{DD}\cr
G_{2}&=V_{b2}\cr
D_{2}&=V_{X}\cr
V_{SG2}&=V_{DD}-V_{b2}\cr
V_{SD2}&=V_{DD}-V_{X}}$$

$$V_{SD2}\ge V_{SG2}-\left |V_{T2}\right| \tag {1}$$

$$V_{DD}-V_{X}\ge V_{DD}-V_{b2}-\left |V_{T2}\right|$$

$$\;V_{X}\le V_{b2}+\left |V_{T2}\right|\; \tag{2}$$

in $N{\rm MOS}$ notation $V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{T}$,
for the $P$, $V_{DS}\le V_{GS}-V_{Tp}$, $V_{Tp}<0$,
$V_{X}\le V_{b2}-V_{Tp}$.

In words: keep the drain of $M_{2}$ at least
a $V_{ov2}=V_{SG2}-\left |V_{T2}\right|$ below $V_{DD}$,
i. {\it e.} at least $V_{SD{sat2}}$ of headroom on
$M_{2}$.

$$V_{DD}-V_{X}\ge V_{ov2}$$

at pinch off

$$V_{X{sat}}=V_{DD}-V_{ov2}=V_{b2}+\left |V_{T2}\right|
      =V_{b2}-V_{T2}$$

$V_{b2}$ must be low enough to turn the $P$ on,
$V_{SG2}>\left |V_{T2}\right|$, i. e. $V_{b2}<V_{DD}-
\left |V_{T2}\right|$, but high enough to satisfy
(2). The normal way to write (2) is in terms of the
$V_{X}$ imposed by $M_{1}$.

If $M_{1}$ is itself saturated

$$\eqalign{
V_{S1}&=V_{X}\cr
V_{G1}&=V_{b1}\cr
V_{D1}&=V_{o}\cr
V_{SG1}&=V_{X}-V_{b1}= \left |V_{T1}\right|+V_{ov1}\cr
V_{SD1}&=V_{X}-V_{o}\ge V_{ov1}\cr
V_{o}&\le V_{b1}+\left |V_{T1}\right|}$$

is the compliance for the cascode.  Neglecting
$\lambda $,

$$I_{D}= {\tfrac12}\mu_{p}C_{ox}{\left({W\over L}\right)}_{1}
        V_{ov1}^{2}= {\tfrac12}\mu_{p}C_{ox}{\left({W\over L}\right)}_{2}V_{ov2}^{2}$$

$$V_{X}=V_{b1}+V_{SG1}=V_{b1}+\left |V_{T1}\right|+V_{ov1}
      =V_{b1}+\left |V_{T1}\right|+
        \sqrt{{2I_{D}\over \mu_{p}C_{ox}(W/L)_{1}}} \tag{3}$$

in (2):

$$V_{b1}+\left |V_{T1}\right|+V_{ov1}\le V_{b2}+
      \left |V_{T2}\right| \tag{4}$$

For the normal $n-$well process the $n-$well of $M_{2}$
is $V_{DD}$, the $n-$well of $M_{1}$ is $V_{X}$ if the
well is strapped to the source, so $\left |V_{T1}\right|
=\left |V_{T2}\right|=\left |V_{T}\right|$ and $V_{SB}=0$.
Then (4) is

$$\;V_{b2}\ge V_{b1}+V_{ov1}\; \tag{5}$$

with $50-150\,{\rm mV}$ of margin over $PVT$.
More generally with the well of $M_{1}$ to $V_{DD}$

$$\left |V_{T1}\right|=\left |V_{T0}\right|+
      \gamma\left(\sqrt{2\phi_{F}+V_{DD}-V_{X}}-
                  \sqrt{2\phi_{F}}\right)>\left |V_{T2}\right|$$

and (4) is $V_{b2}\ge V_{b1}+V_{ov1}+
\left |V_{T1}\right|-\left |V_{T2}\right|$.

So you cannot normally put $V_{b1}=V_{b2}$.  With
$V_{b1}=V_{b2}$ (4) would require $V_{ov1}\le 0$.
You make the cascode {\it wide swing} by level
shifting $V_{b2}$ {\it up} - for a $P$ closer to
$V_{DD}$ - by one $V_{ov}$ from $V_{b1}$.

At the edge of saturation

$$\eqalign{
V_{b2{sat}} &= V_{X{sat}}-\left |V_{T2}\right|
            = V_{DD}-V_{ov2}-\left |V_{T2}\right|\cr
V_{b1{sat}} &= V_{X{sat}}-\left |V_{T1}\right|-V_{ov1}
            = V_{DD}-V_{ov1}-V_{ov2}-\left |V_{T1}\right|\cr
V_{b2{sat}}-V_{b1{sat}} &= V_{ov1}+\left |V_{T1}\right|-
                         \left |V_{T2}\right|}$$

E. {\it g.} for $\left |V_{T}\right|\approx 0.4-0.5\,{\rm V}$,
$V_{ov}\approx 0.15-0.25\,{\rm V}$,

$$V_{b2}\approx V_{DD}-\left |V_{T}\right|-V_{ov2}$$
$$V_{b1}\approx V_{DD}-\left |V_{T}\right|-V_{ov1}-V_{ov2}$$
$$V_{X}\approx V_{DD}-V_{ov2}$$
$$V_{o{max}}\approx V_{b1}+\left |V_{T}\right|
            \approx V_{DD}-V_{ov1}-V_{ov2}$$

and $V_{X}\approx V_{b2}+\left |V_{T}\right|-{\rm margin}$.

In practice $V_{b1},V_{b2}$ are generated from a replica
bias branch carrying the same $I_{D}$ : a diode connected
$P$ for $V_{b2}$ and a diode connected $P$ in series with
a $V_{ov1}$ level shift - a source follower or a large
$W/L$ diode - to generate $V_{b1}=V_{b2}-V_{ov1}-{\rm margin}$
or vice versa.  Any bias that satisfies (1)-(5) with
$\sim 100\,{\rm mV}$ margin will keep $M_{2}$ saturated,
and with (1) satisfied

$$R_{out}\approx g_{m1}r_{o1}r_{o2}\parallel r_{o1}\approx
g_{m1}r_{o1}r_{o2}$$

otherwise $R_{out}\approx r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2{\rm ,triode}}$.

> {\it Remark:} Interchanging the labels $M_{1},M_{2}$
> the usual statement is: the cascode gate must be
> $V_{ov}$ {\it above} - less $V_{SG}$ - than the
> current source gate for a $P$ cascode, $V_{ov}$
> {\it below} for an $N$ cascode.  Making $(W/L)_{2}
> \gg (W/L)_{1}$ makes $V_{ov2}\ll V_{ov1}$ and lets you
> tie the gates together at the price of area and
> capacitance.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is a {\it single ended telescopic NMOS cascode}
with active load, the most common high gain cell in CMOS.

$$M_{1}: Common~Source~input~{\rm device} - {\rm transconductor}$$
$$M_{2}: Common~Gate~cascode~device - {\rm current~buffer}$$
$$I_{1}: DC~bias~and~AC~load.\; r_{o3}= 1/\lambda_{p}I_{1}\; if\; PMOS$$
$$V_{b1}: DC\; bias\; to\; keep\; M_{2}\; {\rm on\;and\;saturated}$$

If $I_{1}$ ideal $R_{o3}= \infty$. In practice
$R_{o3}$ is in parallel with the impedance looking into $M_{2}$.

> Bias $I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{1}$ in normal amplifier mode.

### 1. Large signal - DC operation

For $V_{in}<V_{Tn}$ :

$$M_{1}\; OFF\; , I_{D1}=0$$

No DC path for $I_{1}$. Ideal circuit charges $V_{out}\to V_{DD}-V_{I_{1},sat}$. In reality $M_{2}$ goes deep triode to try to sink $I_{1}$.

For $V_{in}>V_{Tn}$ in saturation:

$$I_{D1}= \frac{1}{2}\mu_{n}C_{ox}\left(\frac{W}{L}\right)_{1}(V_{in}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda_{n}V_{X}) $$
$$I_{D2}=I_{D1}=I_{1}\; {\rm fixed}$$

So the transfer $V_{out}$ vs $V_{in}$ is very steep once $M_{1}$ turns on.
In saturation $V_{in}$ controls $V_{X}$ only logarithmically, the cascode
imposes $V_{X}$:

$$V_{X}=V_{b1}-V_{GS2}$$

$$V_{GS2}=V_{Tn}+V_{ov2}=V_{Tn}+\sqrt{2I_{1}/\mu_{n}C_{ox}(W/L)_{2}}$$

Conditions for saturation:

$$\left. {\rm M_{1}\;sat}: V_{X} \ge V_{GS1}-V_{Tn}=V_{ov1}\right.$$
$$\left. {\rm M_{2}\;sat}: V_{DS2}=V_{out}-V_{X} \ge V_{ov2}\right.$$

Hence

$$V_{b1}=V_{X}+V_{GS2}\ge V_{ov1}+V_{GS2}=V_{Tn}+V_{ov1}+V_{ov2}$$

Normal choice $V_{b1}=V_{Tn}+1.5\,to\,2\,V_{ov}$ with margin.
Minimum permittable output:

$$V_{out,min}=V_{X}+V_{ov2}=V_{ov1}+V_{ov2}$$

Maximum permittable output:

$$V_{out,max}=V_{DD}-V_{ov3}$$

where $V_{ov3}$ is the saturation voltage of the $I_{1}$ PMOS source.
Swing $=V_{DD}-V_{ov1}-V_{ov2}-V_{ov3}$. Main disadvantage of telescopic 
cascode: stack of 3 $V_{ov}$.

Small signal $M_{1}$ and $M_{2}$ must remain saturated for amplification.

### 2. Small signal model

Gate of $M_{2}$ AC ground, source of $M_{1}$ AC ground.
Let $g_{m1},r_{o1}$ ; $g_{m2},r_{o2}$ ; $R_{o3}=r_{o,I1}$.

With body effect for $M_{2}$: $g_{m2}\to g_{m2}'=g_{m2}+g_{mb2}$ if bulk is to
GND. If as drawn $M_{2}$ is in its own $p$-well with bulk tied to source
$X$, $g_{mb2}=0$.

Node $X$:

$$R_{X}\approx \frac{1}{g_{m2}'+r_{o1}^{-1}+r_{o2}^{-1}}\approx \frac{1}{g_{m2}'}\parallel r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2} \approx 1/g_{m2}'$$

$$A_{v,X}= \frac{v_{x}}{v_{in}} = -\frac{g_{m1}}{g_{m2}'+r_{o1}^{-1}+r_{o2}^{-1}}\approx -\frac{g_{m1}}{g_{m2}'}\approx -1$$

for matched devices. So $M_{1}$ sees a low gain load $\approx 1/g_{m2}$.

That kills Miller multiplication of $C_{gd1}$:

$$C_{in}\approx C_{gs1}+C_{gd1}(1-A_{v,X})\approx C_{gs1}+2C_{gd1}$$

instead of $C_{gs1}+ (1+g_{m1}r_{o1})C_{gd1}$ for a simple $CS$.

Output impedance looking into drain of $M_{2}$ with source degenerated
by $r_{o1}$:

Put $v_{in}=0$, apply $v_{x}$ at output, measure $i_{x}$.

$$\begin{aligned}
R_{o,cas} &= r_{o2} + \left(1+g_{m2}'r_{o2}\right)r_{o1} \\
&\approx g_{m2}'r_{o2}r_{o1} \gg r_{o1},r_{o2}
\end{aligned}$$

Total output resistance:

$$R_{out}=R_{o,cas}\parallel R_{o3} \approx g_{m2}'r_{o2}r_{o1}\parallel r_{o3}$$

If $I_{1}$ ideal $\;R_{out}\approx g_{m2}'r_{o2}r_{o1}$.

Voltage gain:

$$A_{v}= \frac{v_{out}}{v_{in}} = -G_{m}R_{out}$$

Effective transconductance $G_{m}\approx g_{m1}\frac{R_{o3}}{R_{o3}+R_{o,cas}}\approx g_{m1}$ when $R_{o,cas}<R_{o3}$, otherwise $G_{m}r_{o3}$ limited.

Hence ideal:

$$A_{v}\approx -g_{m1}\left(g_{m2}'r_{o2}r_{o1}\parallel R_{o3}\right)$$

$$\left|A_{v}\right|\approx g_{m1}g_{m2}'r_{o1}r_{o2}\; {\rm for\; ideal\; load}$$

$x\, g_{m}r_{o}$ larger than simple $CS$ stage $A_{v0}=-g_{m1}(r_{o1}\parallel R_{o3})$.

Example: $g_{m}=1mS$, $r_{o}=100k$ $\to |A_{v0}|=50$, $|A_{v,cas}|= 10^{4}\approx 80dB$.

$$Z_{in}\approx \infty \;at\; low\; frequency\; \left(C_{gs1}\right)$$
$$Z_{out}=R_{out}$$

Isolation is excellent, reverse transmission $C_{gd2}$ small.

### 3. Frequency response

Two poles:

P1 dominant at output:

$$\omega_{p,out}= \frac{1}{R_{out}C_{L}}\;,\;C_{L}=C_{db2}+C_{gd2}+C_{o3}+C_{load}$$

P2 non dominant at cascode node $X$:

$$\omega_{p,X}\approx \frac{g_{m2}'}{C_{X}}\;,\;C_{X}=C_{gs2}+C_{sb2}+C_{gd1}+C_{db1}+C_{db2?}$$

$$\omega_{p,X}\gg \omega_{p,out}$$

because $R_{X}\approx 1/g_{m2}'$ is small. The cascode pushes the internal
pole to very high frequency giving much larger bandwidth and $GBW\approx g_{m1}/C_{L}$ compared to $CS$ with Miller pole.

Zero due to $C_{gd2}$ at $\approx g_{m2}'/C_{gd2}$ usually beyond $f_{T}$.

Bandwidth: $\omega_{-3dB}= \omega_{p,out}$, $GBW = |A_{v}|\omega_{p,out}=g_{m1}/C_{L}$

Slew rate $SR = I_{1}/C_{L}$.

### 4. Other properties

* Noise: Input referred noise dominated by $M_{1}$, $M_{2}$ contribution
divided by $g_{m1}^{2}$, negligible: $\overline{v_{n}^{2}}\approx 8kT/3g_{m1}$

* PSRR: Sensitive to $V_{DD}$ via $R_{o3}$.

* Gain boosting / regulated cascode can raise $R_{out}$ to $\sim g_{m}^{2}r_{o}^{3}$ by
adding auxiliary amplifier $A_{aux}$ to gate of $M_{2}$.

In short: high $R_{out}$, high $A_{v}$, wide band, low Miller effect, but
limited output swing and headroom, requiring $V_{DD}>V_{ov1}+V_{ov2}+V_{ov3}$,
and the bias $V_{b1}$ must be carefully generated, normally with a
diode connected replica.

Want the full derivation with test source, body effect included, or a
numerical/SPICE example for a $0.18\mu m$ bias point?

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is the elementary {\it telescopic cascode} - 
a common source $M_{1}$ loaded by a common gate
$M_{2}$ and an AC current source load $I_{1}$.

In ideal form $I_{1}$ is $AC$ $gnd$ with
$R_{I1}=r_{o3}=1/g_{ds3}= \infty $. In practice
$R_{I1}=r_{o3}< \infty $ of the PMOS that implements
$I_{1}$.

$$R_{oI}= \frac{1}{\lambda_{p}I_{1}}\;\;,\;\; r_{o1,2}=1/\lambda_{n}I_{1}$$

$$g_{m1,2}= \sqrt{2\mu_{n}C_{ox}(W/L)_{1,2}I_{1}}=
\frac{2I_{1}}{V_{ov1,2}}\;\;,\;\;g_{mb2}= \chi g_{m2}$$

> $M_{1}$ = transconductor, $M_{2}$ = current buffer,
> cascode device.

### 1. DC bias

By KCL

$$I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{1}\;\;\; {\rm if\; both\; saturated}$$

So $V_{GS1}$ is fixed by $I_{1}$:

$$I_{1}= \frac{1}{2}k_{n1}(V_{GS1}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda_{n}V_{DS1})$$
$$V_{in,DC}=V_{GS1}=V_{Tn}+V_{ov1}\approx V_{Tn}+\sqrt{\frac{2I_{1}}{k_{n1}}}$$

with $k_{n}= \mu_{n}C_{ox}W/L$.

$$V_{X}=V_{S2}=V_{b1}-V_{GS2}=V_{b1}-V_{Tn}-V_{ov2}$$

Saturation constraints:

* $M_{1}$ sat: $V_{DS1}=V_{X}\ge V_{ov1}$

$$V_{b1}\ge V_{Tn}+V_{ov1}+V_{ov2} \tag{1}$$

* $M_{2}$ sat: $V_{DS2}=V_{out}-V_{X}\ge V_{ov2}$

$$V_{out}\ge V_{b1}-V_{Tn} \tag{2}$$

with finite $I_{1}$:

* $I_{1}$ sat: $V_{SD3}=V_{DD}-V_{out}\ge V_{ov3}$

$$V_{ov1}+V_{ov2}\le V_{out}\le V_{DD}-|V_{ov3}| \tag{3}$$

is the usable swing.  $V_{b1}$ is normally generated
so as to put $V_{X}\approx V_{ov1}$ and $V_{out,min}=V_{ov1}+V_{ov2}$.
Typically $V_{b1}=V_{GS1}+V_{ov2}+ \Delta \approx 2V_{Tn}+2-3V_{ov}$.

Large signal $V_{out}$ vs. $V_{in}$:

* $V_{in}<V_{Tn}$: $M_{1},M_{2}$ OFF, $I_{1}$ charges $C_{L}$ to $V_{DD}-|V_{ov3}|$, $I_{1}$ in triode.
* $V_{in}=V_{GS1}$: both saturated, high gain region
* $V_{in}\gg V_{Tn}$: $M_{1}$ demands $>I_{1}$, $V_{X}$ and $V_{out}$ fall, $M_{1}$ then $I_{1}$ goes triode, $V_{out}\to V_{ov1}+V_{ov2}$ limit.

So for linear amplification $v_{in}=V_{in,DC}+v_{id}$ with $v_{id}\ll V_{ov1}$.

### 2. Small signal

```
vin -o---|G M1 D|---X---|S M2 D|---o vout
         |S     |      |G     |    |
        gnd    ro1     Vb1(AC gnd) ro2
                       gm2,gmb2    |
                                   R_I1 -> VDD AC gnd
```

$M_{2}$ is $CG$ with source degeneration $r_{o1}$.

Impedance looking into source of $CG$:

$$R_{X1}= \frac{1}{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2}}\approx \frac{1}{g_{m2}}$$

Impedance looking into drain of cascode:

Neglecting $R_{I1}$:

$$R_{oc}= \frac{v_{x}}{i_{x}}\Bigl|_{v_{in}=0}$$

$$R_{oc}= r_{o1}+r_{o2}+ (g_{m2}+g_{mb2})r_{o1}r_{o2}$$

$$R_{oc}\approx (1+(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})r_{o2})r_{o1}$$

Without body effect $g_{mb}=0$:

$$R_{oc}\approx g_{m2}r_{o1}r_{o2}\gg r_{o1}$$

That is the cascode multiplication by $g_{m2}r_{o2}\sim 20-100$.

With load:

$$R_{out}= R_{oc}\parallel R_{I1}=R_{oc}\parallel r_{o3}$$

For ideal $I_{1}$, $R_{out}=R_{oc}\to \infty$ to first
order.

Input resistance $R_{in}= \infty$ gate.

Resistance at intermediate node $X$:

$$R_{X}= \frac{1}{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}}\parallel r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\approx 1/g_{m2}$$

low impedance, which is the point.

### 3. Voltage gain

$$A_{v}= \frac{v_{out}}{v_{in}} = -g_{m1}R_{out}$$

i.e.

$$A_{v}= -g_{m1}\left[ r_{o1}+r_{o2}+(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})r_{o1}r_{o2}\right]\parallel r_{o3}$$

$$\left|A_{v}\right|\approx g_{m1}(g_{m2}r_{o2}r_{o1}\parallel r_{o3})$$

If $r_{o3}\gg R_{oc}$:

$$A_{v}\approx -g_{m1}g_{m2}r_{o1}r_{o2}= -(g_{m1}r_{o1})(g_{m2}r_{o2})$$

versus $A_{v0}=-g_{m1}r_{o1}\parallel r_{o3}$ for simple
common source. Increase by $g_{m2}r_{o2}$.

If $R_{oc}\gg r_{o3}$ the gain is limited by the PMOS load:

$$A_{v}\approx -g_{m1}r_{o3}$$

In practice $r_{o1}\approx r_{o2}\approx r_{o3}=r_{o}$,
$g_{m}r_{o}= 2/\lambda V_{ov}\sim 50$,

$$|A_{v}|\sim 50-80\,{\rm dB}$$

against $\sim 30-40\,{\rm dB}$ for CS.

Output phase is inverting, $CG$ is non-inverting.

Body effect: if p-sub NMOS $M_{2}$ has bulk to GND,
$g_{mb2}\ne 0$, $R_{oc}$ is increased slightly to
$(g_{m}+g_{mb})r_{o}$ but effective transconductance
from source to drain is $g_{m}/(1+\chi)$. Some texts
write $R_{oc}= (1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})r_{o2})r_{o1}+r_{o2}$.
If $M_{2}$ is in isolated p-well with bulk tied to $X$,
$g_{mb2}=0$.

### 4. Frequency response - Miller

$$C_{X}= C_{gs2}+C_{sb2}+C_{db1}+C_{gd1}$$
$$C_{L}= C_{db2}+C_{gd2}+C_{dbo3}+C_{gdo3}+C_{L,ext}$$

$$p_{out}= \frac{1}{R_{out}C_{L}}\;\; {\rm dominant}$$

$$p_{X}= \frac{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}}{C_{X}}\approx \frac{g_{m2}}{C_{X}}\;\; {\rm non\; dominant}$$

Because $R_{X}$ is small, $p_{X}\gg p_{out}$ . GBW $\approx g_{m1}/C_{L}$ same as CS, but
pole splitting is much better.

Miller multiplication of $C_{gd1}$:

$$C_{in}= C_{gs1}+C_{gd1}(1-A_{v1})$$

where $A_{v1}= v_{X}/v_{in}= -g_{m1}/(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})\approx -1$.
So $C_{gd1}$ sees $\sim 2\times$, not $1+|A_{v}|$ as in
simple CS. Large bandwidth improvement.

Approximate transfer:

$$A_{v}(s)\approx \frac{A_{v0}}{(1+s/p_{out})(1+s/p_{X})}$$

A RHP zero at $g_{m2}/C_{gd2}$ far away.

### 5. Merit

* High $R_{out}$, high voltage gain without stacking gain stages
* Suppresses Miller effect -> higher $f_{T}$
* Good PSRR if $I_{1}$ is cascode itself
* Cost: reduced output swing by $V_{ov2}$, needs $V_{b1}$ bias, needs headroom $V_{ov1}+V_{ov2}+|V_{ov3}|$, not suitable for low $V_{DD}$. Input common mode limited.

Used as core gain stage of telescopic / folded cascode op-amps, wideband LNAs. To increase swing and $R_{I1}$ the current source is itself cascoded, giving $R_{out}\approx g_{m}r_{o}^{2}\parallel g_{m}r_{o}^{2}$.

If you give $W/L$, $I_{1}$, $\lambda$, $C_{L}$ the numbers can be evaluated for $g_{m}$, $r_{o}$, $A_{v}$, $p_{out}$, $p_{X}$.
