Inverting w.r.t. $M_{2}$, non inverting w.r.t. $M_{1}$.

In square law, $W/L$ matched:

$$\eqalign{
I_{D1}&={1\over 2}\mu_{n}C_{ox}{W\over L}\left(V_{GS1}-V_{T}\right)^{2} \cr
I_{D2}&={1\over 2}\mu_{n}C_{ox}{W\over L}\left(V_{GS2}-V_{T}\right)^{2}}$$

Put $K={1\over 2}\mu_{n}C_{ox}W/L$, $\Delta V=V_{in}-V_{b}$

$$V_{GS1}-V_{GS2}=\Delta V$$

$$I_{D1,2}={I_{1}\over 2}\pm {\Delta V\over 2}\sqrt{2KI_{1}-K^{2}\Delta V^{2}}$$

$$|\Delta V| <\sqrt{2I_{1}/K}= \sqrt{2}V_{ov}$$

linear for $|\Delta V|\ll V_{ov}$ and one device cuts
off for $|\Delta V| >\sqrt{2}V_{ov}$. Then

$$V_{out}=V_{DD}-R_{D}I_{D2} \tag{*}$$

is the large signal transfer characteristic. At balance
$\Delta V=0$

$$I_{D10}=I_{D20}=I_{1}/2\qquad V_{outQ}=V_{DD}-{I_{1}\over 2}R_{D}$$

$$V_{DS1}=V_{DD}-V_{X}\;\;,\;\;V_{DS2}=V_{outQ}-V_{X}$$

with

$$V_{X}=V_{in}-V_{GS1}=V_{b}-V_{GS2}$$

must stay $>V_{ov}$ for saturation and

$$V_{X}>V_{DSAT(I_{1})}$$

to keep the tail in saturation. Hence

$$\eqalign{
V_{in(min)} &\approx V_{GS}+V_{DSATtail}\cr
V_{in(max)} &\approx V_{DD}+V_{T}\;\;{\rm CD\;can\;go\;to\;}V_{DD}\cr
V_{out(min)}&=V_{X}+V_{DSAT2}\cr
V_{out(max)}&=V_{DD}}$$

### 2. Small signal, differential mode

Put $v_{b}=0$, $v_{dd}=0$. Neglect for the moment
$g_{ds}=r_{o}^{-1}$, $g_{mb}$ and $R_{tail}=r_{oI_{1}}$.

$$v_{gs1}=v_{in}-v_{x}\qquad v_{gs2}=-v_{x}$$

$$i_{d1}=g_{m1}v_{gs1}\qquad i_{d2}=g_{m2}v_{gs2}$$

Tail ac KCL: ideal $R_{tail}=\infty$

$$i_{d1}+i_{d2}=0\tag{1}$$
for finite $R_{tail}$, $i_{d1}+i_{d2}=v_{x}/R_{tail}$.

Output KCL:

$$i_{d2}= -v_{out}/R_{D}\tag{2}$$
more exactly $i_{d2}= -v_{out}/R_{D}+g_{ds2}(v_{out}-v_{x})$ etc.

From (1)

$$g_{m1}(v_{in}-v_{x})-g_{m2}v_{x}=0$$

$$v_{x}={g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{m2}}v_{in} \tag{3}$$

$CD$ voltage follower gain $<1$ loaded by the $CG$ input
$1/g_{m2}$.

From (2)-(3)

$$v_{out}= -i_{d2}R_{D}=g_{m2}R_{D}v_{x}$$

$$A_{v}\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{in}}={g_{m1}g_{m2}\over g_{m1}+g_{m2}}R_{D} \tag{4}$$

For $g_{m1}=g_{m2}=g_{m}$

$$A_{v0}=+{1\over 2}g_{m}R_{D}\tag{5}$$

non inverting. This is $1/2$ the balanced
differential pair gain $g_{m}R_{D}$.

In general if $v_{b}\ne 0$

$$v_{out}={g_{m}R_{D}\over 2}\left(v_{in}-v_{b}\right)=A_{d}(v_{in}-v_{b})\tag{6}$$

$$A_{d}=g_{m}R_{D}/2$$

With $r_{o}$:

$$A_{v}= {g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{m2}}g_{m2}\left(R_{D}\parallel R_{o2}\right)$$

$$R_{o2}\approx r_{o2}+(1+g_{m2}r_{o2})R_{S}$$

$$R_{S}=R_{tail}\parallel {1\over g_{m1}}\parallel r_{o1}$$

so for $R_{tail}\gg 1/g_{m}$

$$R_{o2}\approx r_{o2}+{1+g_{m2}r_{o2}\over g_{m1}}\approx 2r_{o}\;\;{\rm matched}$$

Normally $R_{D}\ll R_{o2}$ and

$$A_{v}\approx {1\over 2}g_{m}(R_{D}\parallel r_{o})\tag{7}$$

With body effect, bulk $=GND$, $v_{bs1}=v_{bs2}=-v_{x}$,
$g_{m}\to g_{m}+g_{mb}$ for the source node:

$$v_{x}={g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{m2}+g_{mb2}}v_{in}$$

$$v_{out}=(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})R_{D}v_{x}$$

$$\eqalign{
A_{v}&={g_{m1}(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})\over \sum (g_{m}+g_{mb})}R_{D}\cr
&\approx {g_{m}R_{D}\over 2(1+\chi/2)}\;\;,\;\chi=g_{mb}/g_{m}\approx 0.2-0.3}$$

If the $n$-well process ties bulk to source, $g_{mb}=0$.

> No Miller multiplication: $C_{gd1}$ is from input to
> ac ground, $C_{gd2}$ from output to ac ground.
> So bandwith is $CD-CG$ i.e. cascode like.

### 3. Impedances

$$Z_{in}=1/sC_{gs1}\approx \infty \;{\rm low\;freq.}$$

Output seen by $R_{D}$ is the $CG$ output

$$R_{out}=R_{D}\parallel R_{o2}\approx R_{D}\;\;{\rm if}\;R_{D}\ll r_{o}$$

$$R_{out}\approx R_{D}\parallel \left[{1\over g_{ds2}}+(1+{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}\over g_{ds2}}) (R_{tail}\parallel {1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}})\right]$$

### 4. Common mode

Put $v_{in}=v_{b}=v_{cm}$. By symmetry $i_{d1}=i_{d2}=v_{x}/2R_{tail}$
and $v_{x}\approx v_{cm}$. More exactly

$$A_{cm}={v_{out}\over v_{cm}}\approx -{R_{D}\over 2R_{tail}}{1\over 1+g_{mb}/g_{m}}$$

$$|A_{cm}|\approx {R_{D}\over 2R_{tail}}\ll |A_{d}|$$

$$CMRR=|A_{d}/A_{cm}|\approx g_{m}R_{tail}\tag{8}$$

$10^{2}-10^{3}$ with simple tail, $10^{4}$ with cascode tail.
$PSRR\approx A_{d}$ for supply on $R_{D}$.

### 5. Frequency response

Dominant pole $p_{o}=1/R_{D}C_{L}$ at output,
non dominant pole at common source node

$$p_{s}\approx {g_{m1}+g_{m2}+g_{mb1}+g_{mb2}\over C_{X}}$$

$$C_{X}=C_{sb1}+C_{sb2}+C_{gs1}+C_{gs2}+C_{tail}$$

$p_{s}\gg p_{o}$ giving single pole behavior to high
frequency, which is why the pair is universally used
as the input stage of op amps, comparators, $CML$,
source coupled logic, Gilbert mixers, etc.

In short: a high $Z_{in}$, moderate $Z_{out}\approx R_{D}$,
moderate non-inverting voltage gain $g_{m}R_{D}/2$,
excellent common mode and supply rejection if $R_{tail}$
is large, wide common mode input range to $V_{DD}$,
no Miller effect. Replacing $R_{D}$ by a $PMOS$
current mirror gives $g_{m}r_{o}$ gain and full
differential to single ended conversion.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies the source-coupled pair as a source follower driving a common-gate stage, with M2’s gate at Vb and output at its drain. It also gives the correct non-inverting signal behavior and gain; extra details do not undermine the essential answer.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is the NMOS resistive load differential
pair in single ended form and, up to a
d.c. level shift, the $M_{1}-M_{2}$
source coupled common drain-common gate
cascade.

$$M_{1}:CD\;\;{\rm or}\;SF\qquad M_{2}:CG$$

$$D_{1}\to {\rm ac\;ground}\;\;G_{2}\to {\rm ac\;ground}=V_{b}$$
$$S_{1}=S_{2}=P\to I_{1},R_{T}=r_{oT}$$

in small signal $v_{b}=0$.

Large signal quiescent if $M_{1}=M_{2}$ and
$V_{inQ}=V_{b}$:

$$I_{D1Q}=I_{D2Q}=I_{1}/2$$

$$V_{GS}=V_{T}+V_{ov}\;\;,\;\;V_{ov}=\sqrt{\frac{I_{1}}
{\mu _{n}C_{ox}(W/L)}}$$

$$g_{m}=\sqrt{2\mu _{n}C_{ox}(W/L)I_{DQ}}=
\frac{2I_{DQ}}{V_{ov}}$$

$$V_{SQ}=V_{inQ}-V_{GS1}=V_{b}-V_{GS2}$$

$$V_{outQ}=V_{DD}-I_{D2Q}R_{D}=V_{DD}-\frac{I_{1}R_{D}}{2}$$

for square law

$$\eqalign{
I_{D1}-I_{D2} &\approx {\cal G}(V_{in}-V_{b})
\sqrt{1-\left({\cal G}(V_{in}-V_{b})/I_{1}\right)^{2}}\cr
|V_{in}-V_{b}|&<\sqrt{2}V_{ov}}$$

so steering of $I_{1}$ from $M_{2}$ to $M_{1}$
for $v_{in}>0$.

> $${\rm sign:}\;v_{in}\uparrow \to v_{P}\uparrow
> \to |v_{gs2}|\downarrow \to i_{d2}\downarrow
> \to i_{R_{D}}\downarrow \to v_{out}\uparrow $$
> non inverting.

$$I_{T}=I_{D1}+I_{D2}={\rm cst.}\;\;{\rm to}\;1/R_{T}$$

In saturation

$$V_{P}>V_{in}-V_{T}-V_{ov1}\qquad 
V_{P}>V_{b}-V_{T}-V_{ov2}$$
and for $I_{1}$ to stay saturated

$$V_{P}>V_{oT}+V_{ovT}$$
and for $M_{2}$ to stay saturated

$$V_{out}>V_{P}+V_{ov2}\;\;,\;\;V_{out}<V_{DD}$$

i. e. limited common mode range.

### Small signal

$$v_{gs1}=v_{in}-v_{p}\qquad v_{gs2}=-v_{p}\qquad
v_{bsi}=-v_{p}$$
$$v_{ds1}=-v_{p}\qquad v_{ds2}=v_{out}-v_{p}$$

$$i_{d1}=g_{m1}v_{gs1}+g_{mb1}v_{bs1}+g_{ds1}v_{ds1}$$
$$i_{d2}=g_{m2}v_{gs2}+g_{mb2}v_{bs2}+g_{ds2}v_{ds2}$$

with $g_{dsi}=r_{oi}^{-1}$.

Nodal ${\rm ac\;ground}=V_{DD}$.

$$P: \;i_{d1}+i_{d2}=v_{p}G_{T}\tag{1}$$
$$D_{2}: \;v_{out}G_{D}+i_{d2}=0\;\;{\rm i.e.}\tag{2}$$
$$v_{out}/R_{D}+(v_{out}-v_{p})g_{ds2}
+(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})(-v_{p})=0$$

From (2)

$$v_{out}\left(G_{D}+g_{ds2}\right)=
v_{p}\left(g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2}\right) \tag{3}$$

$$v_{out}=v_{p}\left(g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2}\right)
R_{D}\parallel r_{o2}$$

From (1)

$$g_{m1}v_{in}+v_{out}g_{ds2}=
v_{p}\left[G_{T}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}+g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+
g_{m2}+g_{mb2}\right]\tag{4}$$

and with (3)

$$A_{v}\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{in}}=
{{g_{m1}\left(g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2}\right)
R_{D}\parallel r_{o2}}\over
{G_{T}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}+g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{m2}+g_{mb2}
-\left(g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+g_{ds2}\right){R_{D}\parallel r_{o2}\over r_{o2}}}}$$

$$A_{v}=
g_{m1}R_{D}{\left[(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})r_{o2}+1\right]\over
(R_{D}+r_{o2})\left(G_{T}+g_{ds1}+g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\right)
+(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})r_{o2}+1}\tag{5}$$

Normally $r_{oi}\gg R_{D}$ , $G_{T}\ll g_{m}$

$$A_{v}\approx {{g_{m1}\left(g_{m2}+g_{mb2}\right)
R_{D}}\over {g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+G_{T}}}
\;{1\over 1+{\cal O}(G_{D}r_{o}^{-1})}\tag{6}$$

In the usual neglect $g_{mb}=0$, $r_{o}\to \infty $,
$R_{T}\to \infty $

$${{v_{p}\approx {g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{m2}}v_{in}}}$$

is the source follower division on to the
common source node, and

$$v_{out}\approx g_{m2}R_{D}v_{p}$$

is the common gate gain, so that

$$A_{v0}\approx {g_{m1}g_{m2}\over g_{m1}+g_{m2}}R_{D}>0 \tag{7}$$

For the matched pair $g_{m1}=g_{m2}=g_{m}$,

$$A_{v0}\approx {1\over 2}g_{m}R_{D}\tag{8}$$

with $g_{mb}\ne 0$

$$A_{v0}\approx {g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{m2}+g_{mb2}}
\left(g_{m2}+g_{mb2}\right)R_{D}$$

and for the matched case $g_{mb1}=g_{mb2}=g_{mb}$

$$A_{v0}\approx {1\over 2}g_{m}R_{D}$$

to first order $g_{mb}$ cancels, the more exact
(5) gives $A_{v}\approx
g_{m}R_{D}/2\left[1-(g_{mb}/g_{m})R_{D}/r_{o}\right]$.

I. e. half the gain of the common source stage with
the same $R_{D}$ and same bias current.
If the tail is not ideal $G_{T}=1/R_{T}\ne 0$

$$A_{v}= {A_{v0}\over 1+G_{T}/(g_{m1}+g_{m2})}$$

Common mode gain with $v_{in}=v_{b}=v_{cm}$:

$$A_{cm}\approx -{R_{D}\over 2R_{T}}{g_{m2}\over g_{m1}+g_{m2}}
\approx -{R_{D}\over 4R_{T}}\to 0\;{\rm for}\;R_{T}\to \infty $$

so

$${\rm CMRR}=|A_{d}/A_{cm}|\approx g_{m}R_{T}$$

differential pair behaviour.

* Input resistance: Gate input

$$R_{in}=1/j\omega C_{gs1}\approx \infty \;{\rm at\;LF}$$

of the order of ${\rm G\Omega }$.

* Output resistance: at $v_{in}=0$ looking into $D_{2}$

$$R_{o}=R_{D}\parallel R_{o2}$$

$$R_{o2}=r_{o2}+ \left[1+(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})r_{o2}\right]
\left(r_{o1}\parallel R_{T}\parallel {1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}\right)$$

$$\approx r_{o2}\left[1+{g_{m2}+g_{mb2}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}\right]
\approx 2r_{o2}\;\;{\rm matched}$$

so normally

$$R_{o}\approx R_{D}\qquad R_{D}\ll r_{o}$$

if $R_{D}$ is replaced by an active $r_{o}$ load,
$A_{v}\approx g_{m}r_{o}/2$.

With capacitive load $C_{L}$ at the output and
capacitance $C_{P}$ at the common source node

$$p_{1}\approx -{1\over R_{o}C_{L}}\qquad
p_{2}\approx -{g_{m1}+g_{m2}+g_{mb1}+g_{mb2}\over C_{P}}$$

$p_{2}$ is normally non dominant.

In frequency compensated form this is the classic
first stage of a CMOS op. amp. Replacing $R_{D}$
by a $p$MOS current mirror gives the conventional
5-transistor OTA with

$$A_{v}=g_{m}\,(r_{on}\parallel r_{op})$$

Slew rate is limited by $I_{1}/C_{L}$.

> Remark: With $R_{D}=0$, $M_{1}$ is a normal source
> follower with gain
> $A_{SF}=g_{m1}/(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+G_{T}+G_{L})<1$.
> The present circuit is that follower loaded by the
> low input impedance $\approx 1/(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})$ of the
> CG stage instead of a resistor.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies the source-follower/common-gate cascade (equivalently, a source-coupled differential pair) and gives the correct non-inverting gain.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is the $N$ channel long tailed
source coupled pair with single ended resistive load.
$V_{b}=V_{B0}$ is the $ac$ ground if the pair
is driven single ended.

$$
M_{1}:CD\qquad M_{2}:CG\qquad S_{1}=S_{2}=S
$$

pair in $CC-CB$ cascade.

> * D. C. : $I_{D1}+I_{D2}=I_{1}={\rm const}$
>   A. C. : $i_{d1}+i_{d2}=0$ for $R_{EE}\rightarrow \infty $.
>   $M_{1}$ is a source follower loaded by
>   $1/(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})\parallel r_{o2}$ ,
>   $M_{2}$ is a common gate driven by that
>   follower.

Put for definiteness both $M$ in saturation

$$I_{D}=K_{n}(V_{GS}-V_{T})^{2}(1+\lambda V_{DS})\qquad 
  K_{n}={1\over 2}\mu _{n}C_{ox}W/L$$

$$g_{m}=2\sqrt{K_{n}I_{D}}=2I_{D}/V_{ov}\qquad 
  r_{o}=1/\lambda I_{D}$$

Normal bias for $ \Delta V_{I}=V_{in}-V_{b}=0$

$$I_{D01}=I_{D02}=I_{1}/2\qquad g_{m1}=g_{m2}=g_{m}$$

$$V_{S}=V_{G}-V_{GS}=V_{CM}-V_{T}-V_{ov}\tag{1}$$

$$V_{o}=V_{DD}-I_{D2}R_{D}\tag{2}$$

For saturation

$$\eqalign{
V_{DS1}&=V_{DD}-V_{S}\ge V_{GS1}-V_{T}\cr
V_{DS2}&=V_{o}-V_{S}\ge V_{GS2}-V_{T}\cr}
\qquad {\rm i.e.}\qquad 
\eqalign{
V_{in}&\le V_{DD}+V_{T}\cr
V_{o}&\ge V_{b}-V_{T}\cr
V_{S}&\ge V_{SS}+V_{DS,sat}(I_{1})\cr}$$

$V_{S}$ fixes the common mode range.
Normal linear common mode range $\approx V_{ov}<|\Delta V_{I}|
<\sqrt{2}V_{ov}$.

With $R_{EE}=r_{oI_{1}}<\infty $ :

$$-V_{ov}\sqrt{2}<V_{in}-V_{b}<+V_{ov}\sqrt{2}$$

for both in saturation. Outside one device cuts off

$$V_{o,max}=V_{DD}\;\;{\rm for}\;\;V_{in}-V_{b}\gg V_{ov}\;\;,
  I_{D1}=I_{1},I_{D2}=0$$
$$V_{o,min}=V_{DD}-I_{1}R_{D}\;\;{\rm for}\;\;
  V_{b}-V_{in}\gg V_{ov}\;\;,
  I_{D1}=0,I_{D2}=I_{1}$$

so nominal swing $\Delta V_{o}=I_{1}R_{D}$.

In square law

$$I_{D1,2}={I_{1}\over 2}\pm 
\sqrt{K_{n}I_{1}}\Delta V_{I}\sqrt{1-{K_{n}\Delta V_{I}^{2}\over 2I_{1}}}
\qquad |\Delta V_{I}|\le \sqrt{I_{1}/K_{n}}$$

and

$$V_{o}=V_{DD}-R_{D}I_{D2}(\Delta V_{I})$$

which is $\tanh $ like, linear for 
$|\Delta V_{I}|\ll V_{ov}$ :

$$i_{d1}=-i_{d2}\approx {g_{m}\over 2}\Delta V_{I}$$

### Small signal - differential

Put $v_{b}=0\;ac$.  $v_{gs1}=v_{in}-v_{s}$,
$v_{gs2}=-v_{s}$, $v_{bs1}=v_{bs2}=-v_{s}$ if
bulk $=GND$, $0$ if bulk $=S$.

Ideal $r_{o}\rightarrow \infty ,\;R_{EE}\rightarrow \infty $,
bulk $=S$ for simplicity:

KCL $S$:

$$g_{m1}(v_{in}-v_{s})+g_{m2}(-v_{s})=0$$

$$v_{s}={g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{m2}}v_{in}\tag{3}$$

For $g_{m1}=g_{m2}=g_{m}$, $v_{s}=v_{in}/2$.
The source is {\it not} a virtual ground for single
ended drive. It is for pure differential drive
$v_{in}=-v_{b}$.

KCL drain $2$:

$$v_{o}=-i_{d2}R_{D}\qquad i_{d2}=g_{m2}(-v_{s})$$

$$v_{o}=g_{m2}R_{D}v_{s}=
  {g_{m1}g_{m2}\over g_{m1}+g_{m2}}R_{D}v_{in}\tag{4}$$

$$A_{v}\equiv {v_{o}\over v_{in}}=
  {g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{m2}}g_{m2}R_{D}>0\tag{5}$$

non inverting.  For the matched pair

$$A_{v0}\approx +{1\over 2}g_{m}R_{D} \tag{6}$$

$6\,{\rm dB}$ less than a common source with the same
$R_{D}$ and $I_{D}=I_{1}/2$, $1/2$ the $G_{m}$.

In fact the circuit is follower $M_{1}$ with

$$A_{v1}={v_{s}\over v_{in}}={g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{m2}}
      \approx {1\over 2}$$

driving a $CG$ stage $M_{2}$ with

$$A_{v2}={v_{o}\over v_{s}}=g_{m2}R_{D}$$

so $A_{v}=A_{v1}A_{v2}$.

Differentially

$$v_{o}=A_{d}(v_{in}-v_{b})\qquad 
  A_{d}= {1\over 2}g_{m}R_{D}\tag{7}$$

Double if taken differentially $v_{o1}-v_{o2}=g_{m}R_{D}\Delta V_{I}$.

With $r_{o1},r_{o2},R_{EE}$ and body effect $g_{mb}$:

$$\eqalign{
i_{d1}&=g_{m1}(v_{in}-v_{s})+g_{mb1}(-v_{s})+( -v_{s})/r_{o1}\cr
i_{d2}&=g_{m2}(-v_{s})+g_{mb2}(-v_{s})+(v_{o}-v_{s})/r_{o2}\cr}$$

$$i_{d1}+i_{d2}=v_{s}/R_{EE}\tag{8}$$
$$i_{d2}=-v_{o}/R_{D}\tag{9}$$

which gives to first order for $g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1$

$$A_{v}={g_{m1}R_{D}\left(g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+1/r_{o2}\right)
\over \left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+1/r_{o1}+g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+1/r_{o2}\right)
      \left(1+R_{D}/r_{o2}\right)+R_{D}/r_{o1}\left(g_{m2}+g_{mb2}+1/r_{o2}\right)}$$

$$\approx {g_{m1}(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})\over 
          g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{m2}+g_{mb2}}\,
          \left(R_{D}\parallel r_{o2}\right) \tag{10}$$

For $r_{o}\gg R_{D}$ and $g_{mb}=0$, (10) $\rightarrow$ (5).
For a matched pair $g_{m1}=g_{m2}=g_{m}$,
$g_{mb1}=g_{mb2}=g_{mb}$ and $r_{o}\gg R_{D}$

$$A_{v}\approx {g_{m}\over 2}\left(R_{D}\parallel r_{o2}\right)
      \tag{11}$$

the body effect drops out to first order.
In general

$$G_{m}\equiv {i_{o}\over v_{id}}={A_{v}\over R_{D}}\approx {g_{m}\over 2}$$

$$Z_{in}=1/sC_{gs}\rightarrow \infty \;{\rm at\;DC}\tag{12}$$

$$Z_{out}\approx R_{D}\parallel r_{o2}\parallel
  \left[r_{o2}+ \left(1+(g_{m2}+g_{mb2})r_{o2}\right)
         \left(r_{o1}\parallel R_{EE}\parallel 1/(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})\right)\right]
  \approx R_{D}\parallel r_{o2}\approx R_{D}\tag{13}$$

Dominant pole

$$\omega_{p o}\approx 1/R_{D}C_{L}\qquad 
  \omega_{p s}\approx (g_{m1}+g_{m2})/C_{S}$$

with $C_{S}$ at the common source.

### Common mode

For $v_{in}=v_{b}=v_{cm}$ and $R_{EE}<\infty $

$$A_{cm}={v_{o}\over v_{cm}}\approx
  -{g_{m}R_{D}\over 1+2g_{m}R_{EE}}\approx -{R_{D}\over 2R_{EE}}
  \tag{14}$$

for $g_{m}R_{EE}\gg 1$.  Ideally $R_{EE}\rightarrow\infty $,
$A_{cm}\rightarrow 0$,

$$CMRR=\left|{A_{d}\over A_{cm}}\right|\approx g_{m}R_{EE}\tag{15}$$

$$PSRR\approx g_{m}r_{o}$$

Hence the interest of a high impedance tail source,
cascode $I_{1}$, and of an active $PMOS$ mirror load
instead of $R_{D}$ to get

$$A_{v}\approx g_{m}(r_{on}\parallel r_{op})/2$$

to $50$--$60\,{\rm dB}$.

In modern $CMOS$ the bulk $=GND$ for $NMOS$,
$R_{EE}=r_{oI_{1}}$, $R_{D}$ often replaced by a
$PMOS$ current mirror, and the circuit is the
standard input stage/phase splitter of the
$CMOS$ operational amplifier.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies the source-coupled pair as a source follower driving a common-gate stage and gives the correct non-inverting gain.

answers.question: Explain why the output impedance of the circuit shown in the figure can be inductive.

answer.text:
With $R_{S}=0$ the source is resistive $\approx
g_{m}^{-1}$ and capacitive. ${\rm Im}Z_{o}<0$.
With $Z_{g}\ne 0$ the capacitance $C_{gs}$ is a
feedback element and becomes a gyrator.

Put $v_{i}=0$ for $Z_{o}$ and apply $v_{x}$ on the
source, Fig.1.

$$\eqalign{
M_{1}: & g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{ds1}v_{ds}+sC_{gs}(v_{g}-v_{s})
      +sC_{gd}(v_{g}-v_{d})+sC_{ds1}(v_{d}-v_{s})=0\cr
M_{2}: & g_{ds2}v_{x}+sC_{o}v_{x}\approx i_{2}}$$

$D$ of $M_{1}$ is ac ground, $S\equiv v_{x}$, 
$G\equiv v_{g}$:

$$ {v_{g}\over R_{S}}+sC_{gs}(v_{g}-v_{x})+sC_{gd}v_{g}=0\tag{1}$$
$$i_{x}+i_{M1}=i_{M2}\tag{2}$$

$$i_{M1}=g_{m}(v_{g}-v_{x})-(g_{ds1}+sC_{ds1})v_{x}
        +sC_{gs}(v_{g}-v_{x})\tag{3} {\rm\;into\;}S$$
from (1)

$$v_{g}=v_{x}{sC_{gs}\over {1\over R_{S}}+sC_{g}}\qquad 
C_{g}=C_{gs}+C_{gd}\tag{4}$$

and e.g. to $C_{gd}=C_{o}=g_{ds}=0$ for clarity

$$i_{x}=v_{x}g_{m}+sC_{gs}v_{x}-(g_{m}+sC_{gs})v_{g}$$

$$Z_{o}={v_{x}\over i_{x}}=
{g_{m}+sC_{gs}-(g_{m}+sC_{gs}){sC_{gs}R_{S}\over 1+sC_{gs}R_{S}}}^{-1}
={1+sC_{gs}R_{S}\over g_{m}+sC_{gs}}\tag{5}$$

With $R_{S},g_{ds},C_{gd},C_{o}$ kept

$$Z_{o}(s)={1+sR_{S}C_{g}\over N(s)}\tag{6}$$

$$\eqalign{
N(s)=&g_{0}+sC_{1}+s^{2}R_{S}(C_{g}C_{o}+C_{gd}C_{gs})\cr
g_{0}=&g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}\cr
C_{1}=&C_{o}+C_{gs}+R_{S}C_{g}g_{0}-R_{S}C_{gs}g_{m}\cr
&\approx C_{o}+C_{gs}+R_{S}C_{gd}g_{m}}$$

where $C_{o}=C_{ds1}+C_{ds2}+C_{L}$.
Put $s=j\omega$, for $\omega$ small enough that
$s^{2}$ can be neglected,

$$Z_{o}(j\omega)\approx {1+j\omega R_{S}C_{g}\over g_{0}+j\omega C_{1}}
={g_{0}+\omega ^{2}R_{S}C_{g}C_{1}+j\omega (R_{S}C_{g}g_{0}-C_{1})
\over g_{0}^{2}+\omega ^{2}C_{1}^{2}} \tag{7}$$

Normal low frequency resistance

$$R_{o0}={1\over g_{0}}\approx {1\over g_{m}}\;\;||r_{o1}||r_{o2}$$

and to first order in $s$

$$Z_{o}\approx {1\over g_{0}}+s{R_{S}C_{g}g_{0}-C_{1}\over g_{0}^{2}}
=R_{o0}+sL_{eq}+O(s^{2})\tag{8}$$

$$L_{eq}={R_{S}C_{g}g_{0}-C_{1}\over g_{0}^{2}}
={R_{S}g_{m}C_{gs}-C_{gs}-C_{o}\over g_{0}^{2}} \tag{9}$$

In the stripped model (5)

$$Z_{o}={1\over g_{m}}{1+j\omega C_{gs}R_{S}\over
1+j\omega C_{gs}/g_{m}}\tag{10}$$

$$ {\rm Re}Z_{o}={g_{m}+\omega^{2}C_{gs}^{2}R_{S}\over
g_{m}^{2}+\omega^{2}C_{gs}^{2}}>0$$

$${\rm Im}Z_{o}= \omega C_{gs}{R_{S}g_{m}-1\over
g_{m}^{2}+\omega^{2}C_{gs}^{2}}\tag{11}$$

$${\rm Im}Z_{o}>0\iff R_{S}g_{m}>1+{C_{o}\over C_{gs}}\approx 1$$

i.e. the zero $\omega _{z}=1/R_{S}C_{g}$ lies below the
pole $\omega _{p}=g_{m}/C_{gs}$.  For

$${1\over R_{S}C_{g}}<\omega <{g_{m}\over C_{gs}}$$

$|Z_{o}|$ rises with $\omega$, phase $+\arctan
\omega L_{eq}/R_{o0}>0$, inductive.  In that band

$$Z_{o}\approx R_{o0}+j\omega L_{eq}\qquad 
L_{eq}\approx {C_{gs}\over g_{m}}\left(R_{S}-{1\over g_{m}}\right)
\approx {R_{S}C_{gs}\over g_{m}}\;\;{\rm for}\;R_{S}\gg g_{m}^{-1}
\tag{12}$$

complete with $g_{mb}$ : $g_{m}\to g_{m}+g_{mb}$.
Up to a factor the drain capacitance of $M_{2}$, $C_{g}$
appears as an inductance when seen from the source.
It is the ordinary gyrator action of the $g_{m}$ device:
$Z_{g}=R_{S}+1/sC$ at the gate is transformed to

$$Z_{s}\approx {Z_{g}\over g_{m}r_{o}}+{1\over g_{m}}$$

so $1/sC_{gs}$ becomes $sL$.

Physically: let $v_{x}$ jump $+\Delta V$.  $C_{gs}$
pushes $v_{g}$ up with it.  If $R_{S}$ is large $v_{g}$
follows $v_{x}$ instantaneously, $v_{gs}\approx 0$ so
$g_{m}v_{gs}$ supplies essentially no current: high
$Z_{o}$.  $v_{g}$ then decays to $0$ with
$\tau =R_{S}C_{g}$ and $v_{gs}\to -v_{x}$, $g_{m}v_{gs}$
builds up with delay $\tau$.  Current lags voltage by
$\approx 90^{\circ}$.  That is $v=Ldi/dt$.  For
$R_{S}=0$, $v_{g}=0$ instantaneously, $i=g_{m}v_{x}$
instantaneously, resistive and, from (11) with $R_{S}=0$,
${\rm Im}Z_{o}= -\omega C_{gs}/(g_{m}^{2}+\omega^{2}
C_{gs}^{2})<0$, capacitive.

At very low $\omega$, $C_{gs}$ open, $Z_{o}=R_{o0}$,
at $\omega _{z}<\omega <\omega _{p}$ the $|Z_{o}|$
$\propto \omega$, $+\,j\omega L_{eq}$ lossy inductor
$Q\approx \omega L_{eq}/R_{o0}\approx \omega R_{S}C_{gs}$,
at $\omega \gg \omega _{p}$ $C_{gs}$ shorts $G$ to $S$,
$Z_{o}\to R_{S}$ and then shunted by $C_{o}$, i.e.
second order $R_{o0}+sL_{eq}\;||\;1/sC_{o}$, resonance
$\omega_{0}\approx 1/\sqrt{L_{eq}C_{o}}$.

It is an active inductor made from $R_{S}$ and $C_{gs}$
by the $g_{m}$ gyrator.  With a capacitive load $C_{L}$
it resonates and produces the familiar source follower
peaking, ringing and, if $R_{S}g_{m}C_{gd}$ is large
enough to make ${\rm Re}Z_{o}<0$, even oscillation.  It
is used intentionally as a cheap on-chip shunt peaking
inductor $L_{eq}\sim 0.1$ to $10\,{\rm nH}$ for
$C_{gs}\sim 50\,{\rm fF}$, $g_{m}\sim 1\,{\rm mS}$,
$R_{S}\sim 1\,{\rm k\Omega}$, bandwidth extension.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly derives the simplified output impedance and explains that it rises from about 1/gm to RS as Cgs couples the gate to the source, producing inductive behavior when RS > 1/gm. The extra parasitic-model discussion does not undermine this central result.

answers.question: Explain why the output impedance of the circuit shown in the figure can be inductive.

answer.text:
In common drain with $R_{S}=0$ it is not.

Put $V_{in}=0$ for $Z_{o}$ and put small
signal test ${\cal E}_{x}$ on $V_{out}$.

$$Z_{o}=Z_{o1}\parallel Z_{o2}\qquad Z_{o2}\approx r_{o2}\parallel
 1/sC_{o2}$$

and the essentially new thing is $Z_{o1}$.
Neglect at first $r_{o1}$ and $C_{gd},C_{bd}$,
body tied to source so $g_{mb}=0$ for the
sake of writing. The claim remains with $g_{m}\rightarrow
g_{m}+g_{mb}$.

\begin{center}
$M_{1}$: $g_{m}V_{gs}$ $D\rightarrow S$, $R_{S}$ in series
with $G$ to ground, $C_{gs}$ $G-S$.
\end{center}

$$\eqalign{
i_{g}&= sC_{gs}(v_{g}-v_{x})+sC_{gd}v_{g} \cr
i_{d}&=g_{m}(v_{g}-v_{x})+g_{ds}(-v_{x})+{\rm caps}}$$

In low frequency form:

KCL at $G$:

$${{v_{g}\over R_{S}}+sC_{gd}v_{g}+sC_{gs}(v_{g}-v_{x})=0 \tag{1}}$$

KCL at $S$ with external current $i_{x}$ injected
in $v_{x}$:

$$i_{x}= -i_{s}=i_{d}+i_{g}\tag{2}$$

$$i_{s}({\rm into}\;M_{1})=-g_{m}v_{gs}-sC_{gs}v_{gs}+\cdots $$

To first order keep only $g_{m},C_{gs}$:

$$v_{g}\left({1\over R_{S}}+sC_{gs}\right)=sC_{gs}v_{x}\tag{3}$$

$$v_{g}=v_{x}{sC_{gs}R_{S}\over 1+sC_{gs}R_{S}} \tag{4}$$

$$i_{x}= (g_{m}+sC_{gs})(v_{x}-v_{g}){\rm \;with\; sign\;
convention}\tag{5}$$

i. e. with (4)

$$i_{x}= (g_{m}+sC_{gs})\left[v_{x}-v_{x}{sC_{gs}R_{S}\over
1+sC_{gs}R_{S}}\right]=(g_{m}+sC_{gs}){v_{x}\over
1+sC_{gs}R_{S}} \tag{6}$$

$$\;Z_{o1}(s)={v_{x}\over i_{x}}={1+sC_{gs}R_{S}\over g_{m}+sC_{gs}}\;
 \tag{7}$$

With $r_{o}$ :

$$Z_{o1}={1+sC_{gs}R_{S}\over g_{m}+g_{ds}+sC_{gs}}\approx
{r_{o1}\,(1+sC_{gs}R_{S})\over 1+g_{m}r_{o1}+sC_{gs}r_{o1}}$$

$\parallel r_{o2}$ in total. Including $C_{gd}$ simply
replaces $C_{gs}\rightarrow C_{gs}+C_{gd}$ in (1) with
small $sC_{gd}R_{S}g_{m}$ corrections. With body effect
$g_{m}\rightarrow g_{m}+g_{mb}$.

$${\rm zero:}\;s_{z}=-1/R_{S}C_{gs}\qquad 
{\rm pole:}\;s_{p}=-g_{m}/C_{gs} \tag{8}$$

$$Z_{o1}(s)={1\over g_{m}}{1+s/s_{z}\over 1+s/s_{p}}
     = {1\over g_{m}}{1+sC_{gs}R_{S}\over 1+sC_{gs}/g_{m}} \tag{9}$$

which is $1/g_{m}$ at $s\rightarrow 0$ and $R_{S}$ at
$s\rightarrow \infty$.

Put $s=j\omega$:

$$Z_{o1}(j\omega)={1+j\omega C_{gs}R_{S}\over g_{m}+j\omega C_{gs}}
={g_{m}+\omega^{2}C_{gs}^{2}R_{S}+j\omega C_{gs}(g_{m}R_{S}-1)
\over g_{m}^{2}+\omega^{2}C_{gs}^{2}} \tag{10}$$

$$R(\omega)={g_{m}+\omega^{2}C_{gs}^{2}R_{S}\over
g_{m}^{2}+\omega^{2}C_{gs}^{2}}\qquad 
X(\omega)=\omega C_{gs}{g_{m}R_{S}-1\over
g_{m}^{2}+\omega^{2}C_{gs}^{2}} \tag{11}$$

$R>0$ always, $X$ changes sign with $g_{m}R_{S}-1$.

* If $R_{S}=0$, $v_{g}=0$,

$$Z_{o1}= {1\over g_{m}+sC_{gs}}={1/g_{m}\over 1+sC_{gs}/g_{m}}
\approx {1\over g_{m}}\parallel {1\over sC_{gs}}$$

capacitive, ${\rm Im}\,Z_{o}<0$.

* If $\;g_{m}R_{S}>1\;$ more generally
$(g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{S}>1$ or $(g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{S}>1-g_{ds}R_{S}$,

$${\rm Im}\,Z_{o1}>0$$

for $\omega >0$ . The impedance looks inductive in the
band

$$\omega_{z}=1/R_{S}C_{gs}<\omega<\omega_{p}=g_{m}/C_{gs}
\tag{12}$$

where $|Z_{o}|$ rises with frequency. For
$\omega\ll \omega_{p}$ :

$$Z_{o1}\approx {1\over g_{m}}\left[1+sC_{gs}(R_{S}-1/g_{m})\right]
\approx {1\over g_{m}}+sL_{eq}\tag{13}$$

$$L_{eq}\approx {C_{gs}\over g_{m}}\left(R_{S}-{1\over g_{m}}\right)
\approx {R_{S}C_{gs}\over g_{m}}\;\;{\rm for}\;R_{S}\gg 1/g_{m} \tag{14}$$

with finite $r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}$:

$$Z_{o}\approx {1\over g_{m}}\parallel r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}
+ s\,{C_{gs}R_{S}\over g_{m}}\;\;\;{\rm up\;to}\;1/\omega_{p}$$

So about $Q\sim \omega L_{eq}/R_{eq}$. At $\omega\gg\omega_{p}$,
$Z_{o1}\rightarrow R_{S}$ resistive again; in practice
$C_{gd},C_{db},C_{gs2}$ etc. ultimately shunt $Z_{o}$ capacitively at very high frequency, so the impedance is
$R\parallel L\parallel C$ - band pass.

Physical: It is the source follower feedback through $C_{gs}$.
A change $\Delta v_{x}$ is fed back to the gate through
$C_{gs}$ and the divider $R_{S}-1/sC_{gs}$. If the gate were
ideal ac ground, $i_{x}=g_{m}\Delta v_{x}$ . With $R_{S}\ne 0$
the gate follows $\Delta v_{x}$, $v_{g}=v_{x}sC_{gs}R_{S}/
(1+sC_{gs}R_{S})$, lagging $v_{x}$.

In time domain: $\;v_{x}\uparrow$ pulls $v_{g}\uparrow$ through
$C_{gs}$ but $R_{S}$ delays the charging of $C_{gs}$.
Instantaneously $v_{gs}=v_{g}-v_{x}<0$ so $g_{m}v_{gs}$ decreases,
the transistor supplies {\it less} current when you try to
raise its source voltage. $d i_{x}/dt$ lags $d v_{x}/dt$.
That is $v=L\,di/dt$, $i$ lags $v$. In frequency domain the
loop gain $T\approx g_{m}R_{S}/(1+sR_{S}C_{gs})$ has a pole,
so the closed loop output impedance $Z_{ocl}=Z_{ol}/(1+T)$
acquires a zero before its pole, i.e. a $+90^{0}$ phase.

$M_{2}$ is essentially $r_{o2}\parallel C_{o2}$ to ground.
It limits the $Q$ and together with the inductive $Z_{o1}$ and
any capacitive load $C_{L}$ on $V_{out}$ makes a parallel
$RLC$ circuit,

$$Z_{o}(s)\approx \left[sC_{L}+{1\over r_{o2}}+{g_{m}+sC_{gs}\over
1+sC_{gs}R_{S}}\right]^{-1}$$

which resonates at $\omega_{0}\approx 1/\sqrt{L_{eq}C_{L}}$,
giving inductive peaking, ringing and possibly oscillation.
That is why a source - emitter - follower with resistive source
and capacitive load is a well known ``active inductor'' and is
widely used for shunt peaking / bandwidth extension and as
gyrator based inductor in $LC$ VCOs and filters without coils.
With $R_{S}=R_{source}$ of the previous stage it is often
parasitic. The same mechanism holds for bipolar emitter follower.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly derives the key impedance and explains its transition from about 1/gm at low frequencies to RS at high frequencies as Cgs couples the gate to the source. It identifies the inductive rise when RS > 1/gm; extra discussion does not undermine the essential answer.

answers.question: Explain why the output impedance of the circuit shown in the figure can be inductive.

answer.text:
In common drain with ${\rm g}_{ds}^{-1}
\gg 1/g_{m}$ the only singularity is
$V_{gs}$. Put $V_{i}=0$ for ${\rm Z}_{o}$.
Let ${\rm Z}_{g}=R_{S}$ at the gate and
${\rm C}_{gs}\approx {\rm C}=C_{gs1}$ to first
order, $G_{m}=g_{m}+g_{mb}$.

$${\rm C}_{gd}, {\rm C}_{gb}, {\rm C}_{db}\to 0\qquad
r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}=r_{o}\to \infty $$
can be put in parallel afterwards.

$$\eqalign{
M_{1}:\;\;i_{d}&=G_{m}v_{gs}+sCv_{gs}\cr
{\rm KCL}\;g:\;\;{{v_{g}}\over {R_{S}}}+sC(v_{g}-v_{x})&=0\cr
{\rm KCL}\;x:\;\;i_{x}+G_{m}v_{gs}+sCv_{gs}&=0\;
{\rm with}\;v_{gs}=v_{g}-v_{x}\cr}$$

$v_{x}$ is the test voltage at the source,
$i_{x}$ the current injected into the source,
$d\to {\rm AC\, grd}$.

$${{v_{g}}\over {R_{S}}}=-sC(v_{g}-v_{x})$$

$$v_{g}\left({1\over {R_{S}}}+sC\right)=sCv_{x}$$

$$v_{g}=v_{x}{{sCR_{S}}\over {1+sCR_{S}}} \tag{1}$$

$$i_{x}=-(G_{m}+sC)v_{gs}=(G_{m}+sC)(v_{x}-v_{g}) \tag{2}$$

$$i_{x}=(G_{m}+sC)v_{x}\left[1-{{sCR_{S}}\over {1+sCR_{S}}}\right]
     ={{G_{m}+sC}\over {1+sCR_{S}}}v_{x}$$

So looking into the source alone

$$\;Z_{1}(s)={{v_{x}}\over {i_{x}}}={{1+sCR_{S}}\over {G_{m}+sC}}\; \tag{3}$$

$${\rm Z}_{o}(s)=Z_{1}(s)\parallel r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}
   \parallel {1\over {sC_{L}}}\parallel \cdots $$

where $r_{oi}=1/g_{dsi}$ and $C_{L}$ is the load and
${\rm C}_{db},{\rm C}_{gd}$ etc.  The essential physics is
in (3).

Put $s=j\omega $

$$Z_{1}(j\omega)={{1+j\omega CR_{S}}\over {G_{m}+j\omega C}}
 ={{(1+j\omega CR_{S})(G_{m}-j\omega C)}\over {G_{m}^{2}
   +\omega^{2}C^{2}}}$$

$$Z_{1}= {{G_{m}+\omega^{2}C^{2}R_{S}}\over {G_{m}^{2}
   +\omega^{2}C^{2}}}+j{{\omega C\,(G_{m}R_{S}-1)}\over 
   {G_{m}^{2}+\omega^{2}C^{2}}} \tag{4}$$

$$Z_{1}(s)={1\over {G_{m}}}{{1+s/\omega _{z}}\over {1+s/\omega _{p}}},
\qquad \omega _{z}={1\over {R_{S}C}},\qquad 
       \omega _{p}={G_{m}\over {C}} \tag{5}$$

Low frequency:

$$Z_{1}(0)={1\over {G_{m}}}\approx {1\over {g_{m}}}$$

High frequency:

$$Z_{1}(\infty )={R_{S}C\over {C}}=R_{S}$$

In ordinary voltage follower analysis $R_{S}=0$,
$\omega _{z}\to \infty $ and

$$Z_{1}={1\over {G_{m}+sC}}={1/G_{m}\over {1+sC/G_{m}}}$$

capacitive, ${\rm Im}\,Z_{1}<0$, a ${\rm C}=C/G_{m}$
in parallel with $1/G_{m}$.

In general ${\rm Im}\,Z_{1}$ in (4) is

$${\rm Im}\,Z_{1}\propto G_{m}R_{S}-1$$

> {\it If the resistance seen in the gate is large
> enough}

$$G_{m}R_{S}>1,\;\;{\rm more\;exactly\;(g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{S}>1}$$

$${\rm Im}\,Z_{1}>0\;\;{\rm for\;}\omega >0$$

i. e. inductive.  In $s$-plane the zero
$\omega _{z}$ is below the pole $\omega _{p}$.
Between zero and pole the phase of $Z_{1}$ goes
positive, $+90^{\circ}$ maximum, i. e. $+j\omega L$.

For $\omega \ll \omega _{p}$ we can expand (4):

$$Z_{1}\approx {1\over {G_{m}}}+j\omega {{C\,(G_{m}R_{S}-1)}
      \over {G_{m}^{2}}}+{\cal O}(\omega ^{2})$$

$$Z_{1}\approx R_{eq}+j\omega L_{eq}$$

$$R_{eq}\approx {1\over {G_{m}}}\parallel r_{o}$$

$$L_{eq}\approx {{R_{S}C_{gs}-C_{gs}/G_{m}}\over {G_{m}}}
        \approx {{R_{S}C_{gs}}\over {G_{m}}}\quad {\rm for}\;
           G_{m}R_{S}\gg 1 \tag{6}$$

more exactly $L_{eq}(\omega)=C(G_{m}R_{S}-1)/
(G_{m}^{2}+\omega^{2}C^{2})$.
With parasitics $C\to C_{gs}+C_{gd}$ etc. but the
form is unchanged.  Including $r_{o}$,

$${\rm Z}_{o}(s)\approx {{1+sCR_{S}}\over {G_{m}+g_{o}+sC}}
   \parallel {1\over {sC_{L}}}$$

i. e. a series $R_{eq}+sL_{eq}$ shunted by $r_{o}$ and
$C_{L}$.

In time domain: let $v_{x}=V_{out}$ jump up by
$\Delta V$. $v_{gs}=v_{g}-v_{x}$ wants to go negative,
so the drain current $G_{m}v_{gs}$ wants to fall.
But $v_{g}$ cannot follow $v_{x}$ instantaneously
because it is coupled only through $C_{gs}$ and the
impedance $R_{S}$. For a fast edge $C_{gs}$ looks
like a short but $R_{S}$ holds $v_{g}$ almost constant,
so initially $\Delta v_{gs}\approx -\Delta v_{x}$,
$\Delta i\approx -G_{m}\Delta v_{x}$ is large.
Only with time constant $R_{S}C_{gs}$ does $v_{g}$
charge up through $C_{gs}$ toward $v_{x}$, $v_{gs}\to 0$
and the current recovers towards its DC value.
Current lags voltage - the definition of an inductor,
$v=Ldi/dt$. The capacitance $C_{gs}$ is gyrated by
the transconductance into an inductance $R_{S}C_{gs}/G_{m}$.

The impedance stays $\approx R_{eq}+j\omega L_{eq}$ up to
about the pole $\omega _{p}=G_{m}/C_{gs}$, typically
${\rm GHz}$, after which it becomes $\approx R_{S}$
resistive, eventually capacitive again when $C_{gd}$,
$C_{db}$, $C_{L}$ dominate.

In particular with a capacitive load $C_{L}$ the
circuit is a $R\,L\,C$ second order low pass. The
inductor resonates with $C_{L}$ giving shunt peaked
frequency response, often used deliberately as an
``active inductor'' for bandwidth extension, and, if
$Q$ is high, ringing or oscillation of the source
follower with capacitive load. Damping requires
$R_{S}<1/G_{m}$ or an explicit series $R$.

With $R_{S}=0$ the zero moves to infinity, $\omega_{z}>\omega_{p}$
and $Z_{o}$ is always capacitive. The finite source
resistance of the driving stage is what makes the
follower look inductive. The same duality gives the
common gate input impedance inductive when the source
is capacitively loaded.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly derives the source-follower impedance and explains its transition from about 1/gm at low frequency to Rs at high frequency as Cgs couples the gate to the source. It identifies the rising, inductive behavior when the gate resistance is sufficiently large; the extra body-effect and loading approximations do not undermine the essential answer.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is a ${\rm shunt}/{\rm shunt}\equiv $ voltage sampling
current mixing transimpedance on two high
impedance invertors in cascade.

$$M_{1}:G\equiv X,S=GND,D\equiv V_{o},R_{D1}\,{\rm to\,ac\,GND}$$
$$M_{2}:G\equiv V_{o},S=GND,D\equiv X$$

i.e. two common source stages in a loop,
Fig.1b.

> $$v_{o}=-g_{m1}v_{x}Z_{o}\tag{1}$$
> $$i_{d2}=g_{m2}v_{o}+g_{ds2}v_{x}\tag{2}$$

$g_{o1}=g_{ds1}+1/R_{D1}$, $g_{o2}=g_{ds2}$ in
parallel with $C_{x},C_{o}$ at the two nodes.

With the normal ${\rm body}=S$ small signal model,
$r_{o}=1/g_{ds}=1/\lambda I_{D}$,$g_{m}=\sqrt{2k_{n}I_{D}}$,
$g_{m}^{*} =g_{m}+g_{mb}$ with body effect.

In saturation

$$\eqalign{
I_{D1}&={1\over 2}k_{n1}(V_{x}-V_{T})^{2}(1+\lambda_{1}V_{o})\cr
I_{D2}&={1\over 2}k_{n2}(V_{o}-V_{T})^{2}(1+\lambda_{2}V_{x})\cr
V_{o}&=V_{DD}-I_{D1}R_{D1}\cr
I_{in}&=I_{D2}+I_{G1}\approx I_{D2}} \tag{3}$$

at dc where $I_{G}=0$.
For $\lambda =0$, $V_{o}=V_{T}+\sqrt{2I_{in}/k_{n2}}$ and
$I_{D1}=(V_{DD}-V_{o})/R_{D1}$. The coupling is only
through $\lambda $. In saturation

$$V_{DS1}=V_{o}\ge V_{GS1}-V_{T}=V_{x}-V_{T}$$
$$V_{DS2}=V_{x}\ge V_{GS2}-V_{T}=V_{o}-V_{T} \tag{4}$$

otherwise one device goes triode and $g_{ds}$ rises
dramatically.

### Small signal - nodal

Put $G_{R}=g_{ds1}+1/R_{D1}=1/(r_{o1}\parallel R_{D1})$,

$$\eqalign{
{\rm at\;}X:&\;i_{in}=v_{x}(sC_{x}+g_{ds2})+g_{m2}v_{o}\cr
{\rm at\;}V_{o}:&\;0=v_{o}(sC_{o}+G_{R})+g_{m1}v_{x}} \tag{5}$$

$C_{x}=C_{gs1}+C_{db2}+C_{gd2}$, $C_{o}=C_{db1}+C_{gd1}+C_{gs2}+C_{gb2}$.
In matrix form

$$\pmatrix{sC_{x}+g_{ds2}&g_{m2}\cr g_{m1}&sC_{o}+G_{R}}
\pmatrix{v_{x}\cr v_{o}}=\pmatrix{i_{in}\cr 0} \tag{6}$$

So that with $\Delta =A\,B-g_{m1}g_{m2}$,
$A=sC_{x}+g_{ds2}$, $B=sC_{o}+G_{R}$,

$$\eqalign{
v_{x}&=i_{in}{B\over \Delta}\cr
v_{o}&=i_{in}{-g_{m1}\over \Delta}} \tag{7}$$

Hence the closed loop transresistance and the two
driving point impedances, $i_{in}=0$ for $Z_{o}$ test,

$$R_{m}(s)\equiv {v_{o}\over i_{in}}={-g_{m1}\over AB-g_{m1}g_{m2}}
 ={g_{m1}\over g_{m1}g_{m2}-AB}\tag{8}$$

$$Z_{x}(s)\equiv {v_{x}\over i_{in}}={B\over AB-g_{m1}g_{m2}} \tag{9a}$$

$$Z_{o}(s)\equiv {v_{o}\over i_{t}}\Bigl|_{i_{in}=0}={A\over AB-g_{m1}g_{m2}} \tag{9b}$$

by Blackman, the same denominator. Explicitly

$$R_{m}(s)={-g_{m1}\over s^{2}C_{x}C_{o}+s[C_{x}G_{R}+C_{o}g_{ds2}]
+g_{ds2}G_{R}-g_{m1}g_{m2}} \tag{10}$$

At dc, $s\to 0$,

$$R_{m0}={-g_{m1}\over g_{ds2}G_{R}-g_{m1}g_{m2}}
={1\over g_{m2}-g_{ds2}G_{R}/g_{m1}} \tag{11}$$

$$R_{x0}={G_{R}\over g_{ds2}G_{R}-g_{m1}g_{m2}}=
{1\over g_{ds2}-g_{m1}g_{m2}/G_{R}} \tag{12a}$$

$$R_{o0}={g_{ds2}\over g_{ds2}G_{R}-g_{m1}g_{m2}}=
{1\over G_{R}-g_{m1}g_{m2}/g_{ds2}} \tag{12b}$$

With $g_{mb}\ne 0$, $g_{m}\to g_{m}+g_{mb}$.

For the ideal square law $g_{ds}\to 0$,
$\Delta\to -g_{m1}g_{m2}$ and with $C\to 0$

$$R_{m0}\to +{1\over g_{m2}},\;\;R_{x0}\to -{G_{R}\over g_{m1}g_{m2}},\;\;
R_{o0}\to -{g_{ds2}\over g_{m1}g_{m2}}\to 0 \tag{13}$$

i.e. formally a finite $+1/g_{m2}$ but the
denominator has changed sign.

### Feedback interpretation

Put the forward path with the feedback killed,
$g_{m2}=0$:

$$a_{0}\equiv {v_{o}\over i_{in}}\Bigl|_{g_{m2}=0}
={-g_{m1}\over g_{ds2}G_{R}}=-g_{m1}r_{o2}(R_{D1}\parallel r_{o1})
\tag{14}$$

large, inverting. The feedback current fed back to the
input node is

$$i_{f}=g_{m2}v_{o}\;\;{\rm so\;\;}\beta\equiv {i_{f}\over v_{o}}=g_{m2}\tag{15}$$

sampling $v_{o}$, shunt mixing $i_{f}$ at $X$: shunt-shunt.
Nominally

$$a_{0}\beta ={-g_{m1}g_{m2}\over g_{ds2}G_{R}}\equiv -T_{0}\tag{16}$$

$$T(s)={g_{m1}g_{m2}\over AB}\tag{17}$$

is the usual return ratio. Two CS stages are each
inverting: $v_{x}\to v_{o}$ inverting,
$v_{o}\to v_{x}$ inverting via the $r_{o2}$ load,
so the loop is non-inverting: positive feedback.

In standard form

$$\Delta =AB\,(1-T),\qquad 
R_{m}={a_{0}\over 1+a_{0}\beta}={a_{0}\over 1-T_{0}}\tag{18}$$

so that the characteristic equation is $1-T=0$,

$$AB=g_{m1}g_{m2}\tag{19}$$

### Stability - positive feedback

$$p_{1,2}={-[C_{x}G_{R}+C_{o}g_{ds2}]\pm
\sqrt{[C_{x}G_{R}-C_{o}g_{ds2}]^{2}+4C_{x}C_{o}g_{m1}g_{m2}}
\over 2C_{x}C_{o}} \tag{20}$$

The discriminant $>0$ : both poles are real.
For a Hurwitz polynomial $a_{2}s^{2}+a_{1}s+a_{0}$,
$a_{i}>0$ for l.h.p. Here $a_{2}=C_{x}C_{o}>0$,
$a_{1}=C_{x}G_{R}+C_{o}g_{ds2}>0$ always, but

$$a_{0}=g_{ds2}G_{R}-g_{m1}g_{m2}=g_{ds2}G_{R}(1-T_{0})\tag{21}$$

$a_{0}>0\iff T_{0}<1$ for stable l.h.p. poles.
$a_{0}<0\iff T_{0}>1$ one pole is in the right half plane,
exponential growth.

$$T_{0}={g_{m1}g_{m2}\over g_{ds2}G_{R}}
=g_{m1}g_{m2}r_{o2}(R_{D1}\parallel r_{o1})<1\;\;{\rm stable}\tag{22}$$

For $r_{o}\to\infty$, $T_{0}\to\infty$ : the
ideal long channel circuit is inherently unstable.
Finite $g_{ds}$ is needed to stabilise it as a
linear amplifier. For $T_{0}<1$ the positive
feedback enhances the magnitude:

$$R_{m0}= {a_{0}\over 1-T_{0}},\;\;|R_{m0}|>|a_{0}|
\;\;{\rm and}\;\;R_{m0}<0\tag{23}$$

e.g. $g_{m1}r_{o1}=g_{m2}r_{o2}=20$,
$R_{D1}=r_{o1}$, $G_{R}=2/r_{o1}$,
$T_{0}=200$, far into the unstable region.
Reducing $g_{m}r_{o}$ to $\sim 1$ by low $r_{o}$
or degeneration $g_{m}R_{S}<1$ can make $T_{0}<1$.
Then e.g. $T_{0}=0.5$, $a_{0}=-g_{m1}/g_{ds2}G_{R}$,
$R_{m0}=2a_{0}<0$ : an increase of $i_{in}$ drives
$v_{o}$ negative, as expected for the CS inversion.

In the unstable $T_{0}>1$ region the small signal
slope about the metastable bias is

$$R_{m0}\approx +1/g_{m2}>0\tag{24}$$

the well known negative input resistance

$$R_{x0}={1\over g_{ds2}(1-T_{0})}<0\tag{25}$$

can cancel a passive load and is used as an active
inductor/NIC. Large signal the circuit snaps to the
supply rails: it is the NMOS latch of the SRAM sense
amplifier. With $T_{0}>1$ three dc solutions exist
for a given $I_{in}$: two stable with one device in
triode, one metastable with both saturated and
${\rm d}V_{o}/{\rm d}I_{in}>0$. Sweeping $I_{in}$
gives hysteresis. This is a current mode Schmitt
trigger / comparator with memory.

If linear transimpedance operation is required the
usual remedy is to make the feedback negative:
replace $M_{2}$ by a PMOS source follower or
resistor $R_{F}$ from $V_{o}$ to $X$: $R_{m}\approx -R_{F}$,
$R_{x}\approx R_{F}/(1+g_{m1}R_{D1})$, stable for any
$R_{F}$.

In summary, with the NMOS $M_{2}$ as drawn the
circuit is a shunt-shunt positive feedback
transimpedance stage, loop gain $g_{m1}g_{m2}r_{o2}
(R_{D1}\parallel r_{o1})$. For $T_{0}<1$ it is a
stable but gain enhanced $R_{m}\approx -g_{m1}/
g_{ds2}G_{R}/(1-T_{0})$ with enhanced $R_{x},R_{o}$.
For the usual high gain technology $T_{0}>1$ it is
regenerative, shows negative input resistance,
hysteresis and acts as a latch/comparator, not as a
linear amplifier, unless $g_{ds}$ is made artificially
large or degeneration is added.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies M2’s gate as tied to Vout (not diode-connected), explains the positive-feedback loop, and gives the correct consequences: negative input resistance, instability, and latching.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
With capacities neglected this is the $Y-Z$
combination

* samplig $Z$, $$V_{o}=V_{D1}$$
* mixing $Y$, $$I_{e}=I_{in}-I_{F}$$ on the
high impedance node

$$X\equiv G_{1}\equiv D_{2}$$

so that in the ideal limit it is a transresistance
$R_{M}=V_{o}/I_{in}$. The device used as ${\cal R}_{F}$
is $M_{2}$

$$I_{F}=I_{D2}=f(V_{o}),\qquad g_{F}\approx g_{m2}$$

$$V_{o}=-g_{m1}V_{X}R_{D1}^{\prime}, \qquad 
R_{D1}^{\prime}=R_{D1}\parallel r_{o1}\tag {1}$$

$$I_{F}=g_{m2}V_{o}+g_{o2}V_{X}\tag {2}$$

$g_{oi}=r_{oi}^{-1}=\lambda _{i}I_{Di}$.

In conventional notation $M_{1,2}$ are $n$MOS,
$S_{1,2}$ grounded, $B_{1,2}$ grounded so $g_{mb}=0$.
Put $G_{D1}=R_{D1}^{-1}$. For the small signal

$$\eqalign{
{\rm KCL}_{X}:& I_{in}=g_{o2}V_{x}+g_{m2}V_{o}\cr
{\rm KCL}_{o}:& 0=g_{m1}V_{x}+ \left(G_{D1}+g_{o1}\right)V_{o}} \tag{3}$$

$I_{in}$ ideal $\;R_{in\,S}=\infty $ , $V_{DD}$ AC
ground neglected. In matrix form

$$\left[ \matrix{g_{o2}&g_{m2}\cr g_{m1}&G_{D1}+g_{o1}}\right]
\left[ \matrix{V_{x}\cr V_{o}}\right]=\left[ \matrix{I_{in}\cr 0}\right] \tag{4}$$

$$\Delta =g_{o2}\left(G_{D1}+g_{o1}\right)-g_{m1}g_{m2} \tag{5}$$

$$\eqalign{
V_{o}&=-g_{m1}{\Delta^{-1}}I_{in}\cr
V_{x}&=\left(G_{D1}+g_{o1}\right){\Delta^{-1}}I_{in}} \tag{6}$$

i. e.

$$R_{M}\equiv {V_{o}\over I_{in}}=
-{g_{m1}\over \Delta }=
{g_{m1}\over g_{m1}g_{m2}-g_{o2}\left(G_{D1}+g_{o1}\right)} \tag{7}$$

$$R_{X}\equiv {V_{x}\over I_{in}}=
{G_{D1}+g_{o1}\over \Delta} \tag{8}$$

Output resistance, $I_{in}=0$, $I_{x}$ injected at $o$,

$$\eqalign{
0&=g_{o2}V_{x}+g_{m2}V_{o}\cr
I_{x}&=g_{m1}V_{x}+\left(G_{D1}+g_{o1}\right)V_{o}} \tag{9}$$

$$R_{o}\equiv {V_{o}\over I_{x}}={g_{o2}\over \Delta} \tag{10}$$

That is Blackman with

$$R_{M0}\to \infty ,\;\;R_{X0}\to r_{o2}\;\;,R_{o0}\to R_{D1}^{\prime}$$

and, with the usual sign convention,

$${\cal R}= {V_{r}\over V_{t}}=
{g_{m1}g_{m2}\over g_{o2}\left(G_{D1}+g_{o1}\right)}
={g_{m1}R_{D1}^{\prime}\,g_{m2}r_{o2}} \tag{11}$$

is the {\it return ratio} or loop gain $T$.
Break the loop at $G_{1}$, $I_{in}=0$,
$V_{t}=V_{X}$,

$$V_{o}=-g_{m1}R_{D1}^{\prime}V_{t}$$
$$V_{r}= -g_{m2}V_{o}r_{o2}=+g_{m1}g_{m2}
R_{D1}^{\prime}r_{o2}V_{t}$$

so that

$$1-{\cal R}=1-T={\Delta\over g_{o2}\left(G_{D1}+g_{o1}\right)} \tag{12}$$

and (7)-(10) can be written as e.g.

$$R_{M}= {g_{m1}R_{D1}^{\prime}r_{o2}\over 1-{\cal R}}
{1\over g_{m2}r_{o2}}= {R_{M\infty}\over 1-{\cal R}^{-1}} \tag{13}$$

with the {\it ideal} transresistance

$$R_{M\infty }={1\over g_{m2}}\approx {1\over \beta},
\qquad \beta \equiv {I_{F}\over V_{o}}=g_{m2} \tag{14}$$

apart from sign. In the conventional
voltage - current or shunt - shunt nomenclature $A=R_{M}$,
$\beta =1/R_{M\infty}$.

In particular for ${r_{o}}^{-1}\rightarrow 0$

$$\eqalign{
R_{M}&\rightarrow +{1\over g_{m2}}\cr
R_{X}&\rightarrow {1\over g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}}\cr
R_{o}&\rightarrow 0} \tag{15}$$

with the normal convention for the reference direction of
$I_{F}$, $R_{M}=-1/g_{m2}$, $R_{X}=-1/g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}$,
the circuit is nominally a low $Z_{in}$ - low
$Z_{o}$ TIA. With $r_{o}$ finite

$$R_{M}\approx {1\over g_{m2}}{1\over 1-
\left[g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}^{\prime}r_{o2}\right]^{-1}} \tag{16}$$

$$R_{X}\approx {R_{D1}^{\prime}\over 1-{\cal R}},\qquad
R_{o}\approx {R_{D1}^{\prime}\over 1-{\cal R}} \tag{17}$$

to first order.

> {\it Remark on sign:} With $M_{2}$ $n$MOS CS as drawn
> $V_{X}\uparrow \to V_{o}\downarrow $ via $M_{1}$ and
> $V_{o}\downarrow \to I_{F}\downarrow $ via $M_{2}$ so that
> $\delta I_{F}$ {\it subtracts} from the KCL at $X$ in the
> same sense as $\delta I_{in}$. i. e. the return signal
> is {\it in phase} with the test signal, ${\cal R}>0$.
> It is a {\it positive} or regenerative shunt - shunt loop.
> A normally stable negative feedback TIA is obtained by
> making $M_{2}$ a source follower, i. e. $p$MOS with
> $S_{2}=X$, $D_{2}=GND$, or $n$MOS $D_{2}=V_{DD}$,
> $S_{2}=X$, so that $V_{o}\downarrow\to V_{SG2}\uparrow\to
> I_{F}\uparrow$ and ${\cal R}<0$, $R_{M}\approx -1/g_{m2}$.
> In most text books Eq. 14 is quoted as
> $R_{M}\approx -R_{F}\approx -1/g_{m2}$ for the negative
> feedback version. The analysis above is identical up to
> $g_{m2}\to -g_{m2}$. With the $n$MOS $M_{2}$ to ground
> as drawn the loop is regenerative.

> Large signal DC: $I_{D2}=I_{in}=(k_{n2}/2)(V_{o}-V_{Tn})^{2}
> (1+\lambda _{2}V_{X})$, $I_{D1}=(V_{DD}-V_{o})/R_{D1}
> =(k_{n1}/2)(V_{X}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda _{1}V_{o})$.
> $V_{o}=V_{Tn}+\sqrt{2I_{in}/k_{n2}}$, $V_{X}=V_{Tn}+
> \sqrt{2(V_{DD}-V_{o})/k_{n1}R_{D1}}$.

Stability: From (5) the DC denominator changes sign for

$${\cal R}=1, \qquad g_{m1}g_{m2}=g_{o2}\left(G_{D1}+g_{o1}\right)
\tag{18}$$

$${\cal R}>1 \;\; \Longleftrightarrow\;\;
g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}^{\prime}r_{o2}>1 \tag{19}$$

is the regenerate condition. With normal $g_{m}r_{o}\approx
50-100$ and $g_{m}R_{D1}\approx 2-5$, ${\cal R}\gg 1$ and the
circuit as drawn is normally {\it latching}. Including the
dominant poles

$$p_{o}\approx {1\over R_{D1}^{\prime}C_{o}},\qquad
C_{o}=C_{db1}+C_{gd1}+C_{gs2}+C_{gb2}+C_{L}$$
$$p_{x}\approx {1\over r_{o2}C_{x}},\qquad
C_{x}=C_{gs1}+C_{gd2}+C_{db2}$$

the loop transfer is second order

$${\cal R}(s)={{\cal R}_{0}\over (1+s/p_{o})(1+s/p_{x})} \tag{20}$$

For ${\cal R}_{0}>1$ the closed loop polynomial

$$D(s)=1-{\cal R}(s)=0$$

has a right half plane root and the circuit is astable.
It becomes a bistable latch / Schmitt trigger / regenerative
comparator with hysteresis

$$I_{in\,hyst}\approx {\Delta V_{o}\over R_{M}}\approx
g_{m2}\Delta V_{o}$$

and can be used as a high gain - narrow band regenerative
TIA only for ${\cal R}_{0}<1$, i.e.

$$R_{D1}<{1\over g_{m1}g_{m2}r_{o2}}\tag{21}$$

if negative resistance operation is not desired.
Compensation is normally obtained by making $p_{o}$ dominant,
$C_{L}\gg C_{x}R_{D1}^{\prime}/r_{o2}$, and/or by
degenerating $M_{2}$ to lower $\beta =g_{m2}/(1+g_{m2}R_{S})$.

With the sign flipped to obtain normal negative shunt-shunt
feedback, $g_{m2}\to -|g_{m2}|$, $\Delta =g_{o2}(G_{D1}+g_{o1})+
g_{m1}|g_{m2}|$, ${\cal R}_{0}=-g_{m1}|g_{m2}|R_{D1}^{\prime}r_{o2}$
and

$$R_{M}=-{|g_{m1}|\over g_{o2}(G_{D1}+g_{o1})+|g_{m1}g_{m2}|}
\approx -{1\over |g_{m2}|}{1\over 1+1/|{\cal R}_{0}|}$$

$$R_{X}={G_{D1}+g_{o1}\over g_{o2}(G_{D1}+g_{o1})+g_{m1}|g_{m2}|}
\approx {1\over |g_{m1}g_{m2}|R_{D1}^{\prime}}\parallel r_{o2}\approx 0$$

$$R_{o}={g_{o2}\over g_{o2}(G_{D1}+g_{o1})+g_{m1}|g_{m2}|}
\approx {R_{D1}^{\prime}\over |{\cal R}_{0}|}\approx 0$$

the usual desensitized, low input and low output impedance
TIA with phase margin determined by $p_{x},p_{o}$ and
$|{\cal R}_{0}|\gg 1$, $GBW\approx |g_{m1}|/C_{o}$.

Any moderate $R_{D1}$ then gives stable operation,
$|R_{M}|\approx R_{F}$ where $R_{F}=1/g_{m2}$ is the synthetic
feedback resistor. Adding a physical resistor $R_{F}$ from
$o$ to $X$ in parallel with $M_{2}$ gives $R_{M}\approx
-R_{F}\parallel 1/g_{m2}$.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: It correctly treats M2 as a common-source device with its gate driven by Vout, identifies the regenerative loop through M1 and M2, and states that the usual loop gain causes latching. This satisfies the golden solution’s full-credit rule.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
The device is a ${\rm sh}{\rm -sh}$ i.e.
${\cal V}-{\cal I}$ i.e. transresistance amplifier.
$I_{in}\rightarrow V_{out}$.

$$R_{M}=V_{out}/I_{in}\;\;\;{\rm dim}: \Omega $$

Forward amplifier:

$$M_{1}:v_{g1}=V_{x}\;\;v_{d1}=V_{out}\;\;
i_{d1}=g_{m1}v_{x}+g_{o1}v_{out}+g_{mb1}v_{bs}$$

$$g_{o}=1/r_{o}\approx \lambda I_{D}$$

in this 3 T symbol bulk to $GND$ so $v_{bs}=0$
for $M_{1},M_{2}$. With bulk effect replace
$g_{m2}\rightarrow g_{m2}+g_{mb2}$.

Feedback amplifier:

$$M_{2}:v_{g2}=V_{out}\;\;v_{d2}=V_{x}\;\;
i_{d2}=g_{m2}v_{out}+g_{o2}v_{x}$$

$$R_{D1}$$ to $ac$ $GND$ at $V_{DD}$.

Small signal at $X$ the gate of $M_{1}$ is open:

$$ I_{in}=i_{d2}\tag{1}$$

at $V_{out}$ the gate of $M_{2}$ is open:

$$ {V_{out}\over R_{D1}}+i_{d1}=0\tag{2}$$

i. e. $V_{out}=-i_{d1}R_{D1}\parallel r_{o1}$,
inverting common source.

From (1)(2) neglecting bulk for simplicity

$$\eqalign{
I_{in}&=g_{m2}V_{out}+g_{o2}V_{x}\cr
0&=V_{out}\left({1\over R_{D1}}+g_{o1}\right)+g_{m1}V_{x}} \tag{3}$$

$${1\over R_{D1}}+g_{o1}=1/R_{D1}^{\prime}=
1/(R_{D1}\parallel r_{o1})$$

Elimination of $V_{x}$:

$$V_{x}=-V_{out}{1/R_{D1}^{\prime}\over g_{m1}} $$

$$I_{in}=V_{out}\left[g_{m2}-g_{o2}{1/R_{D1}^{\prime}\over
g_{m1}}\right] \tag{4}$$

$$R_{M}\equiv {V_{out}\over I_{in}}=
{1\over \displaystyle g_{m2}-g_{o2}{1/R_{D1}^{\prime}\over g_{m1}}}
={1\over g_{m2}}{1\over 1-g_{o2}R_{D1}^{\prime}/g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}^{\prime}} \tag{5}$$

With $r_{o}\rightarrow \infty $:

$$R_{M0}= {1\over g_{m2}}\;\;{\rm to\;first\;order}\tag{6}$$

The sign depends on the reference direction of $I_{in}$.
With the passive sign $V_{out}=-|R_{M}|I_{in}$,
$|R_{M}|\approx 1/g_{m2}$.  I.e. the
feedback transistor synthesises a feedback
resistance

$$R_{F}\equiv 1/g_{m2}\parallel r_{o2}$$

The ideal resistive ${\rm sh}-{\rm sh}$ TIA is
$R_{M}=-R_{F}/(1+1/LG)\approx -R_{F}$.  Here
$R_{F}$ is active and tunable by the bias
$I_{D2}=I_{in,DC}$ :

$$g_{m2}=\sqrt{2k_{n}I_{D2}}=\sqrt{2k_{n}I_{in,DC}}$$

So the transresistance is electronically tunable.

The DC bias, in saturation:

$$I_{D2,DC}=I_{in,DC}={k_{2}\over 2}(V_{out}-V_{T})^{2}
(1+\lambda_{2}V_{x})$$
$$I_{D1,DC}={V_{DD}-V_{out}\over R_{D1}}=
{k_{1}\over 2}(V_{x}-V_{T})^{2}(1+\lambda_{1}V_{out})$$
$$V_{x}=V_{DS2}\;\;,\;\;V_{out}=V_{DS1}$$

Saturation requires

$$\eqalign{
V_{out}&\ge V_{x}-V_{T}\cr
V_{x}&\ge V_{out}-V_{T}\cr
&\left|V_{out}-V_{x}\right|\le V_{T}}$$

Otherwise $M_{2}$ goes triode

$$I_{D}=k_{n}\left[(V_{GS}-V_{T})V_{DS}-V_{DS}^{2}/2\right]$$

$$g_{m}=k_{n}V_{DS}\;\;,\;\;g_{o}=k_{n}(V_{GS}-V_{T}-V_{DS})$$

and $M_{2}$ is a voltage controlled resistor
$1/g_{o2}$ from $X$ to $GND$.

### Loop gain - nature of the feedback

Forward gain

$$A_{v}= {V_{out}\over V_{x}}=-g_{m1}R_{D1}^{\prime}$$

Feedback gain

$$i_{f}=g_{m2}V_{out}\;\;,\;\;
\beta \equiv {i_{f}\over V_{out}}=g_{m2}$$

Closing the loop in the usual ${\rm sh}-{\rm sh}$
sense $V_{out}=A(V_{x})$ , $i_{f}=\beta V_{out}$

$$T\equiv -A\beta = g_{m1}R_{D1}^{\prime}g_{m2}r_{o2}$$

more exactly from (3)

$$T_{0}= {g_{m1}g_{m2}\over g_{o2}R_{D1}^{\prime\,-1}}
=g_{m1}R_{D1}^{\prime}\times g_{m2}r_{o2} \tag{7}$$

$V_{x}\to M_{1}\to V_{out}$ is inverting, 
$V_{out}\to M_{2}\to V_{x}$ is also inverting,
common source.  Two inversions $=0$ deg.

> The loop is {\it positive} feedback.

Indeed let $\Delta I_{in}>0\;\Rightarrow\;
\Delta V_{x}>0\;\Rightarrow\;\Delta V_{out}=
-g_{m1}R_{D1}^{\prime}\Delta V_{x}<0\;\Rightarrow\;
\Delta i_{d2}=g_{m2}\Delta V_{out}<0$.
A decrease of the current sunk by $M_{2}$ from
node $X$ leaves more of $I_{in}$ to raise $V_{x}$.
Regenerative.

Normal negative ${\rm sh}-{\rm sh}$ uses a
non inverting feedback stage, e.g. common gate
source of $M_{2}$ to $X$, drain to $V_{out}$,
or a source follower, or a resistor, or a $PMOS$
$M_{2}$.

With positive feedback the closed loop
denominator is $1-T$ not $1+T$.

From (5)

$$R_{M}={A\over 1-T^{-1}} \propto {1\over 1-T}$$

$$Z_{in}\equiv {V_{x}\over I_{in}}=
{1\over g_{o2}-g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}^{\prime}}=
-{R_{D1}^{\prime}\over g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}^{\prime}}
{1\over 1-T^{-1}}\approx -{1\over g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}}\tag{8}$$

for large $T$.

$$Z_{out}\equiv {V_{test}\over I_{test}}\Bigg|_{I_{in}=0}
={1\over R_{D1}^{\prime\,-1}-g_{m1}g_{m2}/g_{o2}}
=-{r_{o2}\over g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}^{\prime}}
{1\over 1-T^{-1}}\approx -{1\over g_{m1}g_{m2}r_{o2}}g_{o2}^{-1}\tag{9}$$

i.e. with the usual design values
$g_{m}R_{D}\gg 1$, $g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1$,

$$|T|\approx 10-100\gg 1$$

the input and output impedances are {\it negative}
and small. The ideal ${\rm sh}-{\rm sh}$ result
$Z_{in}=R_{F}/(1+LG)\rightarrow 0$,
$Z_{out}=R_{D}/(1+LG)\rightarrow 0$ is recovered
in magnitude but with a sign reversal due to the
positive return ratio.

### Stability

For a one dominant pole loop positive feedback is stable
iff

$$T_{0}<1$$

$$g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}^{\prime}r_{o2}<1\tag{10}$$

Otherwise the circuit latches as a bistable or
oscillates when the two poles

$$p_{x}\approx {1\over r_{o2}C_{x}}\;\;,\;\;
p_{out}\approx {1\over R_{D1}^{\prime}C_{out}}$$

add $180^{o}$ to the $0^{o}$ $dc$ phase, i.e.
the usual $360^{o}$ $Barkhausen$ condition.

In practice with $r_{o2}\to\infty$ the ideal
model is singular, $T_{0}\to\infty$, the circuit is
inherently unstable as a linear amplifier.
It is usable as:

* a tunable negative resistance
$R_{in}\approx -1/g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}$ to cancel
loss or to make an active inductor/gyrator,
* a regenerative latch/Schmitt trigger when
$T>1$,
* a very low $1/g_{m2}$ transimpedance stage
if $R_{D1}$ is made small enough or degenerated
so that (10) is satisfied.

To get conventional negative feed-back TIA swap
the feedback device to common gate/drain:
source of $M_{2}$ to $X$, drain to $V_{out}$ or
to $V_{DD}$, gate to $ac$ $GND$ or use $PMOS$
$M_{2}$. Then $A\beta =-g_{m1}R_{D1}^{\prime}
\times (-1)$ and

$$R_{M}\approx -{1\over g_{m2}}\parallel R_{F},\;\;
Z_{in}\approx {1\over g_{m1}}\,{1\over 1+LG}>0,\;\;
Z_{out}\approx {R_{D1}\over 1+LG}>0$$

stable for any $LG>0$.

With the circuit as drawn include $r_{o}$ and
parasitic $C_{gs},C_{gd},C_{db}$ to evaluate

$$LG(s)= {g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}^{\prime}r_{o2}\over
(1+sR_{D1}^{\prime}C_{out})(1+sr_{o2}C_{x})}$$

and compensate with a dominant $C_{c}$ at $V_{out}$
or by source degeneration of $M_{1}$ to reduce $T$.

> In short: $M_{1}+R_{D1}$ is the $A_{v}=-g_{m1}
R_{D1}^{\prime}$ voltage gain stage, $M_{2}$ is a
$g_{m2}$ shunt feedback transconductor synthesizing
$R_{F}\approx 1/g_{m2}$.  As drawn the two stage
loop is non-inverting $\to$ positive ${\rm sh}-{\rm sh}$
feedback, $|R_{M}|\approx 1/g_{m2}$,
$Z_{in},Z_{out}$ negative $\propto -1/T$, stable
only for $g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}^{\prime}r_{o2}<1$.
For normal negative feedback operation the phase of
the feedback stage must be inverted.

If $\lambda =0$, $r_{o}\to\infty$ form gives
$R_{M}=1/g_{m2}$, $V_{x}=-I_{in}/g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}$,
formal $Z_{in}=0^{-}$, $Z_{out}=0^{-}$. Finite
$r_{o}$ must be retained to get finite
$T$ and finite negative $Z$.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies that M2’s gate is tied to Vout, recognizes the positive-feedback loop through M1 and M2, and states the resulting negative input impedance and instability/latching. This meets the golden solution’s full-credit rule.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
The circuit is a shunt-shunt, voltage sampling
current mixing, transresistance feedback amplifier,
normally used as a Transimpedance Amplifier, TIA.
It can be regarded as a regulated cascode.

$$\eqalign{
M_{1}&:{\rm C.G.}, R_{D1} {\rm load} \cr
M_{2}&:{\rm C.S.}, R_{D2} {\rm load}\cr
R_{F}&:{\rm global }\;{\rm feedback}\;\;V_{o}\to I_{i}}
\tag{1}$$

DC can be made $V_{GS1}=V_{b}-V_{A}$,
$V_{DS1}=V_{X}-V_{A}>V_{GS1}-V_{T}$,
$V_{DS2}=V_{o}>V_{GS2}-V_{T}$ by choice of
$V_{b},R_{D1},R_{D2}$ and the d.c. value of
$I_{in}$ and the d.c. drop in $R_{F}$,
$I_{D1}=I_{in,DC}+(V_{A}-V_{o})/R_{F}$,
$I_{D2}=(V_{DD}-V_{o})/R_{D2}$.
In a.c. $V_{DD}$ is ground and $V_{b}$ is ground.
Put $G_{D1}=R_{D1}^{-1},G_{D2}=R_{D2}^{-1},
G_{F}=R_{F}^{-1},g_{ds}=r_{o}^{-1}$.

For the nMOS version the bulk is
strapped to the source so that in first order
$g_{mb}=0$. With $g_{mb}\ne 0$ put
$g_{m}\to g_{m}+g_{mb},R_{D}\to R_{D}\parallel r_{o}$.

> Bias is irrelevant for the feedback
> classification. For a.c. the small signal
> circuit is Fig.1

$$v_{gs1}=-v_{a}\;\;,\;\;v_{gs2}=v_{x}\;\;,\;\;
v_{ds1}=v_{x}-v_{a}\;\;,\;\;v_{ds2}=v_{o}$$

$${\rm drain\;current}=g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}
\tag{2}$$
from drain to source.

With the signs of Fig.1, currents leaving a node
$>0$:

* $X$:

$$ {v_{x}\over R_{D1}}+{v_{x}-v_{a}\over r_{o1}}
+g_{m1}v_{gs1}=0 \tag{3a}$$
$$v_{x}\left(G_{D1}+g_{ds1}\right)-v_{a}\left(g_{m1}+g_{ds1}\right)=0$$
$$v_{x}=v_{a}\,{g_{m1}+g_{ds1}\over G_{D1}+g_{ds1}}
\approx g_{m1}\left(R_{D1}\parallel r_{o1}\right)v_{a}
\tag{3b}$$
i.e. the current $i_{s}=g_{m1}v_{a}$ driven
into the source of the CG is converted to
$v_{x}=i_{s}(R_{D1}\parallel r_{o1})$.

* $a\equiv$ input, $o\equiv$ output:

$$\eqalign{
a:&{v_{a}-v_{o}\over R_{F}}+{v_{a}-v_{x}\over r_{o1}}
-g_{m1}v_{gs1}-I_{in}=0\cr
 &v_{a}\left(G_{F}+g_{ds1}+g_{m1}\right)-v_{x}g_{ds1}
 -v_{o}G_{F}=I_{in}\tag{4a}\cr
o:&{v_{o}\over R_{D2}}+{v_{o}\over r_{o2}}+g_{m2}v_{x}
+{v_{o}-v_{a}\over R_{F}}=0\cr
 &v_{o}\left(G_{D2}+g_{ds2}+G_{F}\right)+v_{x}g_{m2}
 -v_{a}G_{F}=0\tag{4b}}$$

For $r_{o}\to \infty $:

$$ \eqalign{
v_{x}&=g_{m1}R_{D1}v_{a}\cr
I_{in}&=v_{a}\left(g_{m1}+G_{F}\right)-v_{o}G_{F}\cr
0&=v_{o}\left(G_{D2}+G_{F}\right)+v_{a}\left(g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}-G_{F}\right)}\tag{5}$$

Eliminating $v_{a},v_{x}$,

$${V_{o}\over I_{in}}=-{1\over
G_{F}+{G_{F}+g_{m1}\over g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}-G_{F}}
\left(G_{D2}+G_{F}\right)}\tag{6}$$

with $r_{o}$ finite replace $R_{Di}\to R_{Di}\parallel r_{oi}$,
$g_{m1}\to g_{m1}+g_{ds1}$etc. Eq.(6) is the exact
closed loop transresistance $R_{M}=V_{o}/I_{in}$.

It is a shunt-shunt feedback amplifier.
$Y$ - parameters of $R_{F}$:

$$Y_{F}=\pmatrix{G_{F}&-G_{F}\cr -G_{F}&G_{F}} \tag{7}$$

so that the feedback is

$$ I_{f}=G_{F}V_{o}\;\;{\rm with\;a\;minus\;sign},\qquad
\beta ={I_{f}\over V_{o}}=-G_{F}=-{1\over R_{F}} \tag{8}$$

$$R_{M}={V_{o}\over I_{in}}={A_{0}\over 1+\beta A_{0}}
\equiv -{1\over \beta}{T\over 1+T}\tag{9}$$

where $A_{0}=V_{o}/I_{in}\vert_{R_{F}=0}$ is the
open loop transresistance. From (5) with $G_{F}=0$,

$$A_{0}= -g_{m2}R_{D2}R_{D1}\;\;{\rm in\;the\;limit}\;
r_{o}\to\infty \tag{10}$$
more generally $A_{0}\approx -g_{m2}(R_{D2}\parallel r_{o2})
(R_{D1}\parallel r_{o1})$, the cascade of the
$I\to V_{x}$ conversion $R_{D1}$ and the C.S. gain
$-g_{m2}R_{D2}$.

The loop gain $T=-\beta A_{0}$ is in the ideal limit

$$T_{0}\approx {A_{0}\over R_{F}}={g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}\over
R_{F}(g_{m1}+G_{F})}\left(G_{D2}+G_{F}\right)
\approx {g_{m2}R_{D1}\over 1+R_{D2}/R_{F}} \tag{11}$$

for $g_{m1}R_{F}\gg 1$, $g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}\gg G_{F}$.

Indeed from (6) with $g_{m1}\gg G_{F}$,

$${V_{o}\over I_{in}}=
-{1\over G_{F}+{G_{D2}+G_{F}\over g_{m2}R_{D1}}}
=-{R_{F}\over 1+{1+R_{F}/R_{D2}\over g_{m2}R_{D1}}}
=-R_{F}{T\over 1+T}\tag{12}$$

with

$$T\approx {g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}\over R_{F}}\,
{1\over 1+R_{D2}/R_{F}}={g_{m2}R_{D1}\over 1+R_{F}/R_{D2}}\tag{13}$$

Including $r_{o}$,

$$T\approx {g_{m2}(R_{D1}\parallel r_{o1})
(R_{D2}\parallel r_{o2})\over R_{F}} \tag{14}$$
up to the loading of $R_{F}$.

Hence for $|T|\gg 1$, i.e.

$$g_{m2}R_{D1}\gg 1+{R_{F}\over R_{D2}},\qquad
g_{m1}R_{F}\gg 1 \tag{15}$$

$$\;R_{M}\approx -R_{F}\; \tag{16}$$
$$i_{RF}={v_{a}-v_{o}\over R_{F}}\approx -{v_{o}\over R_{F}}
\approx I_{in}\tag{17}$$

the usual shunt-shunt result: the feedback current
almost cancels the input current, the input node is
a virtual ground for current. The sign is inverting:
a positive $I_{in}$ flowing into the source of $M_{1}$
raises $v_{x}$, lowers $v_{o}$.

The error with finite $T$ is from (12)

$${R_{M}+R_{F}\over R_{F}}\approx
{1+R_{F}/R_{D2}\over g_{m2}R_{D1}}
+{1\over g_{m1}R_{F}}+{\cal O}(g_{ds}R_{D}) \tag{18}$$

In the high gain limit the dependence on $g_{m1}$
cancels to first order because the forward
$I_{in}\to V_{x}$ gain is $R_{D1}$, not
$g_{m1}R_{D1}$: $v_{a}=I_{in}/g_{m1}$,
$v_{x}=g_{m1}R_{D1}v_{a}=R_{D1}I_{in}$.

Example: $g_{m1}=g_{m2}=1\,{\rm mS}$,
$R_{D1}=R_{D2}=5\,{\rm k\Omega}$,
$R_{F}=10\,{\rm k\Omega}$, $r_{o}\to\infty$,

$$A_{0}=-25\,{\rm k\Omega}\times 5= -125\,{\rm k\Omega}$$
$$T\approx {g_{m2}R_{D1}\over 1+R_{F}/R_{D2}}=5/3=1.7$$
$$R_{M}\approx -10\,{\rm k\Omega}/(1+1/T)=-6.2\,{\rm k\Omega}$$
increasing $R_{D1}$ to $20\,{\rm k\Omega}$ gives
$T\approx 6.7$, $R_{M}\approx -8.7\,{\rm k\Omega}\to -R_{F}$.

With $g_{m}=5\,{\rm mS}$, $T\approx 8-25$,
$R_{M}\approx -0.9R_{F}$.

Input resistance at the source of $M_{1}$.
Open loop $R_{in0}\approx 1/(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1})
\parallel r_{o1}\approx 1/g_{m1}$.
Closed loop, from (5),

$$R_{in}={v_{a}\over I_{in}}=
{R_{M}\over -g_{m1}R_{D1}g_{m2}R_{D2}}\,
\left(G_{D2}+G_{F}\right)\approx
{1+R_{F}/R_{D2}\over g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}}
\approx {R_{F}\over T\,g_{m1}R_{D2}}\tag{19}$$

$$R_{in}\approx {R_{D2}+R_{F}\over g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}}
\parallel {1\over g_{m1}}\,{1\over 1+T}\tag{20}$$

very low, ${\cal O}(10-100\,\Omega)$ for
$g_{m}R_{D}\sim 10-20$. This is the regulated
cascode action: $M_{2}$ regulates the gate of
$M_{1}$ via $R_{F}$ to lower the input impedance
by $1+T$.

Output resistance, voltage sampling, is lowered:

Inject $v_{t}$ at the output, $I_{in}=0$.

$$0=v_{a}(g_{m1}+G_{F})-v_{t}G_{F},\;\;
v_{x}=g_{m1}R_{D1}v_{a}$$
$$i_{t}=v_{t}(G_{D2}+G_{F})+g_{m2}v_{x}-v_{a}G_{F}$$

$$R_{out}={v_{t}\over i_{t}}=
{1\over G_{D2}+G_{F}+{g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}-G_{F}\over 1+g_{m1}R_{F}}}
\tag{21}$$

$$\approx {1\over G_{D2}+{1+g_{m2}R_{D1}\over R_{F}}}
= R_{D2}\parallel {R_{F}\over 1+g_{m2}R_{D1}}
\approx {R_{D2}\over 1+T'}\tag{22}$$

where $T'\approx g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}/R_{F}$.
For $g_{m2}R_{D1}\gg 1$, $R_{out}\approx
R_{F}/g_{m2}R_{D1}\parallel R_{D2}$, a few
$100\,\Omega$.

Frequency response. Two dominant poles:

$$p_{x}\approx {1\over (R_{D1}\parallel r_{o1})C_{x}},\;
C_{x}=C_{gd1}+C_{db1}+C_{gs2}+C_{gb2}+C_{gd2}(1+g_{m2}R_{D2})$$
$$p_{o}\approx {1\over (R_{D2}\parallel r_{o2}\parallel R_{F})C_{o}},\;
C_{o}=C_{db2}+C_{gd2}+C_{L}+C_{F}$$
$$p_{in}\approx {1\over R_{in}C_{in}},\;C_{in}=C_{gs1}+C_{sb1}+C_{F}$$

very high because $R_{in}$ is small.
The loop gain is two-pole,

$$T(s)\approx {T_{0}\over (1+s/p_{x})(1+s/p_{o})}\tag{23}$$

with unity gain frequency $\omega_{u}\approx T_{0}p_{x}$
if $p_{x}<p_{o}$. Phase $\approx -180^{\circ}$ at
$\omega\approx\sqrt{p_{x}p_{o}}$, so the two stage
shunt-shunt TIA can be underdamped or unstable if
$p_{x}\approx p_{o}$. Normally $p_{o}$ is made
dominant by load $C_{L}$ or a Miller $C_{c}$ between
$v_{o}$ and $v_{x}$ or a series $R_{c}$ with $R_{F}$
is used for compensation. The closed loop
$-3{\rm dB}$ frequency is $\approx (1+T_{0})\min(p_{x},p_{o})$,
i.e. bandwidth extension by feedback, the classic
gain-bandwidth trade-off of the TIA.

In summary, up to output swing and headroom
limitations, the circuit is a negative
voltage-shunt feedback amplifier whose ideal
closed loop behaviour is a transimpedance

$$V_{out}\approx -I_{in}R_{F},\qquad Z_{in}\to 0,\qquad
Z_{out}\to 0$$

with finite loop gain corrections (12),(19),(22) and
stability determined by the poles at $X$ and at the
output. It is widely used as a wideband low $Z_{in}$
current buffer, optical front end, $RGC$ TIA, with
noise, power and bandwidth set by $g_{m1},g_{m2},
R_{D1},R_{D2}$ and $R_{F}$. Including $r_{o}$ and
$g_{mb}$ replace $R_{D}\to R_{D}\parallel r_{o}$,
$g_{m}\to g_{m}+g_{mb}$.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies M1 as the common-gate input device, M2 as a common-source stage driven by X, and RF as feedback from Vout to the input, forming a transimpedance amplifier. This meets the golden solution’s full-credit rule.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
{\it The $R_{F}$ $X\to V_{o}\to R_{F}$ amplifier
is the normal ${\rm shunt\, (at\, the\, input)}\times 
{\rm shunt\, (at\, the\, output)}$ or voltage/current
feedback transimpedance amplifier - current in
voltage out - in its 2 transistor realisation -
the regulated cascode. }With $R_{F}=0$ it is
a conventional cascade $CG-CS$.

$$\eqalign{
M_{1}&:g_{m1},r_{o1}:{\rm CG\; }X-R_{D1}{\rm\; load}\cr
M_{2}&:g_{m2},r_{o2}:{\rm CS\; }R_{D2}{\rm\; load, }v_{G2}=
V_{X}\cr}$$

$V_{b}$ ac ground fixes $I_{D1}$, $I_{D2}$ through
$R_{D1},R_{D2}$.

$$V_{X0}=V_{DD}-I_{D1}R_{D1}\qquad V_{o0}=V_{DD}-I_{D2}R_{D2}$$
$$V_{S1}\approx V_{b}-V_{GS1}\approx V_{b}-V_{TH}
-\sqrt{2I_{D1}/k_{n}}$$
in saturation if $V_{X}>V_{S1}+V_{ov1}$ ,
$V_{o}>V_{ov2}$.

Small signal $V_{DD}=0$, $V_{b}=0$.

>$$v_{gs1}=-v_{a}\qquad v_{gs2}=v_{x}\tag{1}$$

$$i_{d1}=g_{m1}v_{gs1}+g_{ob1}v_{ds1}\qquad 
i_{d2}=g_{m2}v_{gs2}+g_{ob2}v_{ds2}$$
$g_{ob}=r_{o}^{-1}$.  $r_{o}=\infty $ at first.

The $R_{F}$ is the feedback
two port ${\bf Y}_{F}=\left[\,{\scriptstyle 1/R_{F}\;\;
-1/R_{F}\atop\scriptstyle -1/R_{F}\;\;1/R_{F}}\,\right]$.
It samples

$$v_{o}\tag{2}$$

and mixes

$$i_{F}= {v_{a}-v_{o}\over R_{F}}\approx -{v_{o}\over R_{F}}\tag{3}$$

in shunt with the signal current $I_{in}$ at the low
impedance source node $a$ of $M_{1}$ and in shunt
with $v_{o}$ at the output.  It is voltage-sampling,
current mixing, shunt-shunt, $Y-Z$ feedback.
$\beta =i_{f}/v_{o}\approx -1/R_{F}$.

With $i_{F}$ as in (3) the $a$ port KCL is

$$I_{in}+i_{F}= i_{s1}\tag{4}$$

and $v_{o}=Z_{m}I_{in}$, $Z_{m}$ the transresistance,
{\it transimpedance}, ideally $Z_{m}=-R_{F}$.

Cutting $R_{F}$ the forward amplifier loaded by the
feedback is, for $r_{o}\to\infty$,

$$v_{x}=g_{m1}R_{D1}'v_{a}\tag{5}$$
$$v_{o}=-g_{m2}R_{D2}'v_{x}=-g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}'R_{D2}'v_{a}
\tag{6}$$
with

$$R_{D1}'=R_{D1}\parallel r_{o1}\qquad 
R_{D2}'=R_{D2}\parallel r_{o2}\tag{7}$$

if $r_{o1}$ is taken between $X$ and $a$.  More
exactly

$$v_{x}\left({1\over R_{D1}}+{1\over r_{o1}}\right)
-v_{a}\left({1\over r_{o1}}+g_{m1}\right)=0\tag{8}$$

i. e. $v_{x}=g_{m1}(R_{D1}\parallel r_{o1})v_{a}$ to
$g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1$.  Open loop voltage gain
$A_{v}=v_{o}/v_{a}=-g_{m1}R_{D1}'g_{m2}R_{D2}'$.
Open loop transimpedance {\it with the $R_{F}$
loading at both ports grounded},

$$Z_{mo}= {v_{o}\over I_{in}}\Bigl|_{R_{F}{\rm \;as\;
load}}\approx -{1\over g_{m1}}g_{m1}R_{D1}'g_{m2}R_{D2}'
 =-R_{D1}'g_{m2}R_{D2}'\tag{9}$$

since without feedback $R_{in,ol}\approx 1/g_{m1}
\parallel R_{F}$.

Indeed for $r_{o}\to\infty$ nodal analysis without
approximation gives

* $X$ :

$${v_{x}\over R_{D1}}+i_{d1}=0\qquad 
i_{d1}=-g_{m1}v_{a}\tag{10}$$

$$v_{x}=g_{m1}R_{D1}v_{a}\tag{11}$$

* $o$ :

$${v_{o}\over R_{D2}}+g_{m2}v_{x}+{v_{o}-v_{a}\over R_{F}}=0
\tag{12}$$

$$v_{a}\left(g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}-{1\over R_{F}}\right)+
v_{o}\left({1\over R_{D2}}+{1\over R_{F}}\right)=0\tag{13}$$

* $a$ :

$${v_{a}-v_{o}\over R_{F}}-i_{d1}=I_{in}\tag{14}$$

$${v_{a}-v_{o}\over R_{F}}+g_{m1}v_{a}=I_{in}\tag{15}$$

Hence from (13)

$$v_{a}=-v_{o}{1/R_{D2}+1/R_{F}\over g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}
-1/R_{F}}\tag{16}$$

and

$$\eqalign{
I_{in}&=v_{a}\left(g_{m1}+{1\over R_{F}}\right)-{v_{o}\over R_{F}}\cr
&=-v_{o}\left[{1\over R_{F}}+\left(g_{m1}+{1\over R_{F}}\right)
{1/R_{D2}+1/R_{F}\over g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}-1/R_{F}}\right]\cr}\tag{17}$$

i. e. the exact closed loop transresistance for
$r_{o}\to\infty$:

$$\;
Z_{m}={v_{o}\over I_{in}}=
-{{g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}-1/R_{F}}\over 
{{1\over R_{F}R_{D2}}+{g_{m1}\over R_{D2}}+{g_{m1}\over R_{F}}
+{g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}\over R_{F}}}}\;
\tag{18}$$

$$\eqalign{
Z_{m}&=-{R_{D2}R_{F}\left(g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}-1/R_{F}\right)\over
1+g_{m1}R_{F}+g_{m1}R_{D2}+g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}}\cr
&=-R_{F}{g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}-R_{D2}/R_{F}\over
1+g_{m1}\left(R_{F}+R_{D2}+g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}\right)}\cr}\tag{19}$$

For $g_{m1}R_{F}\gg 1$, $g_{m2}R_{D1}\gg 1$,

$$Z_{m}\approx -R_{F}{g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}\over
R_{F}+R_{D2}+g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}}
=-R_{F}{1\over 1+{R_{F}+R_{D2}\over g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}}}\tag{20}$$

and for large loop gain

$$g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}\gg R_{F},R_{D2}\tag{21}$$

$$\;Z_{m}\approx -R_{F}\; \tag{22}$$

the well known $R_{F}$ transimpedance. More generally

$$Z_{m}={Z_{mo}\over 1+\beta Z_{mo}},\qquad 
\beta\approx -1/R_{F}\tag{23}$$

with $Z_{mo}\approx -g_{m2}R_{D2}R_{D1}$.

Including $r_{o}$ $R_{D1}\to R_{D1}\parallel r_{o1}$,
$R_{D2}\to R_{D2}\parallel r_{o2}$ and (18) becomes

$$Z_{m}\approx -{\,R_{F}\parallel R_{D2}'\,g_{m2}R_{D1}'\,
\over 1+g_{m1}(R_{F}\parallel\ldots)}\approx -R_{F}$$
to the same order.

The closed loop port impedances follow from
Blackman.  E. g. with a test $v_{x}$ at the
output, $I_{in}=0$, from (15) $v_{a}=v_{o}/(1+g_{m1}R_{F})$,
$v_{x}=g_{m1}R_{D1}v_{a}$,

$$\eqalign{
R_{in}&={v_{a}\over I_{in}}=
{R_{F}+R_{D2}\over 1+g_{m1}\left(R_{F}+R_{D2}
+g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}\right)}\approx
{1\over g_{m1}}{1\over 1+g_{m2}R_{D2}R_{D1}/(R_{F}+R_{D2})}\cr
&\approx {1\over g_{m1}(1+g_{m2}R_{D2})}
\quad R_{F}\gg R_{D2}\cr}\tag{24}$$

without feedback $R_{in,ol}\approx 1/g_{m1}$.
The extra $1+g_{m2}R_{D2}$ is the regulation.
In RGC terminology $G_{m,eff}=g_{m1}(1+g_{m2}R_{D2})$,
the cascode is ``regulated''.

$$\;
R_{out}={v_{o}\over i_{t}}\Bigl|_{I_{in}=0}
={R_{D2}\left(1+g_{m1}R_{F}\right)\over
1+g_{m1}\left(R_{F}+R_{D2}+g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}\right)}
\approx {R_{D2}\over 1+g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}/R_{F}}
\approx {R_{F}\over g_{m2}R_{D1}}\;
\tag{25}$$

for $g_{m1}R_{F}\gg 1$.  Without feedback $R_{out,ol}
=R_{D2}'$.  Both port impedances are divided by
$1+T$, $T$ the loop gain.  From (24)

$$1+T\approx 1+{g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}\over R_{F}+R_{D2}}
\approx {g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}\over R_{F}}\tag{26}$$

more exactly $T=g_{m2}R_{D2}R_{D1}/(R_{F}+1/g_{m1})$
from breaking the loop at $G_{2}$.  Typically
$10-20\,{\rm dB}$.

Frequency: with $C_{X}$ at $X$, $C_{o}$ at the output
and $C_{in}$ at the input - dominated by the
photodiode -,

$$\omega_{pX}\approx {1\over R_{D1}'C_{X}},\qquad
\omega_{po}\approx {1\over R_{D2}'C_{o}},\qquad
\omega_{pa}\approx {1\over R_{in}C_{in}}\tag{27}$$

Feedback moves the low frequency input pole up by
$1+T$ and splits the $X$ and $o$ poles, giving
large bandwidth for a capacitive source.  The
loop is two pole, $L(s)\approx L_{0}/(1+s/\omega_{pX})
(1+s/\omega_{po})$, so phase margin must be checked.
Usually a small $C_{F}$ in parallel with $R_{F}$ is
added to create a zero and stabilise, at the expense
of a little peaking.

In short the circuit is a wide band low $Z_{in}$,
medium $Z_{out}$ transimpedance amplifier,
$I_{in}\to V_{out}\approx -R_{F}I_{in}$, input current
- e. g. photodiode - is sunk mainly in $R_{F}$,
$i_{RF}\approx -I_{in}$, voltage is generated across
$R_{F}$.  It is universally used as CMOS optical
receiver front-end, TIA, RGC TIA. Noise, referred to
the input, $\overline{i_{n,in}^{2}}\approx
4kT/R_{F}+4kT\gamma g_{m1}+4kT\gamma g_{m2}
(R_{D1}/R_{F})^{2}+\dots$ dominated by $R_{F}$ and
$M_{1}$.

With $r_{o}$ finite replace $R_{D}\to R_{D}\parallel
r_{o}$, $g_{m}\to g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{o}$; the expressions
above remain qualitatively. Body effect $M_{1}$ is
cancelled if $n$-well is tied to $S_{1}$.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: Correctly identifies M1 as the common-gate input device, M2 as a common-source stage driven by X, and RF as feedback from Vout to the input node, forming a transimpedance amplifier. The golden solution’s full-credit rule applies; the feedback sign and detailed calculations are not required.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
Made with the customary small signal model:

$$M_{1}-CG~~~~M_{2}-CS~~~~R_{F}:{\rm global}$$

{\it N.B.} In ordinary operation $M_{1}$ must be
${\rm N}$ so that $A_{1}=v_{x}/v_{s}>0$ so that
with $A_{2}=v_{o}/v_{x}=-g_{m2}R_{D2}'<0$ the
return through $R_{F}$ be degenerative.
With the symbol as drawn $M_{1}$ is $P$ and the
loop is regenerative. In what follows the useful
form, $M_{1}$ ${\rm N}$, $M_{2}$ ${\rm N}$,
is assumed, Fig. 1 with $r_{o}\to \infty $ for
brevity, $g_{ds}=r_{o}^{-1}$ can be put
$R_{D}'=R_{D}\parallel r_{o}$.

> {\it Low Frequency Hybrid-$\pi $}  $V_{b}=ac~0$,
> $V_{DD}=ac~0$,

$$v_{gs1}=v_{g1}-v_{s1}=-v_{a}\tag{1}$$
$$i_{d1}=g_{m1}v_{gs1}+g_{ds1}v_{ds1}
      =-g_{m1}v_{a}+g_{ds1}(v_{x}-v_{a})\tag{2}$$
$$i_{d2}=g_{m2}v_{x}+g_{ds2}v_{o}\tag{3}$$

$${\rm KCL}\;X: {v_{x} \over R_{D1}}+i_{d1}=0\tag{4}$$
$${\rm KCL}\;o: {v_{o} \over R_{D2}}+i_{d2}
        +{v_{o}-v_{a} \over R_{F}}=0\tag{5}$$
$${\rm KCL}\;a: I_{in}+i_{d1}-{v_{a}-v_{o} \over R_{F}}=0\tag{6}$$
the last because $i_{d1}$ enters $a$ at the source,
$i_{RF}=(v_{a}-v_{o})/R_{F}$ leaving $a$ toward $o$.

From (4)

$$v_{x}\left({1\over R_{D1}}+g_{ds1}\right)
      -v_{a}\left(g_{m1}+g_{ds1}\right)=0$$

$$v_{x}=v_{a}\,{g_{m1}+g_{ds1}\over G_{D1}+g_{ds1}}
      \approx g_{m1}R_{D1}^{\prime}v_{a}>0 \tag{7}$$

$CG$ non inverting $A_{1}\approx g_{m1}R_{D1}^{\prime}$.
For $r_{o}\to \infty $ $v_{x}=g_{m1}R_{D1}v_{a}$.

Put $G_{Di}=1/R_{Di}$.

(5): $g_{m2}v_{x}+v_{o}(G_{D2}+g_{ds2}+R_{F}^{-1})
      -v_{a}R_{F}^{-1}=0$ (8)

(6): $I_{in}+g_{ds1}v_{x}-v_{a}(g_{m1}+g_{ds1}+R_{F}^{-1})
      +v_{o}R_{F}^{-1}=0$ (9)

(7)-(9) is the exact closed loop system.  In matrix
form $M_{c}{\bf v}= {\bf i}$,

$$M_{c}=\pmatrix{
G_{D1}+g_{ds1}&0&-(g_{m1}+g_{ds1})\cr
g_{m2}&G_{D2}+g_{ds2}+R_{F}^{-1}&-R_{F}^{-1}\cr
g_{ds1}&R_{F}^{-1}&-(g_{m1}+g_{ds1})-R_{F}^{-1}\cr}$$

$${\rm det}M_{c}= -\left[
G_{D1}(g_{m1}+g_{ds1})(G_{D2}+g_{ds2})
+{G_{D1}(g_{m1}+g_{ds1})+(G_{D1}+g_{ds1})(G_{D2}+g_{ds2})
+(g_{m1}+g_{ds1})g_{m2}\over R_{F}}\right] \tag{10}$$

If the two shunt feedback branches are cut the
$R_{F}$ loads remain but the cross terms
$-R_{F}^{-1}v_{a}$ in (8) and $+R_{F}^{-1}v_{o}$
in (9) disappear:

$$M_{o}=\pmatrix{
G_{D1}+g_{ds1}&0&-(g_{m1}+g_{ds1})\cr
g_{m2}&G_{D2}+g_{ds2}+R_{F}^{-1}&0\cr
g_{ds1}&0&-(g_{m1}+g_{ds1})-R_{F}^{-1}\cr}$$

$${\rm det}M_{o}=-(G_{D2}+g_{ds2}+R_{F}^{-1})
\left[ G_{D1}(g_{m1}+g_{ds1})+{G_{D1}+g_{ds1}\over R_{F}}\right]
\tag{11}$$

For the customary $r_{o}\to \infty $

$${\rm det}M_{o}\approx -(G_{D2}+R_{F}^{-1})G_{D1}g_{m1}$$
$${\rm det}M_{c}\approx -
\left[G_{D1}g_{m1}G_{D2}+{G_{D1}g_{m1}+G_{D1}G_{D2}+g_{m1}g_{m2}\over R_{F}}\right]$$

The ordinary one loop relation

$${\rm det}M_{c}={\rm det}M_{o}(1+T)\tag{12}$$

gives the return ratio $T$ or loop gain.
E.g. $r_{o}\to \infty $

$$1+T={{\rm det}M_{c}\over {\rm det}M_{o}}
      =1+{G_{D1}G_{D2}+g_{m1}g_{m2}\over R_{F}G_{D1}g_{m1}
      (G_{D2}+R_{F}^{-1})}$$

$$T={g_{m1}g_{m2}+G_{D1}G_{D2}\over R_{F}G_{D1}g_{m1}
      (G_{D2}+R_{F}^{-1})}\approx
      {g_{m2}\over R_{F}G_{D1}(G_{D2}+R_{F}^{-1})}
      ={g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}\over R_{F}+R_{D2}}
      =g_{m2}R_{D1}{R_{D2}\parallel R_{F}\over R_{F}} \tag{13}$$

In general, with $R_{Di}^{\prime}=R_{Di}\parallel r_{oi}$

$$T_{0}\approx {g_{m2}R_{D1}^{\prime}R_{D2}^{\prime}\over R_{F}}
      \quad R_{F}\gg R_{D2}^{\prime}\tag{14}$$
$$T_{0}\approx {g_{m2}R_{D1}^{\prime}(R_{D2}^{\prime}\parallel R_{F})
      \over R_{F}}\quad {\rm in\; general}$$

$T_{0}>0$ for the $N-CG+N-CS$ chain, i. e.
degenerative.  With the opposite sign of $A_{1}$
the loop is $T_{0}<0$ regenerative.

The $Y$ matrix of the feedback two port $R_{F}$ is

$$Y_{F}=\pmatrix{R_{F}^{-1}&-R_{F}^{-1}\cr -R_{F}^{-1}&R_{F}^{-1}}$$

so that in the shunt--shunt, $Y$, representation

$$I_{in}=Y_{11}V_{a}+Y_{12}V_{o},\qquad
  I_{o}=Y_{21}V_{a}+Y_{22}V_{o}$$

the feedback factor is

$$\beta =Y_{12}=-{1\over R_{F}},\qquad 
  I_{F}\approx {V_{o}\over R_{F}}\tag{15}$$

i. e. voltage sampling, current mixing,
shunt at the input, shunt at the output,
current in--voltage out, transimpedance or
transresistance amplifier.

> {\it Forward transimpedance} with $R_{F}$ loaded
> to ground at both ports, $I_{F}=0$,

$$R_{M0}={V_{o}\over I_{in}}\Biggr|_{R_{F}{\rm loaded}}
       \approx -g_{m2}R_{D1}^{\prime}R_{D2}^{\prime}
       \parallel R_{F}\approx -g_{m2}R_{D1}^{\prime}R_{D2}^{\prime}
       \tag{16}$$

the $CG$ transfers $I_{in}$ almost unattenuated to
$R_{D1}$, $V_{x}\approx I_{in}R_{D1}^{\prime}$,
$V_{o}=-g_{m2}R_{D2}^{\prime}V_{x}$.

Elimination of $v_{x},v_{a}$ from (7)-(9) gives the
closed loop transimpedance.  For $r_{o}\to\infty$

$$R_{M}\equiv {V_{o}\over I_{in}}
      =-{{\rm N}\over {\rm D}}\tag{17}$$

$${\rm N}=g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{F}-1$$
$${\rm D}=1+{R_{D2}+R_{F}\over R_{D2}R_{F}}g_{m1}^{-1}
        +{g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}+1\over g_{m1}R_{D2}}$$

i.e.

$$R_{M}=-R_{F}{T\over 1+T}+{\cal O}(g_{m}^{-1})\tag{18}$$

Explicitly, $r_{o}\to\infty$,

$$R_{M}=-{R_{D2}\left(g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{F}-1\right)
        \over 1+g_{m1}R_{D2}+g_{m1}R_{F}+g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}}
        \tag{19}$$

with $R_{Di}\to R_{Di}^{\prime}$ if $r_{oi}$ is kept.
For $T_{0}\gg 1$,

$$R_{M}\to -R_{F}{1\over 1+T_{0}^{-1}}\approx -R_{F}
      \left(1-{1\over T_{0}}\right) \tag{20}$$

the ideal shunt--shunt result $R_{M}^{id}=-1/\beta
=-R_{F}$.  The current $I_{in}$ is forced to flow
in $R_{F}$: $I_{in}\approx -I_{RF}=(V_{o}-V_{a})/R_{F}
\approx V_{o}/R_{F}$ because $V_{a}\to 0$ for large
$T$.

Numerical example: $g_{m1}=g_{m2}=2\,{\rm mA/V}$,
$R_{D1}=R_{D2}=1\,{\rm k\Omega}$, $R_{F}=5\,{\rm k\Omega}$,
$r_{o}\to\infty$ gives $T_{0}\approx g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}/
(R_{D2}+R_{F})\approx 0.33$, $R_{M}\approx -1.2\,{\rm k\Omega}$
far from $-R_{F}$; $g_{m}R_{D}=10$ gives $T_{0}\approx
8$, $R_{M}\approx -0.89R_{F}$.

Input impedance:

Open loop, $R_{F}$ to ground,

$$Z_{in0}= {V_{a}\over I_{in}}\Biggr|_{o}
        \approx {1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+R_{D1}^{-1}}
        \parallel R_{F}\approx {1\over g_{m1}}\parallel R_{F}
        \tag{21}$$

the well known $CG$ $1/g_{m}$.  Blackman's theorem

$$Z_{in}=Z_{in0}{1+T_{sc}\over 1+T_{oc}}\approx
        {Z_{in0}\over 1+T_{0}}\tag{22}$$

shunt mixing divides by $1+T$.  Explicitly from
(7)-(9)

$$Z_{in}={V_{a}\over I_{in}}=
        {G_{D2}+g_{ds2}+R_{F}^{-1}\over
        (G_{D2}+g_{ds2}+R_{F}^{-1})(g_{m1}+g_{ds1}+R_{F}^{-1}
        -g_{ds1}^{2}/(G_{D1}+g_{ds1}))
        +g_{m2}(g_{m1}+g_{ds1})/(G_{D1}+g_{ds1})R_{F}^{-1}}$$

$\approx$

$$Z_{in}\approx {1\over g_{m1}+R_{F}^{-1}
        +g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}/[R_{F}(R_{D2}+R_{F})]}
        \approx {R_{F}+R_{D2}\over g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}}
        \approx {R_{F}\over g_{m1}g_{m2}R_{D1}R_{D2}}
        ={1\over g_{m1}}{1\over T_{0}}{R_{D2}\over R_{F}}
        \tag{23}$$

e. very low, ideal $0$ for $T_{0}\to\infty$,
the virtual ground of the $TIA$.

Output impedance:  $Z_{out0}\approx R_{D2}^{\prime}
\parallel R_{F}$; shunt sampling also divides,

$$Z_{out}=Z_{out0}{1+T_{sc}^{(o)}\over 1+T_{oc}^{(o)}}
        \approx {R_{D2}^{\prime}\over 1+T_{0}}\tag{24}$$

ideal $0$ for a voltage output.

Frequency response: with $C_{x}$ at $X$, $C_{o}$ at
$o$, $C_{in}$ at $a$,

$$p_{x}\approx -{1\over R_{D1}^{\prime}C_{x}},\quad
  C_{x}=C_{gd1}+C_{gs2}+C_{db1}+C_{sb2}$$
$$p_{o}\approx -{1\over R_{D2}^{\prime}C_{o}},\quad
  C_{o}=C_{gd2}+C_{db2}+C_{L}$$

$$T(s)\approx {T_{0}\over (1+s/p_{x})(1+s/p_{o})}$$

$$R_{M}(s)\approx -R_{F}{T(s)\over 1+T(s)}$$

a second order loop.  For $T_{0}\gg 1$ the closed
loop poles are approximately the roots of
$s^{2}+s(p_{x}+p_{o})+p_{x}p_{o}(1+T_{0})=0$,
bandwidth $\approx p_{x}p_{o}(1+T_{0})/(p_{x}+p_{o})$,
i. e. bandwidth extension by $\approx 1+T_{0}$ at the
expense of gain desensitivity.  If $p_{x}\approx p_{o}$
peaking and inadequate phase margin,
$PM\approx 90^{\circ}-\tan^{-1}(GBW/p_{x})-
\tan^{-1}(GBW/p_{o})$, may require compensation,
e.g. $C_{F}$ across $R_{F}$ or $C_{c}$ at $X$ to
split poles.  The $R_{F}-C_{F}$ zero can be used to
cancel $p_{x}$.

In the literature this is the prototype
shunt--shunt $TIA$, photodiode -- $CG$ front end,
voltage--current feedback pair, often used as a
wideband transimpedance stage with low $Z_{in}$ to
absorb the photo current.  With $M_{2}$ feeding back
to the gate of $M_{1}$ it becomes the regulated
cascode RGC $TIA$.

Any finite $r_{o},g_{mb}$ is introduced by
$R_{D}\to R_{D}^{\prime}=R_{D}\parallel r_{o1}\parallel
r_{o2}$, $g_{m}\to g_{m}+g_{mb}$ in $A_{1}$ for body
effect.  The sign discussion above remains.

gpt_6_luna_max.rationale: It identifies the common-gate/common-source stages, RF feedback, and transimpedance function, but wrongly says the circuit as drawn has a PMOS M1 and regenerative feedback, then analyzes an assumed NMOS version instead. The actual circuit has an NMOS common-gate input and negative feedback, so this central error limits the score.

answers.question: Analyze the circuit shown in the figure.

answer.text:
This is a ${\rm sh-sh}$ transimpedance feedback
pair. $M_{1}$ is the $\left[{\rm CG}\right]$ 
feedforward amp, $M_{2}$ is the ${\rm CS}$ transconductance
feedback $V-A$ converter, Fig.1.

```
             VDD ac gnd
              |               I1
        |-----|----||--S M2 D---|-----o Vout
        |     S    |G           |G   |
        |          Vout         |   C Y
        |                      D M1  R1=ro1||roI1
        |                      |S  G=0 Vb
        X-----------------------|
```
